News.title: Pensioner found dead at home during cop probe into spate of burglaries – as man in 30s arrested on suspicion of murder
News.content:
'MURDER' PROBE Pensioner found dead at home during cop probe into spate of burglaries – as man in 30s arrested on suspicion of murder







Next

COPS investigating a string of burglaries have arrested a man on suspicion of murder after the body of a man in his 70s was discovered.

Greater Manchester Police were looking into four house raids where a burglar demanded bank cards from the householders which investigators believe are linked.

A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of aggravated burglary.



But when cops went to a fifth address, which they suspected was also connected, police found the body of a man in his 70s.



His death is being treated as suspicious and police have now also arrested their suspect on suspicion of murder.

Cops made the initial arrest on November 7, which then led to them visiting a potential other victim at Whitstable Close in Chadderton, Oldham.

It was during that search that officers discovered the body.



The man’s next of kin have been informed and they are being supported by specially trained officers, according to police.

Cops believe the Whitstable Close incident happened sometime between November 4 and November 7.

Detective Superintendent Amber Waywell said: “First and foremost, our thoughts are with the gentleman who has sadly died and with his family and loved ones at what will be an incredibly difficult and distressing time.

“This remains a complex and developing investigation, and we are working hard to establish the full circumstances surrounding his death.



“I would like to thank the outstanding work of our detectives, who have shown real determination and persistence throughout this investigation.

“We are also extremely grateful to everyone who came forward following our media appeals, with the most recent one being on Friday.

“We received a number of calls from members of the public, and the information provided has been invaluable in supporting our ongoing enquiries.”

Four burglaries between January and March this year have been linked by the cops, as well as a fifth incident in October.

All the victims were targeted in a similar way with the suspect trying to or actually gaining access to the properties before demanding bank cards and pin numbers are handed over, police say.



Det Supt Waywell added: “Protecting our communities and safeguarding vulnerable people remains an absolute priority for us.

“We understand the concern incidents of this nature can cause, particularly when offenders are accused of targeting elderly people in their own homes.

“Let me be clear: we take offences like these incredibly seriously, and we will not tolerate those who seek to prey on vulnerable members of our communities.

“If you feel like you have been a victim of this type of crime that may possibly linked to this investigation, or if you know of anything suspicious that matches these crimes, please get in touch with us.

You can call the GMP in confidence on 0161 856 9577, quoting the log number 2908 of 30/10/2026.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Information can also be submitted online at www.gmp.police.uk.

Alternatively, you can call the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.”

News.title: Moment brave cops wrangle snarling alligator in car park as beast hisses & lunges towards them during rescue attempt
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment brave cops wrangle a snarling alligator after it prowled into a car park.

The scaly fiend snapped its massive jaws at a Florida deputy – who hastily backed away while prodding the beast with a large pole.



The gator had been ripped from its wildlife habitat and washed into the concrete condo during several days of devastating storms.

Powerful rains have battered the sunshine state in recent days – sweeping unsuspecting wild life across highways and into car parks.



One unlucky alligator was swept into a parking garage in Sebastian.

Two cops raced to reports of the gator at around 12.30pm on October 30 in an urgent bid to capture the beast.



Dramatic footage shows one man lassoeing a rope around the predator’s massive jaws and pinning them shut.

Furiously lashing his powerful tail, the alligator can then be spotted lunging around a pole at the officer standing behind.

The second cop quickly secures a second rope around the jaws of the reptile.

The huge alligator started rapidly rotating in what may have been an attempted “death roll” – used in the wild to kill prey.



A deputy can then be seen kneeling on top of the alligator before the animal is loaded into a mobile cage – entwined in ropes.

The massive reptile was later set free in a wild location.

No one was hurt, including the alligator, according to the sheriff’s office.



Online viewers were impressed by the skill of the officers, saying: “Wow like how do u even train for something like that?! They stayed so calm. Impressive!“

Another added: “Good job Deputies! I’m glad you could capture and safely release that gator!”

It comes as commuters were left stunned on a Florida highway after spotting an ominous shark fin bobbing in the waters.

Chilling footage shows a suspected shark fin slicing through floodwaters over a busy junction.

The suspected bull shark can be seen thrashing through the watery chaos in Fort Pierce as trucks and cars zoom past.



Schools of tarpon fish were also spotted swimming through Gleason Park with stunned onlookers gushing that they were “amazed and excited” at the sea-life spectacle.

News.title: Brit holidaymaker, 19, ‘cried to parents for help’ before drowning in sea during family holiday to Bali, inquest hears
News.content:
SEA TRAGEDY Brit holidaymaker, 19, ‘cried to parents for help’ before drowning in sea during family holiday to Bali, inquest hears







Next

A BRIT teen cried out to his parents for help before tragically drowning while on a family holiday in Bali, an inquest has heard.

Mitchell Ogbourne, 19, died after going for a swim while staying at a luxury resort on the Indonesian island in October.



His horrified parents, Lisa and Paul, raced into the sea after hearing their son calling out from the water.

The couple managed to drag Mitchell back to shore before frantically performing CPR in a bid to save his life.



But the teenager was pronounced dead after being rushed to hospital, an inquest in Salisbury, Wiltshire, heard.

The family from Swindon had headed to a beach in Nusa Dua on the afternoon of October 13 when tragedy struck.

Mitchell decided to go for a swim as the water appeared calm and shallow, but got into difficulty as he ventured further out to sea.

His death was confirmed at hospital later that evening.

Heartbreaking tributes have since been paid to the teenager by Stratton Juniors Football Club in Swindon, where he and his dad had been members for years.

In a post on social media, the club wrote: “Mitch and his dad, Paul, have been part of the Stratton Juniors family for many years.



“During that time, they have built friendships and memories that extend far beyond the football pitch.

“Mitch leaves behind many friends and former teammates who remain part of our club, including within our senior section.

“There are simply no words to express the sadness we feel. To lose someone so young, with so much life ahead of them, is truly heartbreaking.



“Mitch was a wonderful young man who was loved, liked and valued by so many.

“His loss will be felt deeply throughout our football family and the wider community.”

Mitchell’s body was later repatriated to Britain, where a post-mortem examination found he had died from water submersion.

The inquest into his death was adjourned to a later date.

News.title: We live in the UK’s PIP capital…shameless kids bomb around in flash cars bought with benefits but are ‘too sick to work’
News.content:
Next

SET in breathtaking rolling valleys, steeped in industrial history and surrounded by beautiful countryside, Blaenau Gwent in Wales attracts more than half a million tourists each year.

According to statistics the sector contributes £43 million to the local economy each year, but conversations with locals in the region’s main town reveal a stark contrast to this success story.



While tourism in Ebbw Vale and the surrounding area is slowly increasing, at the other end of the spectrum so too is the number of people claiming the State’s disability benefits.

Figures reveal its home to the highest number of people who claim the state’s disability benefit, PIP (Personal Independence Payment) due to anxiety or depression.



Around one in 30 people in Blaenau Gwent, the local government district in the county of Caerphilly, claim PIP due to mental health problems, with 34.4 per cent of claimants declaring mental or psychiatric problems.

They contribute to the 211 claimants per 1,000 people, compared to the UK average of 97 claimants per 1,000.



It’s a statistic which weighs heavily on the community, which has previously come under fire as the ‘obesity capital of the UK’.

None of the shopkeepers The Sun spoke to on a weekday visit to the town were willing to be identified as ‘these people are our customers, so we don’t want to lose them’.



One told us: “I have sympathy for those who have legitimate claims, but it seems so easy for people to claim anxiety or other mental health problems and just get a handout.

“I suffer from anxiety and depression myself, but I have to get on with it and come to work every day, and sitting at home without a real purpose isn’t going make it any better, is it?”

New figures released by the Government reveal some 35 per cent of new claimants are under 35-year-olds citing anxiety or mental health as their disability on their claim forms.

The retail worker added: “I don’t think the work ethic is there anymore.

“They’re all out on a weekend driving around in a brand-new car paid for with their benefits and during the week they’re too ill to work.



“We have one customer who claimed she couldn’t walk properly, she was using a wheelchair, but her claim was knocked back, she failed to get PIP and the next minute she’s walking down the road in high heels.

“It makes me so angry because the system is so easy to take advantage of and it’s us taxpayers who have to foot the bill.”

The Department for Work and Pensions reported PIP handed out costs at £28.5 billion in the tax year 2025-26 and with the steep upward trajectory it is expected to rise to £45 billion by the year 2030.



Another business owner Ebbw Wale said: “There are quite a lot of people claiming who shouldn’t be.

“It’s just another way in which we pay more taxes.

“I’m going to have to shut my shop soon because times are so difficult right now.

“Although the customers are there, the rates we pay are too high and it’s no longer sustainable for us.”

We caught up with one of his customers in the town centre, a woman in her 70s who also did not want to be named.



She said: “I worked all my life since I was 15 until I retired because that’s what you had to do.

“These youngsters have it too easy and meanwhile I’ve paid tax upon tax and now after the budget I’ll have to pay tax on my pension.

“It’s like the world’s gone mad, or at least our government has.” PIP pays between £76.20 and £114.60 per week, paid every four weeks.

Mobility enhancements, for help getting around and carrying out daily tasks are between £33.30 and £80 per week.

On one of Ebbw Vale’s most deprived estates, Rassau, is marred by high rates of unemployment, a loss of local amenities and little for young people to do.



One resident Robert Woodward, 78, said the town of Ebbw Vale had not been the same since the loss of the steelworks, which was closed down in 2002.

He was a steelworker before embarking on a career as a carpenter.

He said: “If you speak to someone from my generation, we’ve mostly worked all our lives, but things have shifted somewhat.

“There are a huge number of people claiming benefits and I’m glad the Government chose not to increase them in the budget.



“What they should have spent more on is defence, especially with everything going on in the world at the moment – it’s frightening.

“Some people are genuine, but I think the vast majority see it as an easy way of living.

“I’ve seen one young man walk into the doctor limping and using a stick to walk, but once he was down the street the limp stopped and he could walk fine.

“The way to address both issues is to bring back National Service to straighten them out.”



One man, Darren Dempsey, 42, chose Ebbw Vale as his new home, having moved from London for a fresh start after family bereavements.

He is studying to become a social carer, which will mean he will eventually work with the types of people claiming disability benefit.

Darren said: “It surprises me that there are so many young people now claiming, but anxiety seems to be an easy excuse.



“Things are challenging in the current climate, but people need to be willing to study and work hard to get a more rewarding life.

“Because of the closure of the mines and the steelworks it has meant youngsters may have had a troubled start in life, with little money and social challenges from a young age.

“There are also more women on their own here because many of the men have died from industry related illnesses.

“Many struggle for money and work up here, which is a tough situation.”

Despite some claiming PIP is granted too easily, for others, the struggle with mental health is very real, with devastating effects.



Jessica George, 28, told how her mental state and severe anxiety took over her life after living in an abusive relationship which eventually ended.

She said: “I suffer from anxiety and claim PIP and it’s very, very difficult.

“I’m out with my cousin but if it wasn’t for her, I wouldn’t go out at all.



“I rarely leave the house.

“I used to be a carer, but I left because of the effects of an abusive relationship, and if I didn’t claim PIP I wouldn’t be able to buy food or pay the rent.

“It’s a lot less than minimum wage so ideally I’d like to get another job, but I don’t feel able to at the moment.”

Morgan, 23, believes Ebbw Vale, a town with a population of just 20,000, doesn’t have a lot to offer, and while there are a number of closed shops, there are still a number of independent businesses.

He said: “I’ve applied for 32 jobs, and they’ve either said no or just ignored me.



“Being homeless and sofa-surfing due to troubles at home, and just not being able to land a job despite trying has caused severe mental health.

“I also have a health condition which means if I walk far, it causes me to limp.

“I’m aware lots of people take advantage, but in Ebbw Vale there are not a lot of opportunities or reasons to come here.

“There are also a lot of groups of local youths who go round abusing local people and generally behaving anti-socially, so I think that environment causes people to suffer anxiety too.”

Ebbw Vale has a high crime rate, with 150 crimes per 1,000 people, with anti-social behaviour being the second highest crime, with more than 545 incidences reported last year.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The DWP is currently reviewing its PIP system, considering tightening eligibility and means testing against Universal Credit and awarding food vouchers rather thank directly paying cash into personal bank accounts.

Organisations like Citizens Advice have strongly criticized such measures.

News.title: Woman killed and 4 injured after horror head-on crash in foggy conditions sparks multi-vehicle pile-up – as man arrested
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SMASH TRAGEDY Woman killed and 4 injured after horror head-on crash in foggy conditions sparks multi-vehicle pile-up – as man arrested







Next

A WOMAN has died and four other people left injured following a horror smash involving five vehicles in foggy conditions.

The crash took place between Warmington in Northamptonshire and Elton in Cambridgeshire on the A605 at around 1.30am, today, November 8.

A BMW 2 and a BMW X6 were being driven in opposite directions when the collided, according to Northamptonshire Police.



The drivers of two HGVs stopped to help and a Kia Ceed then smashed into the stationary BMW 2.



The driver of the BMW X6, a woman in her 40s, died of her injuries.

Meanwhile, the driver of the BMW 2, a man in his 20s, was left with serious injuries.

He has also been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving.

Both lorry drivers were also injured, one seriously, during the collision with the Kia Ceed and BMW 2.

A passenger in the Kia suffered minor injuries, according to the cops.

The road was reopened later.

Detectives from the Serious Collision Investigation Unit are keen to hear from anyone who witnessed the collision or who may have dash-cam footage of it.



Anyone with information is asked to email CollisionAppeals@northants.police.uk, call the Drivewatch Hotline on 0800 174615, or contact Northamptonshire Police on 101.

Please quote incident number 26000690175 when providing any information.

News.title: Mystery as Royal Caribbean employee found treading water in Pacific by stunned fishermen 9 hours after going overboard
News.content:
Next

A ROYAL Caribbean employee has been found in the middle of the Pacific Ocean after going overboard.

The man who was rescued by fishermen after treading water for a gruelling nine hours, said he is a pianist on the 14-deck Ovation of the Seas ship.



The cruise ship docked in Los Angeles on Friday morning around 7am, but it was one crew member down.

Newport Beach lifeguards believe that the Royal Caribbean employee, who has not yet been named, somehow went overboard and plunged into the ocean around 2:30am.



He was found by stunned fishermen Sean Norton and Grant Garrett around 20 miles off the West Coast around noon.

Garrett told CBS News how they had been returning to Newport Beach after fishing for marlin near Catalina Island when the captain spotted something in the water.

read more on news YARD LURKER Man claiming to be Lebron James' son arrested for stalking NBA star at his home



“I’m like, ‘Yeah, it’s a human being. Stop the boat; let’s get all of our lines in,” he said.

“Grant and I each got an arm and lifted him up. He was in total shock,” Norton added.

“The only thing he said to me was, ‘Thank you. I thought I was gonna die.'”

Lifeguards raced to the vessel and the man was hospitalized and is expected to survive.



“It was approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, pretty much in the middle of the ocean,” Battalion Chief Adam Yacenda said.

The circumstances of the incident remain unclear, but Norton said the man likely only survived so long because of the super El Niño year that has kept water temperatures higher than usual.

“A different year, no way he makes it,” the fisherman said.

Royal Caribbean Group issued the following statement about the incident:

“We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time.



“To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share.”

An investigation by the US Coast Guard is ongoing.

News.title: Chilling minute-by-minute timeline of Krakow shooting as Brit among 9 dead after ‘terrorist’ fired ‘at random’ from car
News.content:
Next

IT TOOK just three minutes for a gunman to kill six people and injure 16 others in a terrifying rampage in Poland on Saturday afternoon.

Michal Oksinski, 24, is accused of gunning down his parents and younger sister before driving to Krakow to unleash 180 seconds of terror on tourists and locals before being “shot and neutralised” by hero cops.



Shocking footage showed people running for cover in the street as the deadly attack unfolded in front of their eyes.

Authorities have now launched a terror probe into the massacre as inquiries continue to try and piece together the suspect‘s motives.



The attack on the bustling Main Market Square in Krakow, Poland‘s second largest city, started just after 3pm.

Police said a man clad in combat gear and armed with a military-style rifle drove into the square and opened fire “at random” from inside the car.



Footage shows people fleeing in a frenzy through the streets as a black car speeds along the road – the sound of gunshots ringing through the air.

Armed officers raced to the scene after receiving at least 40 calls from members of the public reporting gunshots at 15 seconds past 3pm.

Several municipal guards responded but tragically, six people were killed, including a 32-year-old British national before police could arrive.

Within two minutes of the first emergency call, streams of brave police officers swarmed Krakow, cops confirmed.



A shootout quickly erupted with cops and the suspected gunman exchanging rounds of fire.

Jonathan Balshaw from Ipswich, who witnessed the horror with his Polish girlfriend Dominika, told the BBC how they ran into a church to take cover.

“A lot of shots were fired, more than 20 with it sounding like multiple different firearms – there were two distinctly different noises”, he added.

Three minutes after the first call, the suspect was downed by Jakub Kulik – a hero officer who was captured in footage standing over the alleged attacker.



Kulik, who was shot three times, used his last remaining strength to subdue the attacker and then kneeled to guard him until he collapsed.

Brave doctors, Professor Michał Pędziwiatr and Dr Mateusz Wierdak, were having lunch nearby when they heard the gunshots and ran into the chaos.

Two police officers were lying on the ground “conscious” with “gunshot wounds” close to where the attacker had also fallen down, Prof Pędziwiatr told local media outlet WP.

He added: “As we ran up, we saw a man in uniform and two policemen.

“At first, we didn’t know who the perpetrator was, and I even wondered where the perpetrator was. Of course, everything was resolved very quickly.”



Dr Wierdak used his hands to stem the flow of blood from the open wound in his chest.

“If not for this, the officer probably wouldn’t have survived, as he would have bled to death”, Prof Pędziwiatr said.

Thirty police crews were deployed to the operation within four minutes, Krakow’s police department said.



They were closely followed by 24 State Fire Service units and 62 firefighter-rescuers.

As the badly wounded suspect was arrested and taken to hospital, the emergency teams and police officers attended to the dead and injured.

The victims were soon confirmed as three Polish women, aged 61, 53, 51, a 50-year-old Polish man, a Brit man and a 51-year-old woman whose nationality is yet to be confirmed.

Another 15 people were injured in the shooting, including two heroic Senior Police Constables, Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański.

Among the injured include Polish nationals, a British national, as well as victims from Portugal, Russia, Germany and Austria.



Police spent hours surveying the scene and taping up streets which remain blocked as of Sunday evening.

Dozens of windows were left with bullet holes with smashed glass littered across the street.

The suspect’s car was found at the intersection of Dietla and Stradomska streets, and was checked for explosives, police said.



“Many pieces of weapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle”, a police spokesperson added.

City officials have urged people who live in the city and tourists to stay away from the area while an investigation continues.

As investigations went on late into the night, police raided the home of Oksinski which sat 125 miles away in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski.

Cops found his dad, 53, mum, 52, and sister, 21, dead inside with bullet wounds – bringing the death toll to nine.

One of the police officers seriously injured in the attack, Kulik, remains in a serious condition after surgery.



In an update on Sunday, police said two women who were sent to hospital after the incident had been discharged.

The remaining individuals in Krakow’s hospitals are in a stable condition, she added.

Local governor Krzysztof Jan Klęczar said the alleged gunman – who authorities say is not a soldier – remains in a critical condition at hospital.



Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home.

A minister has said early investigations indicate he was inspired by “far-right ideologies”. The minister also described him as an “ultra-nationalist”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Tusk said: “Until now in Poland we haven’t had such drastic cases of terrorism.”

UK PM Andy Burnham said he was “shocked and saddened” by the “appalling shooting”.

News.title: Brit, 19, desperately cried for help before drowning on family holiday in Bali
News.content:
Brit, 19, desperately cried for help before drowning on family holiday in Bali

Mitchell Ogbourne, from Swindon, died early last month after going for a swim in what he believed were calm, shallow waters off the coast at a Bali luxury resort

View 2 Images Mitchell Ogbourne died aged 19 after getting into difficulty in the sea at Bali (Image: Instagram)

A British teenager who died while on holiday with his family at a luxury Bali resort desperately cried for help as he got into trouble at sea, an inquest has heard.

‌



‌



Mitchell Ogbourne, 19, went out for a swim on October 13 while staying with his family at the Nusa Dua resort in southern Bali. The teen, an inquest held in Salisbury, Wiltshire, heard, had believed the sea was calm and shallow when he ventured out that day, before complications arose.

‌



His parents were alerted to their son's difficulties after they heard his screams from the shore, and they rushed out to haul him back. Hours later the teen was confirmed dead.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Mum of murdered Harvey Willgoose gets tribute tattoo of her favourite picture of her son READ MORE :

View 2 Images Mitchell was a beloved member of the community (Image: Instagram)

The Salisbury inquest heard that his parents, Lisa and Paul, swam out and dragged their son back before administering CPR on the beach. The teen was then rushed to hospital, where he was sadly pronounced dead that evening. The family, from Swindon, had been enjoying their dream holiday abroad in the southeast Asian nation when the disaster struck.

‌



His body was later repatriated, with a post-mortem examination confirming that the beloved teen had died of water submersion. Tributes have since poured in for Mitchell, who was a part of Stratton Juniors Football Club in Swindon.

The club wrote in a post on social media that both the teen and his dad had been a part of the team's family "for many years". Representatives said in the memorial post: "Mitch and his dad, Paul, have been part of the Stratton Juniors family for many years.

‌



"During that time, they have built friendships and memories that extend far beyond the football pitch. Mitch leaves behind many friends and former teammates who remain part of our club, including within our senior section. There are simply no words to express the sadness we feel.

"To lose someone so young, with so much life ahead of them, is truly heartbreaking. Mitch was a wonderful young man who was loved, liked and valued by so many. His loss will be felt deeply throughout our football family and the wider community."

Article continues below

The post added: "Our love, thoughts and prayers are with Paul, Lisa, Mitch’s wider family, his friends and everyone who had the privilege of knowing him. We cannot begin to imagine the pain they are going through, but we hope they find some comfort in knowing just how many people care and how deeply Mitch was loved."

The inquest was adjourned to a later date.
