News.title: Russell Brand trial sparks calls to protect women in showbiz industries with 'huge power imbalances'
News.content:
Russell Brand trial sparks calls to protect women in showbiz industries with 'huge power imbalances'

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said there need to be "far more robust processes in place to protect women" in industries such as media and entertainment "where speaking up can really cost you your reputation"

View 6 Images Russell Brand due to be sentenced on Monday (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said she believes high profile entertainment organisations are not doing enough to protect women.

She was speaking in the aftermath of the Russell Brand trial where the comedian was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. Tomorrow the comedian returns to court to be sentenced following his high profile four-week trial. He has been told by the judge he will face "a significant custodial sentence."

Asked about the situation, Nandy said: "I do think that there is a particular responsibility on media and entertainment organisations... to recognise that these are industries where people often are on short-term, flexible contracts, where there are huge power imbalances and where speaking up can really cost you your reputation and cost you opportunities.

View 6 Images Lisa Nandy issues warning to companies (Image: Wiktor Szymanowicz/Shutterstock)

"We need far more robust processes in place to protect women, like the women who bravely came forward in the Russell Brand case, to make sure that they are protected and treated seriously."

Nandy added: "Hand on heart, I don't think we can say that this couldn't happen today. In fact, I would wager that this is probably happening today, and I don't think that the industry is doing enough to tackle it. I can't see what has changed in terms of the way that many institutions in media and entertainment enable people to come forward, protect and support them. I can't see what has changed in the intervening years."

The cabinet minister urged organisations to sign up to the industry body that protects whistleblowers, and said the government is "considering what further steps we can take".

View 6 Images Russell Brand and wife Laura (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

Brand’s conviction last week is having an impact on both sides of the Atlantic. In the US there are claims his ex-wife Katy Perry is considering writing a book and making a docuseries on their marriage. They were married for 24 months but they split in 2011.

One of the women featured in the 2023 Channel 4 Dispatches documentary, known as Nadia, who accused Brand of raping her in Los Angeles in 2012, said his defence team was welcome to look at all the evidence she had. Her case did not feature in the trial as the alleged incident took place in the US.

She claims s he did not report the incident to police because she was worried her name would be "dragged through the dirt". She said: "It's ridiculous that I have to prove that I am real. It's so hard for any woman to come forward. It wasn't something that I was looking to do until I thought, 'it might help other women and it will make me feel better that I didn't stand up for myself at a time when I should have'."

View 6 Images Russell Brand's wife Laura leaves court after guilty verdict (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

It was claimed in US court papers that Brand boasted that having sex with multiple women was part of the "lineage of celebrated male behaviour". He allegedly claimed that being promiscuous was fine because it "defined famous men". He also allegedly claimed he knew about consent because he had been "in a lot of bathrooms with people he doesn't know very well".

The statement was made as part of a US civil lawsuit filed by a woman who claims that he sexually assaulted her on the set of the 2011 comedy film Arthur, when the Essex-born actor was married to pop star Katy Perry. The case is due to go to trial in the US next March but that could now be delayed.

Legal sources said last night that Brand, 51, is facing the prospect of further civil claims, both in the UK, where one has already been lodged, and in the US. It is possible prosecutors in the US could also decide to pursue Brand with criminal action.

View 6 Images Lisa Nandy with Laura Kuenssberg. (Image: Jeff Overs/BBC/Press Association)

‌



Brand faced allegations from six women during the trial, which dated from between 1999 and 2009. Last week at Southwark Crown Court, a jury unanimously found Brand guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault between 2004 and 2009 - at the height of his fame. Mr Justice Bennathan warned the serial sex offender that he faced a "significant custodial sentence".

Brand was convicted of raping a 21-year-old fan he met after a comedy gig at the Hammersmith Apollo in London. The comic, then 33, forced the woman face-down into a pillow while raping her at his mansion in Hampstead, North West London, removing a condom without consent and leaving her struggling to breathe. Afterwards he ordered his bleeding victim to "clean up the mess you've made" before switching on the TV.

‌



View 6 Images Russell Brand due to be sentenced on Monday (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

Each woman told the court how he forced them into sexual activity, sometimes within seconds of meeting them, while exploiting his fame to feed his sexual appetite. After eight-and-a-half hours of deliberations, jurors convicted him of sexually assaulting an MTV worker at a party in a Soho bar in 2004 but cleared him of orally raping her in a toilet afterwards.

Article continues below

They also found Brand, who is now a born-again Christian, guilty of sexually assaulting a woman at the Choice FM radio studio in 2004 or 2005. She told the court he violently grabbed her buttocks and breasts, while kissing her as his entourage looked on and one laughed. He was also convicted of sexually assaulting a Channel 4 worker in 2009 after she was forced to give him a massage by two of his colleagues.

News.title: Police officers injured as huge brawl erupts outside Glasgow Hydro after fight night
News.content:
Police officers injured as huge brawl erupts outside Glasgow Hydro after fight night

Groups of men began fighting as crowds left a bare-knuckle fighting event at the Ovo Hydro arena in Glasgow with Police Scotland reporting three officers were injured during the disorder

View 2 Images Police attacked in huge street brawl in Glasgow after bare knuckle fighting event

Two men have been arrested following a large disturbance outside a UK arena after a bare-knuckle fighting event.

Groups of men began fighting on Congress Road, outside the Ovo Hydro arena in Glasgow, at around 11.10pm on Saturday as crowds left a bare-knuckle fighting event at the venue.

Police Scotland said three officers were injured during the disorder, with two requiring medical treatment.

Two men, aged 27 and 32, were arrested and charged with offences including assault, obstructing police and threatening and abusive behaviour.

They are due to appear in court on Monday.

Three other men were arrested and issued with recorded police warnings for threatening and abusive behaviour and breach of the peace.

View 2 Images Officers were left needing medical treatment after being attacked

Videos posted on social media show a large number of police vehicles around Finnieston Quay and Finnieston Street.

In some footage, groups of men can be seen punching and kicking each other on the Clyde Arc bridge before police move in to break up the fighting.

Police have said they will bring those responsible to justice.

Chief Inspector Paul Daley said: “Several officers were assaulted whilst carrying out their duties during disorder following an event at the Hydro in Glasgow on Saturday night.

“Violence against officers is disgraceful and will not be tolerated. Being assaulted is not part of the job and it’s extremely fortunate they were not seriously injured.

“Officers are carrying out extensive inquiries in relation to the disturbance which occurred and anyone found responsible will be brought to justice.

“I would appeal to the public for information to assist our inquiries. Anyone with information should contact police via 101, quoting incident 2029 of November 7.

Article continues below

“We continue to work closely with partners and event organisers to assist their plans for maintaining public safety and to ensure that the overall experience is safe for those in attendance and the local community.”

The Hydro hosted an event by the Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship on Saturday, with thousands of spectators gathering to watch the hand-to-hand combat.

News.title: Seven teens injured after car mounts pavement in Dublin as eight rushed to hospital
News.content:
Seven teens injured after car mounts pavement in Dublin as eight rushed to hospital

According to multiple reports, a car is understood to have mounted a footpath outside shops on Oliver Plunkett Road with several people, including a number of teenagers, understood to be injured

View Image A car is understood to have mounted a footpath outside shops on Oliver Plunkett Road (Image: Dublin Live)

Seven teenagers are among those injured after a car reportedly mounted the pavement near shops in Dublin.

‌



‌



The incident happened at around 3:30pm with eight people reportedly injured, including the driver - seven of the victims are teenagers, Dublin Live reports. All of the injured have been taken to hospital.

‌



A Garda spokesperson said: "Gardaí are investigating a serious road traffic collision involving a car and seven pedestrians on Oliver Plunkett Road, Dún Laoghaire, today, Sunday 8th November 2026 at approximately 3:00pm.

‌



"The seven juvenile pedestrians, all teenagers, and the driver of the car, a woman aged in her 40s, sustained varying degrees of injuries. All eight individuals have been taken to different hospitals for treatment. Gardaí are continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding the collision."

Authorities are at the scene and it is understood the road is currently closed

‌



Local Fine Gael Councillor Dan Carson said: "I am aware of a serious vehicle incident in Monkstown farm. My thoughts are with the first responders currently on scene and the families of those affected."

According to multiple reports, a car is understood to have mounted a footpath outside shops on Oliver Plunkett Road. Several people, including a number of teenagers, are understood to have been injured in the incident.

Article continues below

Six people reportedly injured in the incident. It is understood five of the victims are teenagers aged between 14 and 15. Gardai, paramedics and firefighters are at the scene and at least one person has been rushed to hospital.

A Garda spokeswoman told Dublin Live: "Gardaí are at the scene of a serious road traffic collision." No further information has been released by officials.

News.title: Schools and family homes at risk of fires or toxic leaks from gangs' illegal waste dumps
News.content:
Schools and family homes at risk of fires or toxic leaks from gangs' illegal waste dumps

EXCLUSIVE: Environment Secretary Angela Eagle has vowed to treat gangs who dump tonnes of illegal waste like drug criminals - warning them that she is 'coming for you'

Schools and family homes are at risk from potentially dangerous fires or toxic leaks nearby caused by criminal gangs illegally dumping tonnes of waste in their communities.

‌



Environment Secretary Angela Eagle has vowed to treat waste gangs like drug criminals - warning them that she is “coming for you”. The former Home Office minister has been on the frontline of the Government’s work since her appointment as environment chief in July was followed by heatwaves, wildfires and ongoing droughts.

In her first interview with The Mirror, she vowed to tackle environmental issues with the urgency they deserve, adding that climate change is “here now” and El Niño hasn’t happened “by accident”. Her first major drive is cleaning up the mountains of illegally dumped vapes, household rubbish, bricks, asbestos and other waste that are blighting people’s lives across Britain.

Criminal gangs face fresh crackdown over illegal dumping sites READ MORE :

Criminal gangs who illegally dump mountains of rubbish face fines increased by 16 times READ MORE :

View 3 Images Andy Burnham visited a waste dump estimated to hold several thousand tonnes of waste at Midland Road, Bradford, with Angela Eagle (Image: Lauren Hurley / No 10 Downing Street)

Schools have been forced to close because of toxic air and smoke coming from fires, while there are concerns about chemical leaks into groundwater, severe public health risks and the risk of a major environmental crisis. An estimated 20% of waste streams are controlled by organised criminality.

The Mirror joined Dame Angela last week for the first meeting of the waste crime crackdown group, where she told mayors, waste experts and other ministers she will not “tolerate” the scourge. Asked for her message to waste criminals, she told this newspaper: “We're coming for you. We're going to stop you doing this, and we are going to - once we've convicted you - take your ill-gotten gains off you.

“You're not going to profit from behaving in this way and putting our children and communities at risk, having to live next door to these waste sites, anymore. So your low-risk, high-profitable activity is over.”

Waste crime can take place in a variety of ways but can include criminals posing as a legitimate company - such as a white van removal service - or intercepting legal waste disposal processes. It means regular households who are trying to dispose of their waste correctly, such as when they are renovating or moving home, may unknowingly send their money to gangs who then spend it on illicit activities.

Some 36 waste criminals have been arrested since April this year, while several major illegal waste sites have been fully cleared. Among sites cleaned up is Kidlington's waste dump, which was larger than the pitch at Wembley Stadium and contained more than 22,000 tonnes of waste, including tyres, shredded plastic, and household rubbish.

View 3 Images A ginormous dump is blighting people's lives in Andy Burnham's Makerfield constituency (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

The government has also committed to cleaning up some of the country’s most egregious illegal waste sites, including an 18,000-tonne site at Bolton House Road in Wigan, which is in Andy Burnham’s Makerfield constituency. A fire at the site in July caused businesses to close and children to miss several days of school. Locals are being offered dedicated health checks amid fears over chemicals dumped at the site.

In his first month as Prime Minister, Mr Burnham put a crackdown on waste crime at the top of his agenda, saying that mountains of rubbish are “a clear sign to communities that politics hasn’t been working for them”. He visited a waste dump estimated to hold several thousand tonnes of waste at Midland Road, Bradford, with Dame Angela in August, when he announced an increase in fines for waste offences from £300 to £5,000.

Those responsible for serious offences face tougher sanctions, including prosecution and imprisonment. Dame Angela, who is also in charge of the water sector, blamed Margaret Thatcher for the privatisation of the waste management sector - the same analysis Mr Burnham has made of the water industry. The PM in September announced he will bring in new laws to allow the Government to take back control of water.

Asked if public ownership could be on the cards for waste management, Dame Angela said: “It may be at some time in the future we might want to think about ownership, but I think we've got more immediate things to do now, and that is to deal with the serious and organised crime issues and to deal with the toxic waste that is ending up far too close to communities blighting people's lives.”

View 3 Images Angela Eagle said the Labour government is the 'only political party' taking the climate and the environment seriously (Image: Philip Coburn)

The Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Secretary, who has been an MP for more than 30 years, added that the Labour government is the “only political party" taking the climate and the environment seriously, amid the Tories and Reform diverging from the UK's climate change plans.

She admitted it is hard to predict the impact of the El Niño climate phenomenon but that it could cause more extreme storms and wetter winters in the UK, or disruption to global food supply chains.

She said: “This is climate change. It is here now. It is happening now. This El Niño hasn't come about by accident. Now I think the Labour government is the only political party that's actually taking this seriously and thinking about what we can do to adapt, as well as trying to come to international agreements to mitigate the effects.

“I mean, the Tories are moving away from net zero. Reform seems to think that it's all about having nicer wine. Nicer wine is very nice, but you have to deal with the fact that our weather patterns are changing, or what effect that will have not only in our country but on food security more generally. So yeah, it's here now, and we need to realise that it is and adapt our systems to cope with the unpredictability of it.”

News.title: Police logged record number of up-skirting offences last year, but barely one in 10 led to a charge
News.content:
Police logged record number of up-skirting offences last year, but barely one in 10 led to a charge

EXCLUSIVE: Some 527 women reported perverts secretly filming up their skirts – 35% more than the 390 in 2024 and the highest since the law came into force in 2019

View 4 Images Some 527 women reported perverts secretly filming up their skirts (Image: Stuart Wallace/Shutterstock)

Police logged a record number of up-skirting offences last year – yet barely one in 10 led to a charge.

‌



‌



Some 527 women reported perverts secretly filming up their skirts – 35% more than the 390 in 2024 and the highest since the law came into force. But just 58 - 11% - ended with the offender being charged and sent to court.

‌



The Home Office data, obtained under Freedom of Information laws, shows four were let off with a caution and one was handed a community resolution. A further 204 cases were shelved without a suspect being identified, and 122 collapsed due to a lack of evidence.

‌



View 4 Images Up-skirting reports are up 35% on 2024 (Image: Iconic Media / SWNS)

The up-skirting sickos used phones, hidden cameras and even shoes fitted with lenses to film under women’s clothing. The offences took place on trains, escalators, in shops and on nights out. Separately, British Transport Police logged 104 upskirting offences last year, more than any other force, but only two have so far led to a charge.

Up-skirting became a specific crime in 2019 after campaigner Gina Martin was filmed by a stranger at a music festival in London and police failed to do anything. In September, ITV's The Bay star Georgia Scholes, 25, and her sister Alex, 22, were filmed by two men on a flight of stairs after a night out in Manchester. Greater Manchester Police arrested two men in their 20s and 30s on suspicion of voyeurism after the incident in September, but both have been released on bail.

‌



View 4 Images Actress Georgia Scholes reported an up-skirting indicent to the police (Image: ITV/Ben Blackall/REX/Shutterstock)

A Home Office spokesperson said: “We are committed to tackling violence against women and girls in all its forms. We know there is more to do to ensure these victims get the response they deserve and perpetrators are brought to justice. We have supported the development of new training on non-contact sexual offences to support officers to better tackle these crimes.”

‌



Siobhan Blake, CPS national lead for sexual offence prosecutions, said: “Up-skirting violates women’s privacy in a most degrading manner as they go about their daily lives. These are disturbing patterns of behaviour which can in some cases link to other sexual offending.

"We can only prosecute cases referred to us by police and our data shows we have taken more than 200 up-skirting offences to court over the last 12 months – a figure increasing annually. I would encourage victims to report this criminal behaviour to the police safe in the knowledge we will take them seriously.”

‌



View 4 Images The British Transport Police logged 104 up-skirting offences last year (Image: Pete Stonier)

A BTP spokesperson: “As a force, we secured 20 charges and postal requisitions for up-skirting offences last year, and we’re committed to securing justice for every victim. Investigations into many offences reported in 2025 are still ongoing.It is important to note that they are often complex and protracted, involving the seizure of multiple digital devices which require the forensic examination of hundreds, and sometimes thousands, of digital materials before a file can be submitted to the CPS for a charging decision.

Article continues below

“Our solved rate for sexual offences is nearly five times higher than the national average, but we want this higher still to ensure all offenders are put before the courts. Up-skirting is an intrusive and unacceptable crime."

News.title: King Charles' salute to fallen on Remembrance Sunday as Kate pays moving tribute and Harry seen in market town
News.content:
King Charles' salute to fallen on Remembrance Sunday as Kate pays moving tribute and Harry seen in market town

The King and other members of the Royal Family, including the Princess of Wales gathered at the Cenotaph this morning for the annual Remembrance Sunday service

King Charles leads royals in marking Remembrance Sunday at The Cenotaph

The King led the nation as it fell silent today to honour the war dead at a moving ceremony.

‌



‌



Charles, back from his tour of the Caribbean, was joined by the Queen, the Prince and Princess of Wales, other senior royals, politicians and 10,000 veterans for the annual Remembrance Sunday service at the Cenotaph in London.

‌



It came as Remembrance ceremonies took place up and down the country yesterday to recognise the fallen from conflicts dating back to the First World War. Shortly before 11am, the King led out Prince William, Prince Edward and Princess Anne on to Whitehall to stand at the Cenotaph before Big Ben struck and the nation fell silent.

‌



Prince Harry and Meghan's Remembrance Sunday service abscene explained despite UK move READ MORE :

View 8 Images King Charles salutes at the Cenotaph today (Image: Jordan Pettitt/Press Association)

Camilla and Kate, who both dressed in black coats and hats, watched proceedings at the Cenotaph from the balcony of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office, with the princess seen closing her eyes in quiet reflection. She wore three poppies, earrings belonging to the late Diana, Princess of Wales and a HMS Glasgow brooch.

Also at the service were the Duchess of Edinburgh and the Duke of Kent. Prince Harry and Meghan, who moved back to the UK in August, were not at the Cenotaph. Instead, Harry, who served a decade in the Army - including two tours in Afghanistan, was today spotted at a Remembrance service in the market town of Brackley in Northamptonshire..

‌



The Duke of Sussex was seen alone, without Meghan, and wore a suit with a poppy and his service medals pinned to it, as he stood alongside locals paying their respects. An onlooker said: “He was at the memorial service - he was stood next to the pub.

“He was stood there watching and then afterwards he went into the market and started shaking everyone's hand. He was there for the whole service - we were there for 20 or 30 minutes, and he was there before us. He just wanted to show some respect. It is a shame. At the end of the day he’s served so why can’t he show his respects.”

‌



Last week, he also issued a message to a military bereavement charity, Scotty's Little Soldiers, paying tribute to their loved ones and thanking them for their service. It is understood he and Meghan marked the day privately.

View 8 Images The Princess of Wales pauses for reflection at the Cenotaph today (Image: Aaron Chown/Press Association)

‌



After the silence, the King, dressed in his Field Marshal uniform complete with a greatcoat, cap and sword, laid the first wreath, which read 'In everlasing memory' before saluting as he stepped back from the monument. A wreath was then laid on behalf of Camilla by her equerry before Prince William followed in his father's footsteps.

William, wearing the uniform of a Lieutenant Colonel of the Household Cavalry with black cloak and sword, also saluted after laying his wreath, adorned with the Prince of Wales feathers and also signed by Kate.

‌



The prince, who in 2013 completed seven-and-a-half years of full-time operational military service, was followed by wreaths being laid by the Duke of Edinburgh and the Princess Royal.

They were followed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who laid a wreath for the first time at the Cenotaph this morning. Other senior politicians followed including Kemi Badenoch, Sir Ed Davey, Nigel Farage, Shabana Mahmood and Sir Lindsay Hoyle.

‌



View 8 Images Prince William lays a wreath at the Cenotaph (Image: Carlos Jasso/Pool AFP via AP)

At this year’s ceremony, a record nine former prime ministers stood and watched: Sir John Major, Sir Tony Blair, Gordon Brown, Lord Cameron, Baroness May, Boris Johnson, Liz Truss, Rishi Sunak and Keir Starmer.

‌



After prayers and a rendition of God Save The King, the royals left the Cenotaph to a ripple of applause. Following the service in London, some 10,000 armed forces veterans took part in the Royal British Legion’s march-past, with more than 300 Armed Forces and civilian organisations represented.

The veterans included around a dozen of the last surviving Second World War veterans, the oldest of whom is 105.The 105-year-old was Jeffrey Brereton, who served as a mechanic on Hurricane aircraft during the Battle of Britain.

‌



He volunteered for the RAF in 1940, aged 19, and was nicknamed “lucky” by his unit before he left the army to join the fire service in 1946. Mr Brereton said that this was the first time he had ever attended the national Cenotaph ceremony.

View 8 Images Prime Minister Andy Burnham at the ceremony today (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Also taking part for the first time was 103-year-old Women’s Land Army veteran Annie Duplock. Ms Duplock joined the Land Army in 1940, aged 16, having lied about her age to enrol.

Based at a farm in Leicestershire for four years, she worked long days milking cows, ploughing fields and harvesting crops, helping to feed the nation during the Second World War.

‌



Speaking before, she said: “I feel very honoured to be taking part in the parade and to represent the Land Girls. I’m very excited, although a little apprehensive as I don’t quite know what to expect.

View 8 Images A record nine former Prime Ministers at the Cenotaph today (Image: Toby Melville/Pool Reuters via A)

‌



“I think it will be a very emotional day, bringing back memories of all those who didn’t return home. It will be lovely to be there and remember them.”

Gwynneth Pedler, 101, from Dulwich, south-east London, joined more than 40 other blind veterans at the parade.

‌



She joined the Women's Royal Naval Service (WRNS) in 1944 and was posted to Crail, near St Andrews, where she worked as an air mechanic. She cleaned and maintained the guns used by airmen who were learning to drop torpedoes.

Gwynneth said: "I couldn't believe it when they told me what I was going to do. I knew nothing about air mechanics and I'd never even done any DIY. It was important work, and it brought us close to the realities of training.

‌



View 8 Images Around 10,000 veterans took part in the march past (Image: Getty Images)

"Sometimes the young airmen hadn't quite got the hang of swooping away and ended up in the sea, which was very sad." She receives support from Blind Veterans UK and said she was proud to have joined them on this year's parade. Remembrance means a great deal to me," she said. "It goes back through my family's history to my two uncles who were killed at the Somme in World War One.

‌



Meanwhile, the youngest taking part in the march was eight-year-old Ronan Doncaster, who walked in honour of his father – a guardsman with the first battalion Coldstream Guards who died in April 2024.

Other ceremonies today included one at the National Memorial Arboretum in Staffordshire, where poppies attached to crosses were planted to honour the fallen.

‌



View 8 Images Annie Duplock, 103, takes part in her first march past at the Cenotaph (Image: James Manning/Press Association)

Hundreds also took part in a huge Remembrance Sunday parade in Sunderland, where Army personnel from 4th Regiment Royal Artillery and 3rd Battalion The Rifles marched through the city.

‌



Parades were also held in the centre of Manchester and Liverpool, while in Edinburgh, veterans marched on the Royal Mile to a ceremony outside the City Chambers.

View 8 Images Gwynneth Pedler, 101, from Dulwich, south-east London, one of 40 blind veterans who took part in the march past (Image: blind.veterans/Instagram)

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

A service attended by veterans, faith leaders and representatives of the Armed Service was also held in George Square, Glasgow, with a silence at 11am followed by a wreath-laying ceremony.

‌



Meanwhile, in Northern Ireland, Taoiseach Micheál Martin and Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant attended a memorial service in Enniskillen.

In 1987, the event was targeted by an IRA bomb, which killed 11 people on the day and a 12th victim years later, who never woke up from a coma.

Article continues below

News.title: King leads solemn Remembrance Sunday service at Cenotaph
News.content:
King Charles III led the nation in a solemn two-minute silence on Remembrance Sunday in London to honour veterans who had died in conflict.

On a stone-grey autumn morning, he laid a wreath at the Cenotaph in Whitehall before a march-past by 10,000 armed forces veterans.

That included a shrinking number of World War Two veterans, with 12 taking part this year, including 103-year-old Annie Duplock, who described it as a "very emotional day".

Meanwhile, the number of former prime ministers reached a record high, with nine lined up to lay wreaths, while Andy Burnham attended for the first time as the current occupant of No 10 Downing Street.

And for the first time, the leader of Reform UK, Nigel Farage, had enough MPs in Parliament to qualify to lay a wreath alongside other major party leaders.

News.title: Footage shows derailed carriages after fatal train crash in Egypt
News.content:
A train collision has killed at least seven people and injured dozens in northern Egypt.

Footage showed multiple overturned carriages and dozens of people surrounding them.

One train was travelling from Giza to the Fayoum oasis, south west of Cairo, while the other was heading from Cairo to Aswan in the south.

It is yet unclear what caused the accident but Egyptian President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi said an investigation was underway and would "hold accountable anyone who proves their negligence".

Read more about the train collision in Egypt.

News.title: Nandy defends linking Erasmus student scheme to Remembrance Sunday after backlash
News.content:
Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has rejected accusations of politicising Remembrance Sunday after being criticised for linking the event to the UK rejoining the European Union's Erasmus scheme.

Her department announced on Saturday night that "as we mark Remembrance Sunday, Erasmus+ will give a new generation the chance to build connections across Europe".

That sparked a backlash from the Conservatives, who said "veterans did not fight for a student exchange scheme" and accused her of making an "EU membership pitch".

Nandy said she was "horrified" by the Tory response and insisted that the expanded EU scheme for study and work would help young Britons recognise wartime sacrifice.

The UK is rejoining the scheme in January, six years after leaving it as part of the Brexit deal.

On Saturday, the Department for Culture, Media and Sport drew comparisons between that scheme and events on Sunday to commemorate veterans who had died in conflict.

Referring to the scheme, Nandy said in her department's press release: "As we remember the immense courage of those who served our country, we honour them by building the best opportunities for the next generation through closeness and collaboration with our allies."

Conservative Party chairman Kevin Hollinrake described her comments as "tone deaf and frankly shameful" and called on Nandy to apologise.

He said the bonds that veterans forged "run far deeper" than Erasmus.

"It is not a day for a Labour minister to try to make an EU membership pitch," he added.

Reform leader Nigel Farage told the BBC: "For Lisa Nandy to use Remembrance Sunday to announce this and say it's all about peace, it's all about the war - I find that very, very poor taste."

Peter Sharples, chief executive of the Veterans Institute, told the Telegraph that people should "just honour the fallen" on Remembrance Sunday rather than discussing "party political matters".

Asked about the criticism on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme, Nandy stood by her initial remarks.

"It was Winston Churchill after the Second World War who talked about extending the hand of friendship across Europe and making sure that we honoured the legacy of that generation," she said.

She said that after Brexit "we closed off opportunities for young people from this country to understand not just the impact that generation made here in the UK, but the way in which they went off and fought for the freedom of people across Europe".

Asked to respond to accusations she had chosen Remembrance Sunday to "promote part of the new deal the government has done with the EU", Nandy said she was "not choosing today or any day actually to promote a deal with the EU".

Pressed about linking the day to what the government believes are the cultural benefits of the scheme, Nandy said: "There was a time where that wouldn't have even raised an eyebrow as somehow political, it was just common sense - and it is common sense."

News.title: 'Time is up': Minister warns media industry to take abuse seriously in wake of Brand case
News.content:
Abuse in the media industry is probably still happening as organisations are not doing enough to protect women, the culture secretary has warned in the wake of Russell Brand's conviction.

Lisa Nandy told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "Time is up, it really is time for the media industry to take this seriously."

She added that since entering government, "many people" from within the industry had reached out to her "to allege that things have happened to them".

Brand was found guilty of rape and sexual assault after a four-week trial, following allegations from multiple women spanning the decade between 1999 and 2009.

Nandy was asked whether she believed there was still exploitation and abuse within the media industry, following the Brand trial and cancellation of Channel 4 reality show Married at First Sight after the BBC revealed rape allegations.

She said: "I do not see that much has changed in terms of the way that institutions in the media industry and across public life, including politics, deal with women who very bravely come forward to allege abuse."

Nandy added that there was often no protection and a "very heavy cost" for women who speak up in industries such as media and politics, pointing to power imbalances and short-term contracts some staff members are given.

"Hand on heart, I can't say to you as the culture secretary that this is not happening today. In fact, if I had to wager, I would say it is," she said.

Nandy said many had come forward from within the industry, including from the BBC.

But she added that the BBC had been an "exemplar" in signing up to the industry body to protect whistleblowers - the Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority - and urged other organisations to follow suit.

A BBC spokesperson said the broadcaster "has made a significant commitment to improve its culture, processes and standards".

"Last year, following an independent culture review, we set out the behavioural expectations for everyone who works with or for the BBC and we were clear action would be taken if these were not met," the spokesperson added.

News.title: Government looking at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay
News.content:
Vinted and eBay could be included in the list of platforms set to be banned for children aged under 16, the culture secretary has said.

Lisa Nandy said the government was "looking seriously" at including the retailing websites in the social media ban "to keep children safe".

The UK's social media ban for under-16s is set to come into force in March next year, with children barred from accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.

In response, eBay said it was looking forward to "understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government". Vinted said it welcomed "open dialogue" with ministers and the regulator on the issue.

Asked on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme whether the government was looking to ban under-16s from Vinted and eBay, Nandy said: "We are looking seriously at doing so in order to keep children safe."

It came after the Sunday Times reported, external that the UK's social media ban was being expanded to include the popular second-hand online marketplaces.

The move was due to fears that messaging functions on the platforms allowed strangers to groom children, according to the newspaper. It suggested similar reselling platforms, Depop and Facebook Marketplace, would also be included in the list of banned sites.

Businesses and individuals sell a host of goods on eBay, which has been a major global player in the online reselling market for years. The platform states on its website that it currently requires all of its members to be over 18 years old because listings involve "entering into a contract".

Vinted is aimed at over 18s, but its terms and conditions do allow parents or guardians to create accounts for their children, which must be used under parental supervision.

The site, on which users mostly buy and sell unwanted clothes and other fashion items, has grown rapidly recently to reach 17 million UK users.

A Vinted spokesperson said direct messaging was "part of how the platform works" but that it had a "zero tolerance for harmful or explicit content" and had moderation teams and tools to spot and remove "activity that breaks our rules".

"When we identify inappropriate behaviour, we take action, up to a permanent ban or reporting to the relevant authorities," they said.

An eBay spokesperson said the company was "focused on providing a trusted and safe marketplace experience for our millions of customers".

"While the details of the proposed legislation are not yet clear, we look forward to understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government," they added.

News.title: Two arrested after police officers hurt in brawl outside bare-knuckle fighting event
News.content:
Two men have been arrested and three police officers injured during a street disturbance outside a bare-knuckle fighting championship in Glasgow.

Footage circulating on social media shows a group of men trading punches in the street outside the Ovo Hydro where the event was held on Saturday evening.

More than 20 police vehicles and a police helicopter converged on the area. Three officers were hurt, two of them requiring medical treatment, as they responded to the disorder.

Police Scotland said two men, aged 32 and 27, had been arrested and charged with offences including assault, obstructing police and threatening and abusive behaviour.

News.title: The Trump coalition is shattered - what will Republicans do now?
News.content:
Republicans are in soul-searching mode after the coalition that powered Donald Trump to three straight presidential nominations imploded in spectacular fashion in the 2026 midterms.

The stunning election defeat immediately raised questions about the party's future post-Trump.

But there are no easy answers as Republicans face the choice of doubling down on Trumpism or trying to chart a new path forward in his final years in office.

The depth of the problem was captured by outgoing Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, who called the midterms "close to an extinction-level event for Republicans".

Others struck a more optimistic tone. Vice-President JD Vance, who blamed the midterm results on public anger over the war with Iran, argued the party could turn things around. Nevertheless Vance acknowledged the fallout will be messy.

"There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why," Vance said.

The wide range of reactions on the right highlights deep fault lines in the party that formed around Trump's improbable rise to the presidency in 2016 and never really went away.

It's too early to tell which faction will win. But while Republicans are still licking their wounds, the intraparty battle Vance predicted is already under way.

News.title: My parents chose to die together and I was left to grieve alone
News.content:
Some people might find this article upsetting.

Early one morning in June 2024, Bas pulled up next to his parents' campervan, parked on a sunny marina in the north of the Netherlands.

His father and mother, Jan and Els, had spent most of their married life on water. Now in their 70s, they could no longer manage a houseboat. Their campervan, positioned close to the yachts and dinghies, was the next best thing.

Jan and Els got into their son's car. Bas started the engine. This would be the final time he drove his parents anywhere. For Jan and Els, this journey - to the local hospice - would be their last.

At 10:30 that morning they would be administered lethal medication by doctors and die together in what is known in the Netherlands as duo-euthanasia. It's legal and it's rare, but every year more Dutch people choose to end their lives this way.

News.title: Briton among six killed in 'far-right' shooting in Krakow
News.content:
A gunman believed to have been inspired by far-right ideology has killed six people and injured more than a dozen others in an attack in the busy centre of Poland's second largest city.

Police said the attacker drove on to Main Market Square in Krakow, a popular tourist attraction, on Saturday afternoon and fired randomly at people.

Four women and two men were killed. Three were Polish, one was British and two have not been identified.

Among the 16 injured are five foreign nationals from Austria, Germany, Portugal, Russia and Britain.

Another three bodies were found when counter-terrorism police searched the suspect's home around 125 miles (200km) away, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said.

A massive armed police presence was deployed across Krakow on Saturday evening, as security measures were ramped up in the capital Warsaw and elsewhere.

A period of mourning has been declared in Krakow until 11 November.

Two police officers are also among those injured, one critically.

The suspect, who was equipped with military-style weapons and attire, is a 25-year-old Polish man - described by a minister as "ultra-nationalist".

Police shot and arrested him and he remains in hospital having undergone surgery.

Tusk said there were "strong indications" the two women and one man found dead at the suspect's home in Ostrowiec ÅwiÄtokrzyski were his immediate family members.

He said: "Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism... that's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow."

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "I'm shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting in KrakÃ³w today."

"My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence. The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the people of Poland," he added.

The rampage began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in the historic centre of Krakow, an ornate square which has long been a draw for tourists.

Footage showed the attacker's vehicle speeding through the centre of the city, and people fleeing as the sound of gunfire rang out.

The glass front of shops were shattered by bullets and a tram was shot at during the attack, which police say lasted for around three minutes.

Images from the scene show overturned tables and scattered belongings left behind as people ran for their lives.

Armed police officers pursued the attacker's car until it crashed, at which point they engaged him in a firefight.

Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify captured the moment a police officer confronted the suspect as he lay on the ground.

The officer, who is visibly injured, can then be seen falling to the ground.

News.title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10
News.content:
Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught.

The government plans to make Key Stage 3 a more distinct education phase, urging schools to focus less on exams and more on a "richer, more engaging" experience.

The changes come in response to two reviews that found pupils were increasingly becoming disengaged in their early teenage years, affecting attendance and achievement, the Department for Education (DfE) said.

The move will mark a reversal of the approach taken by the previous Conservative government to focus the first three years of secondary school on core subjects and on doing well in assessments.

Former Education Secretary Michael Gove prioritised English, maths and science, while raising grade boundaries, making exams harder and limiting resits.

He also made GCSEs linear, meaning they are sat all in one go at the end of Year 11 instead of over the course of Key Stage 4.

These reforms meant teachers started preparing pupils for exams at an earlier stage at the expense of teaching unexamined parts of their subject.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell said: "The early years of secondary school should be a time when children are excited to go to school and engage in the specialist and much broader teaching on offer, and where they find their passion and develop a love of learning."

She added that ringfencing Key Stage 3 studies would allow for "more time to develop deeper understanding, as well as a richer experience that will engage more young people in their passions".

The DfE has pledged a "more engaging offer" in subjects like drama, PE, music and languages, which have seen a decline in students taking them, when it publishes its new curriculum later this year.

It says persistent absence nearly doubles among pupils between Year 6 and Year 9, from 13% to 15%.

The department pointed to a recent survey commissioned by the International Baccalaureate that found GCSE prep dominated Key Stage 3 learning in England, with 57% of teachers saying it was the leading influence on the curriculum.

"The pressures of GCSEs and an overcrowded curriculum are resulting in too many children receiving a narrower offer during Key Stage 3 and being rushed towards exams without grasping the fundamentals or developing deeper understanding," Powell said. "I'm putting a stop to that."

A 2015 Ofsted report suggested that Key Stage 3 may be "wasted years", echoing the view at the time that pupils aged 11-14 lacked a clear motivation to work hard.

However, the government faced criticism at the time that its reforms made each exam far more significant, meaning teachers refocused lessons only on what could come up in them.

Reacting to the DfE's announcement on Sunday, Lib Dem education spokeswoman Munira Wilson MP said school was "more than drilling kids for exams" but cautioned against "micromanaging" teachers.

She added that a new curriculum "alone won't get children back into the classroom", noting that "too many pupils are missing school because of anxiety and unmet mental health needs" while "schools can't offer more drama, music and languages without the teachers to teach them".

News.title: We face paying £9,000 tax even though our second home is in a war zone
News.content:
A Ukrainian woman who fled to Scotland after Russia invaded her homeland has been told she could face a Â£9,000 property tax charge because she still owns a flat in Kyiv.

Kateryna Stepanovych, 38, discovered the potential charge when she tried to buy a house in North Ayrshire with her Scottish partner Mattias Lindgren.

The couple were told the Additional Dwelling Supplement (ADS) charge would apply because she already owned a property overseas.

Kateryna bought the small flat in 2018, before Russia's invasion. She fled the war zone in 2023, leaving the property behind.

News.title: I won't let my daughter's killer live in my head, says Sarah Payne's mum
News.content:
The mother of murdered schoolgirl Sarah Payne says she wants to change how people see victims of crime.

Sara Payne's daughter was abducted while playing with her siblings and murdered in July 2000, aged just eight.

Roy Whiting - a convicted sex offender - was jailed for life in December 2001 for her killing.

Sara told BBC South East there were many reasons behind how people behaved, but they "still have choices".

"You have to choose which path you're going to take," she said.

"I chose not to allow him [Whiting] to live in my head.

"It had to be her - so I keep Sarah."

Sarah's body was found 17 days after she went missing from a field near her grandparents' house in West Sussex.

Her disappearance prompted one of the most heavily publicised searches in UK history and led to landmark legal changes.

"I don't have anger. I don't have aggression. I don't want to bring back hanging or any of those things," Sara continued.

"I just want to go forward in a humane way and be human."

News.title: Veterans shouldn't sleep rough this Christmas, Burnham says
News.content:
No one who served in the UK armed forces should have to sleep on the streets this Christmas, Andy Burnham has said.

Downing Street said the PM would personally write to councils across England on Armistice Day (11 November) to urge them to draw up plans to offer accommodation for veterans sleeping rough ahead of the festive period.

He will say that national and local government should work under the "simple principle" that "no one who has served our country should ever be left to sleep rough on our streets".

The Conservatives have meanwhile criticised Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy for linking participation in an EU scheme for young people with the armed forces' sacrifices on Remembrance Sunday.

Burnham will ask local authorities to use part of the additional Â£874m already announced to tackle homelessness specifically for housing veterans.

"People who stepped forward prepared to put their lives on the line for the rest of us should never lack a roof over their head," Burnham said in a statement issued on Saturday.

"When they need help, the country owes them more than warm words. It owes them a bed every night, a proper plan and someone in their corner from day one."

The PM will ask councils to work with local organisations and charities to tackle homelessness amongst veterans.

Downing Street said an additional Â£8.7m in funding would be allocated to eight organisations across the UK to help housing providers offer assistance to veterans with complex needs, including those with health or addiction problems.

Among them are Veteran Housing Scotland, Launchpad and SSAFA, the Armed Forces Charity.

News.title: Two seriously hurt in 30-vehicle crash on the M20 in Kent
News.content:
More than 30 vehicles were involved in a crash which left two people seriously injured on the M20 in Kent on Saturday evening.

The crash happened in foggy conditions just after 18:40 GMT on the London-bound carriageway between junctions eight (Maidstone) and nine (Ashford).

Paramedics attended to 11 people, and two were taken to hospital, Kent Fire and Rescue Service said.

The road was shut in both directions early on Sunday, but has since reopened.

An air ambulance crew, three fire engines and a "technical rescue unit" were sent to the scene, where National Highways said "thick fog" had been confirmed.

Kent Police said one of the two people seriously injured had been taken to a hospital locally, and the other to a London hospital.

"Other drivers have sustained injuries not believed to be serious," it said in a statement.

The force has asked anyone with information about the incident or dashcam footage to come forward.

News.title: School Street fines at one location exceed £1m
News.content:
A London council has issued more than Â£1m worth of penalty charge notices (PCNs) to drivers under a School Street scheme in less than two years.

Brent Council issued PCNs totalling Â£1.15m after introducing the scheme outside Manor School in Kensal Rise in November 2024, saying it would improve road safety and the environment.

Ward councillor Barbara Want raised concerns about the scheme and claimed that the signs were "too high and not properly visible".

Brent Council said the signs in place complied with Department for Transport guidelines, but that it had decided to install extra lower-level signs and gateway features to give more clarity to drivers.

In the 21 months the scheme has been in place, the north-west London council has collected Â£54,799 on average per month, with the scheme only in place during term time.

School Streets are being trialled across the borough to enforce road closures during drop-off and pick-up times, policed by CCTV cameras and mobile enforcement teams. Those caught face a PCN of Â£160, reduced to Â£80 if paid within 14 days.

Previously, it was reported that 70,000 PCNs were issued in 12 months, at a rate of 384 per school day.

In July 2025, the two cameras enforcing the scheme outside Manor School raised more than Â£107,000 in a single month, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service.

Want said: "For months I have been highlighting the huge volume of PCNs issued to drivers on the Manor School Street. The fact that it has raked in more than Â£1m in two years should have told them something wasn't right.

"It is failing children's safety if drivers are still using the road. I fear the scheme is more about revenue generation than improving road safety or air quality."

Promise Knight, the council's cabinet member for cleaner streets, transport and public realm, said School Streets existed in the borough "to make the journey to and from school safer for children and families".

"The purpose of the scheme is to protect children by reducing congestion and improving air quality.

"We will continue to review the scheme and make practical improvements where they can help drivers comply."

News.title: Grenfell NHS support service faces funding cut
News.content:
NHS England committed Â£50m to the community's recovery in 2018, which funded the service. The ICB has bid for Â£1.8m to continue it, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said.

The fire in June 2017 killed 72 people. The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has said it will make charging decisions before the 10th anniversary on 14 June 2027.

Lucy Knight, the Kensington and Chelsea council's lead member for adult social care and public health, said "no-one should be left worrying" about whether their care would still be there.

She said the NHS accepted the period ahead could be especially hard for the community, and now was not the time to change the model of care to fit a smaller budget unless it could still meet people's needs.

A cross-party motion asked the council to tell the ICB and local NHS trust that survivors and the bereaved remained a top priority, and to urge NHS England to confirm long-term funding.

Representatives of the ICB and Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust (CNWL), which runs the service, will attend a council scrutiny meeting in December.

In a September update, the service said support would "not simply stop".

The ICB said its priority was making sure future arrangements met the needs of those affected. It said local people were helping to shape proposals, which it aimed to finalise as soon as possible.

NHS England said it supported efforts to ensure people affected could continue to get the care they needed.
