News.title: Man United’s unique comeback leaves no one knowing how to feel
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

As the Manchester United players who had been told they were not fit to wear the shirt, in perhaps the earliest ever airing of that chant in footballing history, celebrated a second ridiculous comeback in five days, the Stretford End launched into a different chorus.

They had told the team they were unworthy of representing them after a mere five minutes, had cheered in damning fashion when the dreadful Diogo Dalot was substituted, had been vitriolic about the Glazer family, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Jason Wilcox. But United left the pitch in the relegation zone while their supporters serenaded Michael Carrick.

“It’s hard to believe it’s not Scholes,” they sang. In one respect, it was hard to believe it was not Sir Alex Ferguson, plucking results from nowhere. In another, it was hard to believe this was not the prelude to a sacking.

open image in gallery Patrick Dorgu popped up to score an extraordinary stoppage-time equaliser ( Reuters )

It may still be. United have one win in 11 games, one point in three in the Premier League but Carrick is starting to specialise in escapology. Bournemouth had seemed the end for him, Roma looked it when his side were 2-0 down. Aston Villa seemed his valedictory game twice, before two two-goal comebacks.

His team talks seem to backfire horribly and yet his side have twice delivered a show of spirit to salvage something from the brink of humiliation. Ferguson’s most famous comeback was delivered by two substitutes, Teddy Sheringham and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. If Carrick has a lifeline now, it came from two replacements, scorers in Fergie Time, when it seemed time had run out for the latest United manager.

First Patrick Dorgu set up Joshua Zirkzee to halve the deficit. Then Dorgu headed in Bruno Fernandes’ 96th-minute corner. A few minutes earlier, the Aston Villa supporters had been taunting their former midfielder Youri Tielemans with a chorus of: “Youri, what’s the score?”

Few foresaw the eventual answer. Villa were on course for their biggest victory at Old Trafford since 1920; then, suddenly, they did not have a win at all. This was confusing and complicated, crazy entertainment. United showed a self-destructive streak at the start of each half and reacted to spread the kind of chaos that put a smile back on their faces.

United were both awful and exciting. They have character, if not competence at the back, where they did an impression of a particularly hungover pub team. A team with a series of historic lows have a pan-European level of porousness. As Villa scored four, no team in Europe’s five major leagues has conceded more goals in all competitions than United. Defensively, they are disastrous, disorganised, struggling at set-pieces, forever caught out by the counter-attack. Dalot is in hideous form and it got worse. Carrick erred by not swapping him with Noussair Mazraoui at half-time. What followed was all too predictable as, unable to contain the outstanding Alysson, Dalot fouled him to concede a penalty.

open image in gallery Dorgu fouled Alysson as United made another catastrophically slow start ( Getty )

open image in gallery Emery stormed down the tunnel before full-time after watching his team fall apart ( Getty )

United looked a shambles as they made a shocking start, and then another. They twice responded to Carrick’s team talks by capitulating, conceding two goals in four minutes at the start of the match and two in eight after the break.

Two goals behind after 18 minutes to Roma, United took terrible starts to another level. This was the earliest they had ever been 2-0 down in a Premier League game when Villa doubled their lead, with Senne Lammens at fault for both.

Dalot should share the blame for Alyson’s first-minute opener, allowing the winger too much room to shoot. He beat the goalkeeper at his near post. When Lammens only pushed another Alysson shot straight to Nicolas Jackson, the summer signing slotted in his eighth goal in his last nine games.

open image in gallery Jackson punished an error from Lammens, on a night when all four goals were down to United mistakes ( Getty )

It was, ridiculously, the fifth consecutive game in which United went 2-0 down. Briefly, they hinted at a second consecutive 3-2 win, only for something still more outlandish to unfold.

The comeback against Roma began with a penalty won by Matheus Cunha and scored by Fernandes. Five days later, Boubacar Kamara fouled the Brazilian and the United captain sent Zion Suzuki the wrong way. Déjà vu.

As United were forced into a pattern of frenetic attacking, Cunha tried to power another fightback. There were echoes of Tuesday night, waves of attack. Cunha, Fernandes and Amad Diallo all came close. Suzuki made fine saves from Cunha and Amad. Tielemans swept in his first United goal from Mazraoui’s cutback.

open image in gallery Tielemans grabbed United’s first equaliser, scoring his goal against his former club ( Getty )

After the interval, Villa felt fired up again. United emerged dopily. Carrick left Dalot up against the outstanding Alysson and tripped him. Either the winger was unstoppable or United made him look so but John McGinn, who missed his penalty against Fulham last week, scored this.

Then Lammens made his save of the game, sparing Leny Yoro an own goal but in vain. Jackson scuffed his shot but Leon Goretzka finished. His first Villa goal, it seemed, would finish off Carrick and United. Somehow, extraordinarily, it did not. They struck back in added time. His reign may be in added time, too.

News.title: Man United latest: Michael Carrick faces uncertain future despite unbelievable comeback
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Michael Carrick applauds the fans after the 4-4 draw between Manchester United and Aston Villa ( Getty )

Michael Carrick said he still expects to be working with Manchester United over the international break after his players scored two stoppage-time goals to rescue an extraordinary 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in the Premier League.

The visitors appeared on course for a comfortable win after restoring their two-goal advantage in a crazy game Old Trafford, but late goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu saw United pull off their second great escape of the week after Tuesday’s incredible comeback victory against Roma.

The result leaves United in the Premier League’s bottom three, however, and they will spend the international break 18th in the table before visiting rivals Liverpool. United have won just once in their first 10 in the Premier League, but Carrick was still applauded off the pitch by the United fans.

“We haven't won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working on things that we've been working on and showing a lot of the good in the game today,” Carrick said. “We need to tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches.”

Villa boss Unai Emery was hugely frustrated to see his side twice throw away a two-goal lead, and stormed down the tunnel before full-time after Dorgu’s equaliser. Villa were unhappy that United goalkeeper Senne Lammens appeared to prevent Zion Suzuki from catching the ball before Dorgu headed in.

Follow reaction from Manchester United v Aston Villa in the Premier League, below

News.title: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery storms down the tunnel after last-gasp Man United equaliser
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery appeared to storm off down the tunnel after Manchester United grabbed a last-gasp equaliser against his side to seal a remarkable 4-4 draw in one of the most chaotic Premier League games of the season.

United looked set for defeat as they trailed 4-2 in the second minute of injury-time at Old Trafford before Joshua Zirkzee gave them a sliver of hope by pulling one back and Patrick Dorgu headed home an incredible equaliser in the 96th minute.

That proved to be the final straw for Emery, who immediately stormed off down the tunnel without even waiting for the VAR check confirming the goal and before the full-time whistle blew for the end of the match.

In his post-match interview with Sky Sports, Emery suggested he simply left because United scored so late that he thought the match was essentially over.

Emery had already watched his side squander a 2-0 lead after the perfect start for the visiting Villans, with Alysson and Nicolas Jackson both finding the net inside the first five minutes.

That advantage didn’t last long as Matheus Cunha was fouled in the box by Boubacar Kamara and Bruno Fernandes stepped up to pull one back, sparking a period of constant pressure that continued until Youri Tielemans scored his first United goal to equalise against his former club before half-time.

Yet the hosts unravelled again however, as Villa scored twice in seven minutes after the restart, with John McGinn netting from the penalty spot after Diogo Dalot fouled Alysson and Leon Goretzka tapping in after more woeful defending from United.

open image in gallery Unai Emery appeared to storm down the tunnel ( Getty )

open image in gallery Man United celebrated the unlikeliest of 4-4 draws ( Reuters )

At that point, Emery must have assumed his team would get over the line but they collapsed again with Zirkzee first pulling one back in the 92nd minute before Dorgu rose highest on 96 minutes to head into an empty net after Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki came off his line and failed to get the ball.

That result – combined with their incredible comeback victory against Roma in midweek – may just have saved Michael Carrick’s job, although his United side still head into this international break in the Premier League’s bottom three, lying 18th in the table.

Meanwhile, Villa’s rollercoaster start to the campaign means they are in 10th, although if they had held on for victory, they would have moved up to eighth.

News.title: Steve Borthwick reveals messages of support from previous England incumbents
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Steve Borthwick revealed that advice from his predecessors as England head coach helped focus his mind entering one of the most important moments of his Twickenham reign.

Australia were crushed 45-22 to launch the autumn with a bang as Borthwick’s players delivered an emphatic rebuttal to a report stating that he presided over a toxic environment during the July tour.

A record win against the Wallabies has relieved the pressure on Borthwick, who on Wednesday was given the full backing of Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney to remain in place for next year’s World Cup.

open image in gallery England’s Maro Itoje with the Ella-Mobbs Trophy (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

However, England needed a convincing win amid an otherwise poor 2026 to stop the storm clouds swirling around their under-fire boss, who was the focus of a newspaper article calling into question his methods and man-management skills.

Borthwick said: “In the last couple of days, a number of my predecessors reached out to me constantly and they certainly do. They’re always supportive.

“I won’t name who they are, but the basic gist of it was ‘been there, got the T-shirt’. As England head coach, you need to focus on the rugby and that’s what I’ve done this week.

“That’s what the players have done. That’s what every member of the staff have done.”

Henry Pollock was among the stars of a conclusive Nations Championship victory after scoring two tries having come on as a wing replacement for Immanuel Feyi-Waboso.

open image in gallery Henry Pollock impressed for England (David Davies/PA) ( PA Wire )

It was the first time Pollock, a back row, had played in the position but impressed as England’s latest hybrid player after Ben Earl emerged as another success story of the afternoon.

Borthwick said: “I say this in all the right ways, but we now have to bear Henry Pollock saying playing on the wing is easy and that he can play anywhere on the pitch!

“We suggested the front row and he said ‘no’, he didn’t want to do that! He was excellent and now we hear a lot about it – that’s the downside.”

The only cloud over the performance were injuries sustained by Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson.

Feyi-Waboso began limping during the first half because of an ankle problem and was replaced at the interval with Borthwick revealing he needs further investigation to assess the extent of the damage.

open image in gallery Seb Atkinson will be assessed (Ben Whitley/PA) ( PA Wire )

Atkinson limped off in the 64th minute with a bruised hip and is a doubt for Saturday’s match against Eddie Jones’ Japan.

It was the third game in a row in which Australia conceded over 40 points and captain Harry Wilson refused to make excuses for the performance.

Wilson said: “It was really disappointing. We didn’t fire a shot in the first half. We felt like we were always trying to exit our half because of the field position England were able to get.

“They were really physical and they made it tough for us. I expected better from us and we have to attack these learnings for Scotland next weekend.

“Every game we want to win and three 20-point losses on the trot is not good enough. We want a big response against Scotland and we need to be more physical.”

News.title: Wirtz breaks goalscoring duck as Liverpool send Palace boss closer to exit door
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

For Andoni Iraola, at the end of a week of vexation following two avoidable one-goal defeats, this was just what the doctor ordered. On a cool November day, a comfortable margin of victory in second gear in South London halted Liverpool’s two-game losing run heading into the internationals and catapulted them back into the top-four, nine points off leaders Arsenal.

Even Florian Wirtz, Liverpool’s ultimate attacking fall guy over the last 15 months, netted a much-needed first Premier League goal of the season. Off a Bradley Barcola assist, too. Here at Selhurst, amid a forward quartet made up of just shy of £400m worth of transfer fees, there were more positive sprinklings of encouragement. And when Alexander Isak, who it should be said is second in the race for the golden boot with seven league goals, smashed the ball home on the cusp of 90 minutes, the three points were safe and heading back up to the north-west.

open image in gallery Alexis Mac Allister glances in Liverpool's opener ( Getty )

That said, this was all against a Crystal Palace side – and a manager in beleaguered Frenchman Pierre Sage – who by the end looked out of ideas and inspiration. No head coach has lost his job in the Premier League this season – yet – but the Eagles are now rooted to the bottom of the table after 10 games with just two wins to their name. Could a change be in the offing from Palace chairman Steve Parish, a man who does tend to afford managers time to put things right? We’ll find out soon enough.

Yet what will frustrate Sage the most on this occasion is that, until Liverpool’s second just after half-time, Palace were well in this match. But the team that has scored the second-fewest goals in the division (ten) were punished here for failing to take their chances in the first-half.

But a week on from failing to have a single shot on target against Arsenal, it took 20 seconds for Liverpool to find their range here as Mac Allister gave Dean Henderson an early test. The diminutive 5’9” midfielder, curiously effective from set pieces, went closer after 10 minutes, heading into the side netting from Dominik Szoboszlai’s free-kick. It was a warning and routine that Palace would not heed.

Yet after the first 15 minutes, Palace were the team on the ascendancy. Yeremy Pino’s neat swivel and shot crashed off the crossbar while Jogen Strand Larsen, in for the suspended Jean-Philippe Mateta, saw a dinked finish ruled out for offside, albeit correctly so.

And when Daichi Kamada gave Barcola a lesson in back-post volleys with a punchy effort kept out by Alisson, it was somewhat against the run of play when Mac Allister’s opener arrived.

Iraola had spoken in the build-up about his team perhaps being “too honest” as a statistic this week did the rounds: while Liverpool have conceded the most fouls in the Premier League, only three sides have won fewer fouls. But it pays to be shrewd. After Cody Gakpo won a questionably-given foul off Jefferson Lerma, Szoboszlai’s near-post free-kick was once again met by Mac Allister, who glanced sweetly home for his fifth goal of the season, equalling his tally from the last campaign.

open image in gallery Alexander Isak scored Liverpool's third in south London ( PA )

open image in gallery Pierre Sage now appears to be on the brink ( Getty )

His provocative celebration in front of the Holmesdale End only added to the home crowd's fury. “One-nil to the referee,” they sang at official Tony Harrington at the interval.

The Reds were, however, fortunate to be ahead at half-time. Their goal was under siege before the interval, with Quinten Timber and Adam Wharton forcing good saves out of Alisson. Palace’s momentum was stymied by the interval though and when Barcola’s square ball after a surge down the right found Wirtz, the German found the attribute he so often has been accused of lacking since his £105m arrival on these shores: composure. Stroking the ball beyond Henderson, it is just his sixth Premier League goal since arriving from Bayer Leverkusen last summer.

But even in the closing stages, Palace carved out decent opportunities. Pino somehow squandered a one-on-one opportunity with the goal gaping and substitute Eddie Nketiah poked over from close range. It was indicative of Palace’s fortunes: neat build-up, a large intake of breath in the box before failing to find the back of the net.

And when Isak put the icing on the cake, set up by Wirtz in the box and coolly cutting inside before lashing home past Henderson, Sage had the look of a man on the brink on the touchline. Even Milos Kerkez’s brainless foul on Dario Osorio in stoppage time, clattering the Palace substitute’s head in the box, which resulted in Nketiah’s consolation penalty and a needless ruining of Alisson’s clean sheet, could not brighten the Palace mood. Now, ahead of a two-week pause in action, the question for Parish is: will he stick or twist?

News.title: Lando Norris wins wet and wild Sao Paulo GP as Mercedes seal constructors’ crown
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Lando Norris won the Sao Paulo Grand Prix after new world champion Kimi Antonelli spun out of the lead in slippery conditions at Interlagos.

Antonelli had jumped pole-sitter Norris during a damp start but fell apart after his stop for dry tyres and ended the race fifth.

Max Verstappen pulled off a typically-brilliant comeback drive from 21st on the grid to finish second, ahead of Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.

open image in gallery Kimi Antonelli spun from the lead

George Russell’s podium hopes were undone by a staggering spin in the pit-lane exit, recovering well to fourth, while an extraordinary start from Lewis Hamilton from the back of the grid only earned him ninth.

Mercedes clinched the constructors’ title, a week on from Antonelli celebrating his drivers’ crown. Norris masterfully claimed pole in soaking conditions on Saturday afternoon, pipping Russell to top spot – before his compatriot’s five-place grid drop for an engine penalty.

Russell was furious with Mercedes after believing their order for him to abort his final flying lap cost him pole.

Norris was joined on the front row by the man who deposed him as champion.

The Italian had a moment of fortune as he made his way to the grid, skidding across the grass and narrowly avoiding the barriers before hauling his Mercedes out the mud.

Behind them was a jumbled-up order – Liam Lawson third, Nico Hulkenberg fourth ahead of Hadjar and Ollie Bearman.

Antonelli jumped Norris on the short run down to turn one. The McLaren man was then undone by Lawson at turn two.

Hamilton began 20th after engine woe on Saturday, with Charles Leclerc 14th after his own penalty.

The seven-time world champion was in familiar company, joined by Verstappen in 21st – who won this race from 17th in the rain in 2024.

open image in gallery Lewis Hamilton dropped down the order after an early rise

Hamilton soared up to ninth by the end of lap one, steaming down the outside off the line past a string of cars, including team-mate Leclerc.

Hamilton’s 400th Grand Prix start came at the end of a week where he launched a fierce criticism of Leclerc – questioning the Monegasque’s mentality after a first-lap overtake on him in Mexico.

Top-10 - Sao Paulo Grand Prix 1. Lando Norris (McLaren) 2. Max Verstappen (Red Bull) 3. Isack Hadjar (Red Bull) 4. George Russell (Mercedes) 5. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) 6. Oscar Piastri (McLaren) 7. Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) 8. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls) 9. Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) 10. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)

The Ferrari pair say their issues are over after showdown talks with boss Fred Vasseur.

Verstappen started sedately but soon ignited with a string of sensational overtakes as he cruised up behind Hamilton.

The two great rivals, with 11 titles between them, duelled it out on the exit of Curva da Juncao but Hamilton had no answer for the Dutchman as he piled through.

Piastri fought gamely but Verstappen hung it out around turn three and passed Alex Albon at turn four.

The Ferrari war was back in the spotlight on lap 10 as Leclerc cruised up to Hamilton – who was complaining about his tyres.

Neither driver gave an inch as Leclerc made his move but Hamilton appeared to have taken life out of wheels as the Monegasque got the move done. To add insult for Hamilton, he was then breezed past by his old foe Fernando Alonso in the lowly Aston Martin.

Hamilton wanted dry tyres but Ferrari wanted to wait. Out front, Antonelli had stormed eight seconds clear with Norris now back in second and Russell up to third.

open image in gallery Mercedes celebrate their constructors' title on the podium ( Getty )

Hamilton pulled the trigger on the soft tyres on lap 15 and was motoring as the pack followed suit.

Norris and Russell went first of the leaders but Russell suffered an extraordinary spin on the narrow pit exit, just keeping it out of the barrier as he slipped to eighth.

Antonelli and Verstappen pitted the following lap but Norris was all over the leader having slashed the gap and the world champion told Mercedes “something weird” was wrong with his car.

The Italian spectacularly spun off at turn one, as the British driver seized the lead.

Hadjar also piled through amid Antonelli’s struggles as Verstappen emerged in his mirrors.

Antonelli was off again on lap 24, with the Dutchman marching past, but Mercedes told their complaining driver his issue was simply tyre temperature.

The leading pack all stopped again, Norris retaining his healthy lead.

But there was a twist in the tale as the heavens opened again. Russell pitted first and gained ground but Hamilton spun down the main straight, clipping the barrier, as he made his way in.

Russell was now on the back of Antonelli – who will be investigated for an unsafe pit release – and the world champion was told to let his team-mate through.

Norris held firm to claim back-to-back wins in Sao Paulo, crossing the line 14.6 seconds ahead of Verstappen.

News.title: England send message with emphatic Australia victory to show faith in Steve Borthwick
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

England’s players had promised a performance that showed their faith in Steve Borthwick; consider that message of unity emphatically sent. Crisis? What crisis? If last November’s victory over New Zealand remains the high watermark of the Borthwick era given the opposition, here, at least, was a performance that rose close to those standards, an answering of critics and call to arms that they needed at the start of this potentially fractious campaign. There was daring, there was dynamism, and there was more than a hint of indignation after a week of questioning over their spirit.

A pot still to boil or a flash in a pan? The next three weeks will reveal plenty about what Borthwick is really cooking but they have, at least, backed up strong words with equally forceful actions. Australia were not at the races but, perhaps, they were not allowed to be, with a refreshed and recharged Maro Itoje leading from the front. Vindication came in a cohesive and connected backline performance and the impact of Henry Pollock, scoring twice after an injury-enforced introduction on the wing following the departure of the irrepressible Immanuel Feyi-Waboso.

open image in gallery England ran in seven tries ( Reuters )

It had been a week of fire and fury for England. The flames had been lit by a report suggesting division in camp and perhaps attempting to sow it, too, which drew out a united, and frustrated, defensive front as Borthwick’s squad hit back. What fractures and fissures might Australia find? The opening skirmishes felt of outsized importance. England had begun strongly in their last outing against Argentina back in July, correcting a concerning trend that had troubled them through the Six Nations.

It looked a perfect start for the hosts, a pull-back from Seb Atkinson helping set a roaming Feyi-Waboso free to career beneath the sticks. An earlier forward pass from Ben Curry wiped the try out, though England’s intent to play was clear. Feyi-Waboso was utilised several times more in the opening 10 minutes and made metres every time, and it was his kick chase that drew a blocking penalty that Fin Smith could kick to the corner. From there, the maul – as is becoming a theme this November – was unstoppable; Jamie George, who had spoken so strongly of his side’s unity on Friday, a fitting scorer from a collective effort.

open image in gallery Jamie George was a fitting first scorer ( Getty )

Ryan Lonergan replied with a penalty but it was about the only kick Australia had in an opening half-hour that, while staccato at times, England controlled. Itoje harried and hustled around the ruck while Feyi-Waboso was a constant threat, given licence to explore and exploit the spaces that appeared. From one such jaunty jape came the position that led to Ollie Chessum’s try, scored at the end of the attacking line down the left edge that Feyi-Waboso had vacated.

It was the Exeter wing at the centre of everything. To see him down on the touchline soon after suggested a major England blow, but it came with one for Australia – Angus Bell shown a yellow card for a “hip-drop” tackle, collapsing his weight onto the ankle of the English carrier in the style that World Rugby are keen to crack down on. From the resultant penalty, the home maul worked again, Joe Heyes this time the try-scorer.

Just about everything had gone right for England; it couldn’t last. With Feyi-Waboso clearly hurt yet hobbling on, Jack van Poortvliet floated a pass in a vague attempt to access his strike weapon, but out of the line shot Australia’s, with Max Jorgensen intercepting and turning on the after-burners.

open image in gallery Max Jorgensen’s intercept try threatened to give Australia hope ( PA )

With no specialist wing cover on the bench, Feyi-Waboso’s inability to continue meant 40 minutes of Henry Pollock on the wing. It felt the sort of swing from which England have sometimes capitulated, but not so here. On turnover ball deep into their own territory, the blond bombshell exploded into life, bursting out of grasping arms up the left touchline. Quick ball allowed Smith and George Furbank to go to work in playmaking partnership, the former to the latter, and on to Tommy Freeman, who gave Van Poortvliet a redemptive gambol beneath the posts.

Pollock was far from done. A try of his own was simple enough to score as the ball broke his way but followed by a rockstar strut; two minutes later, an even more extravagant encore, that shock of hair lighting up even as the evening descended. “We now have to bear Henry Pollock saying playing on the wing is easy,” Borthwick joked. “He was excellent…and now we’ll hear a lot about it. That’s the downside.”

It felt gloomy for Australia, certainly. Les Kiss’s side felt to have made strong strides when they conquered South Africa in September but their last three outings have brought them back down to earth with a bump, first blown away twice in the Bledisloe Cup by the All Blacks and so demonstrably second best here. Filipo Daugunu restored a varnish of respectability with a neatly-taken try and Jeremy Williams added another with a rather more opportunistic finish from a botched English lineout. “Too little, too late,” captain Harry Wilson remarked after – and Ben Spencer ended any prospect of a lasting rally with an intercept try soon enough.

open image in gallery England answered their critics with an emphatic performance ( Getty )

If there is lingering concern for Borthwick over injuries to Feyi-Waboso and Seb Atkinson, he could take heart from the spite and spirit his side showed. This was more points than they had ever tallied against Australia, which spoke both to their performance and that of a lacklustre visiting side. Backing it up against Japan is the next, and significant, challenge.

“I’m delighted we were able to get the win,” Itoje said. “[Borthwick] is a world-class coach and we are lucky to have him. It’s never nice getting criticism, but it is part of the game. If we were scared of criticism, we wouldn’t be here. We have full support in Steve.”

News.title: Stephen Miller and the DOJ hatching plan to throw journalists in jail over leaks: report
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Newly appointed White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and the Department of Justice have reportedly been considering throwing journalists in jail to get them to reveal their sources when government intel is leaked, according to a report.

Following Susie Wiles’ exit as chief of staff, The Atlantic reported that President Donald Trump urged the DOJ to pursue criminal-leak investigations on national security grounds.

There have reportedly been discussions among White House officials about tactics they could use to get journalists to reveal their sources — including arresting them, three people familiar with the subject told the outlet.

Two people described Wiles pushing back against trying to force journalists to divulge their government sources, while Miller was in favor of the move, insisting that it wouldn’t take long for journalists to give up their sources, according to the report.

A DOJ spokesperson told The Atlantic: “This is absolutely false,” and reiterated that when approached for comment by The Independent.

open image in gallery The new White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller is reportedly on board with jailing journalists to get them to reveal their sources, according to a report ( Reuters )

Meanwhile, a White House spokesperson told The Independent: “Unauthorized leaks of sensitive national security information will NEVER be tolerated. They endanger American lives and threaten our national security. Those responsible must be held accountable.”

It is not illegal for journalists to receive — and write about — classified information they have received from a government leaker, even if the source themselves has violated the law by sharing the information.

In 1971, The New York Times published excerpts of a leaked report detailing the U.S. involvement in the Vietnam War, prompting the Nixon administration to try and block the publication of the leaked files. However, the Supreme Court ruled in favor of the newspaper and press freedom.

On Friday, Trump revealed that his longtime aide, Miller, would be replacing Wiles, who Trump was reportedly “furious” with after Republicans lost control of Congress in last week’s midterm elections.

A longtime proponent of expansive presidential authority, Miller takes over at a time when the Republican Party's midterm defeat could leave Trump more reliant on executive power to advance his domestic agenda.

Miller, 41, is one of Trump’s longest-serving aides and one of only a few who have worked for the president throughout both his first and second terms in office.

open image in gallery Wiles is moving to Trump’s political operation as Stephen Miller takes over her job as White House Chief of Staff ( Getty )

However, he is best known for driving Trump’s aggressive immigration crackdown, which has been widely unpopular among Americans. Just 36% of respondents to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed early this week approve of Trump’s mass deportation agenda, with 54% disapproving.

Still, Trump announced Miller as Wiles’ replacement on Friday.

“I am pleased to announce that Mr. Stephen Miller, the current Deputy Chief of Staff of the Trump Administration, and one of my most trusted advisors, will become the Chief of Staff starting Monday, November 9, 2026,” he wrote on Truth Social.

“Susie Wiles, who has done an outstanding job, will be moving over to the Trump Political Operation. I want to thank her for her service as Chief of Staff — She has done a great job!”

News.title: Man Utd pull off another chaotic comeback but Carrick’s job hangs by a thread
News.content:
Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.



United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.



They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.



The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.



Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”



Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.



“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”



Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.



United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence.



More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.



Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership.



Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.



“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

News.title: Energised England deliver statement win to take heat off Borthwick
News.content:
England captain Maro Itoje said this week: “Playing for England, you often don’t need much else to motivate you. But when you have external things coming out, saying things which you don’t think are true... we want to play for Steve, we want to represent him in a way that is fitting of the quality of coach he is. We want to represent ourselves, we want to represent the country where we take great pride in playing for England.

“I have full confidence that the public, the English rugby fans, our families, friends in the stands, you guys are going to see a team that’s fighting for one another, that’s going to put their best forward, that’s going to be aggressive, that’s going to take this game to Australia. There’s no shying away. It’s the first game of autumn. We want to set the tone of how this autumn is going to go.

“It’s a hugely important game. But I often think about these big games and think, ‘What’s the alternative? Where would you rather be? Would I want to play for a country or a team that is not part of these big games, that doesn’t have consequences?’ I want to be playing in teams where games matter, where there’s something on the line.

“These are the games that get your blood pumping and you realise it’s big. In terms of where we want to go, but also we want to do well in this competition, we want to do well, we want to respond to perhaps the inconsistencies of the Six Nations, we want to show ourselves and show the English rugby fans that we’ve turned a corner. So for that reason, this game is huge.”

News.title: Xabi Alonso disgusted after Chelsea bullied by Brobbey and Sunderland
News.content:
Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

The hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored the winner in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

“I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume said.

“We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”

Stay here for all the team news, build-up and action.

News.title: Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo Grand Prix as Mercedes seal constructors’ championship
News.content:
Lando Norris will start today’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix on pole position after a chaotic qualifying session at Interlagos yesterday. A red flag was thrown a matter of moments into qualifying, which led to a lengthy delay of around an hour and a half. When racing did resume, the conditions were treacherous but it was the 2025 world champion Norris who coped best by claiming his third straight pole at Interlagos.

“It has been a long day,” Norris said after taking pole. “It has been a great qualifying. To be on pole again here, two years in a row, different conditions to last year, but I am very happy. It is not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it is going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that is exactly what we did, so it has been a very good day.

“This was my first time driving the car in the wet, so I think I figured it out pretty quick. It is tough because you are wet, intermediates, all different tyres, and it was very windy the last couple of laps. It was certainly a good day for learning for me and good to take into tomorrow [today]. These guys [Mercedes] are also very quick. Just happy. Today [yesterday] is about getting on pole. It does not really matter how you do it, so very pleased with that.”

News.title: Liverpool’s expensive attack feast on Palace to leave Sage looking doomed
News.content:
Major signings need to lay down a marker when arriving at Liverpool. Barcola has his hat-trick at LASK in the Champions League, but we are still waiting for a stirring big-match-defining contribution from him since his summer arrival. Arguably the same could be said for Wirtz, nearly 18 months since he joined.

Neither left Selhurst Park looking like the world-beaters they did occasionally for their previous clubs. Still, one misfiring attacker creating a goal for another represents progress and all great partnerships must start somewhere. Lennon and McCartney would improve after 1958’s Too Bad About Sorrows.

If there was ever a place for the least-productive expensively assembled attacking group in the league to find form it was surely south London on this Sunday lunchtime. Liverpool came in with two defeats in their previous two but, European trophy aside, it has been a lousy 2026 for Palace.

They have the most defeats of any ever-present Premier League team and began (and ended) the weekend with the worst defensive record. They have conceded twice as many goals from headers as any other team. Even their most loyal fan group has disbanded.

Alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring in gut-punching fashion, after a series of Palace near-misses. Chairman Steve Parish rubbed his face in the directors’ box, in the style of peak-stress era Guardiola. None of this looks good for Sage.

“My job is not the most important thing,” Sage said. “The most important thing is to find an efficient solution for the team and for the club.” With the international break beginning on Monday you wonder whether that solution may be a new head coach.

News.title: Lando Norris takes pole at Interlagos after chaotic qualifying session
News.content:
McLaren’s Lando Norris claimed pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix for a third consecutive year as he emerged victorious from a marathon, rain-affected qualifying session at Interlagos lasting two and a half hours.

But there was further frustration for his compatriot George Russell, who lashed out at his Mercedes pit wall after being told to abort a push lap in Q3 which he felt would have been good enough to finish qualifying in first place.

Whether Russell was right was debatable, but you could understand his frustration. The Briton has endured a miserable season, dropping from second to fourth in the drivers’ championship in Mexico last weekend after suffering yet another power unit issue.

Russell ended up leaving the Mexico paddock early while team-mate Kimi Antonelli celebrated becoming the sport’s youngest ever champion.

News.title: Man City look to be crumbling after guilty verdict
News.content:
Is this the day the xG gods reward Nottingham Forest? Oliver Glasner’s team sit 19th having won one game all season, but there is no doubt that their performances have been significantly better than results and they might need their luck to turn against Man City team full of firepower.

Despite all of the positive indicators in Forest’s underlying data, Glasner caused some alarm with his comments after last weekend’s defeat at Brentford.

The Austrian said: “We have to accept it’s not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.

“I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it’s always compromises. It’s a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.”

Dangerous words perhaps when you work for Evangelos Marinakis, but John Percy reported this week that Glasner was backed by his players in a squad meeting.

City are smarting from back-to-back defeats by Aston Villa and Brighton, but they created more than enough in both games to claim some sort of result. Nevertheless, there is a persistent sense that their defensive unit remains too marshmellow-like over the course of 38 games, and Forest have the counter-attacking threat to test them.

Glasner has happy memories of playing City, beating them in the 2025 FA Cup final with Crystal Palace, but his Forest reign is in urgent need of a signature victory and performance.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Rees-Zammit delivers in best position but work to do for sloppy Wales
News.content:
Maybe it is an indication that Wales are improving that this latest close victory over Japan was greeted with a shrug instead of euphoria.

A year ago, almost to the day, Steve Tandy, the Welsh head coach jumped around and hugged his staff, after a one-point win over the Brave Blossoms and there were reports of red-shirted fans in this stadium crying in joy and relief.

Yet that was Wales’s first home success in 10 Tests and, despite the form since hardly raising itself anywhere near levels of excellence, much more was expected on this occasion.

Yes, Tandy’s men prevailed and it was a huge positive to watch player-of-the match Louis Rees-Zammit in great nick on the wing. Nobody should overestimate the Bristol man’s display because the game knows that he can operate even better, but after this there can now be no doubt that he is a wing rather than a full-back. The 25-year-old conjured five line breaks, beat 13 defenders and made 121 metres.

Yet most notably, Rees-Zammit scored his first try for his country in eight matches and that is exactly what he was put on the green-green grass to do. After assisting in fellow wing Josh Adams’s opening try – this other resurgent British and Irish Lion bagged a brace – Rees-Zammit showed his predatory instincts to go over after a wonderful deft offload from centre Eddie James.

Sports.title: Man Utd officially become the worst defensive team in Europe this season with horror show against Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED are officially the worst defensive team in Europe after shipping four goals at home to Aston Villa.

United might have rescued a stunning 4-4 draw on Sunday, but their woeful displays at the back will cause real concern.



The Red Devils went 2-0 down to Unai Emery‘s men in the opening four minutes Old Trafford to sum up their woes at the back.

Michael Carrick‘s side initially pulled it back to 2-2 thanks to Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans‘ goals.



But Villa stunned the home side with two more quick-fire strikes at the start of the second half.

John McGinn netted from the spot before Leon Goretzka restored their two-goal lead minutes later.

United went on to salvage a point after mounting another comeback to secure a draw in the last minute of stoppage time.

Joshua Zirkzee pulled one back before Patrick Dorgu nodded home in the dying seconds.

But a shocking stat revealed just how woeful United have been defensively after conceding their THIRTIETH goal of the season.

It means no team in the big five leagues have let in more goals than United in all competitions.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Before conceding four at home to Villa, they also let in three against Bournemouth in their last game at Old Trafford.

And they were also battered 4-1 by Como last month.

Their draw meant they avoided a third successive defeat against Villa.



And the result could save Carrick from the sack after looking on the brink when United went 4-2 down.

It was his second impressive comeback after masterminding a 3-2 turnaround win against Roma in midweek.

United will now go into the international break with a tough decision to make over his future.

The team remain 18th in the Prem table after just one win all season – the worst tally of any side.

Their solitary three points came in a 5-2 win at home to Ipswich Town in August.

Sports.title: Unai Emery storms down Old Trafford tunnel before full-time as Aston Villa blow two-goal lead
Sports.content:
Next

UNAI EMERY stormed down the tunnel before the end of the match after watching his side concede a heartbreaking late equaliser against Manchester United.

The Spaniard’s side found themselves two goals up on two occasions in the match, and held the cushion heading into six minutes of injury time.



But a dagger from Joshua Zirkzee and an equaliser from Patrick Dorgu in the second and sixth minutes of injury time saw the lead evaporate.

The Dane capitalised on Zion Suzuki‘s flapping attempt to clear a late corner, heading home into an empty net to rescue a point for Michael Carrick and Co.



But Emery was absolutely fuming with the outcome after blowing such a convincing late lead.

He was seen storming off down the line before play had even been restarted for the final seconds of the match.



The strange outburst meant that he was not able to stick around to shake his opponent’s hand after the match, but Carrick will likely have bigger things on his mind after just barely escaping a loss.

VAR delayed the restart after his exit to investigate shouts of a foul on Suzuki, with United keeper Senne Lammens appearing to cheekily nudge the keeper.

But there was very little in it, and the goal was allowed to stand.

It is bizarrely not the first time that Emery has decided he has seen enough before shaking the hand of his opposite number.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Emery also rushed down the tunnel after Villa were smashed for four against his former club Arsenal.

He failed to shake Mikel Arteta‘s hand after the 4-1 loss, with the Gunners boss looking around the sideline for the absent Emery before giving up and celebrating with his players.

Sports.title: Man Utd ratings: Senne Lammens suffers worst outing since joining as Diogo Dalot booed off after horror display
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED will rot in the relegation zone during the November break for the first time in 40 years after a hectic 4-4 with Aston Villa.

Twice they were down two goals, twice they came back, but United still sit 18th in the table and chiefs are set to decide on Michael Carrick‘s future during the break.



Goals from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson in three minutes and 40 seconds turned Old Trafford toxic towards the board.

United’s attack switched into a gear for their best period of the season as a Bruno Fernandes penalty and Youri Tielemans strike levelled the scores before half-time.



But more shambolic defending straight after the restart took the wind out of Carrick’s sails before two late stoppage time goals from subs Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu.

It’s 15 goals shipped since the 4-1 drubbing in Como and 30 goals conceded after 14 games – the worst defensive record across Europe’s top five leagues – with a trip to Anfield up next.



Here’s how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated the United players from Old Trafford.

Senne Lammens – 3

His worst game in a United shirt and not many recent goalkeepers here have bounced back under such calamity.

Two horrendous mistakes in three minutes turned Old Trafford toxic. However, he is a sitting duck behind the worst defence in Europe.

Alysson’s low strike flew under his legs and he pushed the Brazilian’s second shot out to Jackson in a comedy of errors.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Diogo Dalot – 2

Heart in mouth stuff as he returned at left-back, Dalot is forever the scapegoat. He did not challenge Alysson who had hours to shoot before Lammens flumbed.

Alysson had his number from then on as the winger skipped past him repeatedly. He foolishly tripped the Brazilian to concede a daft penalty straight after the restart.

Harry Maguire – 6

The 33-year-old improved on his recent outings, winning a few foot races and handled Jackson better after the two early goals.

Replaced through suspected injury at the break.

Leny Yoro – 5

A real mixed bag. Some good moments, other agonising on his return to centre-half after a stretch of games at right back



The youngster frustratingly headed up into danger zone in the lead up to Villa’s second but recovered with two important interceptions before the break.

But the 20-year-old’s good work was undone when he naively headed against his own bar from a Villa free-kick to make it 4-2.

Noussair Mazraoui – 4

The Moroccan conceded several needless fouls but Villa targeted United’s other flank more.

His head blocked Fernandes’ cross before an impromptu cut back set up Tielemans.

Youri Tielemans – 6

The former Villa man hoofed the ball straight out of the net after scoring his first United goal against his former club.



Starting back in the pivot, the Belgian was strong in the tackle and linked up well with Amad and Mbeumo.

Did well to block out the noise after the away end sang “You used to play for a big club” after United triggered his £35m release clause in the summer.

Kobbie Mainoo – 5

Mainoo lacks pace and struggles to cover space but shows his worth when United have possession. A big tackle after Dalot’s awkward pass saved another shot at Lammens.

Unai Emery‘s tactical changes at half-time meant Vilal controlled United in transition, meaning United lacked control in midfield.

Bruno Fernandes – 6

Good first half, shoddy second. United need more from their skipper who turned it off and on again.



Returned to his to hop and step routine to slot in a composed penalty and had two shots whistle just past the post in a frantic opening 30 minutes. Looked unhappy at the end despite the comeback.

Bryan Mbeumo – 5

Struggled to get involved in the first half waves of attacks.

He is not offering enough in attacking areas in this fluid strikerless system and lacks physicality.



Amad – 6

Maybe the Shea Lacey noise made its way to Amad, who showed flashes of his best self, but still lacked that crucial end product.

The Ivory Coast winger beat his man and offered up chances, giving Ian Maatsen a difficult afternoon, but could not find a way past Zion Suzuki.

Matheus Cunha – 6

After a stellar performance in the Champions League comeback on Tuesday, Cunha repsonded like a United player should to going behind.

He did brilliantly to win the penalty, forcing Boubacar Kamada to wildly slide in and wipe him out and worked relentlessly in his defensive duties in the first half

Gave makeshift right back Taylor Harwood-Bellis the run around before another implosion from the hosts.



SUBS:

Ayden Heaven (Maguire, HT) – 4

Too late in the challenge again and was booked for a dangerous one on Alysson 12 minutes into his cameo.

Mason Mount (Tielemans, 64) – 6

Unlucky not to claw one back here as he latched onto a good ball then clatters off the woodwork before delivering a great final ball at the death.

Patrick Dorgu (Dalot, 64) – 7

Not match fit but had to replace the Portuguese. Changed the outcome of the game with an assist and goal.

Shea Lacey (Amad, 64) – 6

Did well but should have read the final cross at the end, with the back post gaping.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Joshua Zirkzee (Mbeumo, 80) – 6

A good finish drew a consolation.



Subs not used: Darlow, De Ligt, Andrey Santos, J Fletcher.

Sports.title: All the ex-Man Utd stars who attended Sir Alex Ferguson’s 40th anniversary dinner – can you name them all?
Sports.content:

MANCHESTER UNITED legends gathered in numbers to celebrate the 40th anniversary of Sir Alex Ferguson’s club appointment.

The most decorated football manager of all-time stepped into the famous Old Trafford dugout on November 6, 1986.



What started as a chat with then-chairman Martin Edwards at a service station blossomed into a dynasty of silverware over his 26-and-a-half year tenure.

But behind the Scotsman, the historic Treble, and 13 Premier League titles remains a group of players willing to back their boss until their final breath.



Around 100 high-profile guests gathered in the Theatre of Dreams’ lofty halls to raise a toast to the 84-year-old.

In the top picture in this article are all the ex-players who attended – can you name them all?

Current United boss Michael Carrick lined up for a talent-laden snap, alongside legends like Edwin van der Sar and John O’Shea.

Between all of the players present, the icons collectively boasted a huge 75 Premier League titles.



The stars in attendance at the dinner presented fans with a unique glimpse at the cross-section of Fergie’s United.

From the first Premier League era, when Lee Martin scored the winner in the 1990 FA Cup final replay, to Denis Irwin, Clayton Blackmore, and Dion Dublin.

They all turned up suited and booted.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS



Mike Phelan showed up, remembered as one of Fergie’s reliables, especially after becoming his assistant in the next decade.

He is still the only individual to serve as player, first-team coach, and assistant manager with the Red Devils.

Joining the ranks too was Brian McClair – the first United player since George Best to score 20 league goals in a season – alongside Gary Pallister and Paul Parker.

From the 1999 Treble-winning roster, David May, Ronny Johnsen, Wes Brown, and Jesper Blomqvist appeared.



Then came Darren Fletcher, Nemanja Vidic, and Quinton Fortune who all fought for Fergie’s last few titles.

And Ryan Giggs, a man that spent a lot of time with Fergie as United’s all-time record appearance holder also came out to raise a glass.

Even Jonny Evans, who lifted three Prem titles before his return in 2023, turned out.

Attendees Javier Hernandez and Robin Van Persie also popped up on everyone’s tellys this evening when United went two down against Aston Villa (the first time).

But it’s impossible for everyone to make every social engagement with a tightly-packed football calendar.



Both Gary and Phil Neville missed out on the anniversary dinner after a scheduling clash with their joint TV appearance in the US.

Though, supporters will be hoping for many more celebrations with Fergie – after a year of worrying health scares.

In 2006, the Premier League held a celebratory lunch for Ferguson’s 20th anniversary attended by the majority of the club’s managers.

Sports.title: Man Utd 4 Aston Villa 4: Patrick Dorgu scores staggering 96th minute leveller after Red Devils fell apart in both halves
Sports.content:
Next

THESE ARE grave times for Manchester United when they are 18th and a draw is treated like a victory.

After Aston Villa’s 60-second opener, they needed eight more without reply to condemn United to the foot of the table. Villa scored again less than three minutes later.



At that rate, Villa were on course to sink United. The Championship may yet beckon.

Yet there were jubilant scenes at this old ground. United came from 2-0 down and entered added time 4-2 down. They scored twice.



Even the worst United sides can summon spirit from somewhere. Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu, two unlikely game-changers, netted in the 92nd and 96th minutes.

United were bottom for two minutes and 45 seconds on Sunday before Liverpool went ahead against Crystal Palace in one of the early kick-offs. United head into the November internationals in the relegation zone and level on points with basement club Palace.



In the directors’ box, there were reminders of United’s golden days. Robin van Persie and Javier Hernandez, members of the last title-winning side in 2013, attended a dinner to commemorate the 40th anniversary of Sir Alex Ferguson’s appointment.

They will have recognised the first half fightback and the finale. Some things at United remain unchanged post-Ferguson.

“Four-two and you f****d it up,” roared the United fans. Had substitute Shea Lacey gambled he might have made it 5-4.

The manner of this recovery may give Michael Carrick yet another stay of execution. But how low can United go for their decision-makers to make the necessary decision with Michael Carrick? By the time they next play, they may be bottom.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

More banners expressed opposition to the Glazer-Ratcliffe regime. One that draped down from the Stretford End said: “We don’t want a new stadium, we want new owners”

Another sinisterly read, “Your funeral not ours”. “You’re not fit to wear the shirt” was aired by United matchgoers for only the fourth time in my lifetime.

They abused director of football Jason Wilcox again. Stewards adjacent to the directors’ box were on alert whenever Villa scored,

A genuinely positive first half fightback from United was undone by right back Diogo Dalot, tormented all afternoon by the quicksilver winger Alysson.



Despite the boos for Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez in recent weeks, Dalot is scapegoat No.1. He was substituted amid raucous boos at his removal and cheers for the decision.

How low can United go without a change? Even if they had pulled off another comeback triumph, it would barely have mattered.

Villa have won twice at United since 1983 and their supporters have several scars from United comeback defeats. They have another, despite avoiding defeat.

Unai Emery remains winless at Old Trafford 16 years after he first occupied the away dugout with Valencia. He headed for the tunnel before full-time.



There was no repeat of Villa’s collapse from 2-0 up to lose 3-2 at United on Boxing Day in 2023. That was principally down to Dalot, a United starter by default for years.

Senne Lammens’ form is now not a mere early-season wobble. Dalot’s refusal to engage Alysson was unforgivable yet the low side-footer seemed harmless until it flew through Lammens’ legs inside 60 seconds.



Doubtless unsettled by the error, Lammens then mishandled another precise hit by Alysson from the edge of the area that gifted NIcolas Jackson a tap-in.

The £18.1million Lammens was a prudent purchase in his first season yet, with expectations raised and pressure more intense, perhaps his true level has been exposed.

“You’re not fit to wear the shirt,” bellowed the Stretford End after Jackson pounced to make it 0-2 after 220 seconds.

Matheus Cunha, one of the few truly urgent United players, showed he was fit enough. His purposeful charge was halted by a rash Boubacar Kamara that secured the penalty that Bruno Fernandes converted.



Fernandes has scored against Villa more times than any other opponent and sent Zion Suzuki in the opposite direction in the 16th minute.



The United captain pointed at Cunha after he placed the ball on the centre circle to hasten the restart.

The goal improved the atmosphere and if a 21st-minute walkout was planned there was no evidence of it amid another ineffectual attempt at a protest by United followers.

Fernandes’ goalbound drive was deflected narrowly wide by John McGinn in the 25th minute and Suzuki – a United target in the same summer that they signed Andre Onana – kept out uncomfortably.

Suzuki eventually cracked. Tielemans, heckled by Villa fans in his first appearance against them, met Amad’s cutback and Suzuki flimsily failed to keep it out on 44 minutes.

The ‘keeper protested that Bryan Mbeumo was in his eyeline. Mbeuimo was, but he was onside.



Dalot did his utmost to puncture United’s positivity at half-time looming when Alysson got the run on him and dinked the ball over the tentative Lammens and wide.

Villa did not have much longer to wait for Dalot to be their 12th man.

He lazily tripped Alysson inside the area less than two minutes into the restart and McGinn confidently swept in from 12 yards.



The regression continued. Leny Yoro inexplicably headed against his own goalframe from McGinn’s inswinging free kick and Leon Goretzka prodded in from the ensuing scramble.

The ‘funeral’ banner was unfurled just in time for Yoro to create the chaos. United supporters’ mood initially only improved when Dalot was hooked but substitutes Dorgu and Zirkzee combined in added time to threaten a draw.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Suzuki then came to United’s aid again when he misjudged Fernandes’ looping corner and Dorgu, of all people, nodded in to raise the roof.

Amazingly, it lifted United up to 18th.

Sports.title: ‘He’s not unstoppable’ – Xabi Alonso blasts his own Chelsea players after Brian Brobbey dominates them
Sports.content:
Next

XABI ALONSO slammed his Chelsea defenders after Brian Brobbey pounded them into submission at Sunderland.

Levi Colwill was hauled off after giving away the decisive penalty for a foul on the Dutchman while he also ran Wesley Fofana ragged in their 1-0 loss at the Stadium of Light.



Alonso, whose side slipped to fifth, denied Brobbey had bullied his backline but said: “Out of almost nothing, he got a couple of chances. He got the penalty as well, but we have been preparing for that.

“No, [he’s] not unstoppable. He’s stoppable, but when you defend better than we did today.



“No, not bullied. I would say that it was a situation that we could have defended better.”

Chelsea were denied a spot-kick of their own after a VAR check when ineffective Cole Palmer was bundled over by Luke O’Nien shortly before desperate Colwill clipped Brobbey for Enzo Le Fee to stroke home from the spot.

Spaniard Alonso said: “I haven’t seen Cole’s one but I’ve been told that there was a chance that it could be a fair penalty and it could have been given.

“And the other one, I’m not happy with how we defended that situation, something that we could avoid, something that we had worked during the week and from that action to give a penalty is not good for us.”

Chelsea made 648 passes compared to Sunderland’s 292 but only produced four shots on target.

Much of their 69 per cent possession was spent passing from side to side as they struggled without injured striker Joao Pedro.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Alonso added: “For sure we miss him. Even when we win, even when we lose, we miss some players that we have injured and for sure we are waiting to have them back because they are important.

“Now we need to use the time to recover them, but with the players we have to get ready for the next one. It’s quite hard now where one player is out and then another player is back. There are situations.”

Meanwhile, Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders felt it was team-mate Colwill fouled rather than Brobbey for the penalty.



Though the Belgian, 21, admitted: “You know when you come here in this stadium it will be a difficult game and that was the matter tonight.

“We knew it would be tough, we are disappointed we lost the game. At one point it went very fast from side to side. Sometimes we had to control.

“With 11 behind the ball it is difficult to find the spaces. How you do – good or not – it is a matter of staying together.

“The international break is coming so the lads can be calm in the head and when we all come back we need to be motivated to go again.”

Sports.title: Darren Beckford dead at 59: Tragedy as former Man City, Norwich and Port Vale star dies as tributes pour in
Sports.content:
STAR GONE Darren Beckford dead at 59: Tragedy as former Man City, Norwich and Port Vale star dies as tributes pour in







Next

FORMER Manchester City star Darren Beckford has died aged 59.

The ex-striker came through City’s academy before a journeyman career saw him feature for teams like Port Vale, Norwich, Oldham and Fulham.



The cause of death has not yet been confirmed.

City were one of the first of his old clubs to pay tribute after the shock news was confirmed.



They wrote in a statement: “Manchester City is deeply saddened to hear of the passing of former City player and Academy graduate, Darren Beckford – truly one of our own.

“We extend our heartfelt sympathies to Darren’s family and friends at this difficult time.”



Oldham and Port Vale also offered their condolences on social media.

Oldham said: “Everyone at the club is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Darren Beckford. Darren made 52 appearances for Latics between 1993-1996.

“Our heartfelt condolences go out to Darren’s family, friends and former teammates at this time. Rest in peace, Darren.”

Port Vale added: “We are extremely saddened to learn of the passing for former player Darren Beckford who passed away this morning.



“Our thoughts are with Darren’s friends, family and former team mates. He will of course be forever Valiant. RIP Darren.”

Beckford – who was the father of ex-Leeds and Everton striker Jermaine -made his debut for City aged just 16 back in 1984.

He later joined Port Vale for £15,000 and was a hit as he scored 81 goals in 214 appearances.



Beckford went on to join Norwich in 1991 and played in the Premier League for the first time a year later before netting 13 in 49 outings for the Canaries.

He also played in the top flight for Oldham after moving to the Lactics in 1993.

Beckford had a brief stint in Scotland with Hearts in 1996 before returning to England to play for Preston, Fulham and Walsall – all in the same season.

He rounded off his career with Southport and Bury and then retired in 1998.

Sports.title: Barry Daines dead at 75: Tottenham cult hero who was legendary understudy passes away as tributes pour in
Sports.content:
'deeply saddened' Barry Daines dead at 75: Tottenham cult hero who was legendary understudy passes away as tributes pour in







Next

TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR have announced the death of former goalkeeper Barry Daines aged 75.

The Essex-born stopper joined the club as an apprentice in 1969.



He went on to make 146 league appearances for the North London club before departing in 1981.

Spurs announced the news in a statement on Sunday.



The club wrote: “We are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of our former goalkeeper Barry Daines, aged 75.

“The thoughts and love of everyone at the Club are with Barry’s family and friends at this difficult time. Rest in peace, Barry.”

Daines spent much of his 12-year spell with the club as the backup to Spurs and Northern Ireland legend Pat Jennings.

The iconic keeper preceded Daines, arriving from Watford in 1964 before leaving for North London rivals Arsenal in 1977.

Daines took up the mantle of starting goalkeeper in his absence, and featured in all 42 league matches the season after Jennings made the switch.

He was handed a Spurs testimonial upon his exit in 1981, after which he spent two years plying his trade in Hong Kong.



Daines’ former team-mate Micky Hazard led the tributes to the keeper on social media.

Hazard wrote: “Very sad to hear of the passing of the lovely Barry Daines, my thoughts and prayers are with his family and friends at this very sad time.

“Rest in Peace Barry and go do some shotstopping in the sky.”

A Spurs fan replied: “That’s very sad. He was keeper when I first became a Spurs fan as a kid in the 70s.



“Had a hard job following the great Pat Jennings. Thoughts to his loved ones.”

And another distraught supporter added: “My first Spurs keeper as a kid, so Barry always held a special place in my heart, RIP Barry!”

Sports.title: Man Utd finally show fight in Aston Villa thriller - but Michael Carrick's fate hangs in the balance
Sports.content:
Manchester United staged a dramatic late fightback to salvage a point against Aston Villa in a thrilling 4-4 draw despite defensive collapses at the start of both halves, with the result still likely to leave Michael Carrick's position hanging in the balance.

United had slipped into the relegation zone before a ball had even been kicked courtesy of Nottingham Forest's victory over Manchester City on Saturday evening and their fortunes did not improve once they took to the field, instead worsening instantly.

Alysson required less than 60 seconds to slot the ball through Senne Lammens legs to leave Old Trafford shellshocked. The stunned silence that filled the air swiftly turned to anger as Nicolas Jackson doubled Villa's lead just two minutes later after Lammens palmed the ball into his path, condemning Manchester United to the worst possible start.

With the fans' anger ringing in their ears, United dragged themselves back off the canvas after that devastating one-two to hit back, first from the penalty spot after Glen Kamara wiped out Matheus Cunha. Bruno Fernandes, so often United's saviour in years gone by, made no mistake from the spot.

‌



The comeback was complete just before half-time when Youri Tielemans netted against his old club, but United imploded spectacularly once again after the break. First, Diogo Dalot lost all leave of his senses to give away a needless penalty which John McGinn converted with aplomb.

Another episode of calamity saw Villa restore their two goal advantage with Leon Goretzka tapping home after shoddy defending.

It didn't feel like there would be any way back for United this time. But they fought back once more with Joshua Zirkzee netting in the 92nd minute to spark a late barrage which resulted in a last-gasp goal from Patrick Dorgu.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

UNITED FINALLY SHOW FIGHT

View 4 Images John McGinn celebrates after notching Aston Villa's third goal (Image: Ed Sykes/Allstar)

Just when you think things can't get any worse for Manchester United, Aston Villa go and stick two goals past Lammens inside four minutes to turn Old Trafford toxic. It certainly wasn't the start United or Michael Carrick would have envisaged, but it did, at least, trigger a response from their struggling stars.

‌



Kamara didn't need to scythe down Cunha to gift United a route back into the game via the penalty spot. But they did, finally, show some fight to haul themselves back into the game - only to then throw that away with another unforgivable start to the second half.

United have now shipped 30 goals in all competitions - the joint worst in Europe's top five leagues - and started the game languishing in 19th place in the Premier League. But they rallied to snatch a point at the death.

CARRICK'S FATE IN THE BALANCE

View 4 Images Michael Carrick is likely to pay the price for another poor result (Image: James Gill/Danehouse)

‌



For a long time, this felt like the point of no return for Manchester United's beleaguered head coach. And in truth, even United's rousing late fightback may not be enough to save his job.

Carrick should not be the only figure to pay for United's plight with his job, but it's hard to lay out a case for him staying in his post with his team just one point away from propping up the table. He and his staff looked utterly bewildered on the bench following Villa's early goals, as did Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in the stands.

Fightback or not, it's still been a ludicrous start to the season - just one league win in 10 - and while Carrick is not the root of United's problems, he is not the solution, either.

EMERY'S OLD TRAFFORD ANGER

‌



If Manchester United do spend the international break shopping for a new manager, one wonders whether they will cast their eye in Unai Emery's direction.

A combination of the gargantuan compensation fee it would take to prise Emery away from Villa Park - said to be around £20million - and United's sorry plight probably makes that a rather unrealistic prospect. And while that may be bad news for United, it's great news for Villa, who are looking upwardly mobile under the Spaniard after a transitional summer.

But an irate Emery let his anger get the better off him in the final seconds, storming off following United's late leveller after it was allowed to stand.

POST-MATCH SCENES SPEAK VOLUMES

‌



View 4 Images Manchester United players look on after conceding (Image: Carl Recine)

Once the euphoria had died down, the pictures at the final whistle told the story.

On the 40th anniversary of Sir Alex Ferguson's appointment, United may have struck in Fergie time to salvage a point but you wouldn't have guessed it from the look on players' faces.

The mood was sombre given this result was still not the tonic United or Carrick needed heading into the international break, which will bring further scrutiny with United in the relegation zone.
