Sports.title: Fulham star Rodrigo Muniz bravely reveals wife suffered miscarriage in emotional interview
Sports.content:
Fulham star Rodrigo Muniz bravely reveals wife suffered miscarriage in emotional interview

Fulham star Rodrigo Muniz shared the heartbreaking news that his wife suffered a miscarriage last season during a difficult period for the striker both on and off the pitch

View 2 Images Rodrigo Muniz shared the heart-breaking news in a post-match interview (Image: X/@FulhamFC)

Rodrigo Muniz bravely revealed that his wife suffered a miscarriage last season after scoring his first Premier League goal for Fulham in over a year on Saturday.

‌



‌



The striker, 25, salvaged a point for Fulham with a smart flicked finish at Craven Cottage against Newcastle. Prior to finding the net in the 1-1 draw, Muniz had not scored since August 2025, partly due to undergoing surgery on a hamstring injury last November.

‌



Muniz, who was sidelined until February after going under the knife, has been in amongst the goals this season, scoring against West Ham and AFC Wimbledon in the Carabao Cup.

‌



But Saturday's strike ended his long wait for a Premier League goal. And he marked it by dedicating it to his baby, revealing that his wife is pregnant again after last year's heartbreak.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Speaking to club media, Muniz reflected: “Last season was really difficult for me. Now I can say it but I had the surgery, my wife was pregnant last season and unfortunately we lost the baby. But God is good all the time. And now she’s pregnant again. The goal was for my baby and I hope this season will be different than last season.”

‌



Muniz has featured in eight of Fulham's 10 Premier League games under new head coach Alvaro Arbeloa but has failed to start in the league.

He went on to emphasise his desire to play a greater role for Fulham this term, adding: “I train hard every week to get opportunities to play and I want to play more. I cannot control that but I showed to the gaffer I want to play more. And I have to keep training hard for him to say, ‘Okay, now is your time’, and then I’m ready.

‌



View 2 Images Muniz celebrates after scoring for Fulham against Newcastle (Image: David Horton/CameraSport)

“To be a striker, you need to be ready to play five or ten minutes. Of course, I want to play more. And I want to start as well. We have a lot of players in the national team. We train with, I think, ten players.

“It’s really important because we cannot stay out for too long. And when we have time to work it’s really good – because it’s really important that the gaffer can show us what he wants and we have time to do it.”

Sports.title: Man Utd sent relegation threat amid Michael Carrick struggles - 'There is reason to panic'
Sports.content:
Man Utd sent relegation threat amid Michael Carrick struggles - 'There is reason to panic'

Manchester United have dropped in the bottom three and talk of them being relegated continues as Michael Carrick remains a man firmly under pressure

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's future remains uncertain given Man Utd's season (Image: Martin Rickett/Press Association)

Manchester United have "reason to panic" after slipping into the Premier League relegation zone, with former Chelsea defender Frank Leboeuf admitting they may have "no other choice" but to sack Michael Carrick.

‌



‌



The Red Devils have endured their worst ever start to a Premier League season and on Saturday evening dropped into the bottom three for the first time this term. They've won just once in nine games with their decline showing no sign of easing up ahead of a huge game with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

‌



The club have fallen away from being title challengers and two years ago finished 15th, their lowest ever Premier League position. They've now sunk to new depths and despite having an expensively assembled squad, there is mounting talk of them being in a relegation scrap.

‌



Leboeuf concedes that the club aren't going to rid of their underperforming squad, which could eventually leave them with no option but to make a ruthless call in the dugout if they want to change the direction of travel in Manchester.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The Frenchman told ESPNFC: "It’s been a while since you had to panic because we saw the games that they had. There is reason to panic and it’s been like that for a while.

"Nothing is getting good, we don’t see any improvement, we don’t see how it can be better. Again, I’m all for Michael Carrick. But there is a time when there will be no other choices but getting rid of him. You can’t get rid of those players who don’t deserve to play for Manchester United, who aren’t good enough for Manchester United.

‌



"They don’t have the guts, the courage, the pride of fighting for the club. I don’t see any solution, I don’t see anything getting good and if they carry on like that you could see Manchester United getting relegated which is amazing."

View 2 Images Man Utd have only won once in the Premier League this season (Image: (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP via Getty Images) )

‌



United have 13 Premier League titles to their name and their relegation would be among the greatest shocks in the history of English football. After losing at Chelsea eight days ago Carrick was forced to address the prospect of the team dropping into the Championship.

He said: "We've got to keep moving forward and winning games, simple as that. There's no words that I'm going to explain to you now that makes it [being in relegation zone] any difference, it's not going to change it. We've got to move forward and win football matches, it's as simple as that."

Sports.title: Would a Man Utd relegation eclipse Leicester's title as Premier League's great shock
Sports.content:
Would a Man Utd relegation eclipse Leicester's title as Premier League's great shock

HAVE YOUR SAY: Leicester's Premier League title in 2016 will live long in the memory, but would a Manchester United relegation surpass that as English football's greatest shock?

View Image Man Utd go into Sunday's clash in the relegation zone

Leicester winning the Premier League? You're being ridiculous. Well that was the line we all came out with until people actually thought this could happen.

‌



‌



And of course it did, the 5,000/1 shock remains etched in history as the Premier League's greatest ever shock. Having just escaped relegation the previous year, Claudio Ranieri led the Foxes to the title in one of English football's greatest moments.

‌



But at the opposite end of the table another great shock is building. Of course few expect Manchester United to actually go down, but their fortunes show no sign of improving.

‌



They have just one win so far - the joint least in the league. That victory came back in August over newly promoted Ipswich and they've rarely looked like winning again. Michael Carrick is desperately searching for answers - failing to find any in the coming weeks could see him chopped.

United remain the Premier League's most successful side, but they've fallen so far from those heights that some have joked relegation and a reset might actually help. Of course, it wouldn't, but if these results continue into Christmas then we're halfway through the campaign, and that is when the relegation picture becomes clearer.

Sports.title: Kai Rooney's strict diet he copied from dad Wayne and Man Utd wonderkid's cheat meal
Sports.content:
Kai Rooney's strict diet he copied from dad Wayne and Man Utd wonderkid's cheat meal

Manchester United and England legend Wayne Rooney's diet during his playing days has provided a blueprint for his son, Kai, in his burgeoning football career

View 2 Images Kai Rooney is following his father's footsteps in more ways than one (Image: JMEnternational/Getty Images)

Kai Rooney's pre-match diet is identical to what his father, Wayne, used to follow during his illustrious playing career. The Manchester United prospect, who turned 17 earlier this week, is hoping to follow in the footsteps of the Red Devils icon and make his mark on the professional scene.

‌



‌



The youngster is certainly putting his best foot forward on the pitch after his four-goal haul in a 6-0 victory over Burnley's U18's last week. He followed up his stunning showing with a goal in a 4-1 win over Blackburn Rovers four days later before being sent off when shown a second yellow card in the second half.

‌



Kai's productivity on the pitch is matched by his discipline regarding what he consumes to fuel his body. Like his father, the teenager follows a strict diet that includes eating chicken and pasta two days before a game, Mail Sport reports.

‌



He then switches to helpings of salmon, rice and a rice pudding the night before a match. The morning of a game sees Kai tuck into oatmeal with honey and protein powder, as per the Manchester Evening News.

While his dietary discipline has been praised by figures within the United academy, the 17-year-old allows himself a cheat meal on occasion. His favoured choice for a spot of indulgence is said to be the family's regular Chinese takeaway 'WowYauChow' in Altrincham.

‌



It was also revealed that the promising star's favourite dish is the crispy chilli beef. Alongside his focus on his career, Kai's off-the-pitch hobbies include cooking, and the forward is also fluent in Spanish.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Kai Rooney scored four times against Burnley (Image: Getty Images)

His rise through United's academy and his current standing within the club was featured on The Real Rooneys docu-series, which premiered on Disney+ last month. Wayne, 41, opened up about the role his family are playing in his son's development and the importance of hard work.

‌



The England legend said: "Kai is determined to be a football player. I try to give a little bit of advice when I can, really. I think what we are trying to do is help him be ready, whether that's for football or something else.

"He's at that point now in life where you think you know everything. You think you know more, and you're better than everyone. When people talk to me now, they still say the one thing they loved about me, more than anything, was my work rate.

"That's the biggest compliment you can get. This is just the start for Kai. He's the only one who can do it. It's got to come from inside of you."

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho's first act as Man Utd boss offers JJ Gabriel hope after transfer wish granted
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho's first act as Man Utd boss offers JJ Gabriel hope after transfer wish granted

JJ Gabriel has had a glimpse of what his future might look like away from Manchester United should he sign for Real Madrid

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel appears set to join Real Madrid (Image: Anthony Devlin/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Jose Mourinho's defence of his youth policy could see JJ Gabriel fast-tracked into senior football. The wantaway Manchester United wonderkid stunned the Premier League giants in September when requesting to leave the club and have his registration cancelled.

‌



The likes of Real Madrid, Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich all had interest in the 16-year-old, but it's the 15-time European champions who seem to have won the race for the promising youngster.

Gabriel is expected to sign for Mourinho's side in January on a long-term contract at the Santiago Bernabeu. The Athletic reports that the deal to acquire the forward - who is expected to play for Madrid's Castilla team - is subject to FIFA regulations and is reportedly advanced.

The teenager's desire to leave United is said to stem from his camp's belief that the club are not at the level of the European giants that have registered interest in his services. Gabriel's exclusion from the club's Champions League squad reportedly left his family disappointed and was a major factor in his decision to leave.

A speedy ascent to first-team football this season was a clear motivator for Gabriel, whose representatives requested that he feature for at least 20 minutes across United's matches against Sabah, Brighton and Bournemouth, according to the Manchester Evening News.

JJ Gabriel rejects PSG transfer offer as wantaway Man Utd wonderkid picks next club READ MORE :

The request was snubbed and eventually contributed to Gabriel's desire to seek pastures new. While Madrid is known for platforming world-class players rather than promising young talent, Gabriel could find hope under Mourinho, who once outlined his promotion of academy stars in his first press conference as United boss in 2016.

The Portuguese boss had been criticised for the lack of youth players that featured across his tenures at Chelsea, Inter Milan and his first stint at Madrid between 2010 and 2013.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho previously backed his record of promoting youth players (Image: Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

In true Mourinho fashion, he came prepared to challenge his critics as he claimed: "I have promoted 49 youth players from academies. If you want, I can give you that list." He then showed a list to the room and continued: "Two factors that are very important on these records, because sometimes you promote because you don’t have another chance or so many injuries, you have to bring them in.

"The second factor is when you are not playing for big targets, then it is easier to bring them up. My record with injuries is very low – even from the UEFA studies, there were many times the team with the least injuries in the whole of Europe was mine."

Mourinho then discussed the quality of the players he's promoted and the accolades they've earned at the highest level of the game. He added: "Last year, the only season of my career that I was not fighting for the title – every other season I was winning or finishing second, or finish third once but still fighting for the title.

"I still did 49 and some of them we are speaking about big names – players that today are Champions League winners, playing for national teams. Forty-nine is a lot. Once more – it’s one lie repeated many times. Sometimes it looks like it might be true but it is always true. Many of you… the names. If you want them, I’ll give them to you."

While JJ Gabriel is leaving United because of a lack of opportunities, Mourinho's words suggest he will be willing to give anyone a chance to prove themselves if they have the talent.

Sports.title: Jesus de Miguel: Tenerife to support star's one-year-old daughter after tragic death
Sports.content:
Jesus de Miguel: Tenerife to support star's one-year-old daughter after tragic death

Tenerife's chief executive has confirmed the Spanish second division club will financially support Jesus de Miguel's one-year-old daughter following his death earlier this week

View 2 Images Tenerife will support Jesus de Miguel's young daughter following his death (Image: CD TENERIFE/AFP via Getty Images)

The infant daughter of Jesus de Miguel will be financially supported following the striker's death, with the club's chief executive confirming she will be be looked after until she turns 18.

‌



‌



De Miguel tragically passed away this week at the age of 30 after an on-field collision with the Andorra FC goalkeeper, Jesus Owono, during a Spanish Segunda Division match.

‌



Monday's game was abandoned after De Miguel was taken to hospital, with the striker sadly succumbing to his injuries on Tuesday morning.

‌



In the aftermath of his passing, Antonio Manuel Porro Granados has confirmed to The Athletic that De Miguel's one-year old daughter will be supported financially until she becomes an adult.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“Our plan is to stand by the girl and make sure the entire Tenerife family supports her,” he said. “We want to be there for her at least until she reaches adulthood.

‌



“This is a commitment we have made at the initiative of our majority shareholder, Rayco Garcia, and one that we all fully support. It is a commitment that Tenerife, as a club, is making to the family and to their daughter, Carla.

“We will provide the maximum possible support in every respect, beyond what we are legally obliged to provide. We are also exploring other ways of increasing the financial support, so that, at least in material terms, the circumstances do not affect their lives quite so much — although, of course, it is impossible for them not to have an impact.”

‌



De Miguel was laid to rest in in his parents' hometown of Navahermosa, Spain on Thursday.

View 2 Images Tributes have been paid to De Miguel all across the globe (Image: Pablo Blazquez Dominguez/Getty Images)

‌



The striker's agent, Manuel Hernandez, issued a statement on behalf of De Miguel's family which read: “Thank you for loving him, for remembering him and for being with us.

“We cannot find enough words to thank you for every message, every phone call and every gesture of affection we are receiving.

‌



“Feeling such affection for Jesus and seeing the mark he has left on so many people is something we will always carry with us.

“Jesus leaves a void that is impossible to fill, but also cherished memories for all of us who were fortunate enough to share our lives with him.”

Sports.title: Norris wins wet Sao Paulo GP as Mercedes seal constructors' title
Sports.content:
McLaren's Lando Norris recovered from a poor start to claim a dominant victory in a wet Sao Paulo Grand Prix that saw Mercedes seal the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship.

Max Verstappen produced a signature stunning drive in the wet to come from 21st on the grid to finish second, with his team-mate Isack Hadjar completing a double-podium for Red Bull.

Newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli had looked on course for victory after taking the lead at the start but ultimately had to settle for fifth behind his team-mate George Russell, which was more than enough for Mercedes to establish an unassailable lead over Ferrari in the constructors' standings with three rounds to spare.

Norris lost the lead to Antonelli at the start as the pole-sitter dropped to third on the opening lap, but a mid-race switch to slick tyres as the track dried swung the race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Two overtakes in two corners for Max Verstappen to continue his climb.

Antonelli had led by six seconds before the stops but delayed pitting by a lap and then struggled with his tyre temperatures, spinning off to give the lead back to Norris before also being overtaken by both Red Bulls.

The rain returned in the closing stages to force the entire field back onto intermediate tyres, but Norris handled the conditions masterfully to take the chequered flag just short of 15 seconds clear of Verstappen.

More to follow...

Sports.title: Borthwick and Itoje reject reports of England squad rift
Sports.content:
England head coach Steve Borthwick and captain Maro Itoje have rejected claims made in a newspaper article this week of a squad rift, saying it "does not represent the environment" they recognise.

Speaking to media following Sunday's dominant 45-22 Nations Championship victory over Australia at Allianz Stadium Twickenham, Borthwick addressed the article for the first time since its publication on Friday.

Within it, The Times reported that some England players lost faith in Borthwick during a summer campaign which included a 45-21 defeat to world champions South Africa and a nervy win over Argentina.

It is alleged players objected to Borthwick's treatment of them, that he was involved in a training ground bust-up with Ellis Genge and that they wanted RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney - who this week unequivocally backed the head coach - to listen to their gripes.

Speaking to Sky Sports on Friday, Jamie George said England's players were "hurt" by the report, calling the timing of the article "shocking."

On Sunday, Borthwick said: "It's not an environment I recognise. It's not an accurate reflection.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie George told Sky Sports England's players were hurt by the 'shocking' report of a rift with Borthwick

"What I will say is that in the last couple of days, a number of my predecessors have reached out and contacted me, and they certainly did.

"They're always supportive, and I won't name who they are, but a number of them reached out to me and the basic gist of it is: 'Been there, got the t-shirt, focus on the rugby', and that's it.

"As England head coach you get that t-shirt, and what you do is focus on the rugby and that's what I've done this week, that's what the players have done, that's what every member of the staff around the players has done.

"That's what we've done this week."

Image: Henry Pollock starred off the bench for England out of position on the wing as they comprehensively beat Australia

Itoje: We have full support in Borthwick

Sat next to Borthwick at Sunday's post-match press conference, England skipper Itoje gave a passionate defence of his head coach.

"From a player's point of view, we have full support in Steve," he said.

"I've had the privilege of Steve being my coach since 2016, with a little gap when he was in his Leicester years. That's not the man I recognise. The article doesn't represent the environment I recognise, and I think if you speak to players over his coaching career they will say a different story.

"Particularly, often you think about players from other countries. If you speak to some of those guys from the 2017 Lions tour [to New Zealand], they'll tell you about the impact Steve had on them.

"Those guys aren't English I'm talking about, I'm talking about the Irish guys, I'm talking about the Welsh guys who he had the pleasure of coaching and having an influence on.

Image: Maro Itoje gave a passionate defence of Borthwick on Sunday post-match

"Just from a player's point of view, as always there's things that we want to get right, there's things that we try and put on the field, sometimes for whatever reason it doesn't quite click. I think often too much criticism is attached to the coach.

"Whereas, no matter how well Steve coaches us, we as players are the ones on the field. We as players are the ones who have to perform and put it right.

"There's been times where we haven't quite done that which has put a bit of pressure on him. I'm delighted that today we were able to get the win. He's a world-class coach and we're lucky to have him."

What's next?

For England, they next face Japan in their second Nations Championship Test of the autumn at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on Saturday November 14 (4.40pm kick-off).

Sports.title: Pollock stars out of position as England power past Australia
Sports.content:
Nations Championship - England 45-22 Australia: Henry Pollock stars out of position on the wing in morale-boosting Twickenham victory

Henry Pollock starred off the bench for England out of position on the wing, scoring twice in victory over Australia

Henry Pollock impressed out of position as Steve Borthwick's England claimed a much-needed, morale-boosting 45-22 victory over Australia in the Nations Championship at Allianz Stadium.

In a week when Borthwick came under intense scrutiny following newspaper reports of a summer rift with his England squad - claims denied by Jamie George to Sky Sports - England responded with a seven-try performance and record point haul against Australia.

Hooker George, back-row Ollie Chessum, tighthead Joe Heyes and scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet all crossed, while replacements Henry Pollock (twice) and Ben Spencer also got on the scoresheet.

Pollock, ordinarily a back-row forward, replaced the stricken Immanuel Feyi-Waboso (ankle) at half-time, featuring on the wing for 40 minutes and hardly looking out of place.

England 45-22 Australia - Score summary England - Tries: George (8), Chessum (26), Heyes (33), van Poortvliet (43), Pollock (55,57), Spencer (76). Cons: F Smith (27,34,43,58,77). Australia - Tries: Jorgensen (40), Daugunu (62), Williams (74). Cons: Lonergan (41), Donaldson (75). Pens: Lonergan (12).

Fin Smith added five conversions and ran England's attack well from fly-half, while Australia scored via wings Max Jorgensen and Filipo Daugunu, and back-row Jeremy Williams, but struggled for parity in terms of the power stakes.

The Wallabies also suffered a costly blow when loosehead prop Angus Bell was sin-binned in the first half, becoming the first player penalised for a hip-drop tackle since World Rugby outlawed it this month.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

England looked to have scored less than two minutes in when Feyi-Waboso scorched through, but the TMO soon showed replays of a forward pass from Ben Curry to Chessum earlier in the move to chalk off the score.

The sensational Immanuel Feyi-Waboso thought he'd scored in the second minute, but the try was chalked off for an earlier knock-on

England kept up their early intensity, producing a choke-tackle maul turnover and attacking off the consequent midfield scrum with Feyi-Waboso central again, but that good work was undone by lock Alex Coles when he flew off his feet at a breakdown in the Wallabies' 22 to give away a penalty.

The hosts were soon back into the 22 when Australia coughed up a soft obstruction penalty under a high ball - Smith producing a fine kick into the corner - and from the subsequent maul, George was on hand to touch down.

Smith hit the post with the conversion, and soon Australia were onto the scoreboard via the boot of Ryan Lonergan, who split the uprights with a penalty after the England backline were caught offside off a lineout.

Ryan Lonergan kicked Australia's first points of the contest with a penalty

Superb work from Maro Itoje in the Australia 22 to charge down Lonergan then forced a knock-on, earning England a scrum to attack off within the Australia 22, but Heyes was penalised for an early push to see the chance blown.

Errors continued to flow from the hosts as Feyi-Waboso spilled possession on the run in the 22, George was pinged for crooked throw and a scrum penalty was shipped too.

Mistakes then proved contagious when Australia hooker Billy Pollard was pinged for a crooked throw himself in the England half, rendering the contest firmly top-start.

Feyi-Waboso soon displayed his pace and dynamism again at the end of a nice backline move, but England lost the ball again in the 22.

Yet, Australia just couldn't handle Feyi-Waboso and the pressure finally told as the wing made a burst down the opposite wing, and once England chipped the ball wide, Chessum was too powerful for Jorgensen to score.

Ollie Chessum powered over in the corner for England's second try after more good work from Feyi-Waboso

Smith converted well for a 12-3 lead, before Itoje executed a strip for another chance - despite a couple of forward passes being missed - but a George Furbank neck-roll in the 22 saw the Wallabies clear.

Australia were then reduced to 14, however, as the TMO showed images of a Bell hip-drop tackle on Feyi-Waboso.

Henry Slade kicked to corner, and the maul did the trick again as Heyes wrestled the ball out and dived over for England's third of the half.

Joe Heyes scored England's third try as a rolling maul did damage again

Two minutes before half-time, Freddie Steward should have scored England's fourth but knocked on a bouncing ball in-goal after winning the chase.

Instead, the visitors notched a try out of nothing in the final minute before half-time; Jorgenson intercepting a telegraphed Van Poortvliet pass near halfway and showing his pace to sprint over.

Wing Max Jorgensen scored an intercept try before half-time, but the Wallabies were firmly second best

That left the half-time deficit a nine-point one, but just before Bell was due to re-emerge from his sin-bin period, England scored their fourth three minutes into the second half: Pollock carrying brilliantly down the left to start things, and Steward doing fabulous work down the right before finding Van Poorvliet with a long pass.

Australia threatened a try back in response when centre Isaac Henry cut through England and broke to near the 22, but the Wallabies were pinged for sealing off.

Henry then made a big error in skewing a kick out on the full as the Wallabies sought to attack from deep, and England did not let up until they had a fifth try as Pollock finished out wide after Australia had been pushed back in tight carries near the try-line.

Pollock finished out wide for England's fifth try, taking the Test firmly away from Australia

Within two minutes, Pollock was celebrating again, as another rapid backline attack well-orchestrated by Smith saw the makeshift wing finish with swagger down the right.

Pollock made it two tries in as many minutes with his second and England's sixth

Past the hour mark, the Wallabies did score again as Daugunu finished a flowing move in the left corner, but it went unconverted when Lonergan couldn't land the tough kick.

Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii passed up a certain try when he shipped the ball to Jorgensen instead of finishing, but Australia scored from the resulting England lineout in any case - the hosts sloppy near their own try-line and Williams finishing.

England soon forgot about that mistake, though, as Spencer intercepted a Daugunu offload to race into the corner and round off a big victory.

Replacement scrum-half Ben Spencer rounded off the scoring down the right wing

Pollock: Coaches wouldn't put me on wing if they didn't think I could do it

"The biggest thing is the rugby stuff. Pleasure and privilege. For me, the biggest thing is going out there and showcasing myself and the growth of this team throughout the summer and into the autumn.

"I love playing for this team, I love playing back at home. We spoke about being back at home and creating some energy around that.

"The coaches wouldn't put me on the wing if they knew I couldn't do anything there, so the big thing for me is going out there and being as confident as I can.

"If I mess up, I'm playing a new position, I'm going to make some new learnings from it. If there's any young kids out there, playing new positions, just take each step as it comes.

"I made a few mistakes today, but the boys outside me, like Slade in the corner, backed me up. That just made my job so much easier.

"I disagree with that [versatility potentially working agasint him], versatility is a massive thing. Today, my role was coming on in the second half and being a winger. I trust the coaches and the team, whatever they need to do for that.

"It showed in that last 30-40 minutes, the bench came on and did their thing. That shows where we're at as a squad."

George 'proud' of team-mates after tough week

England's Jamie George told ITV Sport:

"I wonder where that's come from? [big try celebration]

"It's [newspaper reports] been a distraction. I'm so unbelievably proud of how the team looked after each other, stepped up for each other, and we are a tight team regardless.

"As I said, it probably brought us even tighter and being back at Allianz Stadium is just unbelievable."

Itoje 'over the moon' on England return

England captain Maro Itoje said to ITV Sport:

"I am over the moon. This week has been great, great for me personally to be back in camp.

"I think we're starting to show what we can do, we've got a very talented team, and it's now time for us to put it all together.

"Sometimes when you have time away from the team, as I did in the summer, it makes you appreciate what playing for England is all about.

"When I stood out there for the National Anthems, it gave me goosebumps. These are the games I want to be a part of."

Maro Itoje returned for England for the first time since the Six Nations in March

Wilson: We can't be waiting until last 15 minutes to start playing

Australia captain Harry Wilson told ITV Sport:

"England put us under the pump, we didn't get too much ball in the first-half. We didn't get too many A-zone entries and England were the better team today.

"They fronted up physically, put us under the pump. Our defence wasn't physical enough in slowing the ball down.

"I feel like we were playing from behind there, so, credit to England.

"A lot of our issues might be mindset. We've got seven days to take some feedback from this game and make sure we're a lot better.

Australia captain Harry Wilson cut a downbeat figure at full-time

"I know Scotland are a really good team, and we have to be ready for it, and we have to be ready for these harsh lessons.

"We know when we hold the ball for long phases and play our style of footy, we can cut teams up. But we can't be waiting for the last 15 minutes to do it."

What's next?

For England, they next face Japan in their second Nations Championship Test of the autumn at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on Saturday November 14 (4.40pm kick-off).

England's Nations Championship fixtures and results South Africa 45-21 England July 4 Fiji 8-73 England July 11 Argentina 24-31 England July 18 England 45-22 Australia November 8 England vs Japan Saturday, November 14 (4.40pm) England vs New Zealand Saturday, November 21 (2.10pm)

Australia travel to face Scotland at Murrayfield for their next Test, on Sunday November 15 (3.10pm kick-off).

Sports.title: Hits and misses: Alisson back to his best while Chelsea go back to square one
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Crystal Palace’s match against Liverpool in the Premier League.

Liverpool hit three at Palace, with three £100m+ players - Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and, with an assist, Bradley Barcola - involved in the goals. But it was their goalkeeper Alisson who was Liverpool's best performer.

Crystal Palace will be so frustrated because on another day, the narrative could have swung their way. But the brilliant Brazilian delivered in key moments in the game.

His save from Daichi Kamada's volley was an exceptional reaction stop. Two minutes later Liverpool took the lead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Alisson's stunning save to deny Daichi Kamada

Alisson was then at full stretch to push away Adam Wharton's header to ensure Liverpool went into the break with the advantage. And on 77 minutes, with the score 2-0, he prevented Yeremy Pino from setting up a grandstand finish by shutting down the angle to save the one-on-one.

Alisson may have had fortune with Pino hitting the bar when he was beaten early in the contest and he lost out on a clean sheet due to a controversial late Eddie Nketiah penalty, but in between he reminded everyone why he has been the Premier League's standout goalkeeper since his arrival in 2018.

Peter Smith

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Sunderland and Chelsea.

Just when you think Chelsea are about to change and show some form, they go right back to square one.

They went into the last international break on the back of a damning 3-0 defeat to Brentford, where without star man Joao Pedro, they were bullied, outfought and deservedly beaten by the Bees.

Sunderland, who started the day bottom of the table, are now another team in red and white who have overpowered them to three points - right in time for the next international break.

In the first half, Chelsea lost 63 per cent of the duels as Brian Brobbey wreaked havoc on the Blues backline. This time it was Levi Colwill who was showing defensive frailties as he was hooked off at half-time, with Wesley Fofana the culprit of some unpunished blunders against Manchester United last week.

Ultimately, this match showed that Chelsea don't have enough defensive solidity and the injured Pedro is their most important player. But we've known that for weeks. More concerningly, Xabi Alonso insists his Chelsea team were "not bullied" despite the eye test and the data backing it up.

The first part of solving these problems is recognising they exist. Until that changes, Chelsea will always end up going the same places.

They are now outside the top four, and with Everton and Bournemouth picking up form behind them, they are drifting towards the middle of the table again.

Sam Blitz

Image: Brian Brobbey was a livewire as Sunderland deservedly beat Chelsea

While Sunderland's defensive solidity to beat Chelsea owed everything to a team effort, there was no-one taking the credit for their best attacking performance of the season away from Brian Brobbey.

Even ignoring the big Dutchman's role in winning the penalty for Sunderland's winner, it was testament to his unrivalled threat that Xabi Alonso sacrificed Moises Caicedo from his midfield to shackle the forward at half-time.

Brobbey is unparalleled in what he does across the Premier League. He has held the ball up 28 times this season, comfortably more than anyone else despite missing two of the 10 matchdays with injury.

He is the only player to have completed 10 or more hold-ups where more than half have retained possession - and he keeps it almost 70 per cent of the time.

Sunderland fans were delighted to see the 24-year-old sign a new deal on Wearside earlier this week despite only scoring in one game this season. But his game is about so much more.

Roy Keane described his bustling run to win Sunday's penalty as "brilliant centre-forward play". Chris Sutton said he "bullied" Fofana. That feels a fitting description.

Sunderland's first concern for their survival hopes must be to keep up their rediscovered defensive compactness to stop leaking goals at an unsustainable rate.

But at the other end, so long as Brobbey is fit and firing they will be a nuisance for anyone.

Ron Walker

Crystal Palace delivered arguably their best performance of the season against Liverpool but still lost 3-1. Pierre Sage has not lost the players but may well lose his job.

Bottom of the table after 10 games and, alarmingly, Palace have conceded more goals at this stage of a league season than they have for 25 years.

Sage's porous defence have shipped 24 goals in the Premier League. That is what will cost him his job if, indeed, he is to be sacked.

Palace came close to scoring on three occasions in the first half against Liverpool only to be undone by the simplest of free-kick routines. That is the sixth non-penalty set piece Palace have conceded this season.

It is a pattern that they cannot afford to keep repeating.

Zinny Boswell

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Brighton and Brentford.

Across their first five Premier League seasons combined - 190 games - Brentford players were shown a total of eight red cards. With 10 games gone in 2026/27, they have already been shown three - and they have all come in their last three games.

Vitaly Janelt's late dismissal at home to Liverpool on October 17 was the result of a second booking. There's nothing really to discuss in that case.

But earlier in that game, Yehor Yarmoliuk was shown a straight red, after a VAR review, for headbutting Jeremy Jacquet. "I do think they were cute, clever - but Yarmo needs to do better," said Bees boss Keith Andrews afterwards.

Brentford were leading at that point and looking good value for their advantage, but the red changed the game and they conspired to lose 2-1.

Against Brighton, they were 1-0 down when Igor Thiago was shown a straight red after catching Chema in the face with his arm, splitting his opponent's lip in the process. Again, referee Michael Oliver was sent to the monitor, where he upgraded his original decision - and again, there was no way back for Brentford.

For a team that has a tendency to drop points from winning positions, this recent lack of discipline is another thing hindering their positive start.

Dan Long

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Ipswich Town’s match against Bournemouth in the Premier League.

European football is supposed to come with a health warning. More games, more travel, more tired legs and, supposedly, a dip in domestic performance. Somebody should tell Bournemouth.

They have played nine times in the last month and have won eight of their last eight. That is an extraordinary return given the relentless schedule.

There is clearly something working brilliantly behind the scenes at the club. Whether it is the conditioning, recovery methods, squad management or simply the infectious culture the players have, Bournemouth look anything but a team running on empty.

Ipswich were the latest to discover that. The 2-1 scoreline was flattering to Gary O'Neil's side, who were second best for large spells and struggled to live with Bournemouth's intensity. The gulf in energy levels was striking.

Bournemouth are not just surviving the extra workload, they are thriving on it.

Lewis Jones

Ipswich have a Enciso problem. More specifically, they have a problem when Enciso is thwarted.

The Paraguayan has become the creative heartbeat of the newly-promoted team but Bournemouth exposed the danger of building so much of an attacking gameplan around one player. Shut off the supply line to Enciso and suddenly Ipswich look rather ordinary. There was precious little invention elsewhere.

Despite trailing for almost the entire contest, Ipswich mustered just 0.30 expected goals from open play. Even more damning, they failed to register a single touch inside the Bournemouth penalty area in the second half until Clarke converted his penalty in the 73rd minute.

That is quite some attacking impotence when you are chasing a game.

Ipswich cannot afford to be so predictable.

Premier League opponents will have watched that performance closely. The blueprint is out there. Ipswich need a plan B.

Lewis Jones
