Sports.title: Australia reach World Cup final as Samoa fume at decisions
Sports.content:
Men's Rugby League World Cup 2026: Australia to face New Zealand in final as Samoa fume at decisions

Australia ran in eight tries as they beat Samoa

Australia are one win away from a record-extending 13th men's Rugby League World Cup title after beating Samoa 44-12 in a fractious clash to secure a showdown with New Zealand in next weekend's Brisbane final.

The Kangaroos, like their female counterparts, are pursuing a fourth consecutive title and if they do defeat their Antipodean rivals on November 15, they will earn a 10th World Cup triumph in their last 11 attempts, stretching back to 1975.

Sunday's second semi-final - New Zealand defeated Tonga 34-10 in the first semi on Saturday - was a repeat of the World Cup final in 2022 at Old Trafford in Manchester, which Australia won 30-10 to land a third title in succession.

Samoa felt aggrieved by refereeing decisions during their defeat in Sydney

In the rematch in Sydney four years later - preceded by Samoa's Siva Tau war dance in which Brian To'o put his forehead towards the face of Australia's former Samoa prop Tino Fa'asuamaleaui - the away side were left fuming at some questionable refereeing calls.

Reece Walsh registered a hat-trick during Australia's eight-try victory as they pounced on errors and ill-discipline from Samoa.

Tom Dearden breached the Samoa defence for the converted try that put Australia 6-2 up in the eighth minute after the tourists had gone 2-0 to the good following a fifth-minute penalty.

Australia never trailed after that, with Jacob Preston, Tom Trbojevic, Walsh and Bradman Best also crossing before half-time to give their side a 26-2 lead - Walsh doing so after a Samoa try was chalked off for an alleged knock-on - and Spencer Leniu sin-binned for their opponents after remonstrating with referee Adam Gee.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Early in the second period, an error from Walsh allowed Stephen Crichton to score for Samoa, only for Walsh to atone with his second try of the game, profiting from a mistake by Ronald Volkman.

Samoa did not wilt and got on the scoreboard again when Izack Tago touched down in the left corner but when Walsh sealed his hat-trick to leave the score 38-12 just shy of the 70-minute mark, the game was all but done.

Samoa had a second try of the night ruled out due to contact between Francis Manuleleua and Liam Martin, a decision that once again left them fuming, before Australia extended their lead when Jack Bostock rushed in down the left.

Cameron Munster chipped in with six conversions for Australia, who rallied from an underwhelming group-stage campaign.

The only side to deny Australia the title since they lost to Great Britain in the 1972 final are New Zealand, with the Kiwis winning 34-20 in the 2008 final in Brisbane.

Sports.title: Dorgu rescues point for Manchester United in eight-goal thriller against Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Does this late, late comeback draw keep Michael Carrick in his job? He urged United to back Tuesday’s breathless Roma comeback victory by building momentum and they did – kind of, by avoiding defeat.

Patrick Dorgu’s 96th-minute equaliser went off his head and in: this made it 4-4 to follow Joshua Zirkzee’s own added-time finish as Aston Villa were somehow pulled back by Carrick’s chaotic unit.

Chris Kavanagh soon blew the whistle for time but not before further bedlam as the referee sent off what appeared to be a member of Villa’s technical staff.

Before all of this Senne Lammens, twice, Diogo Dalot and Leny Yoro were three of United’s rearguard culpable for all Villa goals. What can any manager do if a trio of players shoot the team in both feet with the schoolboy defending that allowed Alysson to score a barely credible 48 seconds in, and Nicolas Jackson to net after four minutes.

Both these goals were Lammens’ fault. Then, after a rousing Roma-like first-half comeback to make it 2-2 via Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans, Dalot’s chop on Alysson two minutes into the second period conceded the season’s clearest penalty, which John McGinn scored.

Further farce followed via Yoro’s own what are you doing moment: a flying header of McGinn’s free-kick at his goal that led to Leon Goretzka’s fourth for Unai Emery’s impressive team.

The bottom line is United have still won three games all season, from 15, and only one of these in the league, back on 30 August, when Ipswich were beaten 5-2.

Carrick may well cling on because Jason Wilcox has been reluctant to fire the manager so far. Yet United enter the international break in a bewildering 18th place, so who knows?

For two minutes 46 seconds Carrick’s men were actually bottom earlier in the day when Sunderland went 1-0 up against Chelsea and Liverpool scored at Crystal Palace.

The toxicity towards the owners from fans was summed up in the message, held up in letters and displayed in the Stretford End, to the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe: “Your funeral not ours, sell up”

Villa’s lighting start was uber-professional from them, dismally-amateurish from United: the ball arrived at Alysson and his shot went through Lammens’ legs.

United’s No 1 was to blame again when Alysson’s effort this time went to Lammens’ left, and instead of pushing the ball away he teed it up for Jackson, who smashed in.

The joke beforehand was that even United could not lose by the 10-goal margin needed to end the day in 20th place. The joke now was that United were in “hold my beer” territory.

Could United get a grip, somehow, and retrieve a two-goal deficit, as they did versus Roma? Cunha, who netted twice against the Italians, made a barnstorming charge into the right of Villa’s area that caused Boubacar Kamara to upend him. Kavanagh awarded the penalty and so Fernandes, as he did versus Roma, had the chance from the spot to pull a first goal back.

Up the captain stepped and a hop-and-skip later the ball was passed by Zion Suzuki’s left, the keeper guessing the wrong way. This was 16 minutes in and the chaos that is Carrick’s United took over as Villa were pummeled by the red blur that came at relentlessly.

United were all they had not been in the calamitous opening four minutes: slick, fast, cut-throat, in-charge. A Fernandes cross-shot troubled Suzuki. Villa’s No 1 leaped left and cat-like to parry Cunha’s curler. Youri Tielemans forced a corner, as did Fernandes via a McGinn up-raised leg.

This was a 20-minute passage that was only finally broken when Villa escaped their half, McGinn dropping a free-kick on to Pau Torres, whose header sailed over.

View image in fullscreen Leon Goretzka bundles home Aston Villa’s fourth goal from close range. Photograph: Darren Staples/AFP/Getty Images

United continued on. Their energy impressed and it said they still believed – in rescuing the match, and Carrick. Hard evidence arrived with Tielemans’ equaliser as Villa folded precisely as United had. Noussair Mazraoui’s cross came to the Belgian and he beat Suzuki. So, at the interval, the contest was all square after a breakneck opening half.

Quick Guide How do I 

What might the second period conjure? The answer: Dalot’s feeble trip on Alysson, as Carrick was a picture of despair. McGinn converted, to Lammens’ right, and a topsy-turvy affair stood at 3-2 to Villa.

Aston Villa deserved credit for the response. And now they scored due to more slapstick United play. McGinn’s free-kick floated in from the right, Yoro’s header forced Lammens to tip the ball on to the frame of the goal: it rebounded and Goretzka bundled in.

Carrick had not found a place for Shea Lacey despite his impact as a substitute against Roma but on 65 minutes he did, the youngster joined by Dorgu and Mason Mount in a triple change.

Tielemans, Amad Diallo and Dalot came off and the Portuguese seemed to be jeered: if so a rare occurrence here for United to boo one of their own. Now came Zirkzee and Dorgu’s goals that grabbed a point for United.

“Sacked in the morning” had been the Villa support’s taunt of Carrick. We wait to see if this is prescient. The smart money would say not.

Sports.title: Le Fée’s penalty stuns Chelsea and breathes life into defiant Sunderland
Sports.content:
A lot can change in five‑and‑a‑half months, but as an early winter chill descended on Wearside last week – both meteorologically and ­metaphorically – Sunderland were determined that some things should remain the same. Just as they had beaten Chelsea on the final day of last season to ensure European qualification for the first time in 53 years, they did so again on Sunday to lift themselves off the bottom of the Premier League.

The Sunderland performance was certainly familiar to their head coach, Régis Le Bris – “the identity, the intensity, the togetherness, the way we managed the game” – on the way to three crucial points.

Ultimately a patched-up defence, ­without the injured Dan Ballard and the banned Omar Alderete, kept ­Chelsea at enough distance to allow Robin Roefs a tranquil ­afternoon amid the tumult. Chelsea may be ­developing into a ­chaotic must‑watch under Xabi Alonso but they were ­subdued here and have fallen out of the top four. “We didn’t produce enough to deserve to win,” Alonso said. “We lacked a bit of patience and creativity.”

Margins were paper-thin in a game decided by two first-half penalty calls, the first not awarded to Chelsea after Luke O’Nien’s clumsy challenge on Cole Palmer, deemed after vide assistant referee consideration to be fractionally outside the area, and the second given to the hosts by Jarred Gillett after Levi Colwill brought down the ebullient Brian Brobbey; the defender argued, not without justification, that the Dutch striker had a handful of his shirt too but the award stood.

Alonso, as ever, made no excuses, ­focusing not on the officiating and more on how he was “not happy with how we defended that situation”. Enzo Le Fée had been equally unequi­vocal just beyond the half‑hour, sending Mike Penders the wrong way and dispatching into the goalkeeper’s bottom-right corner for the game’s only goal.

Europe may be a blessing for Sunderland but the full-time mood had been bleak after the latest alarming performance in the home defeat against Dinamo Zagreb on Thursday. It had felt like a season watershed and only the captain, Granit Xhaka, Thomas Meunier and Roefs survived the cull here. That the talismanic Xhaka, the subject of strong summer interest from his former coach Alonso, had his afternoon truncated by injury after less than three ­minutes, felt like yet more of the ill fortune dogging Sunderland.

View image in fullscreen Sunderland’s Reinildo Mandava attempts to wrestle the ball away from Morgan Rogers. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/Sportsphoto

There was no feeling sorry for themselves, though. With this the start of a challenging quartet of fixtures leading into the Tyne‑Wear derby next month, it felt like this match had to be attacked to prevent an early-season hiccup turning into a full mid‑season tangle with relegation trouble. And Chelsea were greeted with determination and ­aggression, with Xhaka’s withdrawal not ­blowing that plan off course. Two zesty ­incisions by Chemsdine Talbi in the opening quarter-hour, in his first ­Premier League start this season, caused Alonso’s men flutters, the first leading to a blocked Trai Hume shot and the second presenting Brobbey with a clear opening that he would have expected to convert.

The passion was there, the precision maybe less so. O’Nien’s challenge on Palmer elicited a penalty appeal that did not end up being costly after the VAR check and Morgan Rogers headed wide from a Marco Palestra cross, but Chelsea could not capitalise on any potential home nerves. If anyone was prone to belated Halloween frights it was the Blues, particularly at the hands of Brobbey, who led the line with enormous presence. He took on and beat the last man Wesley Fofana before steering his shot just too high, past Penders’ near post, and then won the penalty that led to Le Fée’s winner. “He is stoppable,” Alonso said, “but only when you defend better than we did.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Such was Chelsea’s bluntness in the first 45 that the coach opted for not just a substitution but a reshuffle at the break, with Estêvão replacing the injured Colwill, beefing up the attack with Moisés Caicedo slotting into the defence. Sunderland continued to fight tooth and nail in a game that threatened occasionally to bubble over. Meunier was booked for a late tackle on Caicedo and shortly afterwards Brobbey was cautioned for wrestling Roméo Lavia to the ground, a continuation of an ongoing feud between the pair. When he was substituted, spent, for the ­enduringly ­popular Wilson Isidor halfway through the second half Chelsea must have breathed a sigh of relief.

Estêvão made one burst through the middle on to a Rogers pass but Reinildo Mandava stepped across to snuff out the opportunity. Yet even with little possession Sunderland looked sharper. A ball broke for Isidor after Chelsea failed to clear Le Fée’s through ball, Penders saving and the rebound not breaking for the Frenchman before Pep Chavarría cleared.

As the last 10 minutes approached Alonso sent on Geovany Quenda for Chavarría, and the young winger finally conjured a goal attempt worthy of the description, fizzing a shot just wide of Roefs’s far post via deflection. Talbi, finishing as he started, pinged one just wide from distance on the break as the home side still looked more likely, even with a third of possession. Sunderland had rewarded their crowd’s vociferous faith.

Sports.title: Wirtz provides quality to seal Liverpool win over lacklustre Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
It was the moment when Liverpool knew they would win here in south London and so move on from the Premier League loss to Arsenal at Anfield last Sunday and the one in midweek at Fenerbahce in the Champions League.

Florian Wirtz had timed his run as Liverpool broke up the right and Bradley Barcola’s low pull back was made to measure. Wirtz had to take it on first time and it was a test of his technique under pressure. He never looked like failing it, not least because smoothness in this area is his calling card. Liverpool were 2-0 up, Alexis Mac Allister having headed them in front towards the end of the first half, and all you could hear was the eruption of delight in the away supporters’ enclosure.

In the Crystal Palace seats there was silence and it seemed to go on for an age. The atmosphere inside this stadium has been diminished since the Holmesdale Fanatics stopped their activities during matches in protest over the general treatment of fans by the club. There was no rallying cry from the stands. Only resignation. Acceptance. There were 54 minutes on the clock but they knew as well as everybody else that this was done.

Palace were good in the first half, Jeremy Pino their standout performer. What a lovely player he is to watch. Pino rattled the crossbar and there were other moments when his team threatened. After the Wirtz goal, there was next to nothing from them, only a Pino effort after a quick break that Alisson blocked.

Liverpool eased home and it was no surprise when Alexander Isak glossed the scoreline towards the end. When he smashed home from Wirtz’s touch, it was the prompt for thousands of Palace supporters to make for the exits. Their club is in a parlous position. It was a fourth league defeat on the spin; a late penalty from Eddie Nketiah, on as a substitute, no consolation, except to note that it was their first goal during the mini-run.

There was no anger, no boos for the players at full-time. And there does not appear to be any appetite for the manager, Pierre Sage, to be dismissed. The problems are not all of his making; they are more down to the recruitment department. The absence of Ismaïla Sarr through injury has been a hammer blow.

Liverpool had been careless against Fenerbahce, especially on the concessions. “Cheap, messy goals,” Andoni Iraola said. They could afford to lose that one, having won all three of their opening Champions League matches and yet the fact it added up to successive defeats changed the temperature for them here. Three in a row would have lit up the phone-in lines. They were wobbly at times in the first half but they were on their way when Mac Allister profited from the generosity of the league’s worst defence. It all feels extremely gloomy for Palace.

Iraola, who was a target for Palace before he chose Liverpool at the end of last season, picked the XI that most people expected, Dominik Szoboszlai restored to the midfield from the Arsenal game; it was as strong as Liverpool could be. They took a grip on possession, pressing on to the front foot at the outset. The big question concerned whether they could get into areas to really hurt Palace, particularly when Sage’s team sat deep out of possession.

View image in fullscreen Alexander Isak scores Liverpool’s third goal in the 89th minute. Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/Reuters

Liverpool began with a flurry. They took shots from distance. Barcola wanted a penalty after a nudge in his back from Oscar Mingueza; there was not enough in it. In a sign of things to come, Mac Allister darted for the near post on a Szoboszlai free-kick and flashed a header wide. There was the moment when Cody Gakpo volleyed across the face of goal only there was nobody there.

Palace stabilised. They started to push and it came to feel as though Liverpool might be more dangerous in open play on the counter if the action became stretched. When they broke with numbers in the 26th minute, Palace were indebted to Adam Wharton for a saving challenge on Isak after Wirtz had pulled back from the right.

Palace had almost taken the lead by then. It was their first forward thrust and Tyrick Mitchell played the final pass, clubbed in low from the left. Pino did well to bring it under his spell and the shot was vicious, the connection so pure. It flew over Alisson and crashed against the crossbar.

Palace did not deserve to trail at the interval. They threatened up the left through Mitchell and Pino. Jørgen Strand Larsen had a goal ruled out for offside after a Pino shot had come off Daichi Kamada. The Japan midfielder was also denied by Alisson after catching a volley so sweetly. The cross was supplied by Mitchell and it was a fine reflex save. After the Mac Allister goal, Wharton had Alisson scrambling to touch behind after he stretched to reach a Pino ball in.

Quick Guide How do I 

Barcola had blazed a volley high when unmarked and well-placed from a deep Szoboszlai cross just before the Mac Allister goal and it did not feel as though it was coming for Liverpool. There was fury among the Palace support because they did not feel that the referee, Tony Harrington, ought to have penalised Jefferson Lerma for a foul on Gakpo.

It was a soft award but the decision was right. It did not excuse Palace’s inability to defend the Szoboszlai set piece. Mac Allister darted for the near post and it was just too easy for him to direct the header. Liverpool might have scored from yet another Szoboszlai free-kick in first-half stoppage time only Ronald Araujo could not properly reach a Jérémy Jacquet flick.

Palace felt the belief crumble after the Wirtz goal and it became a gentle slide towards the inevitable. Liverpool have a tonic.

Sports.title: Russo on target again as double fires under-pressure Arsenal to vital WSL win at Liverpool
Sports.content:
If a good striker can always get their team out of a hole, Alessia Russo is doing her best to drag Arsenal out of a deep chasm of uncertainty. Her two goals gave the ­under‑pressure Arsenal head coach, Renée Slegers, some brief respite with a much-needed, albeit still rather unconvincing victory.

Russo’s double took her impressive recent tally to seven goals in her past four appearances. Her goals were priceless for an Arsenal team who arrived on Merseyside with just one win in their previous seven Women’s Super League games. They will be relieved to have won after Liverpool posed plenty of problems and the hosts were unhappy about a ­disallowed goal.

Arsenal began the match brightly, with Lisa Baum’s effort deflecting on to the bar and Olivia Smith firing over from a tight angle. They were rewarded when a good move down their right led to Emily Fox’s cross being angled into the net by Russo’s incisive first-time finish.

Liverpool were level six minutes later, though, and from a defensive point of view it was a familiarly exasperating story for Arsenal, who have conceded from simple long balls through the middle ­several times this season.

They exerted very little pressure as Liverpool found Natalia Ramos in space and her direct ball picked out Beata Olsson up front, with the Arsenal centre-backs Steph Catley and Leah Williamson positioned so far apart that they were almost in different time zones, ­playing Olsson onside. Liverpool’s central striker did enough to keep the ball away from Williamson and lash her strike into the bottom corner.

A curling Ramos free-kick was tipped on to the bar by the Arsenal goalkeeper Misa Rodríguez, before the game’s most contentious moment left Liverpool feeling ­understandably aggrieved. Jenna Clark tucked the ball into the net at the far post after ­Arsenal failed to clear a corner, but the assistant referee disallowed the goal for offside against Vivien ­Endemann, despite the delivery towards the player having been ­inadvertently played off an Arsenal foot rather than being a deliberate forward pass from the home side, who looked baffled.

That seemed to wake Arsenal from their slumber, however, and ­Caitlin Foord went close before Russo restored Arsenal’s lead in the final minute of the first half, as her downward header from Baum’s cross was too precise for Khiara Keating to reach. Slegers praised Russo, as she said: “She’s in top form. The two goals are such clean finishes. She picks up really good positions in the box.”

After a very watchable first half for neutrals, the second half was comparatively less entertaining but still tense as Liverpool fought to try to force an equaliser. They almost found it in the 89th minute but Gareth Taylor had his head in his hands in disbelief after Cornelia Kapocs volleyed wide from a glorious, unmarked position in front of goal. Arsenal clung on.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Liverpool are now winless in five league games but their defender Grace Fisk, who signed a new contract on Saturday, said: “There were so many positives. We made them very uncomfortable for large parts of the game. It’s just the bits in both boxes right now that are letting us down.” ­Taylor, Liverpool’s head coach, agreed: “­Performance‑wise, I couldn’t ask for any more from the girls.”

Slegers, who next has a ­daunting trip to face the European champions Barcelona, said: “The way we defended at the end of the game, for our lives, with so much passion and pride for the shirt, that ball wasn’t going to go in.”

Sports.title: Diego Gómez hits another stunner as Brighton beat 10-man Brentford to go second
Sports.content:
Who can stop Brighton’s ­ascension in English and European football? They are setting standards, ­practices ­leaving almost everybody else ­trailing in their wake. A ­second‑place position in the ­Premier League would once have read like a glitch in a ­Football ­Manager ­session. Not in November 2026, where they appear the only team capable of throwing down any sort of challenge to Arsenal.

Under low winter sun, Brentford, an opposition to which Brighton are often, if lazily, compared, were ­swatted aside. If Keith Andrews’s team, and their fans at the Amex ­Stadium, could level blame at a couple of ­refereeing decisions, they received little chance of rescuing anything. Brighton squeezed them, toyed with them.

If Pascal Gross, scorer of a perfectly hit penalty, attempted to dampen expectations of a title challenge, his manager, Fabian Hürzeler, allowed fans to dream. “They should always be excited, it’s our job to make them excited,” he said.

A successful return to the Amex Stadium following five Brighton away trips, more than 5,000 miles on the road including victories at ­Manchester City and Getafe over the past two outings. Brentford returned to a stadium where they have never won in the Premier League. Normal service was duly resumed, any Brighton negatives coming in a failure to add to their first-half goals.

An up-and-under straight from the kick-off was a rare Brentford foray into the Brighton box. Bart Verburggen catching it on the full prefaced an easy afternoon for the Brighton goalkeeper. There are many further dimensions to ­Hürzeler’s team. Last week Paul Scholes, an unlikely ­progressive, declared himself an admirer of a “level of ­coaching” he suggested is ­unsurpassed in ­English football. “The one thing that is non‑negotiable is to always put the team first,” Hürzeler said.

View image in fullscreen Brighton were already 1-0 down when the VAR upgraded Igor Thiago’s yellow card to a red. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Diego Gómez’s opener was not as spectacular as the halfway-line goal of the season against Crystal Palace but a beauty nonetheless. Caressing the ball first with his left and then with his right, he laid up a thrash past Caoimhín Kelleher. Its trajectory was unerring, unstoppable. Hürzeler revealed: “Yesterday, he changed to shooting with [his] left foot … I couldn’t see him scoring with his left foot. I asked him after where this quality came from.”

The path to a commanding win opened up. Igor Thiago did not last many ­minutes beyond his failed attempt to lob ­Verburggen. Scuffling in midfield with Chema Andrés, his shove was first ruled a yellow by the referee, Michael Oliver. In stepped the video assistant referee, Stuart Attwell: “violent conduct” and “with force” was the verdict from Stockley Park.

Afterwards, Andrews was ­visibly unhappy: “We’ve lost two games and both when down to 10 men. So we need to analyse ourselves first. In both scenarios we can do better. In both scenarios the opposition player has been the one to provoke the situation.”

Infact, both Yehor Yarmolyuk and Vitaly Janelt were dismissed against Liverpool, and if Andrews rues such lapses of discipline he was more unhappy at the initial decision’s video-assisted overturn: “The game is in a state now of a place I don’t particularly like.”

Straying beyond the confines of his technical area in a manner likely to add him to Mikel Arteta’s “massive storage of images” of such breaches, Andrews asked his team to dig deep but Brighton’s dominance of possession became near-total.

Luka Vuskovic, ­serving ­previously as a deep-lying playmaker, won the penalty. Keane Lewis-Potter’s ­panicked response to a physical 18-yard box mismatch was to snatch at the ­Croatian’s shirt. Gross’s penalty was struck as truly as Gómez’s goal. “We need to be cuter,” Andrews said. “I take real pride in the way we defend set pieces and we need to do better because that wasn’t good.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Pascal Gross’ penalty was unsaveable. Photograph: Alex Ferrelly/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

Andrews’s half-time ­adjustments, bringing on Yarmolyuk and Nathan Collins, was an attempt to protect Brentford’s goal difference. Brighton continued to pile on pressure, their ­possession share reaching beyond 75%. A set piece became Brentford’s sole route back, though Mathias Jensen’s diagonal into ­Verbruggen’s hands would not have passed muster in rugby’s Nations Championship.

Ironic cheers from the away end came when Brentford won a corner, and then another – rare excitement at Brighton’s defenders being asked to do something other than build an attack. The visitors’ fighting spirit at least sustained, though threatened to spill over. When Kevin Schade shoved ­Vuskovic to the ground by the touchline, another red card was a possibility, only for Oliver and Attwell to rule a yellow as sufficient this time.

Brighton’s push for honours and further horizons will require more than spectacular goals. “You see the Premier League, the margins, you look at the results – we are not ­getting carried away yet,” Gross said. “Every game we have to suffer a lot.”

Hürzeler, like Andrews constantly straying beyond the confines of his technical area, does not countenance any let-ups. When Brighton meet the unstinting demands of their coach, so many are left in their wing mirrors.

Sports.title: FA Cup roundup: Seventh-tier Wimborne shock Crawley to reach second round
Sports.content:
Seventh-tier Wimborne heaped more misery on Crawley as the bottom side in the Football League lost 2-0 in the biggest upset of the FA Cup first round.

The Dorset part-timers took the lead after only nine minutes when the property surveyor Yang Seung-woo curled a superb strike from just inside the penalty area into the top corner.

Crawley came close to equalising when Kai Jennings flashed a low shot narrowly wide before Jonny Russell headed tamely into the arms of the home goalkeeper Cam Plain.

Crawley’s interim manager, Kevin Blackwell, made a triple change at half-time and Charlie Barker fired inches wide for the team 57 places above their hosts in the pyramid. The Southern Premier League got a huge slice of luck to seal victory 11 minutes from time. Jackson King’s shot hit Cameron Munn to send the ball squirming beyond the former Arsenal goalkeeper Vito Mannone.

Stafford Rangers were denied a historic win after losing 3-2 on penalties to Grimsby after they drew 3-3 after extra time. Two goals from firefighter Darrhyl Mason and one from the Aston Villa youth coach Jack Birch got the eighth-tier side – 89 places below League Two Grimsby – to a shootout.

Mason and Birch had put Rangers 2-0 ahead in front of a crowd of 3,130 at the Stan Robinson Stadium as they chased the second round for the first time since 2007. But set-piece headers inside three minutes from Harvey Rodgers and Maldini Kacurri sent the tie into extra time, where Mason and Géza Turi traded goals.

View image in fullscreen Stafford Rangers’ Luca Navarro (right) appears dejected after missing the deciding penalty. Photograph: Gary Oakley/PA

The home debutant Luca Navarro had to score to send the tie into sudden death but saw his spot-kick saved by Harvey Cartwright to end Rangers’ nine-match Cup marathon.

Lewis Fiorini’s extra-time penalty sent Stockport, who are second in League One, into the second round after they came from two goals down to win 3-2 against Cray Wanderers.

Despite being 112 places below their opponents in the pyramid, it was the Isthmian Premier side Cray who took the lead after 21 minutes when Sammie MacLeod found the bottom corner.

Stockport were then reduced to 10 men in the 31st minute as goalkeeper Luca Ashby-Hammond was sent off for a dangerous challenge on John Ufuah. Alex Hernandez bent a brilliant strike into the top-right corner from the resulting free-kick.

Depleted Stockport pulled one back in the 81st minute when Kyle Wootton tscored with a header. And the Hatters then sent the tie into extra time when Mikael Mandron was in the right place to nod home Jack Diamond’s cross. The decisive moment came in the 101st minute when Cray goalkeeper JJ Briggs clattered into Mandron to give away a penalty, which was dispatched by Fiorini.

Charlie Savage scored against his father’s team as Reading eased into the second round with a 5-0 rout of Peterborough at the Weston Homes Stadium on Saturday.

This all-League One tie turned out to be one of the most one-sided of the day, with the Peterborough manager, Robbie Savage, watching on in disbelief as his side were pulled apart.

Reading went ahead after 26 minutes as slick passing led to Andy Rinomhota playing in Daniel Kyerewaa, who found the bottom corner via a deflection. Reading doubled their lead in the 34th minute when a cross from Haydon Roberts was met by a diving header from top scorer Jack Marriott.

It was in effect game over in first-half stoppage time as Savage deepened his father’s misery when he took possession after the ball ran off Marriott, his deflected effort finding the top corner.

Jamie Reid added a fourth for the visitors in the 72nd minute when Paudie O’Connor nodded Savage’s free-kick into his path for him to lift over the Peterborough goalkeeper Alex Bass. Reading struck yet again four minutes later when Liam Fraser’s pass put Reid clean through to score his second.

Non-league Kidderminster breezed into the second round with a convincing 3-0 victory over League One Doncaster.

The National League club opened the scoring after 22 minutes when Maz Kouhyar pulled the ball back to Lewis Walker, and he fired home at the second attempt after his initial shot had hit the upright.

View image in fullscreen David Davis celebrates a goal in Kidderminster’s FA Cup upset victory. Photograph: Matty Paddock

The Harriers striker continued to cause problems, putting an effort over the bar and another just wide, but in the 36th minute he turned provider, charging upfield before teeing up Kouhyar and the on-loan Notts County midfielder slotted home. Kouhyar was again involved in the third goal, having a shot that Josh Clarke could only parry and David Davis turned in the rebound.

The Kidderminster manager, Paul Wotton, said: “We started well, scored the goal and got the crowd up. It was just a really good day. They are a League One team at the end of the day, no matter what the scoreline suggests. They are two leagues higher than us, so they are going to have moments in the game, but we stood up to it.”

League Two Exeter pulled off an upset with a 2-1 win away to League One leaders Huddersfield. Exeter took the lead after 12 minutes, thanks to a perfectly delivered cross from the left from Luca Woodhouse, with centre-back Jack Taylor stealing in at the far post to finish it off.

Huddersfield looked a different team in the second half and found an equaliser within eight minutes of the restart as Ibane Bowat headed home Cameron Humphreys’ corner at the back post.

Charlie Cummins grabbed the winner nine minutes from time at the end of a well-worked move up the right, culminating in Reece Cole’s cutback and a good finish.

View image in fullscreen Exeter’s Charlie Cummins celebrates after his late winner against Huddersfield. Photograph: Steve Taylor/PPAUK/Shutterstock

Altrincham were denied another famous FA Cup upset as they conceded an 84-minute equaliser against Notts County before bowing out in a penalty shootout.

County took the lead through Jacob Bedeau in the 28th minute but Altrincham responded well with Lucas Weaver grabbing an equaliser six minutes before half-time. Lewis Banks gave the hosts the lead just before the hour but Callum Roberts dashed Altrincham’s hopes of another cup scalp, having beaten 17 Football League sides in the competition, scoring with a first-time strike to force extra-time.

With neither side able to make a breakthrough in extra-time the game went to penalties and Aidan Barlow, Sam Taylor and Eddy Jones all missed from the spot for Altrincham as County triumphed 3-2.

Blackpool survived a scare at Hornchurch, needing to rely on a 118th-minute winner from Josh Bowler to secure a 2-1 comeback victory at the Hornchurch Stadium.

Fleetwood’s hopes of following up their memorable Carabao Cup upset against Premier League champions Arsenal with a long FA Cup run are over after a 2-1 home defeat by fellow League Two side Rochdale. Baba Adeeko’s goal in extra time at Highbury sent the visitors through.

Chesterfield withstood a second-half comeback from Yeovil Town to secure their place in the second round with a 4-3 victory. Yeovil recovered from 3-1 down to level at 3-3 before Joel Randall struck the winner a minute from time.

Late Mansfield goals from Rhys Oates and Jordan Bowery ended the plucky Cup resistance of National League North Macclesfield. Nathan Moriah-Welsh gave Mansfield a first-half lead but the Silkmen were still in the tie under Oates made it 2-0 in the 72nd minute. Bowery added a third three minutes into added time to wrap up victory for the Stags.

League One Plymouth eased through thanks to three goals in a late 11-minute spell in a 4-0 win against Southern League Premier Central battlers Alvechurch. Will Evans finally broke the deadlock after 50 minutes, winning the ball from Jessy Bavanganga before driving a low angled shot into the far corner. Further goals from Evans, Michael Baidoo and Ronan Curtis saw the Pilgrims through.

View image in fullscreen Michael Baidoo makes it 3-0 to Plymouth as they overcome Alvechurch. Photograph: Dave Rowntree/PPAUK/Shutterstock

League One strugglers Barnsley booked their spot in the second round with a 7-2 win over Aldershot at Oakwell, with Cameron McGeehan grabbing a hat-trick.

Leyton Orient held off Harborough 5-1 to progress into the second round while League Two high-flyers Crewe beat Wimbledon 2-1.

Nick Powell and Adam Phillips scored twice as Bradford thrashed National League North side Marine 7-0, while a late goal from Joel Randall helped Cheltenham close out a dramatic 4-3 win over National League Yeovil.

Last season’s quarter-finalists Port Vale booked their place in the second round with a 4-2 victory over National League strugglers Scunthorpe United at Vale Park. MK Dons avoided an upset as they ground out a 2-1 win over League Two Swindon.

Southern League Premier Central team Worcester’s hopes of an upset were ended in a 1-0 defeat at League Two Colchester while Jack Bates scored twice in the first half as Dover progressed with a 2-0 win over Wealdstone.

Ollie Pearce scored after 10 seconds as York sealed a 4-0 win over Northampton. The City captain also bagged a second before Alex Hunt and Josh Stones completed the rout.

Jordan Thewlis’ stoppage-time penalty gave seventh-tier Guiseley a 1-0 win over Sutton at Nethermoor Park as Carlisle beat League Two leaders Salford 1-0. Ryan Graydon missed a penalty for the visitors before David Ajiboye’s goal just before the break proved enough to send the Cumbrians through.

Eighth-tier AFC Rushden + Diamonds slipped to a 4-0 defeat at Burton. Will Collar and Borges Rodrigues scored for the Brewers in the first half, with Charlie Webster and Zac Scutt adding two more late on.

Nathan Odokonyero scored twice as National League South Salisbury saw off seventh-tier Sholing 6-0 to take their place in round two for the first time since reforming in 2015.

Sports.title: Evanilson launches eighth straight Bournemouth win at blundering Ipswich
Sports.content:
Another Evanilson goal helped fire Marco Rose’s Bournemouth to an eighth straight victory with a hard-fought 2-1 win at Ipswich.

Evanilson failed to score in his first six appearances of the season but found the net for a fifth consecutive Premier League match and made it seven goals in eight after five minutes at Portman Road.

It came after a terrible error by Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton, who tried and failed to dribble around the Brazilian forward, before worse followed for the hosts 27 seconds into the second half.

Bournemouth went two up when Ryan Christie’s effort deflected off Leif Davis and in for an own goal.

Gary O’Neil watched Ipswich rally against his former club, with a Jack Clarke penalty halving the deficit with 17 minutes left, but the hosts could not find an equaliser to make it only one win from their last seven matches.

Sports.title: John Aloisi’s Chengdu choke to blow title chances on final day of Chinese season
Sports.content:
John Aloisi’s Chengdu Rongcheng let the Chinese Super League title slip from their grasp on the last day of the season, losing their fourth consecutive game as rivals Dalian Yingbo pipped them to the trophy following their fifth straight win.

Dalian completed a remarkable comeback by overhauling Chengdu’s lead, which once stood at 12 points, with Aloisi’s side picking up just one point in their last five matches. On the league’s final day, Chengdu lost 3-2 to Shandong Taishan, while Dalian’s 3-1 victory over Tianjin Tiger earned Li ⁠Guozu’s side ​the trophy.

The results saw the two teams finish level on 52 points, ​with Dalian winning the title on ‌a better head-to-head record ‌after recording a pair of wins over Chengdu, including in the penultimate ‌round of matches.

Dalian still needed to win on Sunday while hoping Chengdu lost, and Aloisi’s side went two goals down in Jinan when Raphael Merkies and Guilherme Madruga struck in the 15th and 23rd minutes respectively.

Felipe Silva pulled one back for Chengdu with seven minutes remaining ‌in the first half and, while Cryzan restored Shandong’s two-goal advantage in the 63rd minute, Wellington Silva’s 79th minute strike ​set up a tense finish.

View image in fullscreen Chengdu Rongcheng let a 12-point lead slip after losing their final four games of the season. Photograph: Shutterstock

Wang Ziming’s shot from close range was deflected over the bar in the third added minute as an increasingly desperate Chengdu ran out of time.

That left Dalian to secure the title in front ⁠of their own fans after Yang Mingrui gave the home ​side a fifth-minute lead.

Xadas’ ​50th minute penalty levelled ​the scores for Tianjin but Liao Jintao netted from the ​edge of the ‌area with 20 ​minutes left ​to restore Dalian’s advantage.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Football Desk Australia 

Huang Shan then struck from three yards out in the fourth minute of stoppage time to seal the win for Dalian and send the packed-out Dalian Suoyuwan Football Stadium into raptures.

It concludes an historic collapse for Australian Aloisi’s side who began the season with an unusual head-start as one of the only CSL clubs on zero points, while a series of points deductions were made to several rival sides which saw them start their campaigns in the negative.

Sports.title: Leeds condemn disgusting racist abuse aimed at defender Jayden Bogle
Sports.content:
Leeds United have condemned the racist abuse sent to Jayden Bogle following their match against Tottenham on Saturday.

The club revealed that Bogle was subject to racism on social media after the game that saw them beat Spurs 1-0.



2 Bogle has unfortunately been the subject of racist abuse following Leeds' win over Tottenham on Saturday Credit: Getty

Leeds confirmed they would be working with the Premier League to identify the people behind the messages.

And they will be pushing for strong sanctions to be handed out to those responsible for sending the abuse.

Leeds condemn racist abuse sent to Bogle

In a statement released on Sunday, the club wrote: "Leeds United Football Club are appalled at the disgusting, racist social media abuse Jayden Bogle suffered following Saturday’s Premier League victory against Tottenham Hotspur.



"Leeds United condemns this behaviour in the strongest possible terms.

"There is no place for racism in football or society.

"The club will work with the Premier League and relevant authorities to identify the individuals and push for the strongest possible action to be taken against them.



"Jayden has the full and unconditional support of the club and his teammates, and we all stand with him at this time.

"Nobody should ever be subjected to racist abuse."

The messages sent to Bogle on social media after the match included racist comments and offensive emojis.



Messages wishing physical abuse on the 26-year-old's wife and children were also sent to him.

2 Leeds have condemned the disgusting messages, which also included comments wishing harm on Bogle's wide and children Credit: Getty

Bogle was involved in a flashpoint in the match between Leeds and Tottenham on Saturday afternoon.

Whilst tackling Spurs' Mathys Tel in the first half of the clash at Elland Road, he caught the forward on the ankle.



Tel was left rolling around in pain as VAR reviewed the incident that showed Bogle catching his opponent with his studs up.

Eventually though, he avoided any punishment despite huge appeals for a red card, and he went on to play 89 minutes.

Meanwhile, Tel was unable to continue and was substituted with his knock caused by the Leeds defender's tackle.

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi confirmed it was a 'bad injury' for the Frenchman when speaking post-match.

Sports.title: Fan rushed to hospital and five injured after stand collapses during match involving Champions League club
Sports.content:
Fan rushed to hospital and five injured after stand collapses during match involving Champions League club

A fan has been taken to hospital after a stand collapsed during a match in Norway.

The incident saw as many as five people fall through the stand at the fixture between Tromso and Bodo/Glimt.



3 A fan was taken to hospital after a stand collapsed during Tromso vs Bodo/Glimt Credit: AFP

Play at the 6,687-capacity Romssa Arena was suspended after 41 minutes as emergency responders rushed to aid supporters.

Latest on Tromso collapsed stand

Supporters were evacuated from their seats whilst the players left the pitch to return to the dressing room.

A section of the stand housing travelling Bodo/Glimt fans had been affected by the partial collapse.



Around 600 supporters were in that area of the ground when the incident occurred at 3:12pm local time.

Club spokesperson Simen Pederson told VG that the fan taken to hospital was conscious.



Once medical staff had attended to the injured fans, play resumed at 4pm following a suspension of 48 minutes.

Bodo/Glimt went on to claim a 2-0 victory thanks to Ola Brynhildsen's brace.



The win sees the visitors keep pace with Eliteserien leaders Viking, with only goals scored separating the title chasers.

Meanwhile, Tromso are in sixth with four matches of the season remaining.

3 The incident occurred at Tromso's home ground during Sunday's match Credit: Getty

Bodo/Glimt in the Champions League

Bodo/Glimt are also competing in the Champions League once again this term.



Their involvement in the league phase in successive seasons marks their only appearances in the competition proper.

So far this season, they have secured a home win over Borussia Dortmund as well as a goalless draw with Lille.

However, Khetil Knutsen's side have been beaten in each of their opening two away matches.

The four-time Norwegian champions suffered defeats to both Bayern Munich and Napoli on the road.



They will be hoping to emulate last season's success by reaching the knockout stage.

3 Around 600 Bodo/Glimt fans were in the affected area of the stadium Credit: AFP

Bodo/Glimt picked up famous wins over Manchester City, Atletico Madrid and Inter Milan during their maiden campaign.

Sporting Lisbon ultimately knocked them out in the last 16, winning 5-3 on aggregate.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick will die on the hill of Manchester United’s one-man wrecking ball
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick will die on the hill of Manchester United’s one-man wrecking ball

Michael Carrick's persistent selection of Diogo Dalot for Manchester United is proving he's not the man to turn things around.

That's the opinion of talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook, who slammed Dalot for his performance on Sunday.



4 Carrick's persistence with playing Dalot each week for Man United is going to cost him his job, according to Crook Credit: Getty

The Portugal international had another nightmare showing at Old Trafford as Man United played out a thrilling 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa.

As well as being out of position in the lead-up to Villa's opener, Dalot gave away a penalty at a crucial stage of the game, bringing down Alysson in the box just three minutes into the second half.

United had come from 2-0 down to level the match before the break, but the spot-kick completely killed their momentum.



And after John McGinn punished Dalot's error, Leon Goretzka soon restored Villa's two-goal lead, which continued Carrick's side's misery, having won just one of their first ten Premier League games.

Dalot was substituted after 66 minutes, with loud cheers coming from Red Devils fans as his withdrawal was announced.



But the damage had already been done by the 27-year-old, who has already been criticised for his showings this season.

Dalot labelled a 'one-man wrecking ball'

Slamming the United full-back, Crook said on talkSPORT: “Dalot is like a one-man wrecking ball this week.”



Micky Gray then added: “Sometimes you watch a game of football and you can't quite believe your eyes in certain things that you're witnessing on a football pitch.

“You make a mistake in the first four minutes in the first half and you find yourself two goals down from the same individual player.

"That's not defending. That is schoolboy, that’s worse than schoolboy.”

4 Dalot clumsily brought down Alysson in the box to give Aston Villa a penalty, which McGinn converted at Old Trafford Credit: Getty



“You're in your own 18-yard area. Alysson's obviously going to try and work the ball onto his stronger left foot.

"As he comes inside, as a defender you make yourself big, but you don't start poking a leg out. As soon as he makes contact with him, he's going to go to ground.

“Blatant penalty, but just terrible, terrible defending.”

Carrick will die on the Dalot hill

Crook went on to point out that Dalot has now played 260 games for Man United across his eight years at the club so far.

That means he has made more appearances than legends Eric Cantona, Jaap Stam, Andrei Kanchelskis and Dimitar Berbatov.



Crook added: “He's not fit to lace their boots and if that doesn't tell you how low standards have slipped here at Old Trafford, nothing will.”

4 Dalot has now played 260 games for Man United and has started in eight of their first 10 league games this season Credit: Getty

Continuing the criticism, Gray said: “When you've made one big error, you don't go on and make another, and another, and another.

“And every single week we seem to be talking about exactly the same thing. I said it in midweek, he should have been taken off after ten or 15 minutes, and I wasn't being over-cruel.



“It was just a player that wasn't passing to his teammates, he wasn't doing what he was told to do as a defender, and now we're witnessing it yet again.

“But you make a mistake in the first half, you come out in the second half, you wait three minutes and you make another one. Schoolboy errors every single time you see him play.”

Academy product Harry Amass is a player having potential minutes in the first team taken by Dalot each week.

But Crook doesn't think the 19-year-old's going to come into the team any time soon, with the manager sticking by the Portuguese defender.



4 Crook thinks Carrick will continue to play Dalot and that it shows that he won't be able to turn this misery around at Man United Credit: Getty

Crook said: “I think this is a hill that Michael Carrick might die on, to be honest.

“To keep picking an average right-back, who's a calamity at left-back, and ignore a young academy product.

“It's difficult to back a manager who, when his team aren't winning games, and they were bottom of the table at one stage this afternoon. For the first time since 1930, let's not forget that.



"If you don't make any changes to your team line-up, that gives the impression that you don't know how to change things around, and alter the direction of travel.”

Dalot was replaced by Patrick Dorgu, who proved to be the unlikely hero with a last-gasp equaliser as United scored twice in stoppage time to fight back from 4-2 down to claim the draw with Joshua Zirkzee scoring earlier in stoppage time.

Sports.title: Jason Cundy trolled by Sunderland with cheeky post after massive win over Chelsea
Sports.content:
Jason Cundy trolled by Sunderland with cheeky post after massive win over Chelsea

talkSPORT superstar Jason Cundy found himself on the receiving end of a jibe from Sunderland after they beat his beloved Chelsea.

Days after losing to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League, the Black Cats picked up a second Premier League win of the season with their 1-0 triumph.



3 Enzo Le Fee was on hand to score the winner in a much-needed victory for Sunderland Credit: Getty

Enzo Le Fee scored a 36th minute penalty to ensure Sunderland won in the league for the first time since August 30.

The decision to award the spot-kick was controversial as Levi Colwill was adjudged to have fouled Brian Brobbey inside the area.

However, replays appeared to show the Sunderland forward tripping over himself whilst also holding onto Colwill's shirt.



Nevertheless, it presented the hosts with an opportunity to take the lead, one they made the most of to win all three points.

Victory will ease the pressure on under-fire head coach Regis Le Bris as club football prepares to pause for the international break.



Sunderland remain in the bottom three, but they wasted no time in poking fun at talkSPORT's resident Chelsea fan Cundy.

Sunderland post Cundy jibe

In a post on X, they captioned a celebratory full-time picture with: "HAAAAAAAS ANYONE SEEN."



Cundy is famed for his 'Has anyone seen?' taunt on The Sports Bar, especially to co-host Jamie O'Hara whenever Tottenham lose.

However, the roles look set to be reversed on Monday night, with O'Hara likely to give him a taste of his own medicine.

Chelsea were second best throughout the match at the Stadium of Light and have lost in the league for a fourth time this season.

3 Sunderland made sure to rub their victory in the face of Cundy by using his own taunt against him Credit: talkSPORT



For a fourth consecutive match, they were without their main striker Joao Pedro as he recovers from a thigh injury.

Danny Welbeck and Emmanuel Emegha are their other options to lead the line, but they only entered play during the second half.

Before conceding the penalty, Chelsea felt they should have been given the chance to score from 12 yards after Cole Palmer went down.

Luke O'Nien fouled him and was deemed to have done so outside of the penalty box, rather than in it.



Morgan Rogers missed a great chance to put them ahead earlier on, but couldn't guide his header on target.

Chelsea have now lost three of their last four across all competitions, but are only two points outside of the Premier League top four.

3 Jamie O'Hara also caught a stray from a Premier League club this weekend

Cundy wasn't the only talkSPORT host to catch some strays from a Premier League club this weekend.



Fellow Sports Bar post Jamie O'Hara was trolled by Leeds after they beat his beloved Tottenham 1-0 at Elland Road on Saturday.

The club tweeted once Leeds' win was confirmed: "GOOOOOOOOOOD WIN THAT."

This is in reference to O'Hara frequently describing something as good, often sarcastically, on The Sports Bar.

Sports.title: Alex Ferguson surrounded by former players as acting legend shares picture from 40th anniversary dinner
Sports.content:
Alex Ferguson surrounded by former players as acting legend shares picture from 40th anniversary dinner

Actor James Nesbitt has shared a glimpse into Sir Alex Ferguson's celebrations to mark 40 years since his arrival at Manchester United.

The legendary manager was appointed by the Red Devils on November 6, 1986, signalling the start of one of the most successful football dynasties of all time.

3 Fergie won 38 trophies in a legendary 27 years as Man United boss Credit: Getty

In the 27 years that followed, Ferguson would transform United into one of football's greatest powerhouses of the modern era.

The Scot built several legendary teams during his tenure, which saw him land 13 Premier League titles which also included an historic treble in 1999.

Star-studded event

Having retired with one last Premier League success in 2013, Ferguson has spent this week celebrating 40 years since his arrival at Old Trafford.

He was treated to a celebratory dinner, which featured some huge figures from United, the world of football and beyond.

Among the celebrity names in attendance was actor and lifelong Man United fan James Nesbitt.

The Northern Irishman is best known for his roles in The Hobbit and Cold Feet, and was invited to the lavish event.

Nesbitt posted a picture of himself sat at a table with Ferguson and a host of Man United legends.

Also on the actor's table were Old Trafford heroes Edwin van der Sar and John O’Shea, as well as former captain Nemanja Vidic.

So too were Robin van Persie, Darren Fletcher, Jonny Evans and Javier Hernandez, as well as current United boss Michael Carrick.

Taking to Instagram, Nesbitt captioned his post: “Sir Alex 40th anniversary of being made manager of Man Utd. Blessed.”

3 Nesbitt was surrounded by former United heroes as they celebrates Ferguson's landmark Credit: Instagram @jamesnesbittofficial

The United heroes on the star-studded table lifted an eye-watering 26 Premier League titles between them.

It wasn't just Nesbitt who shared pictures from the exclusive event.

Legendary former goalkeeper Van der Sar also uploaded several snaps, where he shared his delight at being part of the event.

The 56-year-old wrote: “What a fantastic evening at Old Trafford celebrating 40 years of Sir Alex taking the reins at United.

“Catching up with the boys and some great speeches about what he achieved to leave such a mark on this club!"

While United's legendary figures celebrated Ferguson's decorated Old Trafford legacy, things could hardly be more different with their current crop of players.

3 Alex Ferguson remains a regular presence at Old Trafford on matchdays Credit: Getty

After a difficult start to the season, Michael Carrick currently finds himself under huge pressure in the Old Trafford hotseat.

However, he bought himself more time in midweek as the Red Devils pulled off a thrilling comeback win over Roma - with Ferguson in attendance.

Now Carrick is bidding to follow this up with a first Premier League win since August against Aston Villa on home turf.

Sports.title: Wrexham chief reacts to chat with Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac
Sports.content:
Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson says he enjoyed having Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney in attendance for their draw with Wolves on Saturday.

Lewis O'Brien cancelled out Adam Armstrong's opener as Wrexham claimed an important point at the Racecourse Ground.



3 McElhenney and Reynolds were in attendance for the 1-1 draw at home to Wolves on Saturday Credit: AFP

Co-owners Reynolds and Mac were in the stands for the game amid issues on and off the field for the Welsh club.

The draw sees Wrexham sit 15th in the Championship table heading into the international break and Parkinson says having their Hollywood duo at the game gave everyone a boost.

"It's always very uplifting, I feel, for the people who work at the club, first of all, the players and the staff when Rob and Ryan come over," he said.



"The crowd as well, they're uplifted by the owners being in town."

Asked if he had talked with the owners, Parkinson added: "I communicate with them when they're back in the States, but equally it's good to have a chat with them when they're over."

Following three league defeats in four games to finish October, Wrexham have beaten Middlesbrough and drawn with Wolves in their last two games.



And the Red Dragons have winnable matches against Lincoln City and Bristol City coming up after the international break.

Parkinson added: "After the defeat in Sheffield [to United, 1-0 on October 30], to go toe-to-toe with Middlesbrough and Wolves and to come out with four points – we have to be pleased with that.



"We asked the lads for one almighty effort. It was always going to be tough to completely match the levels from Wednesday night but there were times where I don’t think we were far away from them.

"You can have the meetings after the game at Sheffield, and you can put the work in on the training ground, but then it’s up to the players when they cross the white line to put that into practice, and show how much they care about the club.

3 Parkinson's side have hit back in their last two games Credit: Getty

Upcoming Wrexham fixtures Saturday, November 21 - Lincoln City (A) 3pm Tuesday November 24 - Bristol City (A) 7:45pm Saturday November 28 - Portsmouth (H) 3pm Saturday December 5 - Norwich City (A) 3pm Tuesday December 8 - Charlton Athletic (H) 7:45pm Friday December 11 - Bolton Wanderers (A) 8pm Saturday December 19 - Queens Park Rangers (H) 3pm

“Caring about the club is running and tackling, we know that, but also concentrating on doing the role you’ve been asked to do with and without the ball.



“In terms of the honesty of the team, I thought that was ten out of ten today.”

He added: “I’m pleased with the lads, and it was another cracking atmosphere here. We’ll take the points to move into the international break.

“We’ve shown what we need to do. We’ve shown we can compete. We’ve had a bit of a reset this week, in terms of what the performances needed to look like for our supporters and everybody at the club. We really were ready for these two games.

“I’m glad the break is only two weeks, like I’m sure all of the other managers are too! For us, it’s about getting [injured trio] Josh Windass, Nathan Broadhead and Callum O’Hare available now. That’s the key.



3 Whilst it has been a tricky period for Wrexham, Reynolds has stressed that there is unity at the club Credit: Getty

“There will be a few days off, but we’ve always stressed to the players, you have to earn those days off. I think they have earned it with their last two performances.

“We have to make sure we have a real hunger and determination about the group.

“Now, come on, it’s a chance to get some work in the lads who need to work and build on what we’ve done this week.”

Sports.title: Bizarre moment footballer sent off for elbowing ball boy – who then wildly celebrates
Sports.content:
Bizarre moment footballer sent off for elbowing ball boy – who then wildly celebrates

A unique VAR intervention caused chaotic scenes in the Canadian Premier League on Saturday.

The incident occurred during the play-off semi-final second leg between Cavalry FC and Supra du Quebec.



3 Supra's Alessandro Biello was sent off for appearing to elbow a ball boy Credit: X formerly Twitter / @onesoccer

With Cavalry leading on aggregate in stoppage time, Supra midfielder Alessandro Biello clashed with a ball boy on the touchline.

The former Canada Under-20 international appeared to shove the youngster with his elbow as he attempted to retrieve the ball.

Red card for ball boy push

VAR subsequently called the referee over to the monitor to review the altercation.



Biello was subsequently shown a straight red card for his antics having also been booked earlier in the half.

His dismissal prompted wild celebrations from the Cavalry FC fans inside ATCO Field.



Amongst them was the ball boy who had been pushed, who was captured on TV cameras reacting to the decision.

They could be seen throwing their arms in the air as they jumped up and down in front of the crowd.



Cavalry FC had been leading 2-0 at the time and 3-2 on aggregate, a lead which they were able to hold on to against the 10 men of Supra.

The visitors' goalkeeper Joakim Milli had earlier been frustrated by the antics of the ball boys around the pitch.

He furiously complained to the officials after a ball boy had withheld the ball after preventing him from retrieving it.

3 The referee dismissed Biello following a VAR review into the incident Credit: X formerly Twitter / @onesoccer



As for Biello, he was shown his second red card in just 30 appearances for Supra.

It follows the 20-year-old's arrival from MLS side Montreal Impact in January.

Supra had been aiming to reach the Canadian Premier League final in what is their first-ever season as a club.

The team were only founded in September 2025 before joining the division at the start of this year.



Meanwhile, their opponents Cavalry FC will be aiming to win the title for a second time.

The Cavs overturned a narrow 2-1 first leg deficit with Saturday's win to set up a meeting with Atletico Ottawa in the final on November 21.

3 The ball boy joined in the crowd's celebrations after the red card Credit: One Soccer

It will be a rematch of last season's Canadian Premier League final.

On that occasion, Atletico Ottawa claimed an extra-time victory at Cavalry FC's expense.

Sports.title: Gary Neville makes surprise claim about brother Phil as they recall infamous tunnel moment
Sports.content:
Some brothers are inseparable, some are distant - and others simply don't know where the other one lives.

Gary Neville grew up alongside his sibling Phil, but currently is not able to send him a Christmas card.



3 Gary and Phil may be brothers and long-term teammates, but they don't know everything about each other Credit: Getty

The former Manchester United defenders appeared on NBC Sports in what was their first-ever joint television outing.

Presenter Rebecca Lowe pointed out the historic moment when she opened the show, as Gary revealed when he and former MLS boss Phil last met.

"We've not see each other for three years either," he explained, before Phil then claimed: "He doesn't know where I live!"



"Correct, he actually doesn't," Lowe confirmed. "He actually asked Phil, 'Whereabouts do you live?' before we came on air."

Nevilles react to tunnel encounter

Gary and Phil played 287 times together for England and United, of which 263 came at club level.



The latter left Old Trafford in 2005 for Premier League rivals Everton, and they were then opponents on five occasions.

One match in February 2010, a 3-1 win for Everton at their old home Goodison Park, saw the brothers have an awkward moment in the tunnel before kick-off.



As the respective captains, they stood at the front of their teams when waiting to walk out onto the pitch.

However, they didn't say a word to each other, with both Gary and Phil being more concentrated on the match than their sibling.

"I played for 16 years at United, and never once shook the hand of another player in the tunnel," Gary said when watching it back.

3 Both Neville brothers put their clubs ahead of friendly reunions when playing for United and Everton Credit: Getty



"I wasn't going to start getting towards the end of my career in 2009, I was like a year away from finishing.

"It just wasn't right, it's not what we did. Maybe it was the Roy Keane mentality from that time, the Sir Alex Ferguson mentality.

"We were going out to play a serious game of football, no distractions. You don't be talking to your opponents."

"I came down the tunnel second, Gary was already there," said Phil. "I didn't know how to play it."



He added: "When I was going down the tunnel, I thought, 'We don't shake hands, we don't really hug, but I wonder if there's just a nod', and there wasn't a nod.

"As I went round the side, Tim Howard went, 'Phil, what's going on?' He thought there was a family feud or something. No, it's just what we did."

3 Gary has revealed that he would have been open to a handshake during their infamous tunnel meeting Credit: Getty

Gary then said that he would have welcomed a handshake from Phil, although he wouldn't have been the one to offer.



"I was already there, you could have come down the side and sort of tapped me on the shoulder, and gone like that.

"I wouldn't have ignored your hand if you put it to me, but I would never have instigated it."

Phil then added: "I think people around us expected something, and we just didn't play to the camera."

Sports.title: Dominant victory over Australia was England's best display of the year: This sweeping, attacking style should now become their blueprint under Steve Borthwick, writes NIK SIMON
Sports.content:
Henry Pollock pulled out his pulse check celebration and suddenly Steve Borthwick's heart rate could settle. This was the performance England's under-fire coach desperately needed. Days after Borthwick was accused of overseeing a toxic environment, his players delivered their best performance of the year. 'Do it for Steve,' was the message from Borthwick's senior players, who were left seething after reports of a split in the camp. Pollock and Borthwick are unlikely bedfellows but it was the peroxide youngster who stole the show. The 21-year-old was providing emergency backline cover from the bench when he was called into action in response to Immanuel Feyi-Waboso's first-half injury. Henry Pollock (left) scored two tries in two minutes as England thumped Australia 45-22 Pollock crosses the whitewash to score his first, and England's fifth of seven, in a dominant win The traditional back-row player came on as winger and made an impact at the Allianz Stadium Playing in the unfamiliar position on the right wing, he scored twice in the second-half, chasing a hat-trick as the final whistle blew on England's record points haul against the Wallabies. At one point, the versatile flanker nutmegged Australian full-back Max Jorgensen - counterintuitively, perhaps - consolidating his status as England's super sub. It is little surprise the RFU are working on projects to find the next Pollock. They want to create a centralised academy pathway, complete with branding experts, to manufacture more young box office talent. They have even pulled up the 1995 Nike commercial starring tennis rivals Andre Agassi and Pete Sampras as inspiration. Pollock stole the show, as he so often does, but this was by no means a one-man effort. England hurt the Wallabies with their sweeping attacking play which should become their blueprint. Maro Itoje looked rejuvenated after his summer off, making life miserable for Australia's half-backs, who barely fired a shot until the game broke up in the final quarter. At the World Rugby coaching meeting last Sunday, Borthwick made clear that England have been putting hours of work into their driving maul. It paid off as Jamie George scored a set-piece try in the eighth minute that put England on track for victory. His cathartic celebration spoke a thousand words. Fin Smith kicked 10 points for England in the Nations Championship clash against the Wallabies Hosts' win was soured by Immanuel Feyi-Waboso's (right) injury which saw Pollock come on In his pre-tournament briefing this week, RFU CEO Bill Sweeney defiantly stated that England are the second best team in the world when they keep 15 players on the pitch. Given the team were hit with a record-breaking 14 yellow cards in eight Tests - one of which was a 20-minute red - it felt like the executive was clutching at straws. Why Sweeney and Borthwick have not clubbed together to bring in a refereeing coach is another matter. Jaco Peyper and Jerome Garces are firmly embedded in the South African and French camps. England have invited Christophe Ridley to officiate team sessions but they have fallen short of a full-time appointment. A couple of cheap penalties meant the game was still in the balance before Pollock's second-half introduction. Crucially, however, England managed to concede no more yellow cards. Instead, it was Wallaby prop Angus Bell who was sinbinned for a hip drop tackle on Immanuel Feyi-Waboso in the 33rd minute. Feyi-Waboso had been England's most dangerous player. He beat seven defenders in the first half but his ankle never recovered from Bell's tackle. Tries from Ollie Chessum and Joe Heyes had built up England's lead but Feyi-Waboso's day was over when he struggled to chase down Max Jorgensen's interception try on the stroke of half time. Pollock came to the rescue. Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus has been the biggest advocate of utility players. He has turned South African centre Andre Esterhuizen into a flanker and now Borthwick is using a similar trick. It is no secret that Pollock loves the camera. His manager, Eddie Hearn, will vouch for that. He bounced around on the wing and charged out of his half with his first touch of the ball. George Furbank and Henry Slade combined in the midfield and Pollock's break led to a bonus-point try for Jack van Poortvliet. England captain Maro Itoje looks rejuvenated after missing the summer internationals The youngster showed the Midas touch. Punishing the Wallabies for a poor clearance kick, the youngster picked up a bouncing ball to score in the 56th minute, after a failed interception by Jorgensen. He scored his second moments later, showcasing his speed to charge down the right wing. Even Borthwick could allow himself a smile at that one. Worryingly for England, Seb Atkinson soon joined Feyi-Waboso in the medical room. Both will now be doubts for next week's meeting with Eddie Jones's Japan. A late exchange of tries kept the crowd entertained but they had no effect on the outcome - this was a convincing victory that reminded us that England have the ability to cause damage when they play the right way.
