Sports.title: This is how Enzo Maresca's tactics have left Elliot Anderson exposed with too much to do, writes JACK GAUGHAN... and why £125m Enzo Fernandez must step up and offer much more to solve midfield riddle
Sports.content:
Manchester City spent £320million on overhauling their midfield over the summer. In doing so, they twice broke their own transfer record. This marked the most aggressive focus on a specific need since the lavish outlay on full backs nine years ago.

All signed weeks before the independent commission’s guilty verdicts were announced, Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi heralded a new era in the City engine room. More energy, vibrancy, dynamism.

Two of them were ready-made replacements for Rodri and Bernardo Silva, with Bouaddi only 18 at the time and purchased as a potential superstar after shooting to global prominence at the World Cup.

But as Enzo Maresca heads into the second international break of the season on the back of three consecutive Premier League defeats, his midfield is the primary area of concern. And has been for a while.

A big fortnight lies in store for City’s manager, whose midfield has been wide open all year. Fine when outscoring opponents – see the 5-3 victory over Sunderland – and it makes for great entertainment yet an obvious gaping chasm when the goals dry up slightly.

The balance has not felt right and Maresca, who has gently batted away persistent questions about the midfield for weeks, must know this.

Elliot Anderson is being asked to do too much and it cost City in the 3-1 defeat at Forest

While studying tapes of all three defeats over the coming days, before City come back after the internationals to host Fulham and then go to Arsenal, he needs to determine a plan moving forward and that will include some tough decisions on individuals and shapes.

Nottingham Forest could have driven a bus through the middle of the park on Saturday night, two goals from counter-attacking situations engineered between the width of the centre circle. Twice the ostensible holding midfielder Anderson tried to nick possession, beaten to it, and City were turned around.

Noises coming from the dressing room suggest that Anderson is effectively being asked to operate as both a No6 and No8 when picked as the deepest of the three, to go and join play high up the pitch. That is Maresca leaning into the England international’s Action Man, everything to everyone style. That also relies on somebody covering for him.

That somebody does not exist in this current setup, Fernandez always too high and wide elsewhere.

So when they lose duels as happened at the City Ground, something the manager openly bemoaned, City are not stable enough to recover.

Liam Delap's fierce finish put Forest 2-0 ahead - and City were left playing catch-up

Club analysts have sat down with Anderson to go over video clips on how best to follow these instructions to the benefit of the team. Watching him, it’s hard not to conclude that this is a quality midfielder being asked to do too much as a single deep midfielder.

Guehi's England doubt England are sweating on the fitness of Marc Guehi as the Manchester City defender battles a hip injury. Guehi came off at half time of Saturday's 3-1 defeat by Nottingham Forest, with Thomas Tuchel's squad set to link up in London on Monday morning. With John Stones already out of Nations League ties with Croatia and Spain, Tuchel would be severely light on experience at centre half should Guehi not prove his fitness. JACK GAUGHAN

It will produce moments of sheer class – that lung-busting run up the right in Leipzig on Wednesday that bore hallmarks of Kevin De Bruyne, a perfect cross for Erling Haaland’s winner – while also leaving the defence exposed.

An exposed defence lends itself to a heightened chance of individual errors, plenty of those around at the moment, and it was noticeable at Forest that the opening goal came from uncertainty in possession. Josko Gvardiol made the error, eased off the ball by eventual goalscorer Jair Cunha, but the plan cannot be to have the left back with his back to goal and no viable passing options.

When Marc Guehi’s ball went into Gvardiol, Anderson was higher and wider on the right – deep in conversation with Abdukodir Khusanov about how they’d failed to move possession well enough earlier in the sequence – and Rayan Cherki was belatedly trotting back to offer himself.

Fernandez never once enters the frame, even when Cunha is in the box and subsequently wheeling away in celebration. Maresca rejected the suggestion that there is an issue with the team’s build-up on Saturday night.

As Man City look to build from the back in the third minute, Anderson (No 5) is busy delivering instructions to Khusanov (out of shot)...

... it means that when Guehi plays the ball to Gvardiol, he has his back to goal and nobody in midfield to pass to - and is already under pressure

... and with no support, three Forest players swarm and Jair Cunha dispossesses him, leading to him scoring the opening goal

What is clear though is that there is not yet that balance, that this is not yet a unit. Maresca moved to include Bouaddi with Anderson and Fernandez against Brighton – a one-goal defeat – but that acted as detrimental to creativity. If nothing else, Brighton proved that City require either Cherki or Phil Foden on the pitch at all times.

Over the past two games, Fernandez has lurked more menacingly at the back post, offering an additional goal threat rather than just relying on Haaland. That ghosting late run saw him score in Leipzig but for a joint-British record £125million needs to offer so much more. There will be growing calls for Bouaddi’s inclusion as a genuine deep-lying midfielder but it’s unlikely that the teenager can manage the league’s physicality as a single pivot.

The Moroccan has more chance of stamping his authority when alongside somebody else, dovetailing with an Anderson as a two. That leaves Fernandez, whose barnstorming league debut at Old Trafford feels like a long time ago now.

To persist with him, he either dislodges Cherki as the No10 on the promise of far more goals or Maresca drops him back into a more conventional role that allows Anderson to flourish properly.

Something has to give because the unevenness of City’s three is giving the rest of the team uncomfortable jitters.

Sports.title: Liverpool played like a team fighting for their manager, but Pierre Sage looks like a dead man walking, writes LEWIS STEELE - as Reds clinch morale-boosting win at sorry Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
Liverpool played like a team fighting for their manager, but Pierre Sage looks like a dead man walking, writes LEWIS STEELE - as Reds clinch morale-boosting win at sorry Crystal Palace

By this time of the season, spirited performances mean little if you don't have the results to go with it.

Pierre Sage, who was sacked at Lyon two years ago, knows as much as anyone that this is a results-based business.

And he simply has not had enough results. Despite having Liverpool on the ropes at times here, Crystal Palace failed to land a knockout blow and that could be that for their under-fire manager, who looked like a dead man walking when he trudged off the pitch at full-time with a face like thunder.

Former Lens over-achiever Sage now seems set for a stuffing six weeks before Christmas and though he may curse at the small margins that denied his team a chance of a heavyweight and potential job-saving scalp here, the boss knows two wins in 10 league games is not good enough.

Liverpool, meanwhile, had the width of the crossbar and a throwback performance from goalkeeper Alisson to thank. In contrast to Sage, Andoni Iraola's side showed grit and determination to win when far from their best.

Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak all scored as the Reds put a tough week behind them that saw them lose back-to-back games for the first time in the Iraola era, which prompted a chorus of the old terrace classic 'Poetry in Motion'.

Florian Wirtz scored a rare Liverpool as they won 3-1 at Crystal Palace in the Premier League

Wirtz scored Liverpool's second on 54 minutes as they ran out as 3-1 winners at Selhurst Park

Things are looking ominous for under-pressure Palace manager Pierre Sage after another loss

This performance was hardly William Wordsworth levels of poetry and Liverpool were far from on song during large swathes of this match but when it really mattered, the attackers demonstrated just why the club spent so much money on them.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS CRYSTAL PALACE (3-4-2-1): Henderson 5; Lerma 6, Richards 6, Disasi 5; Mingueza 6 (Khalali 87), Wharton 5, Timber 6 (Timber 60, 6), Mitchell 6; Kamada 6, Pino 7 (McNeil 87); Larsen 5 (Nketiah 72, 7) Subs not used: Benitez, Canvot, Chilwell, Doucoure, Hughes Booked: Pino, Lerma Scorers: Nketiah 90+5 Manager: Pierre Sage 7 LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 9; Araujo 7 (Gomez 90), Jacquet 6, Van Dijk 6, Kerkez 6; Szoboszlai 7 (Nyoni 69, 7), Mac Allister 8; Gakpo 6 (Ngumoha 76) Wirtz 8, Barcola 7 (Munoz 69, 7); Isak 7 (Koumas 90) Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Endo, McConnell, Tsimikas Booked: Araujo, Barcola, Munoz, Mac Allister Scorers: Mac Allister 40, Wirtz 54, Isak 89 Manager: Andoni Iraola 7 Referee: Tony Harrington 4

Mac Allister resumed his bemusing role of the team's best aerial threat despite being their smallest player, Wirtz got a goal and assist, while Isak made it eight for the season to continue his prolific streak.

Bradley Barcola, meanwhile, proved what an asset he is despite a wasteful first half.

Those attackers were worthy of praise but no one deserved plaudits more so than goalkeeper, Alisson, who was player of the match in an illustration of Palace's first-half supremacy.

'I'm very pleased with Alisson's performance,' said Iraola. 'He has commanded the box very well and in games here a lot of things are normally happening in the boxes. He has shown the level he has for us. Overall we are getting good results away from home at difficult stadiums.'

The Brazilian is in the last year of his contract but put in his best performance for 18 months, dating back to a 1-0 win at Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League knockouts. He will not go on international duty and instead rest up after an injury-hit few years.

He denied Adam Wharton with a glancing header, thwarted Daichi Kamada with a fierce shot and then tipped round Quenten Timber's effort from distance. Palace also rattled the bar through Yeremy Pino in a first half that really should have ended up differently.

Jorgen Strand Larsen also had the ball in the net but was offside.

As it was, though, Liverpool were the team to take their chance when it came after a period of dilly-dallying and playing the wrong ball, guilty again of indecisiveness similar to the flaws shown against Arsenal last weekend and in the 3-2 defeat at Fenerbahce in midweek.

Liverpool led on 40 minutes when Alexis Mac Allister (centre left) scored from close range

The Argentine celebrates after breaking the deadlock for the Reds in the Premier League clash

Sage facing the sack Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage is facing the sack after his side dropped to the bottom of the Premier League. Palace have won just two of their ten league matches this season, with Sunday's 3-1 defeat to Liverpool leaving them at the foot of the league for the first time in nearly nine years. Sage is expected to lose his job during the international break, with Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank leading the race to replace the French coach. However, Sage believes his side have been unlucky with results this season and has requested the hierarchy remain patient. The 47-year-old, who left RC Lens for Palace in the summer to succeed Oliver Glasner, also admitted the Palace squad needs strengthening - perhaps to absolve himself of some blame. 'You can create the links between these two things,' Sage replied when asked whether being bottom of the league heading into the international break could see him sacked. 'But a lot of times I've said we deserved better and it was the case again on Sunday. 'My job is not the most important thing, as I always said from the beginning. The most important thing is to find an efficient solution for the team and for the club. 'I know how important it is for the club to stay in the Premier League. The club just have to believe in that, and if it's not the case, they will take a decision. 'I always have confidence in myself because it's a big, big mistake to not be 100% involved in what I have to do. 'We have to adjust some positions during the winter transfer window to give more solutions and more efficiency and I think it will be okay.' By Bobby Manzi

Mac Allister was the scorer as he continued a fine resurgence this season, with Dominik Szoboszlai the supplier after a week where he too had been criticised. The Hungarian whipped a cross towards Mac Allister, which was glanced past Henderson for 1-0.

The former Brighton player ran straight towards the Palace fans behind the goal and taunted the supporters that were once his rivals on the south coast.

Liverpool weathered another storm at the start of the second half and soon found themselves two up. Barcola, who had left lots to be desired in the first half, swapped wings at the break and made his first attack count.

The Frenchman put the after-burners on and motored down the pitch before feeding Wirtz, who composed himself and passed into the net for 2-0. Iraola praised the run of Isak which took him away from the ball but dragged defenders with him to create space for his colleague.

Isak squandered a one-versus-one chance not long after but was not going to miss another one minutes later, when a blisteringly quick counter-attack was started by Trey Nyoni and ended with Wirtz feeding Isak, who skipped past Chris Richards and finished calmly.

The three goals will delight the hierarchy, with all three of the £100m boys – Isak, Barcola and Wirtz – registering at least one goal or assist apiece, one each in Wirtz's case.

Alexander Isak scored the visitors' third in the 89th-minute with this right-footed finish

Eddie Nketiah pulled one back for Palace from the penalty in second-half stoppage time

This victory would not have been possible, though, without Alisson, now 34 and in the final year of his deal. For all the attacking talent at Iraola's disposal, the Basque will be delighted at his team's defensive determination when under the kosh here as Palace had 10 first-half shots.

Iraola knows his team has flaws and they remain a work-in-progress. But despite a few challenging afternoons, they appear to be heading in the right direction.

The same cannot be said for Sage, whose side pulled one back in stoppage time through an Eddie Nketiah penalty after Milos Kerkez committed a careless foul.

Palace were unlucky in this game but the cold, hard truth is that the recent FA Cup and Europa Conference League triumphs feel a world away now as they enter the international break rock bottom of the Premier League.

West Ham also won a European trophy in the last five years and look where they ended up — that should set alarm bells ringing that no success lasts for ever and Palace are not too big for relegation.

Nketiah's goal felt like it was too little, too late and the sage advice for Palace supremo Steve Parish might be a reluctant change in the dugout.

Sports.title: Marco Rose's Bournemouth should not have the depth to win this many games domestically and abroad but at Ipswich they showed they can do it the hard way, writes JAMES SHARPE
Sports.content:
Marco Rose's Bournemouth should not have the depth to win this many games domestically and abroad but at Ipswich they showed they can do it the hard way, writes JAMES SHARPE

Juggling domestic duties with European adventures should not be as manageable as this for teams like Bournemouth.

Clubs of their size should be creaking under the weight of the extra fixtures. All those games, all that travelling. They have played nine games in a month.

Far bigger outfits have toiled spinning those plates. Remember when Ange Postecoglou stopped bothering about the Premier League entirely just to focus on the Europa League.

And yet here are those brilliant Cherries, three days after a win in Prague in that same competition, making it eight on the bounce with a victory at Ipswich thanks to Evanilson's opener, following goalkeeper Christian Walton's early howler, and an own goal from Leif Davis.

Bournemouth haven't done that since 2013 when they were getting out of League One.

Now, they are seventh in the Premier League, second in the Europa League.

Leif Davies reacts after scoring an own goal to make it 2-0 to Bournemouth

And they're in the League Cup quarter-finals – all while having the squad depth to name Alex Scott and Junior Kroupi on the bench.

Marco Rose's side showed they can also do it the hard way, too, after Jack Clarke's second-half penalty for Ipswich, given for a soft foul on Abdoul Ouattara, provided a far more tense final 15 minutes than anticipated inside a feverish Portman Road where Julio Enciso also twice went close from late free-kicks.

'One goal changed the momentum of the game and that's why I'm much more pleased about the last 20 minutes because we suffered but we did it together,' said Rose.

CALAMITY CHRISTIAN

First James Trafford, now Walton. Bournemouth's win over Leeds last weekend also hinged on a goalkeeping howler, when Trafford's simple pass out from the back was intercepted.

This time Ipswich stalwart Walton took a back pass from Dara O'Shea and decided the best course of action was to try to dummy and turn Evanilson. He failed, of course.

Evanilson rolled the ball into an empty net. That intense Bournemouth press really can do some crazy things to you.

MORE THAN A GOALSCORER

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS IPSWICH (4-2-3-1): Walton 4; Ouattara 5, Diop 6, O'Shea 6, Davis 5; Florentino 7 (Akpom 85), Palacios 6; Maeda 6 (Fatawu 65, 7), Enciso 7; Philogene 6 (Clarke 54, 7); Emersonn 5 (Flemming 54, 6) Scorers: Clarke pen 73 Booked: Enciso, Flemming Manager: Gary O'Neil 6 BOURNEMOUTH (4-2-3-1): Petrovic 6; Smith 6 (Diakite 79), Hill 7, Silva 7; Truffert 7; Adams 7, Christie 6 (Cook 67, 5); Rayan 6 (Adli 86), Kluivert 6 (Kroupi 68, 6), Tavernier 7; EVANILSON 8 (Rodriguez 85) Scorers: Evanlison 5, Davis OG 46 Booked: Smith, Tavernier, Silva Manager: Marco Rose 7 Referee: Simon Hooper 4 Att: 26,396

After scoring the opener in Bournemouth's win last weekend, manager Marco Rose told Evanilson that he was becoming a 'real No9'.

That's six goals now in his last seven games but it's his all-round play that's so impressive.

His goal came from leading the press.

He dropped in and played a beautiful curling through ball into the channel to set Justin Kluivert free down the right.

He collected the loose ball for the second goal.

He made a fine run to latch on to a free-kick over the defence to stab the ball over to James Hill at the back post, who headed over from close range, which would have put him level with Declan Rice as the leading assister in the league too.

'He's so hard-working,' added Rose. 'He does everything out of possession.

'He starts the press, he plays in between the lines, he gives us deep runs.

'But the most important thing is scoring and he understood that he also needs to arrive close to goal if he wants to score.'

SLOW STARTS COSTING IPSWICH

If the Tractor Boys are to make their stay in the Premier League a longer one than last time, they cannot afford to keep giving early leads. The mountain is steep enough.

Evanilson's opener was the sixth time Ipswich have conceded inside the first 15 minutes of a league game this season. They are yet to score one that early.

A howler from Ipswich keeper Christian Walton gifted Evanilson the opener

James Hill celebrates Bournemouth's win which lifts them to seventh

It is what will make this defeat especially frustrating for Gary O'Neil against his former club. 'Gary, what's the score?' chimed the travelling fans.

For so much of the contest, Ipswich looked composed and confident on the ball, played with energy and intent and, after they pulled one back, showed how much pressure they can put teams under and how much this place can bounce.

They are a much better side than the one that came up last time but you cannot come out after the break and have Ouattara give the ball straight to Evanilson again inside 30 seconds as he did before Ryan Christie's shot took two deflections and went in.

'Gutted,' said O'Neil. 'To lose a game that you haven't been outclassed is tough to take. We restricted Bournemouth to nothing of their own doing. If you give the ball to the opposition number nine twice, it's going to be difficult.'

Sports.title: To infinity and beyond! Another stunning Diego Gomez strike has Brighton up to SECOND and daring to dream... as Brentford's Igor Thiago is goaded into a red card
Sports.content:
Onwards and upwards go Brighton. Another victory to send them soaring into second place with only Arsenal above them.

It is a lofty perch for the Seagulls and one more admirable when considering the depths from which they have risen.

Homeless and penniless, on the brink of extinction at the end of the last century they are now daring to dream about the Champions League.

To infinity and beyond. Why not? Fabian Hurzeler’s team have already beaten Arsenal and Manchester City without conceding this season.

The only goals scored against them in the last six Premier League games came at Liverpool, where they lost 2-0 but were not outplayed.

City’s season is mired in uncertainty, awaiting sentence for financial breaches and the other half of the traditional Big Six are so erratic there will likely be scope for interlopers when the prized European tickets are handed out in May.

It is six months away but at this moment in time there are not four teams better than Fabian Hurzeler’s.

Brighton appear fully formed. Delightfully fluent in attack. Creative with zip and imagination and different ways to score goals.

There is a defined style of play. Solid at the back with enough sporting maturity to survive a test of needle, which this became against Brentford after the red card for Igor Thiago’s red card.

Diego Gomez celebrated another memorable strike at the Amex Stadium after his halfway-line stunner in the 5-0 win over Crystal Palace

The Bees already trailed to a screamer from the left boot of Diego Gomez and went further behind before half time when Pascal Gross converted a penalty awarded for a shirt pull by Keane Lewis-Potter on Luka Vuskovic.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Brighton (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen 6; Costinha 6, Dunk 6, Vuskovic 6, Boscagli 7; Gross 8, Andres 6 (Wieffer 46, ); Gomez 7 (Yalcoue 90+3), Ayari 7 (Hinshelwood 78), De Cuyper 7 (Minteh 82); Kostoulas 6 (Rutter 82) Subs not used: Steele, Hadjam, Kadioglu, Svoboda Scorers: Gomez 15, Gross 42 (pen) Bookings: Andres, Boscagli, Wieffer, Dunk Manager: Fabian Hurzeler 7 Brentford (4-3-3): Kelleher 6; Kayode 5, Ajer 6, Van den Berg 6 (Wilson 70), Lewis-Potter 5 (Diouf 59); Sangare 5 (Jensen 59), Janelt 5, Hickey 5 (Collins 46); Ouattara 4 (Yarmoliuk 46), Thiago 3, Schade 4 Subs not used: Valdimarsson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster Booked: Ajer, Schade Sent off: Thiago Manager: Keith Andrews 5 Referee: Michael Oliver 6 Attendance: 31,629

Gross, the 35-year-old midfielder schemer who walloped his penalty into the top corner in emphatic fashion, embodies the confidence pulsing through this team and his goal closed the contest.

The Bees assembled in the deep looking to minimise damage with an eye on a counterattack or a set piece and maybe hoping the officials would see fit to even it up at 10 against 10.

It didn’t happen. Instead, Brighton controlled the ball. They have had more than 75 per cent of possession across 90 minutes and spent the second half probing around the fringes of the Brentford penalty area.

They registered 20 shots in all but there would be no third goal. And nobody minded. They celebrated the victory and a return to the Amex Stadium after five away games in a row and more than 5,000 miles on the road.

Every substitution made by Hurzeler came as a reminder of their strength and quality.

Kaoru Mitoma, yet to feature this season, is expected back from injury soon after the international break.

The Conference League is not proving a distraction to a squad of such depth and Hurzeler gave fans his permission to dream.

'They should be always excited,' said the Brighton boss. 'That’s our job. They can dream. They can have high expectations, but these are things we can’t control. We played good game but always things we can do better.'

Bees' red mist…

This was Brentford’s second defeat in this Premier League season and they had players sent off in both.

'In both scenarios the opposition player has been the one to provoke the situation, antagonise our player and react towards our player in an aggressive way,' fumed boss Keith Andrews, referring to Yehor Yarmoliuk’s red card against Liverpool, when the Bees finished the game with nine men.

'We should do better, but the game is in a state now and a place I don’t particularly like. And we’ll have to have a look at that because it’s costing us.'

Chema Andres fouled Thiago, fell to the ground and sprang up to confront the Brazilian, who tried to push him away but caught him with a forearm under the jaw.

Igor Thiago's yellow card was upgraded to red after a VAR intervention

Andres collapsed for a second time. When Michael Oliver gave them a yellow card each it seemed fair, but VAR Stuart Attwell sent the referee to the pitch-side screens for a review.

Oliver studied the slow-motion replays and upgraded it to a red card. Off went Thiago, smiling wryly and shaking his head, dismissed for standing his ground and being goaded into a reaction.

He will miss games against Everton, Manchester United and Arsenal.

Opinions of Oliver in the away end did not improve when he gave a penalty for a shirt pull by 5ft 7in Keane Lewis-Potter which somehow sent 6ft 4in Luka Vuskovic somersaulting to the turf.

Luka’s flying…

Vuskovic is already a favourite at the Amex Stadium and it is easy to forget he is only 19. He dominates in the air and reads the game like a seasoned central defender.

And after ten games he is ten points better off than those he left behind at Tottenham.

The Croatia international cannot be looking forward to yet another encounter with England. The two nations meet at Wembley on Thursday. England have put 11 past them in two games this year.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso must look at HIMSELF, not the officials, as another questionable line-up sees Chelsea fold at Sunderland - and Cole Palmer has a stinker in miserable response to Tuchel snub, writes KIERAN GILL
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso must look at HIMSELF, not the officials, as another questionable line-up sees Chelsea fold at Sunderland - and Cole Palmer has a stinker in miserable response to Tuchel snub, writes KIERAN GILL

When searching for why Chelsea were beaten by the side who were sitting bottom of the Premier League, the temptation from Xabi Alonso might be to describe this defeat as a tale of two penalties.

First, Chelsea were denied one when Cole Palmer was sandwiched by Luke O'Nien and Jules Ahoka as he entered the Sunderland area, with the officials concluding the contact occurred outside of the box.

Then, Sunderland were awarded one when Brian Brobbey was brought down by Levi Colwill. The striker had hold of the defender at the same time, and arguably clipped his own heel upon second viewing, but Enzo Le Fee gladly accepted the opportunity to score the game's own goal.

However, it would be wrong to blame this deserved defeat on those two decisions alone. Referee Jarred Gillett and VAR Nick Hopton were weak but not the reason that Chelsea lost.

This was actually a two of two strikers. Sunderland had one in the brilliant bully that is Brobbey, whereas Chelsea had nobody after Alonso yet again decided against starting Danny Welbeck.

In the three Premier League games played since Joao Pedro's injury – against Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and now Sunderland – Alonso has gone with Morgan Rogers as a false nine once and Pedro Neto twice. Welbeck was on the bench in all of those matches.

Sunderland handed Chelsea a brutal reality check as they climbed off the foot of the table

The visitors fell victim to two questionable penalty calls at the Stadium of Light

We are not saying the 35-year-old is the answer to all of Alonso's problems, but he is an actual No9 who scored 13 times in the Premier League for Brighton last season.

Neto was hardly going to have a high success rate when wrestling with centre backs for the long balls which were coming from Colwill and Co. It is a question that needs asking, therefore, especially after another loss.

Why did Chelsea sign Welbeck if not to play when Joao Pedro is injured?

Welbeck came on in the 62nd minute here, but by then, a familiar feeling was washing over Chelsea.

They lost 2-1 here at the very end of last season. Malo Gusto scored an own goal, Wesley Fofana was red carded, and Chelsea, managed by Calum McFarlane in the interim, failed to qualify for any form of European football.

They smacked of an utterly unserious side then, and resembled it here, too.

Chelsea had a week to prepare for this Premier League clash while Sunderland were playing – and losing – to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League.

Regis Le Bris' side had not won in the league since August. Yet they were the sharper of the two teams here.

It hardly helped Alonso that Chelsea's attackers never appeared at it individually.

Cole Palmer had a stinker. This was supposed to be an opportunity to show why Thomas Tuchel made a mistake in not naming him in his latest England squad. If anything, he helped make sure those accusations cannot be levelled at Tuchel over this break.

Xabi Alonso tinkered with his line-up and it failed to pay off in a second defeat in three games

Cole Palmer had a stinker in a woeful response to Thomas Tuchel's England snub

Rogers' performance was best summed up by the time he simply sprinted out of play with the ball to gift Sunderland a goal-kick. He and Palmer resembled no-shows.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Sunderland (4-2-3-1): Roefs 6; Hume 7, Mukiele 7, O'Nien 6, Mandava 7; Xhaka 6 (Ahoka 4, 6), Sadiki 7; Meunier 6, Talbi 6 (Rigg 88), Le Fee 6 (Angulo 88); Brobbey 8 (Isidor 67, 6) Subs (not used): Ellborg, Danso, Methalie, Fofana, Tutierov Scorers: Le Fee (36 pen) Booked: Ahoka, Meunier, Brobbey, O'Nien, Angulo Manager: Regis Le Bris 7 Chelsea (4-3-3): Penders 6; Palestra 5 (Gusto 62, 5), Fofana 5, Colwill 4 (Estevao 45, 6), Chavarria 5 (Quenda 79); Caicedo 6, Lavia 6, Henderson 6 (Emegha 87); Palmer 4, Neto 5 (Welbeck 62, 5), Rogers 4 Subs (not used): Sharman-Lowe, Barco, Anselmino, Nicoll-Jazuli Booked: Colwill, Neto, Caicedo, Fofana Manager: Xabi Alonso 4 Referee: Jarred Gillett 4

Neto looked like a lost little boy trying to lead Chelsea's line in the absence of Joao Pedro.

The half-time statistics said Chelsea had sent more open-play crosses into Sunderland's box in the opening 45 minutes than in their entire games v Fulham, Everton, Tottenham, Manchester United, Bournemouth and Brighton.

Except, they had no striker for Alonso's full backs Marco Palestra or Pep Chavarria to try to find. Just 5ft 8in Neto and the odd other box-crasher.

Trailing 1-0 at half-time here, Alonso made a singular substitution. It was to introduce Estevao for Colwill, who had been tormented by Brobbey.

Le Bris was asked in his post-match press conference if there is another player like his striker in the Premier League. He thought long and hard before answering: 'What do you think? I don't think so. His physicality, his intensity, it's impressive, that's for sure. The build-up is so important to have a target man.'

Alonso chipped in on Brobbey: 'He is not unstoppable. He is stoppable but only when you defend better than we did.' On his own attack, he added: 'We didn't produce enough to deserve to win.'

Sunderland's tactic of hoofing the ball up to Brobbey worked wonders. He scared the daylights out of Chelsea's centre backs. When Fofana first arrived at the Stadium of Light, a Chelsea fan shouted at him as he got off the bus. 'Fofana, please be on the bench,' he said. Fofana may have been wishing he was a substitute as well whenever he was wrestling with Brobbey.

It was the long-ball approach which led to Sunderland winning their penalty. They smashed it towards the top of the pitch and Brobbey bullied Colwill. Sunderland won their spot-kick and, in truth, deserved the lead for the sheer energy they brought to this match.

Alonso is ten Premier League games into his Chelsea career. The honeymoon period is over. Sunderland lost their captain Granit Xhaka to an injury after two minutes here. Chelsea had named a line-up featuring three midfielders. But they never showed any signs of control, and for that, Alonso should be looking at himself and his own side rather than the refereeing team.

Sports.title: England 45-22 Australia PLAYER RATINGS: Who made up for giving his opponents a gift? Who was strong as an ox? And which star MUST keep his place despite aerial faux pas?
Sports.content:
England 45-22 Australia PLAYER RATINGS: Who made up for giving his opponents a gift? Who was strong as an ox? And which star MUST keep his place despite aerial faux pas?

England got their autumn campaign off to a superb start with a 45-22 win over Australia at Twickenham on Sunday that saw them land a bonus point and go second in the Nations Championship table. Here's how Daily Mail Sport rated their performances...

George Furbank – 7

His miserable luck has meant he hasn’t appeared as much as he’s deserved. Penalised for a neck-roll tackle but key involvement in Jack van Poortvliet try.

Tommy Freeman – 7

Did well to stay calm and execute with tricky try-scoring assist for Van Poortvliet. Must be retained at wing. Penalised for one aerial faux pas.

Henry Slade – 8

Would have been disappointed not to have stopped Isaac Henry but deserved star accolade as he showed nice hands in contact as England pulled clear. Strong defence at the death.

Seb Atkinson – 7

His appearances at first receiver with No 10 Fin Smith peeling behind delivered promising signs. Worrying that he limped off in the second half as he’s a growing presence.

Henry Slade stops Australia's Max Jorgensen from scoring a try

Immanuel Feyi-Waboso – 8

Beat seven defenders in the first 40. Had try ruled out. Suffered hip-drop tackle and failed to appear for second half, leaving Henry Pollock on the wing who scored twice.

Fin Smith – 7

Recovered from calf injury to start. Quietly effective in the playmaker position and his last-gasp tackle got Slade out of trouble. Moved to centre with Atkinson off.

Jack van Poortvliet – 7

He gifted Australia a way back into the game just before the half-time whistle when he was intercepted by Max Jorgensen but made amends when game resumed.

Fin Baxter – 7

Scrum wasn’t always dominant but a decent enough return to Test duty for the Harlequins prop after two foot operations.

Jack van Poortvliet runs in England's fourth try after gifting Australia a way back in

Jamie George – 7

Spoke out to defend his coach pre-match then did his talking on the field with early maul try which made him England’s highest scoring forward. One wonky line-out throw.

Joe Heyes – 7

Smashed Declan Meredith but gave up a free-kick and then a penalty at the scrum. Responded with England’s third try.

Maro Itoje (capt) – 8

Back in the side after a summer off and looked all the better for it. Executed a first-half charge down and rip in contact.

Alex Coles – 6

Named as a second row, but packed down at scrums on the flank with Ollie Chessum at lock alongside Itoje. Part of dominant pack.

Captain Maro Itoje was back in style after having the summer off

Ollie Chessum – 7

Switched places with Coles at the set-piece. Finished well in the wide channel for his team’s second try and showed athleticism with a line-out steal.

Ben Curry – 6

His forward pass meant Feyi-Waboso was denied. A fine piece of breakdown work showed why he was selected.

Ben Earl – 8

No real X Factor moments but got through a mountain of work and did his basics very well indeed. Strong as an ox in contact.

Replacements: Henry Pollock 8 (for Feyi-Waboso 41min), Luke Cowan-Dickie 6 (for George 56), Greg Fisilau 7 (for Curry 56), Ellis Genge 7 (for Baxter 56), George Martin 6 (for Coles 63), Will Stuart 6 (for Heyes 63), Marcus Smith 5 (for Atkinson 64), Ben Spencer 7 (for Van Poortvliet 74).

Henry Pollock scored two tries after coming off the bench at half-time

AUSTRALIA: Tom Wright 4; Max Jorgensen 5, Isaac Henry 5 (Filipo Daugunu 58,7), Len Ikitau 6, Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii 5; Declan Meredith 4 (Ben Donaldson 54,5), Ryan Lonergan 7 (Tate McDermott 71,5); Angus Bell 4 (Isaac Kailea 64,5), Billy Pollard 6 (Josh Nasser 56,5), Allan Alaalatoa 5 (Taniela Tupou 48,5), Josh Canham 7, Lukhan Salakaia-Loto 5 (Rob Valetini 47,5), Jeremy Williams 7, Fraser McReight 6 (Carlo Tizzano 64,5), Harry Wilson (capt) 7.

Sports.title: Furious Andoni Iraola slams VAR again despite Liverpool winning - 'I'm very upset'
Sports.content:
Furious Andoni Iraola slams VAR again despite Liverpool winning - 'I'm very upset'

Liverpool head into the international break on the back of a win over Crystal Palace, but Andoni Iraola refused to let Palace's late consolation from the penalty spot slide

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola was furious at the decision to give Crystal Palace a penalty (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola was "very upset" after a controversial penalty decision cost Liverpool a clean sheet in victory at Crystal Palace.

‌



‌



Liverpool head into the international break fourth in the Premier League thanks to a 3-1 win at Selhurst Park. Goals from Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak made sure of the points before Eddie Nketiah netted from the spot in injury time.

‌



The consolation goal for Palace came after Milos Kerkez was penalised following a clash of heads with Dario Osorio in the box. Referee Tony Harrington pointed to the spot after the clash which occurred while both players tried to head a bouncing ball.

‌



His call was confirmed by VAR Michael Salisbury and Nketiah beat Alisson from 12 yards to get on the scoresheet. Iraola was furious last weekend after Isak was not given a penalty in the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal for a clear shirt-pull by Jurrien Timber and he made his case once again on Sunday.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"I am very upset because the ones in our box they are calling penalties and in the other box they are not. I know we are 3-0 and it's the 95th minute but I'm very upset," he told Sky Sports.

"It's a head to head but even then it's Osario to Milos. It's a clash of heads. You can say it's 3-0 but, for me, there is more because it is not the first time this season and you compare... I'm really upset.

‌



"The VAR took a lot of time. When you call a penalty and they are two minutes. Two repetitions, three repetitions, they are finding a way not to be called by the VAR. A clean sheet is not cheap in the Premier League and we wanted to win 3-0. It is not just because of this penalty, it's because of a lot of things."

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Eddie Nketiah tucked away the penalty late on (Image: Henry Nicholls / AFP via Getty Images)

Liverpool took the lead through Mac Allister's flicked header at the near post before Wirtz tucked in Bradley Barcola's cutback on the break for 2-0. Isak showed a cool head to bury his seventh Premier League goal in nine appearances to make the points safe.

‌



But Liverpool's fifth clean sheet in the league this season was not forthcoming as Kerkez was penalised and Nketiah beat Alisson with his penalty into the corner.

"It was an important win for us going into the international break after the week we've had," Iraola added. "Also, we arrived very late Thursday night from Turkey so - I know they also played - it was important to finish with a win.

Article continues below

"First half we struggled a little bit defensively but after we closed the game quite well even if I'm a little bit upset with the last penalty."

Sports.title: Liverpool's patience with Alexander Isak pays off as win puts Pierre Sage on the brink
Sports.content:
This season will probably be more about securing Champions League football rather than a full-on title race.

But after results like this, you can see why Liverpool fans have bought into Andoni Iraola’s exciting vision because they were ruthless, clinical and determined as they climbed up into the top four.

Their patience with Alexander Isak has reaped rewards because the Liverpool striker now looks unstoppable after his eighth goal in all competitions sealed the win.

The Liverpool faithful are also still enthusiastically singing Bradley Barcola’s name even though the £123million signing has yet to score in the Premier League since his summer arrival. And, frankly, under-pressure Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage had better hope he gets as much understanding and sees out the forthcoming international break (also known as the sacking window).

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

This was so much better from Palace and, if it had not been for Liverpool keeper Alisson Becker’s heroics, then the score line could have been very different. Instead, Palace have sunk to the bottom of the Premier League table, have the worst defensive record in the division - they have conceded 24 goals - and you suspect Sage will be waiting by the phone in the next fortnight.

It will be a tough decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish because he rarely gets it wrong and he will have seen from the directors’ box the score line was harsh on his team. Yes, there were familiar mistakes and hard luck stories but Palace showed real heart this time and they deserved more than just substitute Eddie Nketiah’s injury-time consolation from the penalty spot.

‌



But the question now for Parish is whether an improved performance is enough or if they should press the panic button and get on the phone to Sean Dyche in the next fortnight. It will probably be the latter.

View 3 Images Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage may have reached the end of the line (Image: Steve Bardens/Getty Images)

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Palace do not have Liverpool’s resources but even big-money talent like Barcola, Isak and Florian Wirtz take time to settle. It was far from a flowing Liverpool performance, but they got the job done.

‌



It seems bizarre to make the keeper from the winning side the best player on the pitch but they would have lost without Alisson. The Brazil keeper still probably does not get the credit he deserves.

Liverpool’s goal lived a charmed life early on as Yeremy Pino crashed a shot against the bar with one of those efforts where the commentator says he “almost hit it too well.” What on earth does that mean?

Jorgen Strand Larsen had the ball in the Liverpool net but was very clearly offside. Palace midfielder Daichi Kamada’s powerful volley forced another brilliant save from the Liverpool keeper who also denied Adam Wharton.

At the other end, Liverpool had plenty of possession but their finishing was wayward as Barcola skied over with a volley which cleared the stand and the crossbar.

‌



View 3 Images Florian Wirtz scored on the break for Liverpool (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

But finally, Liverpool got their breakthrough after a moment of controversy. Referee Tony Harrington gave a free kick when it looked as if Cody Gakpo had just run into Jefferson Lerma. It looked so harsh.

Dominik Szoboszlai whipped in a near post free kick and there was Alexis Mac Allister to glance home past Palace keeper Dean Henderson. Unsurprisingly, the Palace fans vented their anger at the officials. Parish had his head in his hands in the directors’ box.

The trouble is, once Liverpool got themselves in front, there was only ever going to be one outcome. And maybe that is the most damning thing for Sage. Liverpool’s second came nine minutes after the restart.

‌



Barcola’s low cross evaded the Palace defence and Florian Wirtz swept home from inside the box. Wirtz then set up Isak to score in the 89th minute.

There was still time for Palace to get a consolation. Milos Kerkez jumped into Dario Osorio and it was a clear penalty which Nketiah converted. You fear it may not be enough to save Sage.

Sports.title: Gary Neville makes bizarre confession about brother Phil on live TV
Sports.content:
Gary Neville makes bizarre confession about brother Phil on live TV

The two defenders played alongside each other for Manchester United and England before their careers took different turns

View 2 Images Gary Neville had to ask his brother Phil where he lived. (Image: NBC Sports/YouTube.)

Gary Neville has admitted that he doesn’t know specifically where his brother Phil lives in America. The pair were reunited for the first time in three years as they both appeared on NBC Sports' Premier League coverage.

‌



‌



Since they both retired from playing, their careers have taken different paths. Phil has taken more of a coaching role, having previously managed England Women before moving to the USA to manage Inter Miami in 2021.

‌



His most recent position saw him spend just over two years as manager of Portland Timbers. He left the job back in May after 95 matches in charge.

‌



Arsenal rivals put on notice as 'worrying' title claim made after Hull City win READ MORE :

Gary, meanwhile, has made his name in punditry. He makes regular appearances on Sky Sports’ coverage of the Premier League, as well as the Overlap Podcast.

But this weekend has seen both brothers working together again. They were both part of NBC Sports’ coverage of Nottingham Forest vs Manchester City.

Opening the programme, presenter Rebecca Lowe said: “How about this? A little bit of television history about to be made. Phil Neville and Gary Neville on television together on a show for the first time ever, am I right?”

‌



Gary then responded with: "Absolutely. We've not seen each other for three years either."

Phil, then said: "He doesn't know where I live." It's something that Lowe confirmed. "Correct. He actually doesn't," she added.

‌



"He actually asked Phil, 'Whereabouts do you live?' before we came on air. As you sit here together for the first time ever on television, how does it feel?"

Phil answered: "Well, it's just nice to see him. We obviously spent a lot of time together in our careers.

‌



"I live in America, he lives in England, and hopefully tonight we can have a nice glass of wine."

Gary then added: "It's brilliant. We don't see each other, obviously, that much anymore.

‌



View 2 Images Phil Neville was brother Gary's assistant manager at Valencia. (Image: Manuel Queimadelos Alonso/Getty Images)

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"Phil's been in America with Miami and Portland for the last four or five years, and now he's living in Florida, apparently. Very nice place! It beats Manchester. I wish I was there."

The two brothers played together as teammates for both Man United and England 287 times. The duo lifted six Premier League titles, three FA Cups and the Champions League together.

‌



They also worked together briefly during Gary’s stint as Valencia manager in 2015, when Phil joined as assistant. They, however, only lasted 16 league games, winning just three of those.

Speaking in November last year, Phil spoke about his relationship with his brother, amid his induction into the Premier League Hall of Fame. "We are best friends," he told the Premier League.

‌

"That doesn't change if I am on the other side of the world. The first message I receive after most games and before games is from him.

"Because of our relationship, because he is my brother and best friend, only at moments like this, when he gets the recognition that he deserves, do you realise how special your best friend and brother is. What is nice is that he is now getting recognition outside the people who are closest to him."

Sports.title: Arsenal rivals put on notice as 'worrying' title claim made after Hull City win
Sports.content:
Arsenal rivals put on notice as 'worrying' title claim made after Hull City win

Premier League champions Arsenal are already building a healthy lead at the top of the table after recording nine wins from their opening 10 league games this season

View 2 Images Danny Murphy says there is much more to come from Arsenal (Image: BBC)

Premier League title hopefuls should be concerned that Arsenal are already six points clear at the summit despite struggling to hit top form, says Danny Murphy.

‌



‌



The Gunners finally beat Manchester City to the title last term after three consecutive second-placed finishes to end an agonising 22-year wait for glory and were swiftly installed as the red-hot favourites to retain their newly acquired domestic crown.

‌



Mikel Arteta's men have quickly found their way back to the top of the table and Saturday's unspectacular 1-0 win over Hull City opened up a six point gap over City, who may also face a significant points penalty after being found guilty of breaching financial rules.

‌



Arsenal have so far managed to accumulate a healthy advantage without hitting the heights of their performances last season - and Murphy feels that is bad news for any side with aspirations of wrestling the title away from the champions.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"I think what’s worrying for everyone else is they’ve got this amount of wins, this amount of points, and they haven’t really played that well," Murphy said on Match of the Day.

"Maybe in the Chelsea game they were outstanding but they’ve just got over the line other than that."

‌



The former Liverpool and England midfielder added: "There’s more to come from this team, make no qualms about that. I think they’re in a wonderful position and a really great place."

Jamie Redknapp echoed similar sentiments after Manchester City dropped points, falling to a third defeat in a row at the hands of Nottingham Forest. He claims that Brighton could yet emerge as Arsenal's biggest challengers - but feels Arteta's men will runaway with the league as the season goes on.

‌



View 2 Images Martin Odegaard scored the only goal of the game as Arsenal beat Hull City on Saturday (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

"If you look at the league table, I think right now, probably the one you’d point to, and I never thought I’d say this at the start of the year, but it’s Brighton," he said on Sky Sports.

‌



"Arsenal have got Saliba coming back, the players they’ve got defensively, you’d never see Arsenal look as open as we saw Manchester City look [against Forest].

"I don’t really see anything else other than Arsenal running away with this title at the moment. I know it’s really early but I just think they’re so much better than everyone else in every single area.

Article continues below

"It’s the worst-case scenario for every team, when you see a team like that. Today they grind out a result; I just don’t see anybody else."

Sports.title: Man Utd legend's honest reaction sums up decline as they drop into bottom three
Sports.content:
Man Utd legend's honest reaction sums up decline as they drop into bottom three

Nottingham Forest's win on Saturday meant that Manchester United dropped into the relegation zone as their dire season reached new lows

View 2 Images Dimitar Berbatov has his head in his hands when Man Utd dropped into the bottom three (Image: Bein Sports)

Dimitar Berbatov was left in disbelief as Manchester United fell into the relegation zone after Saturday's results.

‌



‌



The Bulgarian played at Old Trafford from 2008 until 2012 back when the club were serial winners and relegation was never even a prospect. The club have fallen massively from those heights and have endured their worst ever start to a Premier League season.

‌



Michael Carrick's side have won just one of their nine games so far this term and Nottingham Forest's 3-1 win over Manchester City on Saturday saw them leapfrog United at the wrong end of the table.

‌



It means they now sit in the bottom three, only above Crystal Palace and Sunderland, where they will remain if they don't beat Aston Villa on Sunday - and Berbatov could not hide his shame.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Berbatov, who won two Premier League titles during his time in Manchester, said: “I don’t believe it, but the way United are playing sometimes they deserve to be there honestly.”

He was left with his head in his hands but then added with some optimism: “Tomorrow they still have a game.”

‌



United haven't won in the league since August, when they beat Ipswich at home. Since then they've endured some horrific results, losing 3-0 to Bournemouth the last time they played in front of their own fans. Carrick has held onto his job despite mounting pressure and he'll need to beat a Villa side that are on the up if they are to avoid the embarrassment of being in the relegation zone during the international break.

View 2 Images Dimitar Berbatov won a host of titles during his time in Manchester (Image: Man Utd via Getty Images)

‌



The Red Devils may take hope from Villa's poor recent record at Old Trafford. Unai Emery ‘s side, for all their good work in recent years, have lost in all of their last three visits to the red side of Manchester.

United's worst finish in the Premier League era remains the 15th position they recorded in 2024/25, when Ruben Amorim took over midway through the campaign from Erik ten Hag. They would lose 18 of their 38 games that season.

Sports.title: Tommy Robinson involved in brawl after boxer jumps out of ring to attack him
Sports.content:
Tommy Robinson involved in brawl after boxer jumps out of ring to attack him

The influencer fight night in Ireland was brought to an end following the brawl between Tommy Robinson and Mo Deen

View 2 Images Chaos unfolded at The Hub in Kilkenny between Robinson and Deen

Tommy Robinson was caught up in a violent brawl at an influencer boxing event in Ireland after fighter Mo Deen leapt out of the ring and lunged towards him. The chaotic scenes unfolded at The Hub in Kilkenny during a fight night that was due to be headlined by a clash between rappers Russ Millions and Kirky.

‌



‌



Deen had been competing on the undercard against fellow influencer MrTikTokUK, securing a stoppage victory after knocking his opponent down three times. However, tensions boiled over shortly after the bout when promoters attempted to drum up excitement for a potential future fight between Deen and Robinson.

‌



Deen jumped over the announcers' desk in an attempt to confront Robinson, who had been watching from ringside. Despite the initial disruption, organisers pressed ahead with plans for an in-ring face-off between the pair, with influencer HSTikkyTokky, whose real name is Harrison Sullivan, attempting to bring them together.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Anthony Joshua's leaked text messages are warning to Tyson Fury READ MORE :

Robinson, the former English Defence League (EDL) leader, was met with a hostile reception from sections of the crowd before appearing to taunt Deen with a book. The pair then became involved in a physical confrontation, sparking a mass brawl that spread throughout the venue.

Chairs were reportedly thrown as the disorder escalated, with hundreds of spectators caught up in the chaotic scenes. Officials eventually intervened, forcing Sullivan to bring the event to an early end.

‌



Speaking afterwards, Deen said: "Listen, I just want to make this clear to every person in the UK and outside of the UK. I'm not trying to cause problems. This is like WWE, they said 'listen, this is what this situation is.' I followed the scripts, I'm getting death threats, people trying to kill me - what the hell?

"I don't know about this - I just know this is what we have to do. What's the problem? Why is everyone trying to kill me right now? I don't know what's going on, and this is a message to all of you. The supporters for Tommy... Bro it's kicking off outside, man.

‌

"This is a message to all of Tommy supporters, I just followed the script that they told me they agreed with. So what's everyone trying to attack me for? You know what I'm trying to say? This is what they told me. Tommy's agreed with it, they've agreed with it. I followed it.

‌



"Look at my hands man [shaking], this is not fair bro. It's not fair. I don't know what's going on, this whole thing is crazy. If anyone tries to attack me or do something to me, I'm just following the script - I don't know about all of this. That's going to be the series. I just want everyone to calm down.

View 2 Images Mo Deen has since addressed the brawl

‌



"I'm just about love bro, I never tried problems with nobody. Hopefully anyone that's with Tommy and his friends, I'm trusting Elon Musk, whoever, don't put hits on me bro. This is all going left, I don't know what's going to happen - I'm just saying my part, you know? I don't want this. I don't want no trouble.

"I love the UK. I love the Queen, I've been praying for the Queen ever since I jumped on social media, I pray for this country, I love every English person more than anyone, more than my own people. So this is not right, what has happened and people hating me. Anyone watching, I love you guys, I love the UK more than anything.

Article continues below

"I prayed for the Queen, it's all over TikTok, when she died, God bless her, I prayed for her and everyone saw that so what's the problem? This is just what they told me to do. God bless you man, I don't know what else to say."

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua's leaked text messages are warning to Tyson Fury
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua's leaked text messages are warning to Tyson Fury

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are finally expected to end their decade-long feud next month, and it is apparent that 'AJ' is leaving no stone unturned

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua (Image: Getty Images for Netflix)

Derek Chisora is seeing promising signs after revealing he is regularly in contact with Anthony Joshua ahead of his fight with Tyson Fury.

The two heavyweight hard-hitters will finally settle their 10-year rivalry once and for all on December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff. Joshua will be working with trainer Ben Davison once again - two years after they split following 'AJ's' crushing knockout loss to Daniel Dubois.

Davison famously cornered Fury for five fights and was instrumental in helping the 'Gypsy King' out of his drink-and-drug fuelled depression and back to the ring. Joshua's decision to reunite with Davison has sent shockwaves around the world of boxing, but it is evident he is leaving no stone unturned.

And Joshua's close friend Chisora has recently given fans an insight into how 'AJ's' training is going after revealing that the pair have been holding regular chats over the phone. During an interview with talkSPORT, he said: "I speak to him every Friday after his week of training camp.

Conor McGregor clears up retirement confusion ahead of final fight READ MORE :

"I send him a message asking him how it was, and he said 'yeah I'm killing it'. So that is all I need to know, he's killing it. Whatever happens it is going to be an exciting fight on December 11."

Given how Chisora has faced Fury three times, the British heavyweight veteran may opt to pass on some crucial tips to his good friend ahead of fight night. Joshua will need all the help he can get - with Fury set to enter fight night as a big favourite.

Sports.title: What Michael Carrick knows about Man Utd future ahead of crunch Aston Villa clash
Sports.content:
What Michael Carrick knows about Man Utd future ahead of crunch Aston Villa clash

Michael Carrick is a man under pressure and continues to be in the dark regarding his future as Manchester United look to avoid dropping into the bottom three

View 2 Images Michael Carrick remains a man firmly under pressure (Image: OLI SCARFF, AFP via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has been given no assurances that he will remain as Manchester United boss after their clash with Aston Villa on Sunday afternoon.

‌



‌



Ahead of kick-off the Red Devils do find themselves in the bottom three following Nottingham Forest's win. Incredibly they are just two points off being bottom of the Premier League.

‌



They still have just one win to their name, that coming over Ipswich back in August, and they're in the midst of a poor run that could be extended by Unai Emery's side. As a result Carrick's future has come under serious threat and the United board know they could be forced into acting.

‌



This is already United's worst ever start to a Premier League season but it could reach new lows if they find themselves in the relegation zone come November's international break.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The upcoming pause in the domestic game is also traditionally when clubs would opt to make a change in the dugout, given the extended time to prepare for their next game. Carrick has continued to field questions over his future, but insists he's been given no assurances, nor does he need any, reports The Sun.

In midweek United calmed the noise somewhat, although only after coming back from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2. Questions have been raised over whether that can be a turning point, or whether it simply covered the cracks that have been exposed all season.

‌



Carrick, who was only given the job permanently in the summer, could yet be the third man axed by the Ineos hierarchy, who themselves have come in for huge criticism. The United boss though has maintained he doesn't need any kind of refresh despite the upcoming break.

View 2 Images If Man Utd are to make a change in the dugout then the international break is seen as the ideal time (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"I think international breaks are always a time when, talking about the players that aren’t going away and for the staff, I think there is a little bit (of time) to re-energise and freshen up," he said.

"I think some of the players that go away in internationals, they get freshened up in a different environment, so there is an element of that, but I don’t really need it. I’m fine as I am."

Article continues below

United face a huge clash on their return to action later in November, heading to Anfield to face arch rivals Liverpool.
