Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

YouTube YouTube , which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enable YouTube cookies or to allow those cookies just once. You can change your settings at any time via the This content is provided by, which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Boxing world stunned by 'worst injury ever seen' as British fighter, 29, is left with gruesome swelling after nasty head collision - as fans question why bout wasn't stopped earlier
Sports.content:
Boxing world stunned by 'worst injury ever seen' as British fighter, 29, is left with gruesome swelling after nasty head collision - as fans question why bout wasn't stopped earlier

Boxing fans were left stunned as Zak Miller's title fight was called off with the Englishman suffering horrific facial swellings.

The 29-year-old from Manchester was fighting in his home city against Gully Powar, on the undercard of Joshua Buatsi vs Willy Hutchinson.

The featherweight bout was ended after 10 rounds following an accidental clash of heads in the seventh that left Miller with gruesome injuries.

With huge swellings on his face and cuts around his eyes, a doctor examined him in round nine before allowing the fight to continue.

Then referee Mark Lyson intervened shortly afterwards, waving off the bout as Miller was left disfigured with a huge lump above his left eye, one on his forehead and another below his right eye.

The injuries appeared to be a hematoma, severe swellings caused by damage where blood pools under the skin.

The fight went straight to the scorecards, with 24-year-old Powar taking the judges' verdict 96-95, 97-94 and 96-94 to land the vacant British featherweight title.

The fight has been STOPPED due to severe swelling on Zak Miller’s face! 😬#BuatsiHutchinson2 | Live NOW on DAZN ▪️ pic.twitter.com/ePPcK5SiPA — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) November 7, 2026

Zak Miller was left with horrendous facial swellings after a head collision

Miller and Gully Powar fought on but the swellings got worse

Miller's face was disfigured as a result of the cuts and swellings

Referee Mark Lyson intervened at the end of the 10th round, with judges awarding the win to Powar

Former world champion Carl Frampton, presenting on DAZN, described the swelling as 'the worst I've ever seen'.

And fans struggled to believe the fight had been allowed to continue, with one posting on X: 'Zak Miller needs to change his corner, the fact that the ref stopped it, as opposed to his corner doing so is ridiculous. I reckon they waiting on his cheeks and chin to be ballooned shaped before pulling him out. Shocking work.'

Another said: 'Was a nasty look for Zak miller! Hope his corner's decision to not throw towel in doesn’t come back to haunt them! Speedy recovery Zak.'

A third said: 'An absolutely disgusting amount of swelling on the head of Zak Miller tonight. I hope he's all okay.'

Sports.title: Olympics gender row boxer Imane Khelif to make professional debut: Algerian announces fight with 21-year-old in December... two-and-a-half years after controversial gold in Paris
Sports.content:
Olympics gender row boxer Imane Khelif will debut as a professional boxer in December – with the goal of winning a world title.

The Algerian fighter will take on women's boxer Clarida Sarabia, 21, in Paris – more than two years after being dragged into a controversy at the Olympics there.

Khelif has a naturally high level of testosterone – though takes medication to reduce it – and was engulfed in a gender row at the 2024 Games after failing a gender eligibility test with the International Boxing Association in 2023.

'It’s been over two years since I last boxed, and I've really missed being in the ring,' said Khelif.

'The last couple of years have been quite difficult. The time has come to turn professional, and I’m going to give it my all.'

The 27-year-old also said: 'Days became weeks, weeks became months. I waited, doubted. But deep inside, the fire never died. Behind closed doors, I kept fighting.

Olympics gender row boxer Imane Khelif will debut as a professional boxer in December

'Because this fight was never only mine. It was for everyone who dared to be, for everyone who refused to give up.'

Khelif's coach, Kamel Abdesselam, said that Khelif could challenge for a world title within three to five professional fights.

The 27-year-old also hopes to compete in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games, but must take a sex test to compete in the women's category after that was universally mandated by the International Olympic Committee.

Khelif won welterweight gold at the last Olympics.

A fellow gender row boxer, Lin Yu-ting, who claimed the featherweight title in Paris, was cleared earlier this year to return to World Boxing events after a sex test, casting doubt on the fairness of the controversy over her gender.

Khelif has not competed since sex tests were introduced by World Boxing in 2025, taking the fight to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in a bid to compete without being tested, for which a hearing is yet to be held.

But the fighter is happy to take a sex test for the next Olympics, saying to CNN in February: 'Of course, I would accept doing anything I'm required to do to participate in competitions.

'They should protect women, but they need to pay attention that while protecting women, they shouldn't hurt other women.'

Last year, Donald Trump signed an executive order entitled 'Keeping Men Out of Women's Sports'. The United States President referred to Khelif as a 'male boxer' who had 'transitioned' and 'stole the women's gold medal' by competing in Paris.

The President doubled down on calling Khelif a 'male' during a speech to Republican lawmakers in January.

Trump has previously claimed that Khelif is transgender. Our current understanding is that that is incorrect. The boxer was, as far as we know, born female, but is believed to possess the SRY gene, which is associated with male sex chromosomes.

'I respect everyone, and I respect Trump because he's the president of the United States,' Khelif told L'Equipe. 'Trump cannot distort the truth. I'm not trans, I'm a girl.

'I was raised as a girl, I grew up as a girl, people in my village have always known me as a girl.'

Sports.title: Jake Paul will make his boxing comeback on Christmas Eve in Dubai - just a year after suffering a double broken jaw in brutal defeat by Anthony Joshua
Sports.content:
Jake Paul has confirmed he will return to the boxing ring on Christmas Eve in Dubai, almost a year after suffering a double broken jaw in his defeat by Anthony Joshua.

The YouTuber turned boxer will headline a Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) event on December 24, marking his first professional fight in Dubai.

Paul's opponent is expected to be announced in the coming days, with the American already understood to have held talks with former UFC star Darren Till.

He has also been in discussions with former UFC heavyweight Alistair Overeem, although Paul is understood to want the Dutchman to lose a significant amount of weight before they could agree to fight.

MVP have yet to confirm who Paul will face as he prepares to return to action following the most damaging defeat of his professional career.

The 29-year-old was stopped by Joshua in the sixth round of their heavyweight showdown in Miami on December 19, 2025, after struggling to cope with the Briton's size, power and experience.

Jake Paul has confirmed he will return to the boxing ring on Christmas Eve in Dubai, almost a year after suffering a double broken jaw in his defeat by Anthony Joshua

Paul pictured fighting AJ at the Kaseya Center, Miami, Florida on December 19, 2025

Paul spent much of the early stages attempting to keep his distance from the former two-time unified heavyweight world champion, using his movement to evade Joshua's attacks.

But the contest began to turn decisively in the fifth round as Joshua increased the pressure, flooring Paul twice and leaving him struggling to cope with the relentless assault.

The American survived the round but was dropped again in the sixth before Joshua delivered the decisive blow, landing a powerful right hand that sent Paul to the canvas for a fourth time.

Paul failed to beat the referee's count, with the contest officially stopped at one minute and 31 seconds of the sixth round.

It marked the first knockout defeat of Paul's professional boxing career and his second loss overall, following his split-decision defeat by Tommy Fury in February 2023.

The damage extended well beyond the result. Paul confirmed immediately after the fight that he had suffered a double broken jaw, later sharing an X-ray on social media showing fractures in two places.

He subsequently had surgery to repair the injuries, with two titanium plates fitted and some teeth removed. Recovery did not go according to plan, with Paul having to go back under the knife for a second time.

The severity of the injury raised questions over how long Paul would be sidelined and whether he would return to the ring.

The YouTuber-turned-boxer pictured alongside his fiancee Jutta Leerdam (Olympic champion)

Paul's opponent is expected to be announced in the coming days, with the American already understood to have held talks with former UFC star Darren Till

But the American has now confirmed his comeback, with Dubai set to host another major event as he looks to rebuild his boxing career.

'I've spent years proving people wrong, taking risks, and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I'd face,' Paul said.

'Nothing that's happened has changed my belief in myself or what I'm working toward.

'I'm hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I'm returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey.

'Dubai is a city that thinks big, breaks boundaries, and doesn't believe in limits. That's exactly the kind of place I want to make my comeback.

'We've got plenty of names on the list; let's see who signs the contract. Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody's getting knocked out.'

Paul, who boasts a professional record of 12 wins and two defeats, has become one of boxing's biggest commercial attractions since making his debut in 2020.

His November 2024 bout against Mike Tyson attracted a reported 125million global viewers, while his showdown with Joshua a year later drew 33m.

He has also been in discussions with former UFC heavyweight Alistair Overeem (above)

The announcement comes as MVP continues to expand its international presence, with the Dubai event being organised in cooperation with the Dubai Sports Council and the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism.

MVP co-founder and chief executive Nakisa Bidarian said Paul's return demonstrated his determination to continue competing after his injury against Joshua.

'Well he is back, and that tells you everything about the competitor Jake Paul is and how much he loves this sport,' Bidarian said.

'This is more than a fight. It's a global event in one of the world's great destination cities, on one of the most special nights of the year, when families everywhere are together and watching.

'We're finalising an opponent worthy of Jake's return and look forward to sharing more in the coming weeks.'

Till, who previously challenged for the UFC welterweight title, has increasingly explored opportunities outside mixed martial arts since leaving the UFC.

Overeem, meanwhile, enjoyed a lengthy career at the highest level of MMA and kickboxing, competing in promotions including the UFC, Strikeforce and K-1.

The 45-year-old Dutchman has not competed in professional MMA since 2021, when he was released by the UFC following his defeat by Alexander Volkov but has stated he's interested in pursing a boxing career.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and wife Paris both break down in tears as they recount how he 'didn't want to live' in deep depression amid his alcohol and drug addiction in new Netflix documentary trailer
Sports.content:
A tearful Paris Fury has revealed how she was left 'scared' over husband Tyson's alarming health decline, with the heavyweight superstar opening up on his paralysing drink and drug addiction in a new documentary.

Tyson, 38, saw his life spiral out of control after reaching the pinnacle of boxing following his heavyweight title triumph over arch rival Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.

The Gypsy King, speaking in Netflix's new documentary Tyson Fury, confessed how he had lost his 'whole point of existence' after his win in Dusseldorf, leading to a crippling addiction to alcohol and cocaine.

In the documentary trailer, Tyson says: 'All I wanted to was beat Klitschko. It was an obsession for me.

'I'd achieved all my childhood dreams, but my whole point of existence had been taken away. I didn't want to live.'

Tyson and Paris Fury both broke down in tears as they recounted his troubling addiction past

Fury revealed how he had lost his whole point of existence after winning the heavyweight title

Fury fulfilled a career-long obsession after beating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015

Tyson's wife and childhood sweetheart Paris, could only watch on as her husband's life unravelled, and was emotional as she recounted the traumatising episode.

'Straight after [the Klitschko fight], Tyson said to me "this is as good as it is ever going to get". I didn't understand at the time what he meant,' she says.

'The Tyson I knew was gone and I was so scared.'

The documentary, which charts Tyson's incredible rise to heavyweight champion of the world, tells how he grew up surrounded by strong male figures - where discussing emotions was off limits.

'Growing up in my family, there was no emotion shown. They were all hard nuts. Like 50cent said: "Show no love, love will get you killed."'

Fury fought back from his addiction problems to make his boxing comeback in 2018, before triumphing over Deontay Wilder in a sensational heavyweight trilogy against the big-hitting American - where he won the WBC title.

The Gypsy King sought to unify the heavyweight division against the all-conquering Oleksandr Usyk, but twice fell short in a pair of thrilling contests against the Ukrainian.

Netflix cameras have documented the lives of the Fury family since 2023. The latest series centred on Fury's decision to come out of retirement, plus the family's move from Morecambe to the Isle of Wight.

The streaming giant will broadcast Fury's mega-fight against Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11.

Sports.title: Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga arrested after striking baby mama on the head with a pistol in heated dispute
Sports.content:
Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga was arrested earlier this week for aggravated battery following a heated physical bust-up with the mother of his child.

Berlanga, who is signed to Dana White's Zuffa Boxing, was arrested and booked in Polk County, Florida, on one charge of battery and one charge of aggravated battery on Monday.

The fighter is alleged to have repeatedly slapped a woman before hitting her on the head with a gun, according to court documents obtained by the Daily Mail.

The alleged victim, the mother of Berlanga's son, told police that the pair became embroiled in a heated argument while the boxer was driving after leaving a gun range on October 18.

She claimed that the dispute turned physical when Berlanga began slapping her before reaching into the vehicle's cupholder and retrieving a pistol, according to police documents.

The boxer is then alleged to have struck the woman on the forehead with the magazine well of the gun.

Professional boxer Edgar Berlanga was arrested earlier this week for aggravated battery

The boxer is accused of hitting the mother of his child on the forehead with a pistol

He lost to Canelo Alvarez for the WBA, WBC and WBO super middleweight titles in 2024

The woman claimed she attempted to escape from the vehicle and flee only for Berlanga to grab her arm and pull her back into the car. She eventually managed to exit the vehicle and sought safety at a nearby 7-Eleven.

Police said they observed swelling and bruising on her face which corroborated her allegations. They also said that they noticed a rip in her shirt and bruising on her inner arm consistent with her claims that Berlanga grabbed her.

When asked by officers if the gun Berlanga struck her with was real, the woman confirmed that it was and that she had witnessed the boxer fire the gun multiple times at the range around 20 minutes earlier.

The police report stated that she was unsure if she wanted to press charges, however, Berlanga was still ultimately arrested as officers declared it a domestic violence case.

Berlanga was booked on felony aggravated battery and misdemeanor battery touch/strike. He made his first court appearance on Tuesday and bond was set at $16,000, per court records.

Berlanga is a top rising boxer with a 24-2 record with 19 KOs. He went up against Canelo Alvarez for the WBA, WBC and WBO super middleweight titles in September 2024 but lost by unanimous decision.

Earlier this year, he headlined an event at Madison Square Garden in New York City, where he delivered a KO loss to Steven Butler in the seventh round.

Sports.title: Teen fighting for life identified after Brisbane boxing night mass shooting - as event official speaks out
Sports.content:
Teen fighting for life identified after Brisbane boxing night mass shooting - as event official speaks out

Jimboomba woman Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau, 19, has been identified as the innocent bystander fighting for life after being shot in the head and neck outside a Queensland pub.

She remained in a critical and unstable condition at Princess Alexandra Hospital on Monday afternoon. Metro South Health confirmed the teenager is still fighting for life in the intensive care unit.

The teenager was active on social media just hours before the shooting. She and her partner were seen lip syncing to Justin Bieber's Daises in a video posted on Saturday afternoon.

Four people were wounded outside Fitzy's Loganholme, south of Brisbane, on Saturday night, while more than 100 spectators, including families with young children, attended the Logan City Titles boxing event.

Phil Austin, from the Australian National Boxing Federation Queensland, categorically rejected suggestions it was a bikie or organised crime attack targeting the boxing.

Austin was in the venue's foyer when the shots erupted.

'The wider community is questioning how can this happen in Logan?' Queensland Police Chief Superintendent Mel Adams said on Monday.

Jimboomba woman Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau remains critically injured after suffering gunshot wounds to her head and neck

Vision of bullet marks on a mirror after four people were shot outside Fitzy's Loganholme during a boxing event on Saturday night

Boxing official Phil Austin was in the foyer when shots erupted, with flying glass striking his arm

'That's a popular local pub, a well-respected institution. That location had children, teenagers, mums and dads at that sporting event.'

Taskforce Maxima is a specialist Queensland Police squad that investigates outlaw motorcycle gangs and serious organised crime.

It is assisting Logan CIB and State Crime Command, which are jointly leading the investigation into the Fitzy's Loganholme shooting.

But Austin told Daily Mail that speculation linking the boxing event to bikies and organised crime was 'people putting two and two together and getting five'.

'I haven't seen any reputed organised crime figures at a fight show in this country in years,' he said.

'Bikies used to go to events, but since the government changed their laws, you just don't see them.'

Austin said he did not recognise any of the victims and could not say whether they had been attending the boxing.

'I don't even know if they were there to watch the boxing,' he said.

Ms Schuster-Togiatau (above) remained in the intensive care unit on Monday afternoon

Austin rejected speculation linking the boxing event to bikies and organised crime

'There's more than just boxing happening at that pub.'

He said no fighters or trainers appeared to have been involved and challenged assumptions that the boxing event itself had been targeted.

'We just happened to be there,' he said.

'It could have been the flower arranging show. It's just the fact that we were there.

'We have no idea why what happened happened. The only thing that we know for sure is it's a tragedy.'

Austin said he had just finished seeing a fighter and left the room being used as the dressing rooms near the venue's front doors when the shooting began.

'I'm in the foyer. I've got maybe a couple of metres, and then there's just a series of shots very, very quickly,' he said.

'We're talking about five or six shots in that or less seconds.'

Police say shots were fired from a Mitsubishi's front passenger window near the venue's drop-off area

Two men wearing balaclavas and gloves were seen inside the vehicle, according to police

Ms Schuster-Togiatau (above) had shared a video lip syncing to a Justin Bieber song just hours before the shooting

Flying glass struck the back of his arm.

'I was wearing a long shirt. Nothing hurt, but it just sort of reinforced me like, okay … this is happening,' he said.

'Before I could sort of basically say to myself, 'Oh crap,' it's over.'

Austin saw a car with its lights on but did not see anyone get out.

'It was my impression that they were actually still in the car,' he said.

Police said a Mitsubishi approached the passenger drop-off area during an intermission and shots were fired from its front passenger window.

Two men wearing balaclavas and gloves were seen inside.

Austin went to alert his crew in the boxing hall at the rear of the venue, away from where the shots had been fired.

Three men aged 27, 37 and 38 remain in hospital with serious injuries but are improving, police said

The Mitsubishi was found burnt out at Waterford West shortly after the shooting

'Then people's reactions start to kick in, and there's a bit of pandemonium, really, a lot of very, very angry people,' he said.

'They used the boxing room, basically, like a safe haven for everybody.'

Patrons began leaving through the back as hotel staff and security marshalled the crowd.

Chief Superintendent Mel Adams said everyone who witnessed the violence would carry some trauma from the night.

'This could have been your family member,' she said.

'This was a random group of people at the front of a popular hotel that became victims.'

The three other victims, men aged 27, 37 and 38, all suffered gunshot wounds to their abdomens. The 38-year-old was also shot in the arm.

All three remained in serious conditions on Monday but were improving, Adams said.

Police have not confirmed whether the men knew one another.

Police believe the attack involved pre-planning but say it remains premature to speculate about gang or organised crime involvement.

The Mitsubishi was found burnt out at Waterford West shortly after the shooting.

CCTV from nearby homes showed its occupants being collected by another vehicle after the car was torched. Police believe one of those involved may have suffered burns or another injury.

A ute was also found burnt later that night, with investigators still examining whether it was connected.

Adams urged anyone who knew or suspected who was responsible to come forward.

'There will be people out there who know who did this or suspect who did this,' she said.

For Austin, who has a son the same age as the critically injured teenager, the shooting has hit particularly hard.

'I've got a son her age, so it's really, really hit home hard,' he said.

He offered the federation's support to the victims, their families and friends.

'This is an awful, awful time for everyone,' he said.

'Let's just hope this girl recovers. It's just awful.'

Sports.title: Conor Benn calls out Conor McGregor for lucrative crossover fight - as he looks to bounce back from brutal second-round knockdown by Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Conor Benn calls out Conor McGregor for lucrative crossover fight - as he looks to bounce back from brutal second-round knockdown by Ryan Garcia

Conor Benn has called out Conor McGregor for a potential crossover fight, just weeks after suffering a devastating defeat by Ryan Garcia.

Benn was stopped in the second round of his world title challenge against Garcia in Las Vegas, with a brutal right hand sending the Briton crashing to the canvas before the American finished the job.

It was the first knockout defeat of Benn's professional career and left serious questions over what comes next for the 30-year-old.

But he appears to have an unexpected opponent in mind.

Benn took to social media to share a fight poster featuring himself and McGregor, accompanied by the caption: 'Benn vs McGregor coming soon, 2027'.

He added to the speculation by responding: 'Any day of the week.'

Conor Benn (pictured above) has called out Conor McGregor for a potential crossover fight, just weeks after suffering a devastating defeat by Ryan Garcia

Benn is understood to be interested in making the fight happen and is expected to explore potential terms with the Irishman.

Benn has previously been tipped to face McGregor in a lucrative crossover bout, with boxing legend Roy Jones Jr suggesting that the fight would make sense.

He said the crossover bout would be one of two major paydays for the Brit before he considers bringing his career to a close.

Jones also suggested such a contest could help Zuffa Boxing recoup its investment in Benn.

The prospect would offer Benn the chance to headline another major event without the pressure of a world title being on the line, while a fight against McGregor would attract an audience well beyond traditional boxing fans.

McGregor is one of the biggest names in combat sports, having become a global superstar during his time in the UFC before stepping into the boxing ring to face Floyd Mayweather in 2017.

The Irishman is also coming off a difficult period of his own, having suffered a fresh setback on his return to the Octagon against Max Holloway.

A fight with Benn would undoubtedly attract huge attention, although there is no indication yet that the pair are close to agreeing a deal.

Roy Jones Jr has said such a contest could help Zuffa Boxing recoup its investment in Benn

Benn's call-out comes after a brutal night in Las Vegas, where his hopes of becoming a world champion were ended in devastating fashion.

The British fighter had talked up his chances of upsetting Garcia, but the American's speed and power proved too much.

Garcia caught Benn with a vicious right hand in the second round, dropping him heavily to the canvas. Benn managed to get back to his feet, but Garcia immediately went on the attack again, forcing referee Thomas Taylor to step in after just one minute and 25 seconds of the round.

It was a crushing result for Benn, who had worked his way back into contention following his two-fight rivalry with Chris Eubank Jr.

Benn lost their first encounter by decision in April 2025 before getting his revenge with a points victory in November.

He subsequently returned to welterweight to challenge Garcia for the WBC title, but the American proved a step too far on the night.

The defeat also raised fresh questions about Benn's future at 147lbs, with making the weight having been a talking point in the build-up.

After the fight, Benn admitted he was unsure what came next and spoke about the sacrifices his boxing career had demanded of his family.

Benn was beaten inside two rounds by Ryan Garcia in their welterweight championship fight

It was the first knockout defeat of Benn's professional career and left serious questions over what comes next for the 30-year-old

He made it clear that spending time with his children was his immediate priority, leaving his next move uncertain.

A lucrative showdown with McGregor would offer a very different route back into the spotlight from another world title challenge.

McGregor, meanwhile, has endured his own difficult return to competition.

The former two-weight UFC champion had been out of action since breaking his leg during his trilogy fight with Dustin Poirier in July 2021.

His long-awaited comeback against Holloway was supposed to mark the start of a new chapter, but things quickly went wrong.

McGregor injured his knee after attempting a jumping kick in the opening seconds of the fight. Unable to continue, he was forced to withdraw after just 69 seconds, handing Holloway the victory.

The result was a frustrating setback for the Irishman, whose return had generated enormous interest among UFC fans.

McGregor subsequently announced plans to undergo surgery, leaving his immediate and long-term future uncertain once again.

McGregor's long-awaited comeback ended in disaster at UFC 329 in Las Vegas (above)

The Irishman blew his knee out after throwing a kick within the first seconds of the bout

At 38, he remains one of the most recognisable figures in combat sports, but another comeback will depend on his recovery and whether he can return to full fitness.

A boxing match with Benn would be a different proposition from another UFC appearance, though it would still require McGregor to make a significant commitment to training and preparation.

McGregor is no stranger to a crossover fight.

His most famous venture outside MMA came in August 2017, when he faced Floyd Mayweather in one of the most heavily promoted boxing matches of all time.

McGregor had never competed in a professional boxing bout before, but that did little to dampen interest in the contest.

The pair embarked on an extraordinary promotional tour, trading insults in front of huge crowds as the fight became a global spectacle.

McGregor made a competitive start, but Mayweather quickly took control before stopping him in the 10th round.

Mayweather improved his professional boxing record to 50-0, while McGregor returned to the UFC having secured a huge payday and further cemented his status as one of sport's biggest commercial attractions.

Sports.title: Boxing world champion Adrien Broner back in hot water as video shows him being handcuffed and hauled into police car in Beverly Hills
Sports.content:
Adrien Broner, the troubled former boxing champion once seen as the future of the sport, had another run-in with police over the weekend in Beverly Hills.

Now more than two years removed from his last fight, the 37-year-old Broner was among a group of men recording content on the streets of Beverly Hills for the social media platform, Kick, when local police arrived.

Viral footage from the incident shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner and his fellow content creator, Deen The Great.

A separate clip shows Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs. Broner is seen trying to poke fun at the situation by doing a funny walk for the officers' benefit, but they did not seem amused.

'Broner was detained during a traffic stop as part of an investigation into a large street gathering in a residential area,' Beverly Hills police told TMZ in a statement. 'He was released from the scene and a citation was not issued.'

The Daily Mail has sought further information from Beverly Hills police.

Adrien Broner dancing while getting put in handcuffs by the police 💀 pic.twitter.com/h9SZlIYfdM — Happy Punch (@HappyPunch) October 26, 2026

Viral footage shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner (center, open gray sweatshirt) and his fellow content creator, DeenTheGreat

A separate clip shows Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs on the streets of Beverly Hills

Adrien Broner and Deen The Great attend the Internet Ball on August 19, 2026

Broner is currently among several defendants being sued in Los Angeles County over allegations of sexual battery, battery and assault.

'Plaintiff alleges that Broner repeatedly pressured Plaintiff for sexual activity after repeated refusals, attempted to isolate Plaintiff, repeatedly pressured Plaintiff while intoxicated, attempted unwanted physical contact, publicly humiliated Plaintiff, and made false sexual statements about Plaintiff to a livestream audience,' read the complaint, obtained by The Daily Mail.

Broner has denied any wrongdoing in the case.

Previously, in September of 2025, Broner was kicked off rapper Cam'ron's popular podcast after ignoring the host's warnings to stop flirting with his on-air co-host.

Sporting a greying beard and speaking in an increasingly raspy voice, Broner repeatedly interrupted the interview to make passes at Treasure 'Stat Baby' Wilson, who co-hosts It Is What It Is with Cam'ron and Ma$e.

Adrien Broner and Deen The great attend Sold Out Saturdays on August 15, 2026 in Atlanta

Adrien Broner punches Gavin Rees during their WBC Lightweight Title fight at Atlantic City Boardwalk Hall in 2013. Broner won the WBO Super Featherweight title at just 22 in 2011

At one point, Broner responded to a question about boxing's welterweight division by telling Wilson: 'Stat, I love you.'

Things ultimately boiled over during a discussion about Sunday's NFL action when Broner appeared to stop himself from making another comment about Wilson: 'I can't talk… You told me to stop.'

Cam'ron took the moment to end his interview with Broner.

'Hey, we going to have to ask you to go, my n*****,' Cam'ron said before pulling a stack of cash out of a small bag to give to his guest.

'I don't have no problems with you, but I'm gonna pay you for your time,' the rapper said, adding: 'You can't violate, bro.' Cam'ron went on to explain that Wilson's boyfriend was on set.

A native of Cincinnati who won the WBO Super Featherweight title at just 22 in 2011, Broner enjoyed a meteoric rise in the boxing world before his career was derailed by a series of arrests, upset defeats and mental health issues.

Sports.title: F1 Brazilian GP: Norris wins in mixed conditions, Mercedes clinch constructors’ title
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has snared his third win of 2026 in a mixed weather Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix, defeating a resurgent Max Verstappen while Mercedes claimed the world constructors' championship.

After reclaiming the lead from his world champion successor Kimi Antonelli early on when he spun off, polesitter Norris thwarted Verstappen's latest stunning Brazil comeback in a race which both started and finished in the wet, bookending a dry spell.

Having survived a scare on the laps to the grid when he slid onto the grass at the tricky Turn 12, Antonelli picked off polesitter Norris for the lead into Turn 1 as the race started in intermediate conditions. Third-place starter Liam Lawson also followed the Mercedes through into second.

Alonso was the biggest loser as he dropped six places by going wide at Turn 3. Lewis Hamilton went the opposite direction, gaining 10 places to sweep into 11th, while Verstappen jumped to 13th after both drivers had started at the back of the grid with engine penalties.

As Antonelli built a five-second buffer to Lawson and Norris, Hamilton and Verstappen soon found each other, with Hamilton starting to struggle on worn rear tyres. The seven-time world champion couldn't follow Verstappen past Oscar Piastri and into the top 10, the Ferrari being passed by Aston Martin's Alonso instead.

Hamilton urged his team to bring him in for slicks and eventually got his wish on lap 15 of 71, being the first driver to make the switch. His immediate speed on the dry weather tyre triggered a flurry of pitstops across the grid as the entire field switched to softs as well, Antonelli and Verstappen waiting one lap longer than the other frontrunners.

Lando Norris, McLaren, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Manuel Eletto / Getty Images

After that shuffle, Antonelli kept the lead from Norris, Isack Hadjar and comeback hero Verstappen, who both made their way past Lawson. Russell, however, lost out by spinning in the pit exit, being fortunate enough to escape damage but dropping behind Piastri and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg.

Antonelli came under increasing pressure from Norris, reporting a problem with the suspension that made his car pull to one side. That became apparent in dramatic fashion as he spun off the track in Turn 1, releasing Norris into the lead but being able to rejoin.

Antonelli's handling woes continued as Red Bull duo Hadjar and Verstappen easily worked their way past into the podium positions, with Hadjar waving Verstappen by on lap 38.

After dropping five seconds behind Hadjar, Antonelli was able to stabilise things in fourth with a healthy buffer to Piastri, Lawson, Russell and Hulkenberg, while neither Ferrari driver was able to make much progress from the middle of the pack.

From starting at the rear, Verstappen suddenly found himself in second place just after halfway, with a nine second deficit to race leader Norris. Verstappen pulled the trigger on a second pitstop on lap 46 for a new set of softs, while Hadjar was bullish on making it to the end without stopping again.

As a light drizzle hit the track with 23 laps to go, McLaren pressed ahead with a second pitstop to softs for Norris. Hadjar abandoned the one-stop plan with a pitstop on lap 51 in response, leaving Antonelli in the lead as Mercedes decided to gamble on heavier rain or a safety car. But with the newly crowned world champion losing over a second per lap, Mercedes soon abandoned that plan with a lap 54 pitstop for new slicks.

As strategies converged again, Norris continued matching whatever Verstappen could throw at him as he defended a seven-second gap, with Hadjar another eight seconds in arrears in third.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

But the heavens started opening again on lap 62, which triggered a mass move to intermediates within the space of two laps, Norris and Verstappen both peeling in on lap 63 as Hamilton survived a spin on slicks right before pitting.

Unperturbed, Norris coolly controlled the treacherous final laps to snare his third win of the campaign, with Verstappen settling for second 14 seconds behind the McLaren driver, while Hadjar third another nine seconds behind.

Russell was fourth ahead of Antonelli, both cars overcoming late balance woes to earn Mercedes its ninth constructors' championship, its first such trophy since 2021.

Piastri was sixth for McLaren ahead of Leclerc and a valiant Lawson, who continues fighting for his F1 future with Racing Bulls but was unable to keep Leclerc behind in the closing laps.

Like Leclerc, Hamilton was unable to sustain a genuine comeback as he settled for ninth, with Hulkenberg taking the final point in 10th despite a 10-secondpenalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage.

Rafael Camara finished 20th and last on his home debut as Esteban Ocon's replacement, as Lance Stroll retired for the 14th time this season in the Aston Martin. Valtteri Bottas did not make the start due to a cross-threaded right-rear wheel nut on his Cadillac.
