World.title: Kaduna-Kano rail line to be inaugurated 3 December – APC Campaign Council
World.content:
The Kaduna-Kano Standard Gauge Railway is scheduled for inauguration on 3 December, as the Federal Government intensifies efforts to complete major railway projects in Northern Nigeria, the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has said.

The council said the 203-kilometre Kaduna-Zaria-Kano railway project had reached approximately 90 per cent completion, while the 400-kilometre Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway project had attained 70 per cent completion.

In a statement on Sunday, Dele Alake, spokesperson for the APC Presidential Campaign Council, said the projects were among the infrastructure initiatives being accelerated by President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

According to the statement, the Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway project was barely five per cent complete when Mr Tinubu assumed office in 2023, while the Kaduna-Kano project was less than 30 per cent complete.

The council said the Kaduna-Kano railway, an extension of the existing Abuja-Kaduna standard gauge line, would provide a continuous rail connection between Abuja, Kaduna, Zaria and Kano.

It added that the railway would strengthen transportation links across major commercial centres in Northern Nigeria, improve passenger transportation and facilitate the movement of goods.

The statement said a Federal Government inspection team led by Funso Adebiyi, permanent secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, recently inspected the two projects on the president’s directive.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Adebiyi reportedly expressed satisfaction with the quality of construction, particularly the railway alignment, drainage infrastructure, embankment protection, stone pitching and soil stabilisation.

The inspection also included a train test-run from Jaji in Kaduna State to Kano to assess the completed track infrastructure and passenger comfort, the council said.

Mr Tinubu has also directed that outstanding land acquisition and compensation issues within Kaduna metropolis be resolved immediately to facilitate completion of the railway corridor from Abuja to Kano.

The statement said the completed 190-kilometre Jaji-Kano section of the Kaduna-Kano railway and the 250-kilometre Dawanu-Kano-Kazaure-Daura-Katsina section of the Kano-Maradi railway would be inaugurated on 3 December.

It said the Kaduna-Kano railway would provide an alternative to road transportation along one of Northern Nigeria’s busiest commercial corridors when operational.

The Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway, on the other hand, is expected to improve cross-border transportation and trade between Nigeria and neighbouring Niger Republic.

The council said the projects reflected the Tinubu administration’s commitment to expanding railway infrastructure and delivering ongoing infrastructure projects across the country as scheduled.

World.title: My regret over 2023 elections – Kwankwaso
World.content:
The vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has expressed regret over his refusal to form an alliance with the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, during the 2023 general election, noting that a united ticket would have given them an advantage at the polls.

Mr Kwankwaso made the remarks on Saturday in Dutse, the Jigawa State capital, while addressing party supporters at the 360 Event Centre.

“I did not truly understand Peter Obi until now. Had I understood him better in 2023, we would have collaborated and ousted the All Progressives Congress from the presidency,” Mr Kwankwaso told the crowd, drawing cheers from the audience.

Background to Mr Kwankwaso’s remarks

Ahead of the 2023 race, Mr Kwankwaso reportedly declined to run with Mr Obi, saying at the time that he was more politically experienced and had higher academic credentials, including a PhD.

He ran on the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) platform, finishing fourth and winning only Kano State with 1,496,687 votes, while Mr Obi, running under the Labour Party (LP), finished third after securing 12 states, including the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), with 6,101,533 votes.

In the February 25, 2023 presidential election, the opposition had three major contenders, helping the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Bola Tinubu, to emerge victorious.

Mr Tinubu won the presidency with 8,794,726 votes, defeating 17 other candidates.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The combined votes of Mr Obi 6.101,533 million and Mr Kwankwaso 1, 496,687 million votes totaled 7.598,220 million votes.

Mr Kwankwaso ran a nationwide campaign, but his electoral base remained concentrated in the North-west, particularly Kano State, where he secured 997,279 votes-nearly two-thirds of his total national vote count.

Mr Obi disrupted traditional two-party voting patterns by winning across the South-east, parts of the South-south regions, and Plateau, Nasarawa, and Lagos states, as well as Abuja (FCT).

Kwankwaso’s political perspective changed

At the event in Jigawa, Mr Kwankwaso stated that their partnership for the 2027 election marks a turning point for national development.

He disclosed an agreement within the NDC leadership that, if elected, he will head the Ministry of Education to drive reforms across the country’s institutions.

“I can confirm to you that Peter Obi has agreed that I will preside over the education ministry. This decision was reached after I presented the educational blueprint from my tenure as governor of Kano State, which aligns with Mr Obi’s track record in Anambra State,” he said.

Mr Kwankwaso said the administration would ensure that children from underprivileged backgrounds have access to quality schooling, alongside plans to renovate public schools, recruit trained teachers, and supply modern instructional materials.

“I have already demonstrated this in public office. We sponsored over 3,000 Kano indigenes on foreign scholarships without borrowing from commercial banks, taking foreign loans, or owing contractors. That was made possible by curbing corruption, and that is our plan for Nigeria,” Mr Kwankwaso added.

He also criticised the current administrations of Kano and Jigawa states, alleging that both governors had deviated from governance centred on the public interest, and emphasised the historical ties between Kano and Jigawa.

He urged voters in Jigawa to support the NDC ticket to help produce the zone’s first vice president since independence in 1960.

World.title: Why reelecting Tinubu is mandatory – Jigawa speaker
World.content:
The Speaker of the Jigawa State House of Assembly, Haruna Aliyu, has stated that supporting President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections is a binding duty for residents of the state.

Mr Aliyu made the remarks on Saturday during the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential and governorship campaign council in Dutse, the state capital.

He framed backing Mr Tinubu’s re-election as a religious obligation and an act of reciprocity, asserting that the President has consistently supported Northern political aspirations throughout his career.

Recalling Mr Tinubu’s instrumental role in the emergence of former President Muhammadu Buhari, the Speaker argued that Northern Nigeria owes him reciprocal loyalty.

“President Tinubu is a devout and dedicated Muslim leader who has the best interests of Jigawa State at heart,” Mr Aliyu said.

He added that although Jigawa was not initially listed on the President’s campaign itinerary, Mr Tinubu chose to visit because of his confidence in the state’s leadership and its people.

“That is why we must vote for him and support the APC at all levels,” he urged party faithful.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Reflecting on the party’s readiness, the Speaker expressed confidence in its electoral strength, pointing to the presence of former governors, senators, and federal lawmakers at the event as proof of the APC’s broad grassroots appeal across Jigawa.

Mr Aliyu, who also coordinates the pro-Tinubu support group City Boy Movement in Jigawa, announced plans to ramp up house-to-house mobilisation ahead of the polls.

“We will mobilise the City Boy Movement across Jigawa, going from household to household to showcase the achievements of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Governor Umar Namadi,” he said.

“We will mobilise the City Boy Movement across Jigawa, going from household to household to showcase the achievements of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Governor Umar Namadi,” he said.

World.title: Nigerian Army regains control of X account two months after hacking
World.content:
The Nigerian Army said it has regained control of its official X account more than two months after it was hacked.

The military said the account had been successfully restored following efforts to resolve the “unauthorised access” reported on 29 August.

In a statement on Sunday, Appolonia Anele, a colonel and acting spokesperson for the army, said administrative control of the account had been fully reinstated.

She said the account was now secured and would resume regular updates on the army’s activities, operations, achievements and institutional developments.

“The successful recovery underscores the Nigerian Army’s commitment to safeguarding its digital communication platforms, protecting the integrity of information and ensuring the continued use of credible and secure channels for public engagement,” Ms Anele said.

The army thanked Nigerians, media organisations and other stakeholders for their patience and support during the period the account was inaccessible.

It also acknowledged their cooperation in helping sustain access to credible information through its alternative official communication platforms.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

ALSO READ: Nigerian Army investigates sexual abuse allegation against serving officer

The military urged members of the public to follow the restored account for timely and verified information about its activities.

It reaffirmed its commitment to strategic communication, public engagement and strengthening trust between the military and Nigerians.

The army did not explain the process of restoring the account, nor did it mention those responsible for the hacking.

World.title: NDLEA arrests Ugandan woman with 87 cocaine wraps at Lagos airport
World.content:
A 34-year-old Ugandan woman has been arrested at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Lagos, with 87 wraps of cocaine weighing 1.15 kilogrammes, the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has said.

The suspect, Farida Nansubuga, was arrested on Tuesday, 3 November, as she prepared to board a flight to Uganda at Terminal 2 of the airport.

In a statement on Sunday by the agency’s Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, the cocaine was strapped around her pelvic region and concealed beneath two layers of underwear.

The NDLEA said operatives became suspicious during a joint passenger screening exercise with aviation security personnel. A subsequent body search raised concerns that she had concealed something around her pelvic region, prompting officers to take her to a private search room, where they recovered the 87 wraps.

During questioning, Ms Nansubuga noted that she arrived in Nigeria on 29 October with members of her church for a prayer session at the Synagogue Church of All Nations (SCOAN), in the Ikotun-Egbe area of Lagos.

She told investigators that the other members of the delegation had returned to Uganda after the prayer session, but she stayed behind to collect the cocaine for a friend, identified as Joy, who lives in Uganda.

According to the NDLEA, Ms Nansubuga noted that Joy linked her with a contact in Nigeria, who arranged a vehicle to take her to a hotel on the morning of her departure. The contact allegedly handed over the drugs and instructed her to conceal them beneath her clothing to avoid detection at the airport.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She reportedly said they had not agreed on a specific payment, but she expected to receive at least $1,000 after delivering the consignment.

The arrest comes amid other reported attempts to smuggle cocaine out of Nigeria using body concealment, mirroring Nigeria’s role as a transit bub in the global cocaine menace.

In May 2025, NDLEA operatives arrested a woman at the Port Harcourt International Airport over an alleged attempt to smuggle 2.523 kilogrammes of cocaine to Iran.

Other seizures at Lagos airport

In a separate operation at the Lagos airport, the NDLEA intercepted 750,000 tablets of Tapentadol 250mg, weighing 526 kilogrammes and valued at N900 million.

The consignment arrived from Ahmedabad, India, on 3 November aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight. It was declared as Paracetamol 500mg tablets.

The agency said officers placed the shipment under surveillance after becoming suspicious of its declaration. They later examined it jointly with officials of the Nigeria Customs Service and other agencies on Friday, 6 November.

The tablets were packed in 11 cartons inside two wooden structures. Ten cartons contained Tapentadol, while the remaining carton held paracetamol tablets.

The seizure follows earlier large-scale opioid interceptions at Lagos ports. In September 2024, the NDLEA reported recovering 25 million Tapentadol tablets and 350,000 bottles of codeine-based syrup at the Tin Can Island Port. It valued the Tapentadol at N13.725 billion and the entire consignment at about N16.1 billion.

The agency also intercepted 32 parcels of Loud, a strain of cannabis, weighing 16.15 kilogrammes at the Lagos airport.

The drugs were concealed inside two wooden sofas in a consolidated cargo shipment from Houston, Texas, which arrived aboard a Turkish Airlines flight on Wednesday, 4 November.

A freight agent, Ibrahim Abdulwaheed Adewale, was arrested when he came to clear the consignment. Two days later, a 34-year-old caterer from Ibadan, Oyo State, Adeoye Sarafa Ojo, was arrested while attempting to collect the package.

Mr Ojo reportedly told investigators that a friend, Taiwo Anuoluwapo Olusegun, had sent him.

Suspected Colorado chemical import network

The NDLEA said it had also uncovered a suspected network importing chemicals from the United Kingdom for the production of Colorado, a synthetic cannabis.

The investigation began with the interception of nine parcels concealed in two cartons of snacks labelled “Michael Tea Guy”. The shipment arrived aboard an Air Peace flight from the UK on 23 October.

Two parcels contained 1.20 kilogrammes of cannabis, while forensic analysis showed that the other seven contained chemicals used in producing synthetic cannabis.

A 51-year-old freight agent, Afolabi Abiodun Wale, was arrested when he came to clear the shipment.

Two additional cartons addressed to the same recipient later arrived from the UK aboard an Allied Air flight. A sting operation between 26 and 28 October led to the arrest of another 51-year-old suspect, Okwuite Benjamin Ojone, when he came to collect the four cartons.

A search of the additional cartons uncovered three parcels weighing 3.30 kilogrammes, concealed in detergent packs, and 11 plastic bottles containing mostly liquid substances weighing 16.25 kilogrammes.

The NDLEA said the operation resulted in the seizure of 1.20 kilogrammes of cannabis and 28.65 kilogrammes of chemicals suspected to be used in producing synthetic cannabis.

The agency has previously reported uncovering a laboratory allegedly used to produce Colorado in a residential building in Ajao Estate, Lagos, in November 2025. The operation followed months of intelligence gathering.

Seizures across states

At courier companies in Lagos, NDLEA operatives intercepted 46 blocks of cannabis weighing 22.2 kilogrammes in two cartons destined for the United Kingdom on Tuesday, 3 November.

Earlier, on 30 October, they intercepted 296 tablets of Swinol destined for Australia.

The agency also reported three tramadol shipments bound for the UK. They included 20 capsules from Benin City and 96 capsules from Sapele, Delta State, both concealed in vitamin C containers, as well as 600 tablets of Tramadol 225mg from Asaba hidden in female headwear.

In another Lagos operation, operatives arrested a 32-year-old man, Abubakar Ali, at Marine Beach, Apapa, on Friday, 6 November.

The agency said officers recovered drugs from a small store he had built inside his sitting room. The substances included 1.06 kilogrammes of Tramadol 250mg, 1.27 kilogrammes of Tramadol 225mg, 400 grammes of pregabalin capsules, 355 grammes of diazepam, 200 millilitres of codeine and 6.07 kilogrammes of cannabis.

In Ondo State, operatives recovered 148 bags of cannabis weighing 1,818 kilogrammes during a raid on Odofin Road, Uso, on 6 November.

Earlier that day, officers raided a cannabis farm in Board Forest, destroyed a one-hectare plantation, recovered 242 kilogrammes of cannabis and arrested a 36-year-old suspect, Itoro Linus Akpan.

In neighbouring Ekiti State, a 53-year-old man, Agbo Paul Peter, was arrested at Osin Forest, Osin Ekiti, on Thursday, 5 November, with 216 kilogrammes of cannabis and cannabis seeds.

In Edo State, officers intercepted a Volkswagen Golf saloon car carrying 19 bags of cannabis weighing 201 kilogrammes along the Auchi-Ibillo Road in Akoko Edo Local Government Area on 6 November.

The driver, Abdulmumid Isah, 39, and a passenger, Danako Godwin, 25, were arrested.

In a separate operation, officers raided a drug joint on Ihama Road, GRA, Benin City, where they arrested Emmanuel Sunday, 25; Samuel Bala, 31; and Loveth Momodu, 20. The suspects were found with quantities of Colorado, Loud and cannabis.

In Taraba State, officers arrested three men with 283 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 226.255 kilogrammes over two days at an NDLEA checkpoint in Lankaviri, Yorro Local Government Area.

On Thursday, 5 November, Ibrahim Abdullahi, 45, was arrested with 156 blocks weighing 149.275 kilogrammes, while Kabiru Usman, 25, was arrested with 80 blocks weighing 40.07 kilogrammes.

The following day, officers arrested Babangida Babayo, 32, with 47 blocks weighing 36.91 kilogrammes.

In Enugu State, a 57-year-old man, Celestine Uzochukwu Ejiakor, was arrested at a checkpoint in Eke Obinagu on Tuesday, 3 November, with 44 blocks of cannabis weighing 22.5 kilogrammes.

At another checkpoint in Ugwuoba, officers arrested Godwin Shaapera, 40, with 24,000 capsules of tramadol weighing 13.4 kilogrammes and 697 grammes of ketamine.

In Delta State, operatives arrested Edugua Othuke, 30, at Ozoro, Isoko North Local Government Area, on Saturday, 31 October, with 10.54 kilogrammes of skunk, 9.4 kilogrammes of cannabis seeds and 4.3 grammes of methamphetamine.

Another suspect, Akpofure Tobore, 34, was arrested at Upper Agbarho, Ughelli, on 4 November with quantities of skunk, tramadol, Rohypnol and laughing gas.

Drug abuse campaign

Meanwhile, the NDLEA said it continued its War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) campaign in schools, religious centres, workplaces and communities across the country.

During the week, the agency held sensitisation sessions for students and staff of St Andrew Basic School, Oyo; Government Technical College, Abakaliki, Ebonyi State; Sa’ad College, Kano; and Inland Girls Secondary School, Onitsha, Anambra State.

Its Zone 1 Command also paid an advocacy visit to the Emir of Bauchi, Rilwanu Sulaiman Adamu, at his palace.

The NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Buba Marwa, commended officers of the MMIA and the Lagos, Ondo, Ekiti, Edo, Delta, Taraba and Enugu commands for the arrests and seizures.

He said the Ugandan woman’s arrest showed how drug cartels exploit religious gatherings and travel opportunities to recruit couriers.

Mr Marwa, a retired brigadier general, urged officers to sustain efforts to disrupt drug supply networks and reduce demand.

World.title: Debate: ‘Lagos must learn from Japan, Venice to tackle flooding’ – GRV
World.content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, has criticised the state government over its approach to infrastructure development, traffic management and urban planning, saying the city needs visionary leadership to address its challenges.

Rhodes-Vivour, popularly known as GRV, made the remarks during the Lagos governorship debate held in Lagos on Sunday and organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard.

GRV outlined his proposals for improving infrastructure and preparing the state for climate-related challenges.

He argued that Lagos should learn from other coastal cities, including Japan and Venice, in developing infrastructure that accommodates water flow and reduces the impact of flooding.

“We lack visionary govt. They should be looking at what Japan is doing, Vernice is doing, they are coastal cities too. Vernice is standing on trees, but allows for water to flow,” he said.

The ADC candidate also questioned the quality of road construction in Lagos, arguing that infrastructure projects should meet proper technical standards and include long-term maintenance plans.

“What are the standards of road we are building in this city? Roads are not built to standard. We need to set proper standards and technicalities, and tie in maintenance to the construction of those road,” he said.

Rhodes-Vivour further called for climate scenario planning and better communication between the government and residents to prepare Lagos for future environmental challenges.

On traffic congestion, he said residents should not have to spend excessive time commuting to work, calling for an integrated transportation system that connects different parts of the state.

“Traffic is not a lifestyle, we must not have to work to get to work. We need to connect the entirety of Lagos. It is a bankable project that will pay itself over the years,” he said.

He proposed expanding water transportation through functional ferry terminals and increasing the availability of ferry services across the state.

“We need to normalise water transportation, have ferry terminals that are not just audio, have enough water transportation. We need to normalise bicycle lanes,” he added.

The ADC candidate said improved water transportation and dedicated bicycle lanes would provide residents with more commuting options and help ease pressure on Lagos roads.
