World.title: 2027: Sokoto PDP backs Tinubu’s re-election bid
World.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Sokoto State has declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s second-term ambition, disclosing that it is negotiating a political alliance with the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) through the Nyesom Wike-led Rainbow Coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The PDP governorship candidate in the state, Abubakar Abdullahi Sokoto, disclosed this at a stakeholders’ meeting held at the party’s secretariat along Bodinga Road, Sokoto metropolis.

Abdullahi said the proposed arrangement was aimed at mobilising support for Tinubu’s re-election, declaring that the PDP in Sokoto had no alternative presidential candidate apart from the incumbent president.

“Our position is to work towards President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s second-term ambition through the Rainbow Coalition, which we consider a strategic political platform for cooperation between interested PDP stakeholders and the ruling APC,” he said.

He, however, maintained that the alliance would not require the PDP to abandon its political structure or candidates contesting elective positions in the state.

According to him, the party would continue to mobilise support and campaign for its candidates in the 2027 elections.

“We are not abandoning our party structure or our candidates. We will continue to mobilise, canvass and campaign aggressively for PDP candidates seeking elective positions across Sokoto State in 2027,” he said.

Abdullahi explained that in areas where PDP candidates might lack sufficient electoral support, party members and supporters could be encouraged to support APC candidates in line with the coalition arrangement.

“Where our candidates may not have the necessary electoral strength or sufficient support, our members and supporters could be encouraged to support APC candidates as part of the political understanding under the Rainbow Coalition,” he stated.

He said the arrangement was intended to strengthen political cooperation and improve the electoral prospects of parties and individuals involved in the coalition.

Abdullahi added that the Rainbow Coalition remained open to political groups, organisations and individuals willing to identify with its objectives, irrespective of their party affiliations.

“The Rainbow Coalition is open to everybody, political groups, organisations and individuals who share our vision and are prepared to identify with its objectives, irrespective of their political backgrounds,” he said.

The PDP governorship candidate also appealed to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to reconsider his presidential ambition and support Tinubu’s re-election bid by joining the emerging alliance.

“I want to appeal to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to reconsider his position and join this emerging political understanding rather than pursue an opposition agenda against President Tinubu’s second-term ambition,” he said.

He argued that the proposed alliance provided an opportunity for broader consultations and political cooperation, urging political leaders to prioritise collective interests over partisan differences.

The declaration signals a possible political realignment in Sokoto State, where the PDP is seeking to combine its independent ambitions in state elections with support for Tinubu’s presidential bid.

However, the extent to which the proposed arrangement will shape the party’s electoral strategy at the state and national levels remains unclear as consultations continue.

The development also raises questions about the PDP’s opposition role in Sokoto and the implications of the Rainbow Coalition for the party’s relationship with the APC ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: Hamzat, GRV unveil contrasting plans at Lagos governorship debate
World.content:
By Efe Onodjae

Lagos State Deputy Governor and governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, and his African Democratic Congress, ADC, counterpart, have outlined contrasting development plans, with emphasis on housing, transportation, security, infrastructure and accountable governance.

The candidates spoke at the 2026 Lagos State Governorship Debate, where they presented their credentials, policy proposals and vision for the state ahead of the governorship election.

Hamzat, who described the debate as a job interview, said his experience in public service and previous appointments had prepared him for the responsibility of leading Lagos.

He said: “I take tonight as a job interview. The first question you ask anybody that wants this type of responsibility is, what have you done to prepare for this job?”

Recounting his professional background, Hamzat said he had worked as a teacher, case manager in New York and systems manager before joining public service.

He said his experience as Commissioner for Science and Technology equipped him to oversee the development of the state’s residents and structural database, while his tenure as Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure saw him lead the team that delivered the decade-long bridge project, described as the first cable bridge in West Africa and second in Africa.

According to him, effective governance requires a leader who understands the people, the state and the responsibilities of the office.

On his governing philosophy, Hamzat identified respect for citizens, hard work and truthfulness as the principles that would guide his administration.

He said government must place work before announcements and ensure transparency by telling citizens the truth about its activities.

Unveiling his development blueprint, tagged Jacob’s Promise, Hamzat said it was built around seven pillars, seven broad areas of action and 100 pledges.

He urged voters to assess candidates based on the substance of their plans and the work behind their promises rather than mere political announcements.

Meanwhile, the Lagos ADC governorship candidate Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour said Lagos needed a departure from what he described as two decades of bad governance, insisting that the state must work for all residents rather than a privileged few.

He said his political activism and manifesto had consistently prioritised the interests of ordinary people, adding that anyone seeking to govern a state with about 20 million residents must demonstrate a record of putting public interest above personal ambition.

The ADC candidate said his administration would adopt an integrated approach to urban development, arguing that waste management, housing, transportation, healthcare, education and urban planning were interconnected.

On housing, he promised to deliver 100,000 housing units within his first four years through a combination of luxury taxation to fund social housing, development of the eastern foreshore and intergenerational areas, and decentralisation of development across the state.

He also proposed expanding rail infrastructure, promising to connect the state’s rail lines within two and a half years through a private-sector-driven approach that would be transparent, equitable and cost-effective.

World.title: ANC suffers worst-ever election result in South Africa
World.content:
The African National Congress (ANC), which has dominated South African politics since the end of apartheid, has recorded its worst-ever electoral performance, securing 30.76 per cent of the votes in municipal elections, according to the country’s electoral commission.

The final results, announced on Sunday, showed that the party’s support had declined further, setting the stage for difficult multiparty coalition negotiations in several major cities where no party secured an outright majority.

The liberal Democratic Alliance (DA), the ANC’s closest challenger and main partner in the national unity government, secured about a quarter of the votes, according to the final tally.

Chairperson of the Electoral Commission of South Africa, Mosotho Moepya, said voter turnout stood at 52 per cent, six percentage points higher than the 2021 municipal elections, which were affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.

Moepya also disclosed that voting would be repeated in one municipality after party supporters stormed a polling station and destroyed ballot papers.

The outcome represents a significant decline for the party of late liberation icon Nelson Mandela, which won nearly two-thirds of the votes in South Africa’s first democratic elections in 1994.

Although the ANC remains the country’s largest political party, its support has steadily declined amid widespread unemployment, which has exceeded 34 per cent, as well as crime and corruption scandals.

Water shortages, electricity outages and poor service delivery were among the major issues that shaped Wednesday’s elections as voters assessed the performance of parties governing their communities.

Describing the outcome as “catastrophic”, ANC Secretary-General, Fikile Mbalula, acknowledged the party’s shortcomings on Saturday.

“Where we have fallen short, this movement does not dispute it. Communities have gone without water. Refuse has not been collected. Roads have not been maintained,” he said.

“We have been weighed in the balance, and where we have been found wanting we dare not quarrel with the scale,” Mbalula told reporters.

More than half of South Africa’s 213 municipal councils failed to produce an outright majority for any party, making coalition arrangements necessary for the formation of local governments.

Previous coalitions in the country have often been characterised by internal disagreements and shifting political alliances, resulting in administrative instability and disruptions to basic services.

President Cyril Ramaphosa urged political parties to prioritise the interests of communities in their coalition negotiations, warning against allowing political disagreements to disrupt essential services.

“The people have spoken. Their verdict must be respected. Their concerns must be heard and their expectations must now be met,” he said on Sunday.

The parties face a tight timetable, as newly elected councils are legally required to hold their inaugural meetings within 14 days of the formal declaration of results to elect mayors and other office-holders.

All but one of South Africa’s eight major cities require coalition negotiations, with the DA securing an outright majority in Cape Town.

The DA was also leading in Johannesburg, the country’s economic hub, where it fielded 75-year-old veteran politician Helen Zille, a longtime critic of the ANC who previously built her political career in Cape Town.

Meanwhile, centre-right ActionSA, founded by former Johannesburg mayor Herman Mashaba after his departure from the DA, finished fifth nationally but could play a decisive role in coalition negotiations in major metropolitan areas, including Tshwane, which is home to the administrative capital, Pretoria.

AFP

World.title: Man United stage late comeback to snatch 4-4 draw against Aston Villa
World.content:
Manchester United’s Danish defender #13 Patrick Dorgu (front L) celebrates with Manchester United’s Portuguese midfielder #08 Bruno Fernandes (front R) after teammate Manchester United’s Dutch forward #11 Joshua Zirkzee (not pictured) scored the team’s third goal, during the English Premier League football match between Manchester United and Aston Villa at Old Trafford in Manchester, north west England, on November 8, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE. No use with unauthorized audio, video, data, fixture lists, club/league logos or ‘live’ services. Online in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No video emulation. Social media in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /

Manchester United twice came from two goals down to salvage a remarkable 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday and potentially save manager Michael Carrick’s job.

Goals in stoppage time from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued a point, but United will spend a two-week international break in the relegation zone.

Carrick’s men conceded twice inside the opening four minutes as Alysson and Nicolas Jackson punished errors from goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

The Red Devils rallied to level at half-time thanks to a Bruno Fernandes penalty and Youri Tielemans’s first goal since moving to Old Trafford from Villa.

A thrilling fightback from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday gave Carrick a lifeline.

This time the comeback fell short as more woeful defending handed Villa two more goals inside the first eight minutes of the second period.

John McGinn converted from the spot after Diogo Dalot upended Alysson before Leon Goretzka bundled in from close range.

Yet, there was a final twist in the tale as Zirkzee steered home before Dorgu pounced when Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki failed to connect with a corner in the 96th minute.

– ‘We want new owners’ –

Carrick was handed a stay of execution after a 3-0 home drubbing by Bournemouth a fortnight ago.

However, he faces an anxious wait to see if the United board install a replacement before a daunting trip to Liverpool on November 22.

Former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Bayern Munich and Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann are among the leading contenders to take charge if Carrick is dismissed.

Saturday’s results saw United slip into the relegation zone after August for the first time in 40 years.

A draw keeps them in the bottom three with just eight points from 10 games.

For the first time in Premier League history they found themselves 2-0 down inside four minutes, in large part due to goalkeeper Lammens.

The Belgian allowed Alysson’s strike to slip between his legs with just one minute on the clock.

From another tame Alysson effort less than three minutes later, Lammens could only parry and present Nicolas Jackson with a gift for his sixth goal in his last six league games.

The United fans had again turned their ire towards the club’s owners pre-match.

A banner read: “We don’t want a new stadium, we want new owners,” as protests towards a move away from Old Trafford gather steam.

That anger was directed towards the players in cries of “you’re not fit to wear the shirt” in the wake of the second Villa goal.

Yet, the shock of going behind summoned a response as United again found their feet at 2-0 down.

Just as against Roma, the fightback was started by Matheus Cunha winning a penalty, converted by Fernandes.

Boubacar Kamara dived in rashly to clip Cunha before getting a touch on the ball and Fernandes coolly sat down Suzuki to slot home the spot-kick.

United built momentum before levelling just before the break when Tielemans drilled low beyond Suzuki, with the aid of a deflection.

What should have been the launching pad for another stirring fightback quickly fell flat at the start of the second half.

Dalot dived in foolishly to trip Alysson and McGinn made amends for missing from the spot in last weekend’s 1-1 draw against Fulham.

Moments later Leny Yoro headed a McGinn free-kick off his own crossbar and Goretzka forced the ball over the line in the goalmouth scramble that ensued.

The closing stages were played out to the tune of more protests against United’s unpopular American owners, the Glazer family, until the home side hauled themselves off the canvas again.

Zirkzee’s cool finish reawakened the crowd and left Villa clinging on.

Much to the frustration of Unai Emery, his side could not resist the late assault as Suzuki flapped at Fernandes’s corner and Dorgu accepted the gift.

World.title: Ogun to convert 6,000 Amotekun, So-Safe personnel to state police — Abiodun
World.content:
Gov. Dapo Abiodun

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has said the state is ready for the establishment of its own police force, disclosing that more than 6,000 personnel of the Ogun State Security Network, known as Amotekun, and the So-Safe Corps are available to provide the manpower for the proposed outfit.

Abiodun said his administration had laid a solid foundation for state policing through the establishment of community-based security structures, noting that the existing personnel and operational experience of the two outfits would facilitate the transition.

The governor spoke at the 50th anniversary celebration of Ereke Day in Ikenne, Ikenne Local Government Area of the state, where he described the Ogun State House of Assembly’s approval of the establishment of state police as a significant step towards strengthening security and protecting lives and property.

Abiodun, who chairs the Nigeria Governors’ Forum Committee on State Police Creation and represents President Bola Tinubu on the committee, expressed confidence in the state’s readiness to implement the initiative.

He said: “I am the Chairman of the Governors’ Forum on State Police Creation and the representative of the President in the Governors’ Forum on State Police Creation. I am proud to announce that the Ogun State House of Assembly has approved the creation of state police.

“Between Amotekun and So-Safe Corps, we have over 6,000 personnel. We are ready for the Ogun State Police Command, and that will make the difference in protecting the lives and property of our people.”

The governor stressed that security was essential to economic prosperity, investment and sustainable development, adding that meaningful progress could only be achieved in an atmosphere of peace and stability.

He called for sustained collaboration between communities and security agencies to ensure the safety of residents, businesses and investors across the state.

In a related development, Abiodun directed the immediate reconstruction of the Delabo-Ikenne Road, assuring residents that the project would improve accessibility, enhance connectivity and stimulate economic activities in the community.

Speaking on the golden jubilee of Ereke Day, the governor described the 50-year celebration as a significant milestone reflecting the unity, common heritage and shared aspirations of the people of Ikenne.

“Fifty years is very remarkable in the tradition and history of any people. It speaks to a united and common heritage, shared values and a collective determination to build a better future,” he said.

He commended traditional rulers and the Ikenne Traditional Council of Chiefs for their leadership and commitment to preserving the community’s cultural identity while promoting development.

Abiodun also congratulated the people for sustaining the annual celebration over five decades, describing the achievement as a testament to the foresight of their forebears, the sacrifices of successive generations and the strength of their communal spirit.

He noted that Ereke Day had evolved beyond a cultural celebration into a platform for intellectual engagement, institutional development, infrastructural advancement and the preservation of the community’s heritage.

The governor particularly praised the Ikenne Community Development Association for mobilising the human, intellectual and financial resources of indigenes to address the community’s developmental needs.

According to him, while government has a responsibility to provide leadership and create an enabling environment, sustainable development also requires active participation and ownership by the people.

Describing Ikenne as a community of historical importance to Ogun State and Nigeria, Abiodun recalled its association with prominent national figures, including the late nationalist and statesman, Chief Obafemi Awolowo, and renowned educationist, Dr Tai Solarin.

He said their contributions to education, democratic governance and national development remained enduring legacies for younger generations to emulate.

Providing an update on his administration’s infrastructural interventions, Abiodun disclosed that more than 1,700 kilometres of roads had been constructed and rehabilitated across the state, including over 40 roads in Remoland.

He said the projects were aimed at improving transportation networks, opening up rural communities, enhancing connectivity and stimulating economic activities.

The governor, however, maintained that infrastructural development must go hand in hand with peace and security, stressing that no society could make meaningful progress without a stable environment.

He also urged youths in Ikenne to shun political violence and resist attempts by politicians to use them as instruments of violence ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“No political ambition is worth the peace of our community, and no temporary inducement is worth sacrificing your future,” he cautioned.

Abiodun urged the youths to demonstrate political maturity, patriotism and responsible civic engagement, insisting that electoral contests should be based on ideas, credible leadership, performance and issue-based campaigns rather than intimidation and violence.

He also appealed to traditional rulers, community leaders, professionals and Ikenne indigenes in the diaspora to sustain their contributions to the development of their ancestral community.

Earlier, the Chairman of the occasion, Mr Kunle Soname, described Abiodun as a worthy son of Remoland and commended his administration’s contributions to Ikenne’s development.

Soname specifically acknowledged the governor’s donation of a 500KVA transformer and the reconstruction of Awolowo Road, alongside other developmental interventions.

He assured Abiodun of the continued support and cooperation of the people of Ikenne and Remoland, expressing confidence in the administration’s commitment to the area’s development.

World.title: Enugu pensioners recount past ordeals as Mbah pays 26-year gratuity arrears
World.content:
…Pensioners hail governor as promise keeper

...Mbah: No retiree should go to bed hungry

Enugu State pensioners under the auspices of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) have hailed Governor Peter Mbah for keeping his campaign promise to clear legacy arrears, describing their decades of disappointment after serving their fatherland as a harrowing experience.

The pensioners spoke as retirees started receiving their gratuities dating back to the year 2000, with some also extending to the military era, saying the development had restored life to their bodies.

The Chairman, Enugu State chapter of NUP, Ikechukwu Ekere, confirmed the development at the weekend, describing it as “an emotional moment for pensioners, many of whom had long given up hope of receiving their gratuities in their lifetime.”

“Yes, I can confirm to you that our members have started receiving the alerts. Governor Mbah is a promise keeper; he has done it again and we can’t thank him enough,” he said.

In the same vein, the Caretaker Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, Local Government Staff Pensions Board Branch, Kenneth Ugwueze, told journalists that the development had restored hope and joy in many homes, saying that Mbah had, once again, proven himself as a leader who could be trusted.

“You know what it means for a governor to pay debts incurred by many governors before him? It takes a large quantity of milk of human kindness. We are happy to see a day like this in our lifetime. We will continue to pray for him.

“We are also grateful and happy with the new dimensions brought in by our governor in pension administration, especially in the local government system.

“Before now, local government workers and primary school teachers who retired had to wait for two years before receiving their pensions. But since the conclusion of the verification exercise in July 2024, no pensioner in the local government system has been denied pension. We have been receiving our pensions as and when due.

“Now that our people have started receiving alerts for their gratuity, it is a thing of joy,” he said.

Some beneficiaries of the ongoing payments also expressed gratitude to the governor, describing the development as a rekindling of hope after years and devades of waiting. They said previous governments had not paid them even in the days of excess crude revenues.

Mr. Luke Obi Ezea, who retired in 2014, said he had since resigned himself to fate and put everything in the hands of God.

“I put in 35 years in service. Already, I had put everything in the hands of God because previous governors had made promises, but to no avail. They were just empty promises at the end of their eight years. But Peter Mbah is an action governor and keeps his word,” he stated.

Mr. Sunday Nwadi, a 2015 retiree, described Mbah as a godly and listening governor who does not play politics with the welfare of his people.

“I am enjoying today because, apart from this gratuity, he is not owing monthly pensions. He is up to date. He is not like the others, who would owe us pensions for many months. Nothing will happen to Mbah. He is returning for a second term.”

Susanna Emehelu, whose husband retired in 2013, said the man had been sick for a long time, and they had been hoping against hope that the gratuity would come to help ameliorate their challenges.

“When I broke the good news to him, he was so happy and asked me to rush to the office to confirm. Now, he is so happy that he would eat the fruits of his labour in his lifetime. May God bless our governor,” she stated.

Mr. Paul Ozoeze, a 2010 retiree, said the gratuity payment had restored life to his body, noting that it had been nearly 20 years of suffering for him.

Meanwhile, the Accountant-General of Enugu State, Mr. Tony Okenwa, recalled that Mbah had always insisted during discussions leading up to the verification and payment of backlogs that no senior citizen should go to bed hungry.

“These are old debts. Some of them date back even to the military era. But the governor has said that no retiree will stay without receiving his or her pension and gratuity, and he is very passionate about it.

“Whenever I went to him, he would ask: ‘Do you mean that people retire and then don’t go home with their gratuity?’

“He could not understand how somebody would work for many years, retire and still not receive what he had earned,” Okenwa said.

He said the State Executive Council, after several layers of verification, approved N32bn, with the governor releasing an initial N10bn, assuring that the releases would continue until the entire liabilities were cleared.

World.title: Governorship Debate: Why many Lagos residents remain poor – GRV explains
World.content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, has accused successive state governments of prioritising elite interests over the welfare of ordinary residents.

Rhodes-Vivour, popularly known as GRV, made the allegation during the Lagos governorship debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium held in Lagos on Sunday, where he outlined his plans to address the state’s challenges.

He said his manifesto was designed to put residents first, adding that his administration would introduce practical solutions to problems including waste management, traffic congestion, healthcare and housing.

“My manifesto has always stood with the people, putting the interest of the people first. I have that track record. We’re bringing solution thinking to the problems of Lagos State, waste management, traffic, healthcare, housing,” he said.

The ADC candidate criticised the Lagos government over what he described as decades of policies focused on wealthy neighbourhoods and the elite, particularly in housing development.

He cited the government’s approach to communities such as Makoko, accusing the authorities of celebrating the state’s development while pushing out residents from their communities.

Rhodes-Vivour also questioned the impact of Lagos State’s internally generated revenue (IGR), arguing that the figures often celebrated by the government did not reflect the economic realities of ordinary residents.

“Lagos government, in the last 20 years has its focus on elite policies, eyebrow areas for housing. That’s why on paper, Lagos celebrates a high IGR, but on ground, people are not feeling it. We would focus on people, our policies are tailored towards that.”

He promised that an ADC-led administration would prioritise policies that directly address residents’ needs, reiterating his commitment to delivering 100,000 housing units.

The debate was organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard.

Other major contenders at the debate include Lagos Deputy Governor and All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Obafemi Hamzat; Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Funso Doherty; and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Deji Doherty.

Vanguard News

World.title: Kwara NDC Guber Candidate Unveils Six-Point  Agenda to Advance Good Governance
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

Ahead of the 2027 elections, the governorship candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress(NDC ) in Kwara State, Professor Abdulmumin Olayinka Ajia, has unveiled a six-point agenda that will take the state to greater heights if given the mandate to lead the state.

Prof. Ajia made the presentation in Ilorin weekend while participating in an interactive session for all the governorship candidates of political parties in the state organised by the Kwara State Chapter of the Association of Kwara Online Media Practitioners (ASKOMP).

He listed the six-point agenda as

security and justice; enterprise and jobs; education and skills; health and household security; infrastructure and energy; and transparent governance.

Ajia said that his vision is to build “a safe Kwara, a productive Kwara, a prosperous people” through functioning institutions, measurable commitments and public accountability.

“Kwarans deserve to know when a decision will be made, who is making it, what it will cost and how it will be judged,” he said.

On security, Ajia proposed a Kwara Rural Security and Recovery Compact to strengthen coordination among security agencies, local governments and communities, protect confidential reporting, and support communities recovering from attacks and displacement.

To expand employment, he outlined Productive Corridors and Itesiwaju Districts, connecting agriculture and enterprise to roads, reliable power, storage, processing facilities, skills and markets.

He also proposed three pathways for young graduates: a predictable annual public-sector recruitment season based on funded vacancies; an annual private-sector hiring season supported by incentives tied to verified employment; and enterprise grants or affordable loans, alongside mentoring and business support.

“My ambition is that every young graduate in Kwara can find a route into productive and gainful employment,” Ajia stated.

“My education proposals include a 90-day enrolment and attendance drive, better teacher deployment, career guidance and technical training linked to employment opportunities.

“In healthcare, he pledged stronger primary health centres, improved referrals and phased health-insurance expansion towards universal coverage.”

For workers, Ajia proposed working towards a sustainable N120,000 public-service wage benchmark, subject to payroll verification, full costing, consultation with organised labour and a published funding and implementation timetable.

He also committed to transparent promotion processes and a verified, funded pension and gratuity settlement schedule.

On infrastructure, he outlined improved public transport, worker and student passes, dependable waste collection, roads, water and power.

His proposed Ilorin light rail, according to him, will undergo demand, feasibility, operating-cost and financing assessments before any construction decision.

Ajia pledged to establish a baseline of state finances, liabilities, contracts and assets within his first 100 days.

He also said that his administration would publish revenues, expenditure and contract details, including security-vote spending subject to narrow safety exceptions.

The NDC governorship candidate also proposed ward councillors’ offices as accessible entry points for public services and a 25-commitment first-term delivery compact, tracked quarterly through a public green, yellow and red dashboard.

World.title: NDC: Tinubu Repeats Ibom Deep Seaport Promise, Questions APC’s 2020 Approval
World.content:
* Opposition party says Buhari-era FEC approval for $4.6bn project remains unfulfilled

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his renewed promise to construct the Ibom Deep Sea Port in Akwa Ibom State, questioning why the All Progressives Congress (APC) continues to make fresh commitments on a project that was approved by the previous administration in 2020.

The opposition party described Tinubu’s latest pledge as a repetition of an earlier campaign promise, insisting that the Federal Government had yet to demonstrate tangible commitment to translating the proposed multibillion-dollar project into reality.

Tinubu reportedly renewed the promise on Friday, November 6, 2026, while addressing supporters during his visit to Uyo, Akwa Ibom State.

However, in a statement Sunday, the NDC’s National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, accused the APC of using the proposed deep seaport as a political campaign instrument rather than demonstrating the political will to implement the project.

The party recalled that the Federal Executive Council (FEC), under former President Muhammadu Buhari, approved the implementation of the first phase of the $4.6 billion Ibom Deep Sea Port project on December 16, 2020.

According to the opposition party, the approval had identified Bollore/Power China as the preferred bidder and was expected to pave the way for the commencement of construction.

It argued that the renewed commitment by Tinubu was particularly troubling because he had also promised to build the port during the APC’s 2023 presidential campaign in Akwa Ibom State.

At the party’s presidential campaign rally held at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on January 30, 2023, Tinubu reportedly promised to establish the seaport alongside other development initiatives.

The NDC quoted the president as telling supporters: “We will do mechanised farming. We will export food from Akwa Ibom. We will build your seaport.”

The opposition party, however, accused the APC of failing to fulfil that commitment more than three years after making it.

It questioned the rationale behind making another promise on the same project without providing an account of what had happened to the earlier federal approval.

Describing the development as an indication of what it called the APC’s unfulfilled campaign promises, the NDC asked how many times the Federal Government would announce its approval of the Ibom Deep Sea Port before actual construction would commence.

“What a hocus-pocus, what hogwash, and what barefaced lies and shenanigans of a rudderless party! How many times will the APC approve the Ibom Deep Sea Port?” the party asked.

The NDC further accused the ruling party of elevating political promises above measurable performance, arguing that Akwa Ibom residents deserved concrete explanations on the status of the project rather than repeated assurances during electioneering.

It maintained that the deep seaport, if successfully implemented, would have significant economic implications for the state and the country, particularly in expanding maritime activities, facilitating international trade and creating employment opportunities.

The party also drew a comparison between the unfulfilled seaport promise and the Federal Government’s commitment to providing uninterrupted electricity across the country.

“As Nigerians are still waiting for the APC and President Tinubu to give us uninterrupted electricity supply, so Akwa Ibomites are waiting endlessly for the promised deep sea port that has become a campaign tool of deceit,” it stated.

The opposition party urged Nigerians to hold the ruling party accountable for its campaign commitments, insisting that electoral promises should be measured against actual delivery.

It called on voters to reject the APC in the 2027 general election, arguing that the country required a change in political leadership and governance priorities.

The NDC said its proposed political alternative offered Nigerians an opportunity to pursue what it described as a new direction for the country.

“Nigerians must shine their eyes and dump the APC into the abyss of socio-political irrelevance and make a new Nigeria possible,” the party added.

The statement was signed by Director, who reiterated the NDC’s position that a new Nigeria was possible under its political platform.

World.title: SSDC Moves to Rescue Bille As Gas Seepage Threatens Lives, Livelihoods
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The South-South Development Commission (SSDC) has delivered humanitarian relief materials to residents of Bille Kingdom in Degema Local Government Area of Rivers State following persistent gas seepage and methane emissions that have contaminated underground water sources, rivers and local wells.

The intervention, initiated by the commission’s Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Ms Usoro Akpabio, is aimed at alleviating the hardship imposed on residents by the environmental crisis, which has disrupted livelihoods, threatened food security and affected access to safe drinking water.

Leading the SSDC delegation to the affected community, the Executive Director, Social Services and Human Capital Development, Preye Aganaba, conveyed the commission’s assurance that Bille would not be abandoned.

Akpabio, in a statement, described Bille as a significant economic hub in Rivers State and the South-south region, warning that the environmental emergency posed serious humanitarian and economic consequences.

“The plight of the people of Bille is of great concern to the commission. Their recovery remains a priority, and we want to assure them that they will not be overlooked in our developmental agenda,” she said.

She disclosed that the commission provided 86 categories of food and non-food items, including rice, beans, garri, noodles, cooking oil, mattresses, mosquito nets, wrappers, buckets, sanitary pads and baby diapers.

According to her, the intervention aligns with President Bola Tinubu’s directive to the commission to provide relief to vulnerable communities and accelerate development across the six South-south states.

Akpabio added that the SSDC’s response was designed to complement the efforts of Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, the Rivers State Emergency Management Agency and the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA).

She pledged the commission’s continued commitment to environmental protection, disaster resilience, sustainable infrastructure and livelihood restoration across the region.

Speaking on behalf of the Bille Council of Chiefs, its Chairman, Chief Bennett Okpoke, commended the SSDC for responding to the community’s plight but urged the federal and state governments to address the root cause of the crisis.

He said residents had endured prolonged gas and methane seepage, with devastating effects on their water sources, livelihoods and daily activities.

Okpoke appealed to relevant environmental and regulatory agencies to urgently develop a lasting solution to the pollution, warning that the community’s health and economic survival were at stake.

Also speaking, NEMA’s Head of Operations for Bayelsa and Rivers States, Dr Chidi Ogundu, said the agency had approached the SSDC over the emergency and commended the commission for its swift intervention.

He disclosed that an Environmental Impact Assessment had been conducted, with findings indicating significant adverse effects on the community.

Describing the situation as a collective responsibility, Ogundu said: “An injury to one is an injury to all.”

He further revealed that NEMA’s technical team had commenced efforts to address the community’s potable water challenges and reduce residents’ exposure to potential health hazards.

The relief materials, provided on behalf of the SSDC’s Managing Director, Board Chairman and management, were formally handed over to the community through NEMA.

The delegation was received by the Bille Council of Chiefs, representing King Igbikingeri Ngowari Cornelius Herbert, Agbaniye-Jike XVIII.

World.title: OAU Drama Dept Set to Celebrate 50th Anniversary, Calls for Urgent Infrastructure Development
World.content:
Yinka Olatunbosun

The Department of Dramatic Arts at Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife, is set to celebrate its 50th anniversary, marking five decades of shaping African performance, indigenous scholarship, and cultural activism.

Founded in the mid-1970s at what was then the University of Ife, the department emerged as a radical hub for African total theatre. Central to its identity is its founding Head of Department, Africa’s first Nobel Laureate in Literature, Prof. Wole Soyinka.

This was disclosed during a press briefing held on November 6 at KAP Cinema, Ikeja.

Speaking on the anniversary milestone, the current Head of Department, Dr. Toyin Bifarin, highlighted the Golden Jubilee as a moment to reflect on the department’s founding ethos: using drama as an instrument for human rights, civic awareness and social transformation.

“The Department of Dramatic Arts, Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU) Ile-Ife has been the breeding ground for some of the most influential figures in African literature and performing arts. We are excited to celebrate its 50 years of excellence starting with this press conference. The flag-off ceremony will hold on November 12 at the Pit Theatre with the pioneering HOD of the department, Prof. Wole Soyinka, unveiling the official logo for the anniversary at the Pit Theatre, OAU. The anniversary lecture is scheduled to be held on January 12, 2027,” Bifarin said.

The anniversary lecture would be delivered by Prof. Bode Sowande and the panellists session would be moderated by Prof. Ahmed Yerima and Paulyn Ugbodaga.

A four-day celebration featuring a major homecoming gala will be held in the first quarter of 2027. It will conclude with Variety Night, Academic Session, Juma’at Service, Campus Excursions, Veterans Day, Grand 50th Gala Dinner, Fundraiser and an interdenominational service at OAU, Ile Ife.

The celebration is expected to bring together alumni, cultural icons, theatre practitioners, and scholars from around the globe to honour the department’s foundational history and explore the future of African performance in the digital age.

Members of the alumni association are calling on government, corporate bodies and distinguished individuals to support the institution which currently holds a capacity of 900 students.

The infrastructure deficit has remained one of the most daunting challenges with sustaining qualitative education at the department. At the moment, there is a need to renovate the theatre and install modern lighting and sound equipment for performances, toilets and changing rooms for performing students and lecturers, radio, podcast and film studio and a tour bus for performances.

Professor Ola Rotimi was the structural and artistic architect who engineered the transition of OAU’s theatrical arts from a research wing into a fully-fledged academic department.

Serving as a Senior Research Fellow at the Institute of African Studies, he physically and programmatically laid the groundwork between 1976 and 1977 for what is now the OAU Department of Dramatic Arts before handing leadership over to Professor Wole Soyinka and proceeded to establish the Department of Theatre Arts at University of Port Harcourt.

Over the past 50 years, OAU’s Department of Dramatic Arts has trained generations of prominent playwrights, directors, actors, scholars, and media producers who dominate Africa’s creative industries including Prof. Ahmed Yerima, Dr. Sola Fosudo, late Dr. Kola Oyewo and late Dr. Tejumola Olaniyan. Other notable alumni include Yemi Solade, Yemi Sodimu, Segun Arinze and Asake.

World.title: Defence Minister Calls for Reintroduction of Modernised Tollgates to Track Criminals, Safeguard Lives
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (rtd), has called for the strategic reinstatement of modernised, technology-driven tollgates across the nation’s major highways, describing them as critical non-kinetic security infrastructure essential for tracking criminal elements and safeguarding lives and livelihoods.

He stated that tollgates serve as vital security checkpoints globally and should be re-established under a modernised framework.

According to a statement by the Minister of Defence’s Special Assistant on Media, Leah Katung-Babatunde, the minister stressed that the removal and destruction of tollgates across the country was a strategic mistake.

General Musa made this call while participating as a panellist at the Abuja Round Table, tagged ‘Promise to Proof: The Renewed Hope Conversation,’ during a session focused on ‘Safe to Farm, Travel and Trade: Protecting Lives and Livelihoods in Every Community.’

He said: “With modern Information and Communications Technology (ICT) and automation, toll collection no longer requires cash transactions. Automated systems can instantly capture vehicle registration numbers, track vehicular movements across interstate corridors, and seamlessly trace or apprehend suspects.”

The minister noted that while tollgates faced operational abuses in the past, modern technological integration eliminates those vulnerabilities, positioning automated tolling as a formidable non-kinetic security tool.

Musa also highlighted the urgent need for a streamlined, foolproof national identification system to address the broader challenges of national security.

He stressed that integrating unique identification numbers, facial recognition and biometric data is vital for verifying records and eliminating identity ambiguity.

According to the minister, establishing a comprehensive and centralised digital identification architecture will effectively close persistent security loopholes and enhance real-time intelligence gathering across the federation.

On military deployment, he clarified that while the constitutional mandate of the Armed Forces of Nigeria is to defend the nation’s territorial integrity, the military legitimately steps in to support internal security when challenges exceed the capacity of the police.

However, Musa expressed deep concern over personnel fatigue resulting from prolonged internal deployments.

“Our troops have spent years deployed across regions such as the North-west, away from their families and loved ones,” he observed.

He reiterated that active measures are underway to strengthen police recruitment, training and operational capacity.

The overarching objective is to build a robust civil policing system that will enable the military to gradually withdraw, return to barracks and rest, shifting the national security apparatus from reactive measures to a proactive stance ahead of 2027.

He stressed that Nigeria’s greatest strength lies in its unity, asserting that the country’s primary challenge is not a shortage of resources or firepower, but internal divisions and a lack of cohesion among citizens.

World.title: 2027: Support Tinubu’s Re-election Bid, Danjuma Urges Adamawa Residents
World.content:
Daji Sani in Yola

General Theophilus Danjuma (rtd) has appealed to Adamawa residents to support the re-election bid of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the 2027 general election, rather than that of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar.

According to him, the Tinubu administration had appointed more Christians into key government positions, a development he said had contributed to the progress and development of the country.

He advised Christians to vote wisely in the forth coming general election as he also donated N250 million for the expansion of the Adamawa Government House Chapel and the construction of residences for its chaplain and deputy.

The donation was announced over the weekend in Yola during the 20th anniversary celebration of the Chapel, where Danjuma was represented by General Ishaya Bamaiyi (rtd).

The anniversary, themed ‘Thus far has the Lord helped us’ taken from 1 Samuel 7:12, brought together top government officials, former governors, religious leaders and other dignitaries from across the state.

Danjuma commended the founding fathers and organisers of the anniversary for their vision, commitment and sacrifices towards the establishment and growth of the Chapel over the past two decades.

Meanwhile, the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, urged youths, particularly Christian youths, to shun political thuggery and embrace peaceful conduct ahead of the 2027 general election.

Mrs Tinubu, who was represented by the Deputy Governor of Adamawa State, Professor Kaletapwa Farauta, advised young people not to allow politicians to exploit them for selfish interests, but to promote peace, tolerance and responsible participation in the electoral process.

Farauta, who also represented Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, said the governor wants the Chapel to remain a unifying platform for Christians across all denominations and not to be identified with any particular church.

Governor Fintiri urged members of the Chapel to sustain its spiritual activities and ensure that the fire on the altar continues to burn, adding that God’s presence would continue to guide the government and inspire development and peaceful coexistence.

“Adamawa belongs to all of us. We must all join hands to ensure that the state continues to move forward, while living together as one another’s keepers,” the governor said.

In his remarks, former Governor Boni Haruna who was the originator of the Government House Chapel, explained that the Chapel was established in 2005 to fulfil the original architectural design of the Government House complex, which provided for two places of worship, a mosque and a chapel, in line with equity and fairness, and to address historical imbalance.

He expressed hope that it would remain a symbol of unity for all residents irrespective of religious differences.

The Chairman of the Board of Trustees, and former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Mr Boss Mustapha, described the anniversary as a celebration of faith, courage, perseverance, unity and God’s faithfulness, urging the leadership to preserve its ecumenical character while respecting religious diversity.

The celebration also featured the presentation of awards to the First Lady, Governor Fintiri, founding fathers and past chaplains of the Chapel, as well as donations from dignitaries including Boss Mustapha, Boni Haruna, Bala Nggilari, Senator Amos Yohana and Dr Edgar Amos, among others.

World.title: Face of the World Nigeria Beauty Pageant Honours Okpebholo, Tenebe, Adeniyi, Others
World.content:
Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo; state Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Emperor Jarrett Tenebe; and Dr. Ifetayo Adeniyi were among prominent personalities honoured at the 20th edition of the Face of the World Nigeria Beauty Pageant, tagged the ‘Akpakomiza Edition’ on Saturday.

The colourful ceremony, organised by the Chairman of Divine Smiles Foundation International, Prince Eric Odigie, featured glamour, cultural displays, entertainment and the recognition of distinguished individuals for their contributions to societal development.

Okpebholo, Tenebe and other award recipients were celebrated for their respective roles in leadership, community development and impactful service, while Adeniyi emerged Best Journalist of the Year 2026 in recognition of his outstanding contributions to journalism and humanitarian advancement.

Adeniyi’s award, which was received on his behalf by Patrick Ochoga, was presented under the ‘Megastar Man of the Decade Award CSR’ category in acknowledgement of his commitment to national development and giving back to society.

In his appreciation, Adeniyi expressed gratitude to the organisers for the recognition, describing the honour as a motivation to deepen his contributions to the journalism profession and humanitarian causes.

Other distinguished awardees included Dr. Paddy Iyamu, Chief Edobor Ozakpolor, Chief Ebipade Karl, Hon. Cyril Oshiomhole, Excalibur Hotel, Mr. Elvis Edoba and Mrs. Edesili Okpebholo.

Speaking during the event, Odigie commended members of his organising team for their dedication and resilience in sustaining the beauty pageant over the years, noting that the platform had continued to provide opportunities for discovering and nurturing talents.

He acknowledged that the journey had been challenging, but said the experiences and disappointments encountered in previous editions had provided valuable lessons for improving the quality and organisation of subsequent events.

“The experiences and disappointments of the past years have taught us valuable lessons, which have helped us shape subsequent editions and make each event better than the previous one,” Odigie said.

The organiser also expressed appreciation to Tenebe for hosting the team in South Africa and facilitating international contacts, which he said had opened new opportunities for the organisation.

Odigie further applauded the contributions of sponsors and partners, including Wells Carlton Hotel and Apartments, Modela Couture, Pure Gold Sparkle Cosmetics, Ebenezer Apartment, Andy Modu Global Vision, Megastar Life & Style Magazine and Well Hosa Farm, describing their support as instrumental to the success of the event.

The beauty contest’s major highlight was the crowning of Blessing J. Oaikhena as Face of the World, Osato Omozokpia as Face of Edo, and Ebuba Simon as Face of Tourism.

Other winners were Ebuba Ugonwa, who emerged Most Beautiful Girl in Edo State; Chiwen Anamanya, Miss Amity; and Amenaghawon Idemudia, Miss Hospitality.

The winners were applauded for their beauty, poise, talent and impressive performances throughout the competition.

The 20th edition also featured captivating cultural performances by different ethnic nationalities, musical renditions by contestants and other groups, alongside exciting entertainment that added colour and splendour to the occasion.

World.title: NAF Redeploys 41 Air Vice Marshals to Strengthen Command Effectiveness
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has redeployed no fewer than 41 Air Vice Marshals (AVMs) in a major strategic realignment of its senior leadership.

According to a statement by the Director of Public Relations and Information, Nigerian Air Force, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, the postings and appointments are designed to strengthen command effectiveness, enhance institutional capacity and sustain operational readiness in support of national security objectives.

He noted that the exercise, approved by the Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, takes immediate effect.

Air Commodore Ejodame said: “The appointments span Service Headquarters, operational commands, Defence Headquarters, training institutions and other strategic establishments, reflecting a deliberate effort to align leadership competencies and professional experience with the Service’s evolving operational and institutional priorities.”

Air Commodore Ejodame, said that

at Headquarters NAF, AVM AK Ademuwagun has been appointed Chief of Transformation and Innovation; AVM IV Ajiboye as Superintendent of Standards and Evaluation; AVM PN Amadi as Chief of Air Intelligence; AVM NN Ananaba as Chief of Operations; AVM AH Bakari as Air Provost Marshal; AVM EE Efiom as Chief of Training; AVM MS Ibrahim as Chairman, Air Expo and International Liaison; AVM AG Kehinde as Chief of Civil-Military Relations; AVM MA Sulaiman as Chief of Communications and Information Systems; AVM S Peters as Coordinator, Project Implementation Team; and AVM AJ Laoye as Chief of Aircraft Engineering. Other strategic institutional appointments include AVM AY Dari as General Manager, Nigerian Air Force Investment Limited Group of Companies, and AVM NS Okoro as Director-General, AFRDI.

At the operational command level, AVM NI Ilo has been appointed Air Officer Commanding (AOC), Tactical Air Command, while AVM BR Mamman assumes command of Mobility Command. AVM OS Ogunsina becomes AOC, Logistics Command; AVM MN Onyebashi is appointed AOC, Special Operations Command; and AVM FCS Nwakara takes over as AOC, Ground Training Command.

In major institutional appointments, AVM PB Philips has been appointed Commandant, Armed Forces Command and Staff College (AFCSC), while AVM MC Ekwueme becomes Commandant, Armed Forces Resettlement Centre (AFRC). Other appointments in this category include AVM AO Akinbunwa as Commandant, Air Force War College; AVM A Idris as Commandant, Air Warfare Doctrine Centre; AVM JA Ekwuribe as Commandant, Regiment Training Centre; AVM OC Ubadike as Commandant, Air Force Institute of Technology; AVM AI Sambo as Commandant, Nigerian Air Force College of Logistics and Management; and AVM M Yusuf as Deputy Commandant, Nigerian Defence Academy.

At the strategic defence level, AVM UK Abdullahi has been appointed Director of Defence Operations at Defence Headquarters (DHQ), while AVM EOE Ebiowe moves to the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) as Deputy Coordinator, National Intelligence. Other appointments include AVM DDG Pwajok as Director of Technical Services, Defence Intelligence Agency (DIA); AVM I Sani as Deputy Chief of Defence Intelligence; AVM AA Shinkafi as Director of Liaison, DHQ; AVM AO Shogbamu as Director of Military Strategy; AVM RK Olanrewaju as Director of Search and Rescue; AVM J Usman as Director of Special Duties; AVM JJ Ijudigal as Director of Sports; AVM ZA Usman as Director of Cyber Operations; AVM EK Gabkwet as Director of Civil-Military Relations; and AVM GAA Bello as Director of Joint Warfare Doctrine, all at DHQ. Additionally, AVM AA Suleh has been appointed Deputy Chief of Defence Space Administration (DSA), while AVM OA Oyename becomes Director of Earth Observation and AVM SS Lazarus takes up appointment as Director of Launch Vehicles and Space Operations, both at DSA. AVM OT Salami has been posted to the Defence Space Command Centre (DSCC) as Deputy Chief, while AVM AI Hanidu moves to the Air Power Centre of Excellence (APCOE) as Director of Integrated Air Power Studies. Other appointments at APCOE include AVM OF Akinboyewa as Deputy Director-General and AVM MM Omar as Director, Museum/Hall of Fame. AVM DO Dickson has also been appointed General Manager, Operations, Defence Health Care Limited (DHCL).

Other appointments at Headquarters NAF include AVM AK Famuyiwa as Director of Coordination and Cooperation; AVM AK Bello as Director of Armament; AVM YA Katabiya as Director of Logistics; AVM EO Ashiegbu as Director of Policy; AVM GA Mbaka as Director of Aircraft Engineering; AVM AL Dakwat as Director of Research and Development; AVM SO Eyekosi as Director of Plans; and AVM AG Akinyimika as Director of Personnel Management.

To further strengthen operational command structures, AVM JI Ukeh has been appointed Commander, Nigerian Air Defence Corps (NADC). Other appointments include AVM OA Abu as Chief of Staff, Mobility Command; AVM I Subi as Chief of Staff, Special Operations Command; AVM NB Folaji as Chief of Staff, Tactical Air Command; AVM F Ekpah as Chief of Staff, Ground Training Command; AVM ES Odekina as Chief of Staff Logistics Command and AVM M Umar as Chief of Staff, Air Training Command. AVM GI Jibia has also been appointed Deputy Force Commander, Operation HADIN KAI. In other appointments, AVM CE Akubue has been appointed Managing Director, Aircraft Engineering and Technical Services Limited (AETSL), while AVM CE Akpa becomes Commander, Headquarters NAF Camp.

Other professional military education and training appointments include AVM SA Eyoma as Deputy Commandant, Air Force Institute of Technology; AVM FO Ankeli as Commandant, Air Traffic Services Training Centre; and AVM U Ariahu as Deputy Commandant, Nigerian Air Force College of Logistics and Management.

NAF spokesperson said the strategic realignment reflects the NAF’s commitment to continuous leadership renewal, stronger institutional accountability and enhanced operational effectiveness.

The CAS expressed confidence that the professional competence and wealth of experience of the newly appointed officers would further advance his Command Philosophy and strengthen the Service’s capacity to deliver decisive airpower effects in support of joint operations and national security objectives.

All affected officers are to assume their new appointments and complete the necessary handover and takeover formalities not later than 13 November 2026.

World.title: Confirmed: Carling Knockout semi-finals draw, Chiefs, Pirates travel away
World.content:
The Premier Soccer League confirmed the two matchups following Sunday’s live draw. Fans have learned of two mouthwatering battles involving the traditional big three.

The semi-final lineup was completed on Sunday after Stellenbosch FC and Kaizer Chiefs secured their places in contrasting fashion.

SUNDOWNS TO FACE KAIZER CHIEFS, ORLADO PIRATES DRAW STELLENBOSCH

Stellenbosch FC booked their ticket with a 2-1 victory over AmaZulu FC at the Danie Craven Stadium.



Kaizer Chiefs produced a determined comeback to beat Siwelele FC by the same scoreline.

Mamelodi Sundowns had edged Golden Arrows 1-0 during the week. Defending champions Orlando Pirates did their job over Sekhukhune United on Saturday in Soweto.

The meeting between Mamelodi Sundowns and Kaizer Chiefs is arguably the standout fixture of the semi-final round.



Amakhosi will have to overcome one of the strongest sides in the country if they are to move within touching distance of ending their lengthy wait for another domestic cup triumph.

Miguel Cardoso’s Sundowns, meanwhile, will be determined to add another trophy to their collection after securing their place in the last four.

The other encounter promises just as much intrigue. Orlando Pirates face a Stellenbosch FC side that has developed a reputation for being a difficult opponent in knockout football.



The Buccaneers are chasing another Carling Knockout crown and will be eager to defend the title they won last season. However, Stellenbosch will fancy their chances of causing an upset and ending the champions’ hopes of retaining the trophy.

Both ties will be decided over 90 minutes, with the winners advancing to the Carling Knockout final.

The PSL is expected to announce the semi-final dates, venues and kick-off times in due course. Supporters now waiting to see when the four heavyweight contenders will battle for a place in the final.

World.title: ELECTIONS 2026 | Here are the FINAL results
World.content:
South Africa's political landscape has shifted following the announcement of the final results of the 2026 Local Government Elections. Image: X @IECSouthAfrica

South Africa’s political landscape has shifted following the announcement of the final results of the 2026 Local Government Elections, with the African National Congress (ANC) recording its lowest-ever national election support.

The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) announced the final results on Sunday, 8 November, confirming that the ANC remains the country’s largest party nationally but has failed to secure an outright majority in any of South Africa’s metropolitan municipalities.

READ | ‘RACIAL HATRED’ | Roland Schoeman blasts Julius Malema



The ANC received 30.76% of the national vote, followed by the Democratic Alliance (DA) with 24.64%.

The uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MK) Party secured 9.76%, while the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) received 6.22%. ActionSA recorded 5.67%, the Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) 4.69% and the Freedom Front Plus (FF Plus) 2.99%.

How the parties performed nationally

The national results were as follows:



Party Share of national vote ANC 30.76% DA 24.64% MK Party 9.76% EFF 6.22% ActionSA 5.67% IFP 4.69% FF Plus 2.99%

Who won the metros?

The results across South Africa’s eight metropolitan municipalities showed a divided political picture.

The ANC emerged as the largest party in Buffalo City and Mangaung, while the DA led in five metropolitan areas:

City of Cape Town

City of Ekurhuleni

City of Johannesburg

Nelson Mandela Bay

City of Tshwane

The MK Party was the leading party in eThekwini.



Eight metro results

Metro 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 5th Johannesburg DA 34.79% ANC 20.25% ActionSA 16.27% EFF 6.52% MK 5.57% Tshwane DA 34.37% ActionSA 22.07% ANC 20.22% FF+ 7.63% EFF 5.77% Ekurhuleni DA 30.68% ANC 22.11% ActionSA 18.50% MK 7.02% EFF 6.49% Cape Town DA 56.42% ANC 13.95% PA 3.77% EFF 3.73% FF+ 3.42% eThekwini MK 38.29% DA 25.45% ANC 16.43% IFP 6.79% ActionSA 2.85% Mangaung ANC 33.91% DA 33.49% EFF 8.59% FF+ 5.92% PA 4.34% Nelson Mandela Bay DA 44.17% ANC 25.48% EFF 5.55% SACP 3.19% PA 3.04% Buffalo City ANC 41.93% UDM 18.39% DA 16.85% EFF 6.79% SACP 4.45%

ANC acknowledges election setback

ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula described the party’s performance as “catastrophic”.

He said the ANC would not beg for positions during coalition negotiations and acknowledged that voters had delivered a message to the party.

“When the people tell us we have fallen short. The honest answer is not to argue with them but to go home and put our house in order,” Mbalula said.



The results place renewed focus on the ANC’s declining electoral support, following its loss of a national parliamentary majority in the 2024 general election.

Coalition negotiations begin

With several municipalities lacking an outright majority, political parties will now turn their attention to coalition negotiations.

Parties have 14 days to negotiate before municipal councils are formed.



The DA has said it will initiate discussions with parties that share its stated commitment to clean and accountable government, fighting corruption, service delivery, the rule of law and non-racialism.

FF Plus leader Corne Mulder has also called for the DA and ActionSA to work together to govern Gauteng’s three metros.

The negotiations will be particularly important in Johannesburg, Ekurhuleni and Tshwane, where the composition of council majorities will determine who forms the municipal administrations.



The 2026 election results have therefore set the stage for a new round of coalition politics, with parties required to negotiate working arrangements in municipalities across the country.

World.title: Miguel Cardoso’ bold Sundowns claim after USM Alger shock
World.content:
Sundowns suffered a 3-1 defeat at Loftus Versfeld. It follows weeks after the shocking disappointing of going in the CAF Champions League preliminary qualifying rounds.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign as African champions, Ka Bo Yellow have now endured two major continental disappointments in a short space of time.

MIGUEL CARDOSO EXPLAINS MAMELODI SUNDOWNS DEFEAT

Their failure to qualify for the Champions League group stages after losing to Wiliete SC was particularly damaging. It was the first time in more than a decade that the club will miss out on the competition’s group phase.



Cardoso believes Sundowns created opportunities against USM Alger but failed to make them count, while their opponents were far more clinical.

“We made mistakes that were penalised by goals. There wasn’t much actions from USMA, the difference was the level of profit they had from what they created, compared to what we didn’t take from what we created,” he said.

The Portuguese tactician also pointed to the difficult playing conditions after heavy rain affected the pitch during the second half. However, he refused to use the weather as an excuse for the result.



“When I saw the conditions of the pitch in the second half. I knew it would be tough for us, it was not easy to play [with the rain]. It was catastrophic, but it’s not excuses. I think we had bad luck to get the sparkle to get us back in the match.

“We then went down by two goals on counter attack and then there’s the emotions that follow. We tried, we knew USMA had character as a North African team. It became tricky, congratulations to USMA, the players and the club.”

Sundowns now have a two-and-a-half-week break during the FIFA international window, with their continental commitments over for the remainder of the season.



Cardoso acknowledged the disappointment. He insisted that the team must use the setback as an opportunity to improve rather than dwell on what has happened.

“There’s always something to learn from negatives, I don’t see another way forward, we wanted to win this,” he said.

The Sundowns coach also recalled a previous encounter at Loftus Versfeld during his time with Esperance. Rain similarly affected the conditions and made it difficult for his opponents to perform at their best.



“You remember the match I played here a few years ago [with Esperance]. Sundowns dominated, and then there was the rain that delayed. It was not conditions for Sundowns to show the best they have.

“Results like this bring you down to the floor, but only one way to react, we have challenges in the short-term, that’s how big teams get out of it. It’s not disaster or catastrophe, there’s no losers in this. I won’t say who was the better team.”

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs flop scores 13 goals in 16 games abroad
World.content:
Former Kaizer Chiefs striker Efmamjjasond González is enjoying life in China, scoring goals for fun.

The Colombian striker joined Amakhosi on loan from Real Santa Cruz during the 2023/24 season with high expectation but failed to score or register a single assist in what turned out to be a dreadful campaign for the Soweto giants, who also missed out on a place in the top eight.

González was considered a flop by many Chiefs supporters and was eventually let go after just one season.



After moving between various clubs, the 27-year-old has finally found his scoring boots at Chinese League One outfit Nantong Zhiyun.

Kaizer Chiefs flop flourishing

On Saturday, González continued his red-hot scoring form by guiding Nantong Zhiyun to yet another victory. The striker netted a hat-trick, taking him to second place in the Chinese League One Golden Boot race.

He has scored 13 goals in 16 appearances this season and also added an assist.



González is not the only former Kaizer Chiefs striker who struggled at Naturena but is now thriving abroad.

Ranga Chivaviro, who was often booed by Amakhosi supporters, is also enjoying life in Saudi Arabia. The experienced striker scored 13 goals in 28 appearances for Al Fahaheel last season.

Like González, Chivaviro appears to have put his disappointment at Kaizer Chiefs behind him and is finding the back of the net regularly in a different league.

World.title: Springboks alter squad as veteran earns call up and rookie returns home
World.content:
Experienced lock Eben Etzebeth has been called up to the national squad and will join the Springboks in France on Monday, while uncapped flyhalf Yaqeen Ahmed will return to South Africa on Sunday due to a shoulder niggle.

Etzebeth, the most capped Bok with 147 Test appearances, was ruled out of Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus’ initial touring squad for the second phase of the Nations Championship due to injury. However, he is now fit and has been recalled to the squad in place of Ahmed.

The 20-year-old Ahmed, one of six uncapped players in the squad, was sidelined with a sore shoulder which saw him miss most of the training sessions in the build-up to the Boks’ 66-7 victory against Italy in Turin on Saturday.



RASSIE ERASMUS ON HIS SQUAD CHANGE

“We are very sad for Yaqeen after earning his first call-up to the national squad, but we feel it will be best for him to return to South Africa to recover,” said Erasmus on Sunday.

“After being with us for a week, he has a good idea of how we operate and has more insight into our systems, and we are confident that the experience will benefit him immensely as a player going forward.

“With enough backline cover in the squad and a number of versatile players among them, we opted to call up Eben, who will not only bring vast experience to the group at this vital stage of the Nations Championship, but also valuable leadership skills, especially with two important matches against France and Ireland in the next two weeks before the Finals Weekend of the tournament.”

SPRINGBOKS VS FRANCE INFORMATION

Erasmus will name his match-23 to face France on Monday. The Test at the Stade de France kicks off at 22h10 (SA time) on Friday and will be broadcast live on SuperSport.

World.title: Springboks: One player called up, another heads home
World.content:
On Sunday evening the Springboks confirmed that star lock Eben Etzebeth – the most capped South African Test player with 147 caps – has been called up to the national squad, and he will join the squad in France on Monday.

Etzebeth was ruled out of Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus’ initial touring squad for the second phase of the Nations Championship due to injury, but the stalwart has made a quick recovery.

However, uncapped flyhalf Yaqeen Ahmed will return to South Africa on Sunday due to a shoulder niggle that saw him miss most of the training sessions in the build-up to the Springboks’ 66-7 victory against Italy in Turin on Saturday.



Springboks add experience to team ahead of battle with France

After starting their tour with a comprehensive win over Italy, the Springboks next face France on Friday.

“We are very sad for Yaqeen after earning his first call-up to the national squad, but we feel it will be best for him to return to South Africa to recover,” said Erasmus on Sunday.

“After being with us for a week, he has a good idea of how we operate and has more insight into our systems, and we are confident that the experience will benefit him immensely as a player going forward.

“With enough backline cover in the squad and a number of versatile players among them, we opted to call up Eben, who will not only bring vast experience to the group at this vital stage of the Nations Championship, but also valuable leadership skills, especially with two important matches against France and Ireland in the next two weeks before the Finals Weekend of the tournament.”

Focus turns to next challenge

Erasmus will name his match-23 to face France on Monday, with the Test at the Stade de France kicking off at 22:10 (SA time) on Friday.

Coming into this clash after outplaying Italy, Erasmus said he was happy with the team’s discipline: “I think we only conceded one penalty in the first half, and about five penalties and five turnovers in the game, which is pretty disciplined, even though the second half was a little soft.”



Asked what the main contributing factors were to the team’s ability to consistently keep building, Erasmus added: “The biggest thing is that we’ve been together for eight years now, and we’re slowly bringing in guys like Ethan (Hooker), ‘Krappie’ (Morne van den Berg), Sacha (Feinberg-Mngomezulu), Ruan (Nortje), Cameron (Hanekom), Jan-Hendrik (Wessels), and Thomas (du Toit) is now back with us too.

“So we’ve been able to bring people in here and there, and when you go to a game like this and pick a team that’s match fit and ready, and everybody is calm and understands the system because we’ve been coaching them for a while, it’s satisfying.”

World.title: Sundowns lose CAF Super Cup final on homesoil
World.content:
The victory over Sundowns sees the Algerian giants secure their second CAF Super Cup title in three years. They previously beat Al Ahly in the 2023 edition.

Sundowns had to make an early change before kick-off after Nuno Santos picked up a hamstring injury. Cassius Mailula was brought into the starting line-up as his replacement.

CAF SUPER CUP: MAMELODI SUNDOWNS 1-3 USM ALGER

However, the Brazilians struggled to contain USM Alger’s early attacking threat, particularly down the left side of their defence.



The visitors took the lead through veteran midfielder Zakaria Draoui. He finished from close range after Sundowns failed to deal with an attacking move.

Miguel Cardoso’s men eventually found a response when Thabang Matuludi won a penalty following a handball. The referee awarded the spot-kick after consulting VAR.

Iqraam Rayners converted to make it 1-1 after replacing the injured Brayan León, who had earlier been stretchered off.

But Sundowns’ celebrations were short-lived as USM Alger regained the advantage just over 10 minutes later.

Captain Saadi Radouani reacted quickest after a header from a corner struck the crossbar, turning home the rebound to make it 2-1.

EXTENDED HALF TIME BREAK

The Brazilians headed into the interval trailing, with the second half also getting off to a delayed start because of heavy rainfall in Pretoria.



Water on the pitch affected the opening stages after the restart, but Sundowns attempted to take control and find another equaliser.

Instead, USM Alger delivered the decisive blow on the counter-attack.

Ahmed Khaldi produced a superb finish from the left side of the Sundowns defence, curling the ball beyond Ronwen Williams to extend the visitors’ lead to 3-1.

The goal left the Brazilians with a mountain to climb, and they ultimately failed to find a way back into the contest.

USM Alger walked away with the trophy, while Sundowns suffered another painful continental setback following their recent CAF Champions League elimination.

World.title: ANC tops the polls in shifting political landscape
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The African National Congress (ANC) has come out on top in the 2026 Local Government Elections, securing the biggest share of the vote and the most council seats.

Announcing the final election results on Sunday, IEC chairperson Mosotho Moepya confirmed that the party clinched 30.76% of the vote.

The Democratic Alliance came in second with 24.67%. uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party was third with 9.76% of the vote.

The Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) was fourth with 6.22%, as ActionSA rounded off the top five with 5.67% of the vote.

Municipalities tell a different story.

READ | IEC declares 2026 Local Government Elections free and fair

The ANC's dominance has been spread out among other players.

The former liberation party achieved outright control in 53 municipalities, compared to 122 in 2021.

The DA achieved majorities in 12 municipalities, including the stronghold of Cape Town.

The Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) achieved outright control in five municipalities, down from nine at the last municipal polls.

Newcomer MK Party secured three councils and leads in 19 municipalities.

Another surprise package was Northern Cape’s Rise Tsantsabane Communities. The party collective clinched the Tsantsabane Local Municipality.

World.title: IEC declares 2026 Local Government Elections free and fair
World.content:
HEADLINE - The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) has declared the 2026 Local Government Elections free and fair.
