World.title: Yemeni army reports nearly 1,000 strikes on Houthi targets, 97 military assets damaged or destroyed
World.content:
ADEN: Yemen’s armed forces said on Sunday they carried out nearly 1,000 strikes against Iran-backed Houthi forces as part of Operation Dawn of Yemen, targeting positions, reinforcements and military equipment across several fronts.

A military spokesperson said preliminary field reports indicated that about 267 Houthi commanders and fighters had been killed, wounded or had fled the battlefield.

The military also reported destroying or damaging 97 military assets, including vehicles, artillery pieces and launch platforms, along with an unspecified number of positions and fortifications. Efforts to verify the full toll were continuing, the spokesperson said in a statement on X.

The operations included 19 airstrikes on the Marib, Taiz and Tur Al-Bahah fronts and 29 drone strike missions targeting Houthi positions, vehicles, weapons and equipment.

Artillery and multiple-launch rocket systems carried out another 944 strikes against reinforcements, firing positions, fortifications and sniper positions, according to the spokesperson.

On the ground, units from the Sixth, Seventh and Third Military Regions continued operations across the Marib fronts, targeting Houthi positions and movements, the military said.

In Taiz, troops backed by the Popular Resistance fought Houthi forces, repelled attacks and targeted firing positions across several sectors, according to the statement.

Farther north, including in Al-Jawf, Emergency Forces units and Nation’s Shield Forces reported further advances while clearing mines from areas recaptured in earlier fighting. The statement did not identify the locations or extent of those gains.

On the southern and southwestern fronts, the Nation’s Shield Forces, Giants Brigades and National Resistance took control of several positions, the military said. Fighting continued in other sectors.

The armed forces said they were taking precautions to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure during the operations.

World.title: Industrial powers’ climate finance debt trap at COP31
World.content:
This month’s COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkiye, is ostensibly being convened to finalize global climate finance and operationalize the Loss and Damage Fund. However, environmental restitution has decisively mutated into a theater of geopolitical conflict.

The structural advantage is already evident: while Turkiye hosts the summit, which opens on Monday, the core climate negotiations are being directed by Australia — a Western industrial and mining heavyweight. Since the 2009 Copenhagen conference established an annual $100 billion funding pledge, major economies have systematically circumvented their obligations. Oxfam data reveals that more than 71 percent of this capital reaches developing nations as interest-bearing debt rather than emergency grants.

Meanwhile, climate devastation accelerates. The World Meteorological Organization records global economic losses exceeding $2.8 trillion over the past decade and the Independent High-Level Expert Group on Climate Finance projects that developing nations will require $2.4 trillion annually by 2030. This vast capital requirement has transformed climate finance from humanitarian relief into an instrument of strategic hegemony. Industrialized nations — responsible for 79 percent of cumulative historical carbon emissions — are actively rewriting the global financial architecture to consolidate economic dominance under the guise of ecological protection.

Rigid credit regulations, marketed as governance and transparency safeguards, effectively operate as geoeconomic traps. Legally and functionally, they replicate the catastrophic “structural adjustment” programs that suffocated the Global South in the 1980s. The International Monetary Fund confirmed in 2024 that more than 60 percent of low-income countries are in, or at high risk of, sovereign debt distress, yet they remain subject to crippling conditionalities for adaptation funding.

This artificial institutional friction paralyses capital deployment. World Resources Institute metrics indicate that a single project approval under the Green Climate Fund takes 12 to 24 months. Vulnerable nations are forced into a binary trap: succumb to compounding climate disasters without capital or accept draconian terms that erode sovereign autonomy, surrendering fiscal policy to the exact industrial powers that engineered the climate crisis.

Entering the Antalya summit as a fractured, subservient bloc is no longer an option for the Global South. Dr. Bader bin Saud

This structural subversion is most evident in the Loss and Damage Fund, ratified in Sharm El-Sheikh in 2022 and operationalized in Dubai the following year. Designed as a vehicle for unconditional restitution for irreversible climate impacts, its legislative framework has been quietly restructured to mirror a commercial investment bank.

UN assessments place developing world loss and damage requirements at $400 billion annually. Total institutional commitments currently hover at a negligible $700 million — less than 0.2 percent of the actual need. Entrusting the fund’s interim management to the World Bank Group exacerbates the crisis, enabling high administrative extraction and imposing structural conditionalities that tie compensation to Western economic dictates. This strips climate restitution of its moral and legal foundation, reducing it to a political bargaining chip granted for compliance and withheld for sovereign defiance.

Mandatory privatization of sovereign environmental sectors will form the critical front line at the Antalya summit. Zambia’s grueling 2023-24 debt restructuring process provides a grim preview: to secure fiscal lifelines from international creditors, the state was heavily pressured to offer sweeping concessions in its copper and cobalt sectors — the exact strategic minerals the West requires for its own energy transition.

Under these frameworks, developing nations can access capital only by privatizing strategic assets — water infrastructure, renewable energy grids and land management — granting transnational corporations controlling equity. This strategy effectively resurrects the Washington Consensus of the 1990s.

The geoeconomic motive is laid bare by the International Energy Agency, which states the global green transition requires $4 trillion in annual investment leading up to 2030. Conditional climate finance is engineered not to build resilience in the Global South but to guarantee foreign capital absolute control over emerging market resources in the name of green infrastructure.

Tethering climate finance to asset privatization initiates an advanced phase of economic neocolonialism. Transnational corporations and industrialized states are leveraging climate vulnerability to acquire sovereign environmental assets at distressed valuations, exploiting the Global South’s desperate liquidity requirements.

The 2024 UN Conference on Trade and Development report revealed developing nations spend more than $840 billion annually servicing external debt — repaying Global North creditors exponentially more than they receive in climate aid. This structural asymmetry strips vulnerable nations of their victim status, reconstituting them as captive consumer markets forced to finance their own adaptation by liquidating their national sovereignty.

Entering the Antalya summit as a fractured, subservient bloc is no longer an option for the Global South. Vulnerable nations must form a unified sovereign coalition to demand the absolute removal of financial conditionality from environmental commitments. This necessitates establishing independent, grant-based financing mechanisms outside the traditional Bretton Woods architecture, which was designed in 1944 specifically to entrench Western economic hegemony.

The persistent argument that global budgets cannot sustain climate restitution is a statistical fiction. The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute documented global military expenditure reaching $2.4 trillion in 2023 — a figure identical to the annual climate finance required by the developing world. The capital exists in abundance. The current system is not a rescue operation but a calculated strategy by industrial cartels to impose climate debt and strip the Global South of its sovereign resources.

Dr. Bader bin Saud is a columnist for Al-Riyadh newspaper, a researcher in media and knowledge management, a university professor, an expert in crowd management and strategic planning, and the former deputy commander of the Special Forces for Hajj and Umrah in Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Train collision in Egypt’s Giza kills 4, injures 88: health ministry
World.content:
Al Ayyat – Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday, derailing several carriages, killing four and injuring dozens, according to the authorities.

Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan.

The health ministry said an initial count put the toll from the crash at four passengers killed, with 88 others currently being treated for injuries in hospitals around the Giza area.

State-owned media had earlier reported 120 people were wounded, without clarifying the degree of injury.

President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the accident “with great concern”, and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to “hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent”.

Emergency crews used cranes to remove the wreckage, the authority said.

Several carriages lay on their side, AFP journalists at the scene reported. One end of a train had crumpled into a mangle of steel, while the end of the other — spliced open in the impact — had toppled off the tracks into an adjacent farm.

First responders and passersby helped lift one of the victims out of the wreckage in a black body bag, AFP images showed.

Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza’s Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt’s worst-ever rail disaster.

In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo.

In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens.

Egypt’s 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents.

Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.

World.title: Iraq reportedly delivers US message to Iran during Tehran visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – According to sources cited by Saudi-owned Al Hadath television, an Iraqi delegation headed to Tehran for an eight-hour diplomatic trip to convey a message from the United States to Iranian leaders.

The alleged visit coincides with rising tensions between Washington and Tehran, with Iraq increasingly aiming to position itself as a diplomatic middleman between the two nations.

The allegation was carried by Iran International and other Iranian media sites, and it linked the delegation’s travel to a recent phone call between US President Donald Trump and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, as well as a visit to Baghdad by US Special Envoy Tom Barrack.

However, neither Iraqi nor Iranian officials have officially acknowledged the claimed mission.

The identity of the delegation members, the nature of the supposed American message, and Tehran’s reaction are unclear.

The accusations come after a November 6 phone call between Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi, during which Hussein suggested forming a committee of regional foreign ministers to visit Washington and Tehran in an attempt to defuse tensions.

Iraq’s diplomatic attempts take place amid a background of differences over Iran’s nuclear program, security in the Strait of Hormuz, and the actions of Iran-aligned armed organizations in Iraq.

Baghdad has tight political and economic ties with Tehran while simultaneously working with Washington on security issues, putting Iraq in a potentially advantageous position to facilitate indirect contact between the two administrations.

World.title: Turkey to gradually hand over military base to Iraq as Baghdad-Ankara ties strengthen
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkey will begin taking steps to gradually transfer control of the Bashiqa-Zilkan military base in northern Iraq to the Iraqi federal government, according to a joint announcement issued on Sunday, November 8.

According to the Office of Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, Baghdad and Ankara have also agreed to set up a joint security coordination committee to monitor efforts to restore full Iraqi government authority in Sinjar, Nineveh Governorate, and to end the presence of armed groups operating outside state control.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan struck an agreement in New York on September 23, leading to the announcement.

The two heads of state agreed to coordinate security measures in northern Iraq and plan for the eventual handover of the Turkish military station.

Turkey maintained a presence at the Bashiqa-Zilkan base near Mosul during the 2015 anti-ISIS battle.

However, the deployment sparked long-standing tensions, with Baghdad frequently objecting to Turkish forces operating on Iraqi soil without federal authority.

Turkey has also maintained military bases and carried out cross-border operations in northern Iraq against the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK), which Ankara deems a terrorist group.

Baghdad has condemned transgressions of Iraqi sovereignty while expanding cooperation with Turkey to combat the group’s operations.

In April 2024, Erdoğan visited Baghdad and signed agreements on security, commerce, energy, water management, and infrastructure development, leading to an improvement in relations between the two nations.

In August 2024, Iraq and Turkey inked a military and security cooperation pact to improve information sharing, counterterrorism coordination, and military training.

Beyond security, Baghdad and Ankara are pursuing big economic projects, such as the Development Road Project, which intends to link Iraq’s southern ports to Turkey and European markets via new transportation infrastructure.

The anticipated surrender of Bashiqa-Zilkan is another step toward settling a long-standing border conflict, while Turkey continues to retain military posts in northern Iraq.

World.title: Chelsea shocked by Sunderland, Liverpool cruise
World.content:
London – Chelsea suffered a shock 1-0 defeat at Premier League strugglers Sunderland, while Liverpool got back on track with a 3-1 win against lowly Crystal Palace on Sunday.

Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea arrived at the Stadium of Light hoping to bolster their bid to qualify for the Champions League via a top-four finish.

Instead, they departed red-faced after an embarrassing loss to third-bottom Sunderland, who celebrated a league victory for only the second time this season.

Fifth-placed Chelsea have already been beaten four times in 10 league matches under former Real Madrid boss Alonso.

Chelsea were rocked in the 36th minute when Enzo Le Fee converted a penalty after Brian Brobbey was up-ended by Levi Colwill.

Blues boss Xabi Alonso was furious that Chelsea were not given a foul on Cole Palmer in the build-up to the spot-kick.

Liverpool had been beaten by Arsenal in the Premier League and Fenerbahce in the Champions League before arriving in south London, sparking pointed questions about Andoni Iraola in the former Bournemouth manager’s first season in charge at Anfield.

But Alexis Mac Allister headed Liverpool in front at Selhurst Park from Dominik Szoboszlai’s cross after 40 minutes.

Florian Wirtz bagged Liverpool’s second with a composed finish from Bradley Barcola’s cross in the 54th minute.

It was Wirtz’s first league goal this season and only the second in all competitions for the inconsistent German playmaker this term.

Alexander Isak finished off Wirtz’s pass in the 89th minute to wrap up fourth-placed Liverpool’s much-needed victory after a two-game losing streak.

It was Liverpool’s fourth consecutive away league win this season.

Eddie Nketiah’s stoppage-time penalty after a foul by Milos Kerkez was no consolation for Palace.

Palace manager Pierre Sage — hired to replace Oliver Glasner in the close-season is on the brink of being sacked after his side slumped to the bottom of the table following their seventh defeat in 10 league matches.

– Seagulls flying high –

Brighton extended their superb start to the season, climbing to second place with a 2-0 win against Brentford at the Amex Stadium.

While Fabian Hurzeler’s side might not have the staying power to challenge Arsenal for the title, they have established themselves as contenders for a Champions League place.

Diego Gomez’s 25-yard rocket gave the Seagulls the lead in the 15th minute.

Brentford striker Igor Thiago was sent off for clattering Chema Andres in the face midway through the first half.

Pascal Gross doubled Brighton’s advantage with a 42nd minute penalty after Keane Lewis-Potter fouled Luka Vuskovic.

The Seagulls’ sixth win in their last seven league games lifted them above third-placed Manchester City and within five points of champions Arsenal, who beat Hull on Saturday.

Evanilson maintained his hot streak in Bournemouth’s 2-1 win at Ipswich.

The Cherries’ Brazilian forward struck with a clinical finish in the fifth minute, taking him to seven goals in his last eight games.

An own goal from Leif Davis in the 46th minute increased Bournemouth’s lead and Jack Clarke’s 73rd minute penalty wasn’t enough to rescue Ipswich.

In Sunday’s late game, Manchester United manager Michael Carrick cannot afford a defeat against Aston Villa at Old Trafford as he fights to save his job ahead of the international break.

United are without a victory in their last seven league games and have won just once in the top-flight this term.

They ended a miserable nine-match winless run in all competitions by coming from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday.

smg/ea

World.title: Spain’s Alcaraz wins Paris Masters for first time
World.content:
Paris – Carlos Alcaraz gained a measure of revenge on Ben Shelton on Sunday as the seven-time Grand Slam champion beat the American 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 to win the Paris Masters for the first time.

In defeating the man that ended his US Open title defence earlier this season, the 23-year-old Spaniard claimed the ninth 1000-level title of his career.

Unlike their five-set quarter-final epic in New York two months ago, the clash in Paris lasted just under two hours.

Ahead of the ATP Finals, which run November 15-22 in Turin, world number three Alcaraz now holds five tour-level titles this year — only the injured Jannik Sinner has more with six.

In Italy, he will be seeking a first coronation at the season-ender.

After winning two French Opens and now the Paris Masters, Alcaraz is undefeated in title matches in the city.

But not for the first time in the French capital, Alcaraz won the title by saving match points en route — this time against Taylor Fritz in the quarter-finals in scenes reminiscent of his iconic Roland Garros final win against Italian Sinner last year.

For world number four Shelton, it was a first defeat in a Masters final after winning his two previous appearances in showpiece matches at that level– both coming in the last two editions of the Canadian Open.

– ‘Ten out of ten’ –

Serving at 1-2 in the first set, Alcaraz flirted with danger as he offered up four break points, but dug in to secure the hold when Shelton misfired at the end of a seven-minute long game.

Shelton then found himself two break points down in the seventh game but responded with a perfect drop volley and blistering passing shot to bring up deuce, before holding and keeping his nose in front.

Although both players threatened on the other’s serve and drew repeated gasps from the crowd with some audacious shot-making, the opener nonetheless required a tie-break to separate them.

A Shelton error at 4-4 followed by a leaping backhand smash by Alcaraz brought up two set points.

The first came and went when Alcaraz thundered the ball into the top of the net cord and the expectant arena froze in time as it rose and fell in seeming slow motion, only to land on the Spaniard’s side of the court.

Alcaraz was not to be denied a second time, however, as Shelton overcooked a forehand on the next point to cede the opener.

At 2-2 in the second set, Shelton let out a bellow of frustration after missing a groundstroke at 15-30 on Alcaraz’s serve, but the American could smile at the end of the game as a double fault and missed forehand produced the first break of the match.

Alcaraz had said after booking his spot in the final that his reflexes would need to be “ten out of ten” when facing Shelton’s serve and they were just that three games later as he levelled the set at four-all.

A deft exchange of angled drop shots ended by an Alcaraz winner down the line brought the Spaniard’s finger to his ear and the crowd again to their feet as Shelton suddenly found himself serving to keep the final alive.

He did so at the first time of asking but when required to serve again to force a breaker, Shelton cracked as Alcaraz again pounced to seal the title with a flicked backhand winner.

World.title: Iraq accelerates completion of 1,640 MW Anbar power plant
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has authorized authorities to repay overdue payments to the Chinese business that is building the Anbar Combined-Cycle Power Plant, a significant electrical project with a projected capacity of 1,640 megawatts.

The decision was issued at a meeting with business executives on Sunday, November 8, 2026, during which Al-Zaidi stressed the importance of maintaining construction quality and completing the project’s technical criteria.

SEPCOIII, a Chinese engineering and construction firm linked with state-owned PowerChina, is implementing the project.

The project, near Hit in Iraq’s western Anbar Governorate, is being built for the Iraqi Ministry of Electricity.

The facility will be powered by four gas turbines and two steam turbines, with combined-cycle technology used to create extra energy from heat generated during gas-fired power production.

Construction started in 2013 but was halted after the Islamic State group’s control of sections of Anbar.

Work restarted in late 2022, with the Chinese contractor taking over responsibility for finishing the project.

The plant is scheduled to receive natural gas from Anbar’s Akkas gas field.

The connecting pipeline must be completed, and stable fuel supplies are still required before the plant can be fully operational.

Once finished, the Anbar power plant is projected to improve energy supply across the province and add producing capacity to Iraq’s national grid.

World.title: Iraq’s Kurdish parties face government split as Baghdad’s influence grows
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Political disputes between the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), headed by Masoud Barzani, and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), led by Bafel Talabani, have prompted fears about the possibility of two opposing governments in Iraq’s Kurdistan.

The issue erupted when the KDP convened a parliamentary session in Erbil without the PUK’s participation.

Bafel Talabani, the head of the PUK, later announced his party’s resignation from the regional government, increasing the likelihood of a breakaway administration centered in Sulaymaniyah.

The KDP, headed by former Kurdistan Region President Masoud Barzani, is the region’s major political party, having primary bases in Erbil and Duhok.

The PUK, led by Bafel Talabani, the son of former Iraqi President Jalal Talabani, has its major stronghold in Sulaymaniyah.

Despite strong political conflicts, the two parties have traditionally shared power in the autonomous territory.

The widening split comes as Iraq’s federal government in Baghdad strengthens its control over disputed territory, notably Kirkuk and sections of Nineveh province, including Mosul.

Following the Kurdistan Region’s independence vote in 2017, Baghdad reasserted federal sovereignty over Kirkuk and numerous contested territories.

Mosul, however, remains under federal control, with Kurdish groups vying for political power in the surrounding districts.

A sustained schism between Barzani’s KDP and Talabani’s PUK might erode the Kurdistan Regional Government’s bargaining power with Baghdad over oil income, public-sector wages, budget transfers, and disputed territory.

The likelihood of rival Kurdish administrations has heightened fears about political fragmentation, possibly increasing Baghdad’s clout as the two parties battle to reach an agreement on a single regional government.

World.title: Erbil flash floods kill two, cause widespread damage
World.content:
Erbil (IraqiNews.com) – At least two people have died and widespread property damage has been reported after overnight flash floods struck Erbil, in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region, on Saturday, November 7.

Erbil’s governor acknowledged the deaths as rescue crews continued to react to floods in the city and neighboring regions. The casualties were believed to be a five-year-old youngster and a 24-year-old adult.

The flooding occurred when torrential rains inundated areas of the city, causing damage to houses, businesses, and infrastructure, with preliminary estimates indicating damage in the tens of millions of dollars.

According to Iraq’s Kurdistan Region Meteorological Department, Erbil received roughly 70 millimeters of rain in 24 hours.

For instance, Halabja got 80.6 millimeters over the same time with no corresponding destruction.

The disparity has sparked concerns about Erbil’s drainage infrastructure, urban planning, and preparation for inclement weather, especially given the city’s rapid urban development in recent years.

The catastrophe has also sparked political criticism, with media sources linked with opposing Kurdish political groups trading allegations about infrastructure management and government accountability.

Critics contend that recurring floods demonstrate the need for more investment in stormwater drainage infrastructure and better urban design to safeguard people and businesses.

Emergency response efforts continue as officials analyze the full scope of the devastation and aid impacted populations.

NEW DELHI: Thousands of earthen lamps lit up Srinagar's iconic Lal Chowk on Sunday evening as tourists and local residents came together to celebrate Diwali around the city's historic clock tower, popularly known as Ghanta Ghar.Dozens of tourists gathered at the clock tower and lit diyas, illuminating the area around the landmark.Local Hindus and Muslims also joined the celebrations, with people lighting firecrackers.Ankush Chatterjee, a tourist from Kolkata, said he was delighted to celebrate the festival in Kashmir. The atmosphere here is radiant," he told PTI.Diwali celebrations at Ghanta Ghar have become a regular sight in recent years, with tourists and residents gathering at Lal Chowk to mark the festival.Elsewhere in the Valley, security personnel celebrated Diwali by lighting lamps at their camps and distributing sweets.

Senior party leaders, including BJP national president Nitin Nabin, attended the ceremony, held between 10am and 10.30am.PM Modi marked the occasion by writing an article on Advani's contribution to Indian politics and the BJP. World.title: Watch: Sonia, Priyanka take a trip down memory lane, recall Diwali with Rajiv Gandhi
World.content:
Screengrab from the video posted by Sonia Gandhi on social media.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Veteran Congress leader Sonia Gandhi and her daughter, Priyanka Gandhi, revisited memories of Diwali celebrations with former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi.In a conversation shared on social media, Sonia Gandhi recalled her fondness for Diwali, describing the elaborate decorations, traditional rituals and festive gatherings that marked the celebrations."Oh, Diwali I loved. So, Diwali was always beautiful," she recalled in a video shared on her Instagram account.Recalling the traditional rituals, Sonia said a Ganesh idol was placed at the entrance of the house, where the first diya of the celebrations was lit. She added that the idol is now kept at her residence."At the entrance, there used to be a Ganesh Murti, which is now in my house. And so, we would do the first lighting of the diya in front of Ganesh Ji's Murti. And it was always decorated. In those days, we didn't have those little lights everywhere, but we had diyas everywhere - around the pond, all along the roof, veranda, and along the path, wherever there was a path. So, it was very pretty," she said.Priyanka Gandhi, the MP from Wayanad, also recalled how festivals were celebrated with great enthusiasm, with people from different walks of life gathering in the Gandhi family's garden.Sonia remembered how the family would sometimes get carried away with firecrackers, while Priyanka recalled how her father, Rajiv Gandhi, would take them to Chandni Chowk in Old Delhi to buy crackers."Papa used to take us to Chandni Chowk to buy crackers. We used to go to Old Delhi to buy crackers," Priyanka recalled.Sonia also remembered phuljhadis, or traditional sparklers, saying she enjoyed them, although she was less enthusiastic about some of the noisier fireworks.Beyond the lights and firecrackers, Sonia said the atmosphere during the festive season remained particularly memorable. Recalling the weather during those celebrations, she spoke about the clear blue skies that formed the backdrop to the festivities."Weather at that time was beautiful. Blue skies and all, which you hardly see now. Yeah, it was lovely," she said.Sonia also recalled that festivals were marked by Kashmiri cuisine and a traditional sweet rice preparation, a culinary tradition that continues in the family."And then, on festivals, we always used to have Kashmiri food and that sweet rice, like that, which we still make, by the way," she said.Sonia Gandhi has also documented several personal experiences and significant moments from her life in her memoir, titled *Belonging: A Journey of Love*. The book is scheduled to be launched on November 10.The memoir chronicles Sonia Gandhi's journey, from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance that brought her to India to the personal losses that profoundly shaped her life and her relationship with her adopted country.In the book, the 79-year-old Congress veteran, who holds the distinction of being the party's longest-serving president, revisits her childhood in Italy, her relationship with Rajiv Gandhi during their time at Cambridge, and the assassinations of her mother-in-law, former prime minister Indira Gandhi, and her husband, Rajiv Gandhi.

World.title: 3 Nigerian nationals arrested in Delhi for staying without valid documents

NEW DELHI: Three Nigerian nationals were arrested by the Delhi Police for allegedly staying in India without valid documents and subsequently sent to a detention centre, news agency PTI reported citing officials on Sunday.

Following their arrest, they were produced before the foreigners regional registration office (FRRO) and later sent to Sewa Sadan detention centre in Lampur, officials said.

World.title: Air pollution over 50 times WHO limit in parts of Delhi as people defy ban on firecrackers on Deepavali
World.content:
As Delhiites burst firecrackers well past the 10 p.m. deadline set by the Supreme Court for Deepavali night, air pollution shot up to over 50 times World Health Organisation (WHO) limits in parts of the city, official data showed.

The level of PM2.5 (a major pollutant) in Akshardham was 760.99 micrograms per cubic meter at 11 p.m. on Sunday (November 8, 2026), as per Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) data. This is about 50.73 times the WHO permissible limit of 15 micrograms per cubic meter for a 24-hour period.

Deepavali 2026: All you need to know about Supreme Court-permitted time slots, green crackers and other directives

PM2.5 (Particulate Matter 2.5) are fine inhalable particles, which can get into lungs and bloodstream and lead to a range of respiratory and other diseases.

The level of PM2.5 in Anand Vihar was 767 micrograms per cubic meter at 11 p.m. on Sunday (November 8, 2026), as per DPCC data — This is about 51.13 times the WHO permissible limit.

The level of PM2.5 in Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium was 702 micrograms per cubic meter, as per DPCC data, which is about 46.8 times the WHO permissible limit.

Also Read | Supreme Court calls Deepavali fireworks a ‘religious practice’, allows green crackers for two days in Delhi-NCR

The overall air quality of Delhi continued to be in the “very poor” category while many parts of the city continued to reel under “severe” air quality.

Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Also, pollution from stubble burning during October and November and bursting of firecrackers during the festive season add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

World.title: 19 Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen evacuated, Embassy says
World.content:
Nineteen Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen's Hodeidah and Sana'a for the past two weeks have been evacuated, with all of them safe and on their way back to their country, the Indian Embassy in Yemen said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

“All seafarers are safe, in good health, and on their way back to India. The Embassy sincerely thanks all concerned for their valuable cooperation and continued support in facilitating the safe evacuation of our Indian nationals,” the mission said in a post on X.

The Embassy of India to Yemen has successfully evacuated 19 Indian seafarers who were stranded in Hodeidah and Sana'a (Yemen) for the past two weeks. All seafarers are safe, in good health, and on their way back to India. The Embassy sincerely thanks all concerned for their valuable cooperation and continued support in facilitating the safe evacuation of our Indian nationals. @MEAIndia — India in Yemen (@IndiaInYemen) November 8, 2026

The evacuation comes days after India said 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht involved in an incident off the Yemeni coast were safe.

It is not immediately clear whether the 14 are among the 19 seafarers evacuated.

On October 23, the Indian mission had said all 14 Indian nationals aboard a yacht near Hodeidah were safe and that it was in contact with relevant parties to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Also Read | All 14 Indians in yacht incident off Yemen coast reported safe: Embassy

Some Arab media outlets had earlier quoted spokesperson Yahya Saree of the Yemen-based Houthi group as claiming that Saudi forces targeted the Indian yacht near Yuqar Island in the Red Sea, close to the Yemeni coast.

Mr. Saree had said the yacht was carrying 14 Indian nationals and that Houthi forces were rescuing them.

The incident came amid renewed escalation between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis, with attacks and counterattacks reported in recent days.

Saudi Arabia has intercepted Houthi missiles and drones, while Saudi-led coalition forces have carried out airstrikes in Yemen, raising fears of a return to wider conflict after relative calm under a 2022 truce.

The latest violence has also affected civilian and energy infrastructure and heightened concerns over security in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key international shipping route.

World.title: Tens of thousands march in Amsterdam, pressing Dutch government on Gaza, Israel
World.content:
Tens of thousands of people, many of them dressed in red, marched through Amsterdam on Sunday (November 8, 2026) in a mass demonstration aimed at pressing the Dutch government to take more decisive action against Israel over Gaza.

The organisers of the “Red Line” demonstrations in the Netherlands called for measures including stricter trade sanctions on Israel, officially declaring that Israel’s actions in Gaza amount to genocide, and halting all arms sales to Israel. The Dutch branch of Amnesty International, one of the organisers, said in an online post that more than 200,000 people joined the march.

“What is happening there is inhumane,” said Mike van Dongen, as he walked in the huge throng. He was critical of the Dutch government’s actions. “As far as I’m concerned, they are doing nothing,” he said. “They don’t dare take any serious steps.”

As the protesters marched along a normally busy Amsterdam street that was closed to traffic on Sunday, a man stood on a bus stop with a loudspeaker shouting “Free, free Palestine!” Many of the marchers echoed his cry as they passed.

Israel strongly rejects suggestions it is committing genocide in Gaza in its military campaign, which followed the attacks by Hamas-led militants in southern Israel on October 7, 2023. Militants killed about 1,200 people and took 251 hostages.

Israel’s retaliatory offensive has killed tens of thousands of Palestinians and destroyed much of Gaza. More than 1,550 Palestinians in Gaza have been killed by the Israeli military since a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas began in October 2025, according to the territory’s Health Ministry.

The ministry, part of the Hamas-run government, does not distinguish between civilians and militants, though it says women and children make up roughly half of the dead.

The campaign in Gaza has strained relations between the Netherlands and Israel. The Dutch Foreign Minister resigned last year after failing to secure new sanctions against Israel. Since then, a new minority coalition government has taken power and introduced an import ban on products from Israeli settlements, which the Dutch government and most of the international community consider illegal, a move that provoked a diplomatic spat with Israel.

Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who took part in a march last year but was not present on Sunday, defended his government’s actions at his weekly press conference on Friday (November 6, 2026). “Every single day and every single week, we do what we can to alleviate the terrible situation there,” he said.

He added that his administration was “exerting greater political and diplomatic pressure” on Israel to abide by its agreements on Gaza. At the same time, he said, the government was applying more pressure on Hamas and other organisations that continue to carry out “various operations that endanger the safety of ordinary Israelis.”

World.title: Democrats eye Musk, Miller probes after midterm rout
World.content:
Tech megabillionaire Elon Musk and President ‌Donald Trump's newly appointed White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller, ​will likely be targets of congressional probes when Democrats take control ⁠of Congress in January, a senior lawmaker said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

California Representative Robert Garcia, who is in line to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee next year after Democrats' sweeping midterm election victory, ‌said investigations will focus on Mr. Musk's involvement in the Department of Government Efficiency's firing of federal workers last year, and Mr. Miller's role in Mr. Trump's ‌hardline immigration crackdown.

"I think there's a lot of interest, not just from ‌our committee, ⁠but from committees across the Congress to speak to Mr. Musk," Mr. Garcia ⁠told CNN's "State of the Union."

Mr. Miller — whom Mr. Garcia called the architect of a "horrific, unjust" immigration policy — has been promoted to White House chief of staff, Mr. Trump said on Friday (November 6, 2026).

"Stephen Miller is at the centre ​of the major policy decisions that ‌are happening in the administration, and so it does deserve oversight and investigation," Mr. Garcia said.

The crackdown on immigration, which included operations in which two people were fatally shot in Minnesota by federal agents, has proven widely unpopular. A Reuters/Ipsos ‌poll in October found that only 37% approved of Mr. Trump's handling of immigration, ​down from 50% when he took office.

Voters delivered a historic rebuke to Republicans in Tuesday's (November 3, 2026) midterm election, but with Mr. Miller as White ⁠House chief of staff, the Trump administration is expected to continue its aggressive approach to immigration enforcement, amplify cultural conflicts and give no ground to a Democratic-controlled Congress, say officials ‌and experts who spoke to Reuters.

HEGSETH 'HAS GOT TO GO'

Hakeem Jeffries, who will become speaker of the U.S. House in January, said on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that Democrats would support a measure to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, a congressional process that could remove him from office.

Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, has said he will reintroduce articles of impeachment against Mr. Hegseth soon. Mr. Jeffries said he is a "hard yes" on ‌backing that measure.

"Pete Hegseth has got to go... I believe there will be incredibly strong support for ​that resolution," Mr. Jeffries told ABC's "This Week," citing the defense secretary's oversight of the unpopular Iran war launched by Mr. Trump in February, which has led ⁠to a spike in gas prices.

Attorney General Todd Blanche signalled on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that the Trump ⁠administration was prepared to battle the Democrats in Congress, calling threats by some Democrats to target administration officials and allies "not something we can tolerate in ‌this country."

"If that's what this new incoming leadership wants to do, we are ready," Mr. Blanche said. "If you work in this administration, you have a lawyer. ​It's me."

World.title: Thick smog blankets Delhi on Deepavali night, AQI at 20 stations ‘severe’
World.content:
A smoky haze hung over Delhi on Deepavali night, blurring streetlights and blanketing neighbourhoods as celebrations intensified across the capital, pushing air quality at 20 monitoring stations into the ‘severe’ category, with the overall Air Quality Index standing at 371 at 10 p.m..

The haze grew denser as the evening progressed, with smoke from firecrackers hanging over roads and residential neighbourhoods. The smell of burnt crackers lingered in the air, while visibility dropped in several parts of the capital and residents reported difficulty breathing.

Despite restrictions on bursting firecrackers, several parts of Delhi continued to witness their use on Sunday evening (November 8, 2026), with reports of fireworks emerging from areas, including Pitampura, Burari, Mayur Vihar and parts of Lutyens’ Delhi.

Ahead of Deepavali, the Delhi government had appealed to people to comply with the Supreme Court’s directions on sale and use of green firecrackers.

The District Magistrate (East), in an order, had permitted the bursting of green firecrackers only on November 7 and 8, between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. and 10 p.m..

Residents reported that firecrackers were being burst in outer Delhi’s Pitampura and Burari, with the intensity particularly high in Burari. Similar reports came from Mayur Vihar, while people in the Bishambardas Marg area and Lutyens’ Delhi said fireworks continued, although the intensity had reduced slightly.

Of the 59 monitoring stations, 19 were in the 'severe' category at 7 p.m., seven in the 'poor' category, and the remaining 33 in the 'very poor' category. Jahangirpuri recorded the highest AQI at 460.

The city's average AQI for the day settled at 376 in the 'very poor' category, compared to 369 on Saturday, amid a layer of smog and reduced visibility.

The court prohibited bursting of firecrackers within 300 metres of hospitals, nursing homes, health centres, old-age homes, educational institutions and other notified silence zones.

Only CSIR-NEERI-certified green firecrackers were permitted for sale, with the administration directing that they be sold exclusively at locations designated by the Delhi Police. The administration had also announced joint patrolling and enforcement teams comprising district officials and Delhi Police personnel to check unauthorised sale and use of prohibited firecrackers.

Meanwhile, the Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS) has forecast that Delhi's air quality is likely to slip into the 'severe' category from November 9 and remain there for the subsequent few days.

Weather and air quality experts have attributed the anticipated deterioration to unfavourable meteorological conditions, vehicular emissions, Deepavali celebrations and the ongoing peak stubble-burning season in neighbouring states.

PM2.5 remained the predominant pollutant in the national capital on Sunday (November 8, 2026), with firecracker emissions adding to the particulate matter levels.

World.title: Habitual offender arrested for murdering 65-year-old woman in Bengaluru
World.content:
The Kengeri police have arrested a habitual offender for allegedly murdering a 65-year-old woman who was sleeping outside a temple and robbing her of cash and a gold ring in Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout.

The deceased, Narayanamma, was found dead in front of the Pataladamma Temple at Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout, Konasandra, within Kengeri police station limits, on November 3.

According to the police, Narayanamma had left her house due to family problems and had been sleeping outside the temple for the past few days.

A local resident who noticed her body informed her son, who arrived at the spot and identified her. The Kengeri police initially registered an unnatural death report based on his complaint.

However, following the post-mortem examination and information gathered during the investigation, police suspected that she had been murdered and robbed. A murder case was subsequently registered on Thursday.

During the investigation, police apprehended a suspicious person moving around Vrushabhavathi Nagar Layout on Friday. During interrogation, he allegedly confessed to the crime.

The accused reportedly told investigators that he had noticed Narayanamma sleeping alone and decided to rob her to arrange money to fund his vices.

In the early hours of November 3, he allegedly went to the spot, covered her mouth, assaulted her and robbed her of the cash she was carrying and a gold ring before fleeing, leaving her dead.

Police said the accused has a criminal history and was previously involved in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and robbery cases at Girinagar and Cottonpet police stations.

Further investigation and interrogation are under way, police said.

World.title: Eisenkot warns of Israel crisis as he seeks to replace Netanyahu’s government
World.content:
Israel's former military chief Gadi Eisenkot started the tough task on Sunday (November 8, 2026) of forming a government, reaching out to Benjamin Netanyahu's allies as he warned the veteran Prime Minister had brought the country to a historic crisis.

Mr. Eisenkot, 66, a political novice who has vowed to bridge Israel's deep polarisation under Mr. Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from President Isaac Herzog, giving him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority.

"We are in a state of emergency, approaching a point of no return for the State of Israel," Mr. Eisenkot, who had traded his usual all black for a suit and tie, said at a ceremony at the Presidential office.

"We must form a national emergency government. This will require creative and unconventional political steps."

Mr. Eisenkot, born to a family of working-class Moroccan immigrants, would be the first Sephardic Prime Minister — a community mostly descended from West Asian or North African Jews — in a country long dominated by an Ashkenazi elite with ties to Europe.

Mr. Netanyahu is Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, having led the country on and off for nearly two decades. He has taken the country in a sharply rightward direction and led wars in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran since the October 7, 2023, attacks by Hamas.

Both Mr. Eisenkot and Mr. Herzog acknowledged Israel's growing isolation under Mr. Netanyahu, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court.

In the United States, the most vital ally of Israel, Democrats on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) swept elections with calls to rein in Israel after the devastation in Gaza and the unpopular Iran war which Mr. Netanyahu launched with President Donald Trump.

"We are in the midst of a devastating diplomatic crisis. Even our closest friends and strategic allies are saying their relationship with Israel must be reassessed," Mr. Eisenkot said.

Mr. Eisenkot appealed to Mr. Netanyahu's Likud Party as well as the far-right party of Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich to join — but only with himself as Prime Minister.

"My door is open and my hand is extended, wholeheartedly and willingly, to anyone who understands the gravity of this moment," he said.

Wooing the ultra-Orthodox

In consultations last week with Mr. Herzog, Mr. Eisenkot received recommendations from parties accounting for 67 lawmakers, against 46 for Mr. Netanyahu.

But that vote count included Israeli Arabs, whose seat haul surged to a historic high on anger over Mr. Netanyahu's government and whom several parties oppose having in government.

Avigdor Liberman, a former Netanyahu aide turned sharp critic who nonetheless shares his hawkish views, has been adamant against any alliance with Arab Israelis, who are descendants of Palestinians who stayed after Israel's creation in 1948.

Taking back one of his signature campaign pledges, Mr. Liberman instead voiced an openness to an alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jews, whose almost singular priority is ensuring that they remain exempt from military service.

The exemption for the ultra-Orthodox — whose two main parties had been aligned with Mr. Netanyahu but could push Mr. Eisenkot to a majority — has been a source of growing resentment for many Israelis as reservists fight on multiple tours of duty.

Mr. Liberman said on Sunday (November 8, 2026) he still backed conscription for all Israelis but that he had to make "difficult decisions" for the higher priority of ousting Mr. Netanyahu, who faces corruption charges that could land him in jail if he loses power.

Naftali Bennett, the second strongest opposition leader after Mr. Liberman, has also been outspoken against the ultra-Orthodox community's military exemption and has stayed quiet since Mr. Liberman's about-face.

Fragile power

Mr. Eisenkot has appeared to suggest he is willing to start off with a minority government — relying on outside votes from Arab-Israeli parties — before bringing other lawmakers into his coalition.

Assaf Shapira, a political expert at the Israel Democracy Institute, said Mr. Eisenkot would face an exceptionally fragile government if it only had 48 lawmakers in the 120-member parliament, with extensive negotiations needed on every piece of legislation.

Mr. Eisenkot has vowed to put an end to rampant violence against Palestinians by extremist West Bank settlers supported by Mr. Netanyahu's government and has warned that the incumbent premier does not have the mandate for another attack on Iran.

But he has largely backed Mr. Netanyahu's war decisions and as military chief during the 2006 Lebanon war advocated massive force against civilian infrastructure where enemies operate, a policy critics say amounts to a war crime.

In Tel Aviv, Neri Bar-On, who works in educational technology, said he expected Mr. Eisenkot to succeed in forming a government.

"But the problems run deeper," he said.

"The country is facing a massive internal conflict; even if he manages to form a government, it won't solve the underlying issues."

World.title: South Africa's ANC suffers worst election result as decline continues
World.content:
South Africa's African National Congress party faced its worst election results ever on Sunday (November 8, 2026) and a new low point on its gradual decline in popularity as voters rebuked it for a failure to deliver basic services like water and electricity in towns and cities.

The once-dominant ANC — the party of Nelson Mandela — had received around 30% of the vote in Wednesday's (November 4, 2026) local government elections with 99% of ballots counted. The final results were expected late on Sunday (November 8, 2026), according to the Independent Electoral Commission.

The ANC remained the largest party by total share in an election involving hundreds of parties, but the Democratic Alliance that is its main Opposition had received around 25% of votes in the near-complete count.

That brought closer to reality the once-unthinkable notion that the ANC that led South Africa out of the white minority rule of apartheid and delivered freedom in 1994 under Mandela might one day not be its biggest party. It used to command 70% of the vote.

Catastrophic outcome for the ANC

The ANC's popularity has declined for more than a decade. It won 45% support in the last local elections in 2021, the first time it had dropped below 50% in any election. In 2024, it then lost its Parliamentary majority for the first time in a national election, which brought about a coalition national government and a seismic shift in South African politics.

The ANC was on course Sunday (November 8, 2026) for a steep drop of about 15 percentage points from the last local elections and the loss of approximately one-third of its support from five years ago.

“If anyone has not heard what the people are saying in this election, then you are lost,” said ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula. “This has been a very catastrophic outcome for the ANC.”

He said the results called for the ANC “to be humble, to hear our people and respect them,” and to “earn again through service and not through slogans the trust people have lent to others.”

DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis said his party — which was around 20% points behind the ANC in the 2024 national election — had now “taken a big step forward” in its aim to be South Africa's biggest.

As the ANC declines, voters leave for several parties

But, while the ANC's popularity has dropped sharply, no single party has overtaken it as the vote has fragmented among many parties on a local and national scale.

Another seven major parties shared around 30% of the vote in these local elections, which had more than 500 parties contesting and many picking up small shares. The MK Party led by former South African President Jacob Zuma, who broke away from the ANC and was expelled by it, held the third-largest share of votes at around 10%.

Failed public services key issue

Voters across South Africa have long expressed frustration over failed public services that have left many cities and towns with regular water and electricity outages, broken roads and streetlights, and uncollected refuse.

Those local government failures, along with long-held anger over corruption scandals connected to the ANC, largely were the key issues in this election. The election was to choose local government councilors that run South Africa's eight biggest cities as well as its 44 district and 205 local municipalities.

The ANC loses major cities

The ANC was on course to lose its place as the largest party to the DA in the economic hub of Johannesburg, the capital of Pretoria, and the large Ekurhuleni municipality east of Johannesburg. The DA retained its control of the second biggest city of Cape Town.

In Johannesburg, where failed services have been most under scrutiny, the white-led DA put forward its former leader, 75-year-old Helen Zille, as a candidate for mayor.

Her campaign included stunts like her snorkeling in a trench filled with water in the middle of one of the city's roads in an attempt to highlight the failures.

There will now be complex coalition negotiations

While the ANC's decline was obvious in the biggest cities, most of them could be left with hung councils because no party was set to win a majority.

That meant a series of complex coalition agreements will be required to decide who governs and the ANC could be part of the governing coalitions.

World.title: PML-N retains both Gujranwala's NA-77 and Sahiwal's PP-203, unofficial results show
World.content:
LAHORE: The ruling PML-N retained Gujranwala’s National Assembly constituency NA-77 and Sahiwal’s Punjab Assembly constituency PP-203 in Sunday’s by-election.

Both seats had fallen vacant after the deaths of their respective lawmakers in September. Polling in the constituencies began at 8am and concluded at 5pm, with the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) reporting an uninterrupted and largely peaceful process.

In NA-77, PML-N candidate Rashid Basheer Virk was among 11 candidates contesting for the seat left vacant after the Sept 11 demise of his father, Chaudhry Mehmood Bashir Virk, a five-time MNA.

He secured victory by bagging 43,365 votes, while Pakistan Markazi Muslim League’s (PMML) Mohammad Ibrahim remained runner-up with 30,218 ballots, according to the Form-47 seen by Dawn.

Form-47 is the provisional consolidated statement of results of the vote count of all polling stations in a constituency, prepared by the returning officer (RO) concerned.

In PP-203 of Chichawatni, PML-N’s Muhammad Asad Hanif Jutt won with 42,114 votes, defeating his closest rival, Muhammad Awais Mahmood of Tehreek-i-Ehsas Pakistan (TEP), who secured 24,512 votes, according to its Form-47.

Both by-elections were marked by a low voter turnout, with 15.7 per cent in NA-77 and 27.6pc recorded in PP-203, according to Forms 47.

The by-poll was held following the death of PML-N MPA Chaudhry Muhammad Hanif Jutt. This was the second time that a by-election was held in the constituency after the 2024 general elections.

Notices were also issued to several PML-N lawmakers for alleged violations of the election code, mostly over visiting polling stations in the two constituencies.

Earlier in the day, Chief Election Commissioner Sikander Sultan Raja visited the provincial election chief’s office, where he was briefed on the polling process in both constituencies, ECP said.

After the balloting process concluded, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, whose PML-N is in power in the province, made multiple posts on X, claiming her party was in the lead in both NA-77 and PP-203.

In one post, CM Maryam wrote, “This electoral victory is no ordinary victory. It is a resounding public rebuke to conspiracy peddlers, hate mongers and those who refuse to read the writing on the wall.”

She contended that the results portrayed that the “politics of delivery is far more enduring than the politics of hate and revenge”.

“I am glad politics has returned to delivery and performance. Wake up and smell the coffee… or keep sleeping in denial!” the PML-N leader added.

Notices over alleged electoral conduct violations

While the polling was under way, notices, copies of which are available with Dawn, were issued to Punjab MPA Qudsia Batool, MNA Saira Afzal Tarar and Parliamentary Secretary for Information and Culture Shazia Rizwan for alleged violation of the Code of Conduct after reports emerged on social media that the three had visited various polling stations within NA-77, a statement issued by the office of the provincial election commissioner said.

Notices were also issued over alleged violations of the Code of Conduct to PML-N’s MNA Syeda Nosheen Iftikhar and MPA Hina Arshad Warraich for allegedly visiting polling stations.

The officials were directed to appear at the Election Complex in Gujranwala for an explanation at 3pm.

Separately, PML-N leader and Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari claimed in a post on X that supporters of PMML candidate Qazi Ibrahim Gujjar were caught “openly stamping ballots” with the election commission staff present.

Acting on the complaint, the provincial election commissioner said the returning officer concerned has been directed to probe the matter and submit a report.

On Saturday, the ECP took notice of an alleged violation of the Code of Conduct by Information Minister Attaullah Tarar during by-election campaigning in NA-77 .

According to a cause list issued on Sunday, Tarar, along with Virk, Batool and others, has been summoned to appear at the next hearing on Nov 12.

According to the ECP, the minister visited the constituency by helicopter and addressed a campaign event for Rashid, violating a provision in the Code of Conduct , which bars public office holders from participating in campaign activities.

ECP has sought a report from the district monitoring officer and the district returning officer to inquire into the matter. The watchdog also said that the result of the constituency could be withheld until a final decision is made on the matter.

Meanwhile, notices were also issued to PML-N MPAs Malik Qasim Nadeem and Motiya Begum for allegedly visiting several polling stations in Chichawatni’s PP-203 on the polling day.

The notices issued by the district monitoring officer, seen by Dawn, accused both of violating Para 48 of the Code of Conduct, which bars “all kinds of campaigns” and canvassing within a 400-metre radius of a polling station.

The MPAs were asked to appear either in person or through counsel at the Municipal Committee Office at 5pm on Nov 9 (Monday) to clarify their position.

Polling in PP-203

The seat was initially won in 2024 by independent candidate Rai Murtaza Iqbal, backed by the PTI, with 55,874 votes against Jutt, who polled 35,163 votes.

However, Iqbal, along with four other PTI-backed parliamentarians, was disqualified and denotified by the ECP following their conviction by an anti-terrorism court in Faisalabad on July 31.

Subsequently, the ECP scheduled a by-election for Nov 23, 2025, which was won by Jutt with 46,820 votes. His closest rival, independent candidate Falik Sher, secured 10,975 votes.

Jutt died of cardiac arrest on Sept 17 this year, necessitating Sunday’s by-election in the constituency.

Around 1,370 polling personnel, including 574 women and 796 men, were deputed at 185 polling stations across the constituency.

District Police Officer Usman Tipu said 1,100 personnel had been deployed to ensure security during the by-election.

A total of 185 polling stations had been established in the constituency, including 11 in Category A, 37 in Category B and 137 in Category C.

A comprehensive traffic management plan had also been devised, with more than 65 personnel assigned duties.

World.title: Eisenkot says Israel in 'devastating diplomatic crisis' as he seeks to form govt
World.content:
Israel’s former military chief Gadi Eisenkot started the tough task on Sunday of forming a government, reaching out to Benjamin Netanyahu’s allies as he warned the veteran prime minister had brought the country to a historic crisis.

Eisenkot, 66, a political novice who has vowed to bridge Israel’s deep polarisation under Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from President Isaac Herzog, giving him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority.

“We are in a state of emergency, approaching a point of no return for the State of Israel,” Eisenkot said at a ceremony at the presidential office.

Both Eisenkot and Herzog acknowledged Israel’s growing isolation under Netanyahu, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court over allegations of crimes against humanity and war crimes in Gaza.

“We are in the midst of a devastating diplomatic crisis. Even our closest friends and strategic allies are saying their relationship with Israel must be reassessed,” Eisenkot said.

“We must form a national emergency government. This will require creative and unconventional political steps,” Eisenkot stressed.

He said Israeli democracy was at a vulnerable moment at a time when it faced immense challenges. “There is great urgency for new leadership, leadership that people can look in the eye and trust,” he said.

Eisenkot appealed to Netanyahu’s Likud Party as well as the far-right party of Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich to join — but only with himself as prime minister.

“My door is open and my hand is extended, wholeheartedly and willingly, to anyone who understands the gravity of this moment,” he said.

Meanwhile, Herzog cited a threat of attack from Iran, the need to progress towards peace in Gaza and negotiations with Lebanon and other neighbours.

“We need to start shaping the political horizon in the region, and we also have to present the 20 points of the agreement in the Gaza strip, and consultations with our neighbours in Lebanon and the region,” he was quoted as saying in a translation by Al Jazeera.

“We also have to deal with the sanctions and the political challenges in light of the recent political developments in the United States,” the Israeli president said.

In the United States, the most vital ally of Israel, Democrats on Tuesday swept the midterm elections with calls to rein in Israel after the devastation in Gaza and the unpopular Iran war which Netanyahu launched with President Donald Trump.

Eisenkot, born to a family of working-class Moroccan immigrants, would be the first Sephardic prime minister — a community mostly descended from Middle Eastern or North African Jews — in a country long dominated by an Ashkenazi elite with ties to Europe.

Netanyahu is Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, having led the country on and off for nearly two decades. He has taken the country in a sharply rightward direction and led wars against Gaza, Lebanon and Iran since the Oct 7, 2023 attacks by Hamas.

Netanyahu called for a unity government of all Zionist parties to preserve a Jewish state, while giving no indication whether he was prepared to serve under Eisekenkot’s leadership.

“This is the will of the people and the need of the hour,” he said in a statement, ruling out a coalition government with Arabs — who make up 21 per cent of Israel’s population.

Nearly all Jewish parties now share Netanyahu’s rejection of an eventual independent Palestinian state, the basis of internationally endorsed peace efforts since the 1990s.

Negotiations can take 6 weeks

Eisenkot’s potential pathways to power include trying to form a minority government with Arab party support for key issues; forming a coalition with ultra-Orthodox parties that he and his allies have shunned in the past; or forging a unity government with Netanyahu. All three options face formidable obstacles.

Eisenkot has appeared to suggest he is willing to start off with a minority government — relying on outside votes from Arab-Israeli parties — before bringing other lawmakers into his coalition.

He said he will call on all parties to join who meet his main principles. These include recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state; a duty of national service for all to strengthen the military and expand its ranks; and recognition of Hamas as a terrorist organisation and a commitment to destroying its military and governing capacity.

“I am convinced that it is possible and right to form a new government quickly, one that will win a large majority in the Knesset,” Eisenkot said, referring to Israel’s parliament.

Eisenkot now has 28 days plus a possible 14-day extension. If he fails, Netanyahu will likely get his shot at forming a government. Should he also be unable, new elections could be called.

Assaf Shapira, a political expert at the Israel Democracy Institute, said Eisenkot would face an exceptionally fragile government if it only had 48 lawmakers in the 120-member parliament, with extensive negotiations needed on every piece of legislation.

Eisenkot’s views

Eisenkot has vowed to put an end to rampant violence against Palestinians by extremist West Bank settlers supported by Netanyahu’s government and has warned that the incumbent premier does not have the mandate for another attack on Iran.

But he shares Netanyahu’s hawkish security views that have hardened since Oct 7, 2023: he opposes Palestinian statehood and says Hamas’s military wing must be destroyed or dismantled.

He emphasised his security credentials on the campaign trail, citing his “ Dahiya doctrine ” of responding to attacks with disproportionate force, which he deployed as a commander during Israel’s 2006 war with Hezbollah in Lebanon.

Both Eisenkot and Netanyahu say Israeli troops will not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas ​is disarmed, and that Israel is prepared to ​restart fighting to achieve this.

Although Eisenkot has criticised settler violence against Palestinians in occupied West Bank, which has surged since 2023, he favours settlement in principle and says it should comply with Israeli law.

He opposes settlements built without authorisation, aims to dismantle outposts in areas where ​they are forbidden and has pledged to rein in violent settlers.

Wooing the ultra-Orthodox

In consultations last week with Herzog, Eisenkot received recommendations from parties accounting for 67 lawmakers, against 46 for Netanyahu.

But that vote count included Israeli Arabs, whose seat haul surged to a historic high on anger over Netanyahu’s government and whom several parties oppose having in government.

Potentially making Eisenkot’s job tougher is the position of one opposition leader, Avigdor Lieberman of the Israel Our Home party, who has ruled out a unity government with Netanyahu or a minority government that has backing from Arab parties.

Lieberman, a former Netanyahu aide turned sharp critic who nonetheless shares his hawkish views, has been adamant against any alliance with Arab Israelis, who are descendants of Palestinians who stayed after Israel’s creation in 1948.

But Lieberman has softened his stance on sitting with ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties as long as they agree to support a law under which ultra-Orthodox men serve in the military.

Taking back one of his signature campaign pledges, Lieberman instead voiced an openness to an alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jews, whose almost singular priority is ensuring that they remain exempt from military service.

The exemption for the ultra-Orthodox — whose two main parties had been aligned with Netanyahu but could push Eisenkot to a majority — has been a source of growing resentment for many Israelis as reservists fight on multiple tours of duty.

Lieberman said on Sunday he still backed conscription for all Israelis but that he had to make “difficult decisions” for the higher priority of ousting Netanyahu, who faces corruption charges that could land him in jail if he loses power.

Naftali Bennett, the second strongest opposition leader after Lieberman, has also been outspoken against the ultra-Orthodox community’s military exemption and has stayed quiet since Lieberman’s about-face.

In Tel Aviv, Neri Bar-On, who works in educational technology, said he expected Eisenkot to succeed in forming a government.

“But the problems run deeper,” he said.

“The country is facing a massive internal conflict; even if he manages to form a government, it won’t solve the underlying issues.”

World.title: Husband held, investigation launched after anchorperson shot dead at Rawalpindi home
World.content:
RAWALPINDI: Anchorperson Rabia Ahsan was found shot dead at her home in the Gulshanabad area of Rawalpindi on Sunday, police said.

In a statement, City Police Officer (CPO) Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera said Ahsan’s husband was taken into custody and the suspected weapon was seized.

He added that an investigation has been launched.

CPO Sukhera, along with the senior superintendent of police (SSP) operations and the SSP investigations, arrived at the scene with a team of forensic experts to inspect the crime scene.

As per the statement, a male domestic worker at their house informed the police that the victim’s husband said the gunshot had been fired accidentally.

CPO Sukhera said that Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) teams were collecting evidence from the scene of the incident, while the body was being taken to the hospital for postmortem examination.

Sukhera said that a case of the incident was being registered, adding that an investigation on merit will be ensured.

While investigation into the motive was under way, First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari “expressed deep sadness over the killing” and “strongly condemned the violence”.

She called for a thorough, impartial and transparent investigation to establish the facts and ensure that those responsible are held accountable, a statement by the Presidency said.

She also expressed dismay over the “disturbing pattern of killing of another professional woman in the same metropolitan area”.

Aseefa recalled the murder case of Hina Javed, a 45-year-old digital media executive who was found dead at her Rawalpindi residence in August with signs of torture.

“Such incidents demand serious attention and accountability. Women must be able to live and work without fear for their lives,” she stressed.

The First Lady noted that the outcome of the investigation into Hina’s case was still awaited. According to a DNA analysis report, DNA samples of Hina’s domestic servant matched postmortem swabs collected from her body, while her husband’s DNA also matched samples taken from multiple items at the crime scene.

In a subsequent comment, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz had noted that “DNA test results and polygraph test suggest that the murder and rape were committed by the servant; however the investigation is ongoing”.

On Oct 29, Aseefa had met with Hina’s family at the Parliament and called for the family’s demand of a judicial commission to be “given due consideration”.

World.title: Hamza Zahoor’s unbeaten century guides Pakistan U-19 to thrilling win over India
World.content:
Hamza Zahoor produced a match-winning unbeaten century as Pakistan Under-19 defeated arch-rivals India by three wickets in a thrilling Group ‘A’ encounter of the ACC Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Muscat on Sunday.

Chasing 209, Pakistan reached the target in 48.1 overs, finishing on 211 for seven, with Hamza holding his nerve under pressure to steer his side home.

The wicket-keeper-batter remained unbeaten on 100 off 108 balls, striking 10 fours and three sixes, and was named Player of the Match.

Pakistan’s chase, however, was far from straightforward as India’s bowlers made early inroads to reduce them to 61 for five. Hamza then joined Hasnain Abbas Dar, who contributed 38, to revive the innings with a crucial partnership.

With wickets falling at the other end, Hamza showed remarkable composure, combining caution with timely aggression to keep Pakistan on course. He eventually guided the lower order across the finish line with 11 balls to spare, completing a memorable century in the process.

Earlier, India, after electing to bat, were bowled out for 208 in 46.3 overs. Their innings got off to a disastrous start when captain and opener Lakshya Rajesh Raichandani was dismissed for a duck off the second ball.

India slipped further to 22 for three, leaving their middle order under considerable pressure.

Arjun Rajput then mounted a spirited recovery with an outstanding 107 off 85 deliveries, hitting 11 fours and five sixes.

However, the right-hander received little support from the other end as Pakistan’s bowlers maintained pressure and regularly picked up wickets to restrict India to a modest total.

Ali Raza, Rizwanullah and Niqab Shafiq shared the spoils with three wickets apiece, while Mohammad Sayyam claimed one.

The victory takes Pakistan to the top of Group ‘A’ with four points from two matches, having registered back-to-back wins.

India, meanwhile, have two points from as many games, with one victory and one defeat.

Both teams have one group fixture remaining, with the top two sides advancing to the semi-finals.

World.title: Aramco skyscraper damaged as Houthis target Riyadh financial district
World.content:
An Aramco building in Riyadh was targeted in an “attempted attack”, the Saudi energy ministry said on Sunday, with eyewitnesses telling AFP the skyscraper sustained damage, after the Saudi-led coalition fighting Houthis said it had intercepted missiles launched by the group.

Houthis claimed responsibility for the attack. Aramco facilities and infrastructure have been repeatedly struck by the rebels in Yemen in recent months, with tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company headquarters all targeted by the group.

The energy ministry said in a statement that “an administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh was subjected to an attempted attack today”.

“The incident resulted in falling shrapnel that caused minor damage to the building, with no injuries or fatalities reported, thankfully.”

Houthis “carried out four qualitative military operations, using a number of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones”, the group claimed in an English-language statement, listing targets including the financial centre, Riyadh airport, Aramco oil storage tanks and the eastern Saudi city of Abqaiq.

“Aramco tower in KAFD has been targeted, that’s the sure thing,” an eyewitness told AFP, referring to the King Abdullah Financial District. Two other witnesses confirmed seeing damage to the building.

The Houthis seized the Yemeni capital Sanaa in 2014.

A 2022 truce that had paused fighting in the long-running conflict fell apart in July, and Saudi Arabia has since traded blows with the Houthis, who have struck Saudi airports, energy infrastructure and military sites.

This picture shows Aramco tower in the King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD) in Riyadh on March 3, 2025. — AFP/File

KAFD is one of the most visible manifestations of the kingdom’s ongoing economic and social reforms drive, with towering glass skyscrapers, high-end retail outlets and green spaces dotting the area.

The area is home to some of the kingdom’s biggest homegrown companies and blue-chip international firms like Goldman Sachs.

The headquarters of the kingdom’s influential sovereign wealth fund — the Public Investment Fund — and the Saudi stock exchange are also located in the heart of the district.

Targeting the area, which is also home to residential housing and a large metro station with heavy commuter traffic during the morning rush hour, would mark a major escalation in the kingdom’s fight with the Houthis.

Loud explosions heard

The attack came hours after the kingdom’s education ministry announced, late on Saturday, the return of in-person schooling after weeks of remote learning in Riyadh following an earlier wave of strikes.

Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki, in a Sunday morning social media post, said that “air defences intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi terrorist militia towards Riyadh”, as loud explosions were heard in the Saudi capital.
